summary: Honesty/correctness sweep of the 22 unexamined Tradermigos tabs

tabs.summary: PRIMARY_NAV + MORE_NAV cover 21 of the 22 registry tabs — 'analytics' has no entry, and Header is the only nav rendered above 768px. The api-badge (line 579-586) claims "Connected to live APIs" from an OR'd flag while the adjacent Ticker (line 589) can be rendering hardcoded sample sales. Account menu, More portal, badges, and prefetch wiring are all sound.

PRIMARY_TABS (5) + MORE_TABS (17) = all 22 VALID_TABS, every key routable. Lite filtering uses LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY / LITE_HIDDEN_ALL correctly and matches what App.jsx's redirect enforces. No claims, no data reads, no dead controls.

22 tabs, all with renderTab cases and (except analytics) at least one nav entry. navRouting.test.jsx only asserts nav ⊆ VALID_TABS, never VALID_TABS ⊆ nav, which is why the analytics gap shipped undetected. Seaport target pinning (resolveSeaportTarget, line 138-143) is fail-closed and correct.

All 22 VALID_TABS entries have a renderTab case and parseRoute 404s cleanly on anything else. Deep-link parsing is strict-digits, the /nft/ close paths land on the explicit /gallery segment, and each tab is wrapped in a keyed ErrorBoundary. The two defects are at the edges: the LIVE/DEMO badge is OR'd across two independent read paths (line 820), and the Lite-mode redirect (line 423-434, default mode is Lite) bounces deep links to 9 tabs including analytics.

Lore, origin prose, ecosystem, and shortcut panels are static reference content and read honestly. Two problems: the four stat cards render the same fallback stats Hero explicitly badges 'cached', with no marker at all; and the hardcoded Discord invites contradict the collection's own lore record (discord: null).

tabs.component: frontend/src/nakamigos/components/ActivityFeed.jsx (+ api.js fetchActivity, useCollection.js, useActivityWebSocket.js, useOpenSeaStream.js, lib/eventFeed.js, lib/trades.js, lib/washTrade.js)
tabs.summary: Empty-state copy is genuinely well differentiated (apiEmpty vs apiFallback vs no-data, ActivityFeed.jsx:334-375) and the wash-trade exclusion (lib/washTrade.js) is a model of not-guessing. But the time axis is broken in two independent places: live OpenSea events are dated 1970 because event_timestamp (Unix seconds) is fed to new Date() as milliseconds, and live on-chain transfers get a hardcoded 12.000 s/block extrapolation whose error grows monotonically. On top of that the SALES/VOLUME headline is a count over one 50-row API page presented as a stat for the selected 24h/7d/30d window, and the Alchemy fallback silently substitutes all-time results when the selected window is empty.

The copy is unusually honest — it says plainly that alerts monitor the collection floor, not individual tokens. But the floor poller ignores the fallback flag on the stats read, so when both upstreams fail it displays and fires alerts on a hardcoded 0.1048 ETH.

Unreached. The tab renders and routes, but there is no clickable path to it on desktop at all, and for the default (Lite) user it is unreachable on every viewport — see finding 'Analytics tab has no nav entry on desktop'.

'My Bids' and 'Bid History' are honest — both call openseaGet directly and set a visible fetchError banner when the read fails, and the active/expired filtering is correct. NetProceeds on received offers is a model of honesty (exact tier from the order's own ERC20 consideration, disclosed estimate otherwise, never a fabricated royalty). The accept/cancel money paths are chain-guarded, target-pinned and function-allowlisted. But the 'Received Offers' tab launders TWO independent failed reads into the sentence 'No offers received', the 'Counter' button is dead for essentially every offer, and criteria bids render as a specific token id.

tabs.component: CommunityChat (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/CommunityChat.jsx, 947 lines) plus lib/supabase.js, lib/supabaseProxy.js, lib/dm.js, hooks/useSiweAuth.js, hooks/useHolderStatus.jsx, and the embedded DirectMessages.jsx DM sub-view
tabs.summary: Reachable in prod (VALID_TABS constants.js:93, Header.jsx:149, MobileNav.jsx:22, App.jsx:781). Credit where due: this component already fixes the headline read-honesty case — fetchMessages returns null (not []) on backend error (supabase.js:176-182) and CommunityChat renders a distinct "Chat Unreachable" state (lines 695-702) instead of the cheerful be-the-first empty state, and DirectMessages.classify() (lines 172-178) properly separates needs-auth / not-enabled / transient error. The XSS sanitizer (DOMParser, lines 65-77), the ENS resolve-never-auto-trust flow (DirectMessages 254-293), and the no-trade-history impersonation warning are genuinely careful work. The material problem is the holder gate: fetchWalletNfts (api.js:660-663) swallows every error and returns totalCount:0, so a failed Alchemy read renders as the factual sentence "Own a Nakamigos to post" AND is cached to localStorage for 5 minutes. Secondary: fetchMessages pages the oldest 100 rows rather than the newest; likes fail silently; a network blip is reported as "Reactions aren't enabled yet"; the "Live" badge is an env-var check, not a connectivity check. No money path in the room itself; the only tx-signing surface reachable from this tab is acceptTrade via the DM trade card, which is correctly scoped to trades already addressed to the viewer.

Grid, empty state, retry generation-guarding and the Bundle flag gate are all honest. The listings half is not: ACTIVE LISTINGS / "N listed" reads OpenSea only, so the native-orderbook listings this tab's own Bulk List button creates are invisible and un-cancellable here; a failed listings read renders as "no listings" with no error; the Cancel button sends the cancel to a hardcoded Seaport 1.5 while the order's own protocolAddress is discarded, then reports success; and FLOOR PRICE / EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE / the CSV export render the hardcoded fallback floor unbadged.

The deal math itself is defensible — the >=3-listings-per-trait gate (line 544) and the exclude-own-listing logic close the obvious fake-discount hole, the slow-load message is honest, and the scatter plot has a real a11y equivalent. But the tab is structurally blind to a listings outage: fetchListings swallows both upstream failures and never emits an error field, so Deals renders 'All listings are priced at or above their trait floors' as a verdict on a read that returned nothing. The Buy button also has no max-spend bound.

The component itself is the cleanest of the four: id normalization is correct (FavoritesContext maps to String on both load and toggle), it renders through Card which suppresses approximate ranks and handles null price honestly, and it explicitly tells the user when favorited NFTs are not yet loaded rather than silently dropping them. Two issues, both inherited: the cross-device restore read is blocked by RLS so a favorites list saved elsewhere renders as "No favorites yet", and the EST. VALUE tile can never render because allTokens always carry price: null.

Honest. Favorites are read from context, the grid renders only tokens actually loaded, and line 74-78 explicitly discloses how many favorited NFTs are not yet loaded rather than silently dropping them. The EST. VALUE card is gated on totalValue > 0 and, because gallery tokens carry price:null, simply never renders — it never shows a fabricated 0.

The data itself is trustworthy: every recordTransaction call site (Listings, Modal, ShoppingCart, SweepCalculator, Deals, OrderBookPanel) fires only after tx.wait() confirms a non-reverted receipt, and the EIP-5792 batch path checks per-call receipt status before reporting success — so no unconfirmed purchase is ever written. The Etherscan link is regex-guarded (line 153). The problems are scope and copy: this is a browser-local localStorage log presented under the unqualified heading 'Transaction History' with the factual empty-state 'No {collection} transactions yet', and the empty state promises offers and bids that no code path ever records.

Renders a per-browser localStorage log under the heading 'Transaction History' with no disclosure that it is device-local and capped at 50. Etherscan links are regex-validated before rendering, which is good. The empty state asserts 'No {collection} transactions yet' on any read failure or new device.

The best-behaved of the three — the detection core genuinely self-gates to measured:false, never substitutes synthetic data, and discloses sales/owner outages. Four real gaps remain: the '30 days' label can silently cover a decade because fetchActivity retries at daysBack 3650; a listings-feed failure is the one feed with no unavailable flag and renders as 'No active listings to measure'; a floor with zero attributable makers scores a green 'Well distributed' badge over an empty set; and 'TOP 10 OF SUPPLY' actually reports a share of counted-holder supply, which diverges badly when the owner list hits the 8-page truncation cap.

The buy grid, buy path and price math are sound (native fulfillment pins the Seaport target, checks expiry + on-chain order status, and the displayed price_eth is provably the same consideration sum that fulfillNativeOrder sends as msg.value — frontend/api/orderbook.js:686-692 sums ALL consideration items, so the buyer is not undercharged/overcharged). Sorting, median-leading price stats, purchased-id suppression, and the render-chunk windowing are all honest. Two material honesty defects: a total listings-read outage renders as a green, definitive 'No active listings right now', and the hardcoded FALLBACK_ACTIVITY sample sales render unlabelled in the RECENT SALES grid. Floor/owners/supply stat cards can also be the hardcoded FALLBACK_STATS with no 'cached' badge that Hero.jsx already implements.

This page contains the best failed-read handling in the three tabs — MyListings.jsx:304-307 explicitly detects the server's degraded 200-with-empty-list soft-fail, keeps what is on screen and shows a banner rather than rendering 'No active listings'. The fee math is correct: computeRevenue subtracts exactly the 1% platform fee that createNativeListing actually carves out of the seller's consideration, and the cancel path cancels on-chain first with the backend notify strictly best-effort. The defects are copy and provenance: the empty state instructs sellers to do something that provably cannot make listings appear here, and the floor-relative badges can be green-lighting a listing against a hardcoded constant.

The tab has real honesty work in it (F724 retryable-error state on the wallet read, F722 gas attribution, F723 FIFO buy matching, split gainers/losers), and the wallet-NFT read is handled correctly. But three layers below it are not: every USD figure is computed from a hardcoded 3200 ETH/USD that can never be overridden on this mount; a swallowed Alchemy failure in calculatePnL turns every held token into cost-basis-0 + a green MINT badge and reports the entire portfolio value as pure profit; and the floor that drives PORTFOLIO VALUE, FLOOR and the 90-day snapshot chart can be the hardcoded 0.1048 fallback with no CACHED badge (Hero badges the exact same object).

tabs.component: ProMembership (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/ProMembership.jsx, 96 lines) plus hooks/useProAccess.jsx and lib/constants.ts
tabs.summary: Reachable in prod (VALID_TABS constants.js:94, Header.jsx:140, MobileNav.jsx:13, App.jsx:769). The page is honest about its own launch status — PRO_PASS_LIVE derives from isDeployed(TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS) which is currently the zero address, so the pill reads "MINTING SOON", the CTA is disabled, and no number, count, or track record is fabricated anywhere on the page. What is not backed: the five-item perk list plus the line "perks light up automatically for holders" describe flair, a referral fee cut, and Pro-only tools that have zero implementation — useProAccess is imported by exactly one file (this component), and grep for referral inside frontend/src/nakamigos returns only this page's own copy. Two latent landmines arm themselves the instant the operator sets the address with no further review: the button labeled "Mint Pro Pass" only opens Etherscan, and useProAccess turns a failed Alchemy read into "NOT YET A MEMBER" + a mint invitation shown to an existing holder.

Correctly gated. PRO_PASS_LIVE derives from isDeployed(TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS), so with no address the pill reads MINTING SOON, the CTA is disabled with a non-committal label, and useProAccess short-circuits to isPro:false without a network call. Perk copy is forward-looking ('will', 'drops with the next wave') rather than asserting live benefits. The failed-read path returns isPro:false, which fails closed.

Not honest and not usable as shipped. The precomputed rarity file it depends on is an empty placeholder (data/rarity.json: totalTokens 0), so every 'Rank ~#N' it shows is a rank within the ~40 tokens the app happened to load, not within the 20,000-token collection — and all of them get painted top-1%-rarity gold. Because rarity is considered 'present', every listing whose token isn't in that 40-token page is silently discarded, so the tab typically shows 0-2 rows (or the flat-out false 'No Nakamigos listings available') while hundreds of listings are live. It is also the only listings-consuming tab given neither listingsLoading nor listingsError.

The tab's single primary action (SEND TRADE) cannot succeed for any token: it requires `theirNft.owner`, but every token in `nfts.allTokens` comes from Alchemy getNFTsForContract, which never populates `owners`, so normalizeToken sets owner:null for all of them. Two other call sites in this codebase already patch that field precisely because it is unreliable. Separately, a failed wallet read is laundered into the confident sentence 'Your wallet does not hold any <collection> NFTs to trade.' The Seaport order-building path it delegates to (lib/trades.createTradeOffer) is itself sound — pinned conduit, typed result, honest failure toasts.

The P2P send path itself is well built — it routes through the audited trades SDK and surfaces typed failures instead of toasting phantom success. But the counterparty guard at line 248 can never be satisfied for a token picked from the collection search, so SEND TRADE dead-ends. Also, both navs label this tab 'Compare' while the page is titled 'P2P TRADE' and does no comparison.

The panel's own load path is honest — it distinguishes a real /api/orderbook outage from an empty inbox and shows a retry banner (lines 415-420, 562-567), the 'fee-free' copy is backed by buildTradeOrderParameters emitting zero fee legs, and the push-alerts toggle is correctly hidden when VAPID is unconfigured. Two real problems: TradeCard quotes the MAX of a Dutch cash leg as the live amount (the same trade shows a different number in TradeSummary right beside it), and three separate inventory reads turn an Alchemy failure into a positive claim about what a wallet holds.

The core trait-rarity math is unusually honest — it divides by the LOADED sample rather than full supply, marks every percentage with '~' when sampled, and says 'trait % from loaded sample' on the Tokens Loaded card (TraitExplorer.jsx:397-402, 677-681, 800). The failures are around it: the trait-offer panel turns a failed OpenSea read into the sentence 'No trait offers'; trait/type floor prices are computed over the loaded subset but rendered with no qualifier at all; the 'Rarest Trait' headline names a specific trait from a 40-token first page; and CharacterTypeExplorer's click-to-filter controls hardcode guessed attribute keys/values. All controls (Offer, Bid on Trait, Filter Gallery, Show all, search, sort) are wired to real handlers — none are inert.

Local persistence, collection-switch reset and the add/remove/note/target writes are all sound. The feature it advertises is not: "set price alerts" cannot ever fire because the tokens it is given always have price: null, so the target-price input is write-only and the "Below target price!" badge is unreachable. It also silently drops watched NFTs outside the loaded ~40-token window (no loadAll prop, and unlike Favorites no "not loaded" note), tells the user "No results found" for tokens that merely have not been paged in, and renders ranks that every other surface in the app suppresses as approximate.

Two defects: the TARGET PRICE input and the 'Below target price!' badge are permanently dead because the tokens passed in never carry a price, while the subtitle and empty state both promise price tracking and alerts; and persisted watchlist entries whose token is outside the loaded page window vanish with no message and no empty state.

The holder read is unpaginated (fetchTopHolders calls getOwnersForContract once and never follows pageKey, unlike the marketIntegrity adapter that paginates the same endpoint), yet the page prints 'N unique owners' and a Holder Concentration chart as facts. The holders fallback IS disclosed with a banner, but the activity fallback is not: a double API outage renders 4 fabricated sample sales and then states 'None of the 4 recent Nakamigos sales involved top 5 holders.' The Holder Concentration panel also renders the fabricated FALLBACK_WHALES counts with no warning of its own.

survived.title: Rarity ranks are fabricated from a 40-token page — every row is painted top-1% rare
survived.claim: The 'Rank' column, the rank colouring and the 'Snipe Score' all present collection-wide rarity that does not exist. frontend/src/nakamigos/data/rarity.json is a committed placeholder ({"generatedAt": null, "totalTokens": 0, "rarity": {}}), so `_precomputed` is null at api.js:846 and computeRarity falls to the runtime path, which sorts only the LOADED tokens and assigns `rank = i + 1` (api.js:891-897). useNfts fetches 40 tokens per page (hooks/useNfts.js:33) and explicitly does not auto-load for collections with supply >= 1000 (hooks/useNfts.js:96-98), so Nakamigos sits at 40 of 20,000. RaritySniper renders those 1..40 ranks, and rankColor(rank, 20000) paints anything <= 200 gold (RaritySniper.jsx:16-21), so every single row gets the top-1%-rarity colour. computeSnipeScore's rarity term is (20000 - rank)/20000, i.e. ~0.998-0.99995 for all of them (RaritySniper.jsx:10-14), so the advertised rarity-vs-price 'Snipe Score' collapses to 10 / pricePercentile — a pure cheapest-first ordering wearing a rarity label.
survived.failure_scenario: User opens /nakamigos?tab=sniper on a fresh session. 40 tokens (ids 0-39) are loaded. The table shows rows labelled 'Rank ~#2', 'Rank ~#7' in gold with Snipe Scores of 999/412/88. The user reads that as 'the 2nd rarest Nakamigo of 20,000 is listed under floor' and buys it. In reality #2 is merely the rarest of tokens 0-39, and the score ranked it first only because it was the cheapest listing in the set. The only hedge on screen is '(ranks approximate — loading more Nakamigos data)', which understates a 40/20000 sample as a loading state.
survived.suggested_fix: Either generate data/rarity.json (scripts/compute-rarity.mjs) so hasPrecomputedRarity() is true, or make RaritySniper refuse to show a Rank column / rarity-weighted score when `rankApproximate` is set and coverage is below some threshold — fall back to the honest price-only 'Value Score' path it already has for no-trait collections.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end from the files. rarity.json is a committed placeholder with totalTokens:0 and the generator it references (scripts/compute-rarity.mjs) does not exist in the repo at all (git ls-files), so _precomputed is permanently null at api.js:846. computeRarity therefore always takes the runtime path and assigns rank = i+1 over only the loaded tokens (api.js:895-897). useNfts fetches limit:40 (hooks/useNfts.js:33) and disables auto-load for supply >= 1000 (useNfts.js:98); Nakamigos is supply 20000 (constants.js:34), and App.jsx:786-796 passes no loadAll to RaritySniper, so the set never grows on this tab. RaritySniper.jsx:505 colours via rankColor(rank, effectiveSupply) which golds rank <= 200 (lines 16-21), so all 40 rows get the top-1% colour. computeSnipeScore (10-14) has a rarity term of (20000-rank)/20000 varying only 0.9980-0.99995 across those ranks while the price percentile spans 0.01-1.0, so the 'Snipe Score' is effectively 10/pricePercentile — cheapest-first wearing a rarity label. Every mechanical claim checks out.
verdicts.correction:
Real, but overstated as critical and two scenario details are wrong; also the write-up misses a worse sibling defect.

ACCURATE VERSION — severity HIGH (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/RaritySniper.jsx:505, :16-21, :10-14; frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:846,:895-897; frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useNfts.js:33,:98):

For any collection with supply >= 1000 (Nakamigos 20,000; GNSS Art 9,696; Jungle Bay 5,555), the Rarity Sniper renders ranks that are positions within the ~40 loaded tokens as if they were collection ranks. rankColor(rank, 20000) golds everything <= 200, so every row carries the top-1%-rarity colour, and the 'Snipe Score' reduces to a cheapest-first ordering because its rarity term varies by 0.2% while its price term varies 100x.

Downgrade critical -> high: the UI does hedge more than the finding allows. The column header renders 'Rank ~' (RaritySniper.jsx:484), cells render '~2' — the '~' REPLACES the '#', so the scenario's literal 'Rank ~#2' is not what appears (line 506) — and a gold banner states the ranks are approximate (399-403). No funds are misdirected; price, fee and the + Cart path are unaffected. The harm is decision-quality on a purchase.

THREE CORRECTIONS / ADDITIONS:

1. The finding misses RaritySniper.jsx:286 (`if (hasRarity && !hasRank) return null;`), which drops every listing whose tokenId is not among the ~40 loaded tokens. For Nakamigos the table is the intersection of hundreds of listings with 40 token IDs — typically 0-3 rows, not a full fabricated leaderboard. This shrinks the finding's blast radius.

2. But that same guard produces a WORSE, separate defect that should be filed on its own: when the intersection is empty, the empty state at RaritySniper.jsx:463-475 tells the user 'No Nakamigos listings available' and 'Waiting for Nakamigos listings to appear' while listings.length is in the hundreds. That is a flat false factual sentence generated by a partial read — the exact failed-read-laundering class this sweep targets — and it is the COMMON outcome for Nakamigos, whereas the fabricated-rank table is the rarer one.

3. The hedge itself is false. '(ranks approximate — loading more Nakamigos data)' (line 402) describes a transient loading state, but for supply >= 1000 nothing is loading and nothing will: useNfts auto-load is off and the sniper tab never calls loadAll. The condition is permanent.

CORROBORATION: Card.jsx:45, Hero.jsx:46, Hero.jsx:78 and VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:353 all gate on `nft.rank && !nft.rankApproximate` — every other surface suppresses approximate ranks. RaritySniper is the only surface that displays them, and the only one that colour-codes and scores off them, which is strong in-codebase evidence that showing them is the bug.

Also minor: 'every row painted top-1%' holds at 40 loaded tokens; if the user browsed the gallery first and ~400 tokens are loaded, ranks 201-400 render blue (top 5%). Every row still lands in a top-5% colour band, so the substance holds.

NOT EXAMINED, likely same root cause: frontend/src/nakamigos/components/RarityPriceScatter.jsx also consumes this rarity path.

verdicts.reasoning:
VERIFIED, with two narrowing corrections.

Confirmed at file:line:
- frontend/src/nakamigos/data/rarity.json is 81 bytes: {"generatedAt": null, "totalTokens": 0, "traitCount": 0, "rarity": {}} -> api.js:846 `_precomputed = precomputedRarity?.totalTokens > 0 ? ... : null` evaluates to null.
- The comment at api.js:843 names "scripts/compute-rarity.mjs" as the generator. That file DOES NOT EXIST anywhere in the repo (frontend/scripts/ lacks it; repo-wide find returns nothing). rarity.json has been the placeholder since the initial integration commit b0fe56e3 and no build step or CI job writes it. So the precomputed path is permanently dead, not merely unpopulated in this checkout. This kills the strongest maintainer defense.
- api.js:891-897 runtime path: sorts loaded tokens, `rank = i + 1`, tags `rankApproximate: !!isPartial` where isPartial = tokens.length < supply*0.8 (api.js:895).
- useNfts.js:33 `limit: 40`; useNfts.js:100-102 auto-load gated on `collection.supply < 1000` (finding cited 96-98, actual 100-102 — trivial drift). Nakamigos supply 20000 (constants.js:34).
- RaritySniper.jsx:16-21 rankColor golds rank <= supply*0.01 = 200. Max achievable rank is 40, so EVERY row is gold by construction; the colour carries zero information.
- RaritySniper.jsx:10-14 computeSnipeScore rarityScore = (20000-rank)/20000 in [0.998, 0.99995], so the rarity term is a no-op and "Snipe Score" reduces to 10/pricePercentile. Neither rankColor nor computeSnipeScore consults rankApproximate.
- The hedge string (RaritySniper.jsx:399-403) says "loading more Nakamigos data". Nothing is loading: useNfts skips auto-pagination at supply>=1000, and App.jsx:786-795 passes the sniper no loadAll/hasMore (unlike Analytics/TraitExplorer at App.jsx:706,736,749,753). A permanent 40/20000 sample is described as a transient load state — the project's own defect class.
- Secondary: the app converged on shared rankTier (gold<=0.5%/blue<=2.5%, constants.js:16-25, pinned by rankTier.test.js F809, used by Modal/ShareCard/TheaterMode). RaritySniper keeps a private 1/5/10% scale, so one token reads gold here and blue in the modal.

Corrections that NARROW the finding:
1. Row volume is overstated. RaritySniper.jsx:286 `if (hasRarity && !hasRank) return null` drops every listing whose tokenId is not among the 40 loaded tokens. Listings come from an independent collection-wide query (hooks/useListings.js), so overlap with tokens 0-39 is typically 0-2 rows, not 40. The user most often sees the empty state. The defect is real but fires rarely.
2. "The only hedge on screen" is inaccurate — there are three (per-cell "~", "Rank ~" header at :484, caveat line). The rendered cell is "~2", not "Rank ~#2" (:506). The substance survives: the caveat misattributes the cause.

Also state-dependent: visiting Analytics or Trait Explorer first triggers loadAll, isPartial goes false, and the tab becomes honest — so the same URL is fabricated or correct depending on tab history, which is itself why the on-screen caveat cannot be trusted as a signal.

Severity high, not critical: every rank does carry a "~", and line 286 keeps reach narrow. But each row that renders shows a gold rank badge and a rarity-labelled score next to a one-click "+ Cart" (:529), i.e. a fabricated collection-wide claim on a money path.
verdicts.correction: Accurate title: "Snipe Score and rank colouring treat a 40-token sample rank as a 20,000-collection rank". frontend/src/nakamigos/data/rarity.json is a permanent placeholder whose generator (scripts/compute-rarity.mjs, named at api.js:843) does not exist in the repo, so _precomputed is null (api.js:846) and ranks always come from the runtime path over only the loaded page (api.js:891-897, 40 tokens via useNfts.js:33 with auto-load disabled at supply>=1000, useNfts.js:100-102). Both consumers of `rank` ignore the rankApproximate tag: rankColor(rank, 20000) (RaritySniper.jsx:16-21) can only ever return gold because max rank is 40 < 200, and computeSnipeScore (RaritySniper.jsx:10-14) pins the rarity term at ~0.999 so the score is pure 10/pricePercentile under a rarity label. The caveat at RaritySniper.jsx:399-403 blames loading, but App.jsx:786-795 never passes the sniper loadAll/hasMore, so no load is in progress. Corrected scenario: RaritySniper.jsx:286 drops listings not in the loaded 40, so the table is usually empty or 1-2 rows — but each row that renders shows a gold "~2" rank and a "Snipe Score" derived only from price, beside a one-click "+ Cart" (RaritySniper.jsx:529). Severity: high.

survived.title: Listings for unloaded tokens are silently dropped, so the tab reports 'No listings available' while hundreds are live
survived.claim: `if (hasRarity && !hasRank) return null;` discards every listing whose tokenId is not in `tokenMap`. tokenMap is built from the `tokens` prop (RaritySniper.jsx:253-257), which is App's `nfts.allTokens` — only the pages actually fetched. With 40 sequential tokens loaded and listings spread across ids 0-19,999, the expected intersection is roughly 40/20000 x N, i.e. about one listing out of 600. Unlike Deals (App.jsx:736-737) and TraitExplorer (App.jsx:753), RaritySniper is not given `loadAll` or `hasMore` (App.jsx:786-796), so the user has no control that fixes it. The header '{filtered.length} / {opportunities.length} opportunities' (line 366) counts only survivors, so the undercount is invisible.
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea returns 600 live Nakamigos listings; the app has loaded 40 tokens. `opportunities` comes back with 0 or 1 entries. The user sees the empty state 'No Nakamigos listings available' / 'Waiting for Nakamigos listings to appear. Hit Refresh or they will show automatically as the market updates.' (lines 463-476) and concludes the collection has no floor. Hitting Refresh refetches listings, not tokens, so it never resolves. If one listing does survive, the summary line asserts '1 sniping opportunity found' and names it 'Best deal' — the best of one arbitrary row.
survived.suggested_fix: Keep unmatched listings with rank = null instead of dropping them (the component already renders an em-dash for null ranks at line 506), and/or pass loadAll/hasMore through from App.jsx and surface a 'showing X of Y listings — load full collection for ranks' notice.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this on four fronts and every one of them held up.

1. The drop is real and unconditional. RaritySniper.jsx:286 `if (hasRarity && !hasRank) return null;` sits inside the `.map()` at 277-304 and is followed by `.filter(Boolean)` at 305. `rank` comes only from `tokenMap.get(String(listing.tokenId))` (280-282), and tokenMap is built solely from the `tokens` prop (253-257). 2. I looked for a key-shape mismatch that would make the join fail for a benign reason, and there isn't one: listings normalize `tokenId: String(...)` (api.js:691, 740) and tokens normalize `id: nft.tokenId` (api.js:131), matching tokenMap's `String(t.id ?? t.tokenId)`.

3. `hasRarity` really is true on the live collection, and NOT via the path the finding assumed. I checked frontend/src/nakamigos/data/rarity.json — it is `{"totalTokens": 0, "rarity": {}}`, so `_precomputed` is null (api.js:846) and the Nakamigos precomputed branch (api.js:852) is dead code. Rarity therefore always comes from the runtime branch, which assigns `rank: i + 1` to every scored token (api.js:897). Every loaded token gets rank >= 1, so `hasRarity` (RaritySniper.jsx:260-262) is true for any trait-bearing collection, and the 286 guard is always armed. (It correctly goes false only for trait-less on-chain-generative collections, where api.js:876 returns rank null — that path degrades honestly to the price-only "Value Score".)

The token set really is ~40. fetchTokens defaults `limit = 40` and pages by `startToken` (api.js:154-163), so page 1 is tokenIds 0-39. useNfts.js:101 auto-loads further pages only when `collection.supply < 1000`; Nakamigos is `supply: 20000` (constants.js:34), so it does not. The header "{filtered.length} / {opportunities.length}" (line 366) and the empty-state copy (lines 463-476) are as quoted, so the undercount is invisible and the empty state asserts a market fact that is false.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING:

The bug reproduces on direct navigation to /nakamigos/sniper ("sniper" is a valid direct-route tab, constants.js:94) or on sniper-first browsing. That is still the default cold-load path, but the finding overstates it as unconditional.

(b) Severity should be high, not critical. No funds are at risk, no transaction is built wrong, no fee is misquoted, and the true listings are visible one tab over on Listings/Deals. It stays high rather than medium because the surface makes two affirmatively false statements, not just an omission: "No Nakamigos listings available" when hundreds are live, and "1 sniping opportunity found ... Best deal: #X" where #X is the best of an arbitrary 1-in-600 sample presented as the best of the collection.

AGGRAVATING CASE THE FINDING MISSED — this is the true failed-read laundering. When the Alchemy token fetch throws, fetchTokens (api.js:168-170) returns `FALLBACK_NFTS`: 12 hardcoded demo tokens, ids "0" through "11", with hand-written attributes (constants.js:211-223). Those 12 flow into computeRarity, get runtime ranks, and set `hasRarity = true`. tokenMap then contains exactly ids 0-11. A *successful* listings read of 600 live orders is filtered down to ~0 by a *failed* token read, and the user is told "No Nakamigos listings available / Waiting for Nakamigos listings to appear." Nothing on screen indicates the token API is down. That is precisely the defect class this sweep targets: a broken upstream rendered as a confident factual negative about the market.

Secondary honesty defect in the same component: when `isApproximate` is true, line 400-402 renders "(ranks approximate — loading more Nakamigos data)". Nothing is loading — RaritySniper has no `loadAll`, no `hasMore`, and no loader of any kind. The copy promises background progress the code does not perform.

CONFIRMED at RaritySniper.jsx:286. Every mechanical claim reproduces.

Chain verified end to end:

The maintainer defense I constructed (the guard is a deliberate two-mode design: require rarity when the collection has it, fall back to the price-only score at line 294 when it does not, and dropping is more conservative than rendering a blank rank) fails on three checks:

1. `hasRarity` does not mean "the collection has rarity data." data/rarity.json is an empty stub ({"totalTokens": 0, "rarity": {}}), so `_precomputed` is null (api.js:846) and EVERY collection takes the runtime path at api.js:866-897, which assigns rank = i+1 to every loaded token with any attributes. `hasRarity` (lines 260-262) is therefore true whenever the token fetch merely succeeded, and the gate degrades to "did we happen to fetch this token?" — a data-availability accident. The honest rank-free alternative already exists at line 294 and is simply unreachable per-token.

2. Dropping is only conservative if the drop is disclosed. Instead the tab makes a positive factual assertion — "No {collection} listings available" (lines 467-473) — which is precisely what a broken/partial upstream produces. That is the defect class, not a defense against it.

3. The codebase's own pattern for this exact join is different and RaritySniper is the one call site that skipped it: Deals.jsx:484-486 calls loadAll() on mount, and Deals.jsx:756-765 / 791-797 refuse to assert emptiness while hasMore, printing "Scanning... N of 20,000 tokens analyzed — results refine live."

The finding UNDERSTATES the harm in one respect (see correction): survivors are not merely arbitrary, they carry fabricated ranks and saturated scores.

Severity corrected critical -> high: the tab is functionally dead and states a false market fact, and the surviving row is an actively misleading buy signal sitting next to a + Cart button (line 529) — but no funds are misdirected and nothing is unrecoverable, which is what "critical" denotes in this repo's taxonomy. Accurate version — the finding is right on mechanism but understates the harm, and the severity should be high rather than critical.

Part (a), as filed and confirmed: with `hasRarity` true (which is effectively always, since data/rarity.json is an empty stub and the runtime path at api.js:866-897 ranks every loaded token), RaritySniper.jsx:286 drops every listing whose tokenId is outside the ~40 loaded tokens. On Nakamigos (supply 20000, no auto-load, no loadAll prop) that is ~99.8% of live listings. The tab then asserts "No Nakamigos listings available" (lines 467-473), and Refresh only refetches listings (App.jsx:793) so it never resolves.

Part (b), MISSED by the finding and worse than "an arbitrary row": the ~1 listing that survives is rendered with a fabricated rank and a saturated score. The runtime rank is a rank WITHIN the 40 loaded tokens (1-40), but it is displayed as an absolute collection rank and passed to computeSnipeScore with effectiveSupply = stats.supply = 20000 (RaritySniper.jsx:293, App.jsx:789). Therefore rarityScore = (20000 - rank)/20000 ≈ 0.998-1.0 for every survivor, yielding verified scores of 100-999 against a gradient that already tops out at >= 5 (line 24); rankColor golds anything <= 200 (line 17), so every survivor renders in top-1% gold. A row reads "Rank ~3" for a token whose true rank may be ~8,420. The "~" prefix and the "(ranks approximate — loading more data)" note (lines 399-403, 484, 506) cannot carry that: an error of three orders of magnitude, shown in gold as top-1% rarity with a near-ceiling snipe score, sits in the same row as a "+ Cart" button (line 529).

Aggravating path: if Alchemy is down, fetchTokens returns the hardcoded FALLBACK_NFTS demo array for Nakamigos (api.js:169-170, constants.js:211). Those tokens have attributes, so hasRarity stays true and the join runs against demo data — a total token-API outage renders as the market fact "No Nakamigos listings available" while listings load fine.

The fix the codebase already knows: pass loadAll/hasMore to RaritySniper the way Deals and TraitExplorer get them (App.jsx:736-737, 753), call loadAll() on mount (Deals.jsx:484-486), and while hasMore never assert emptiness — report coverage instead ("Scanning: N / 20,000 tokens loaded"), per Deals.jsx:756-765 and 791-797. Separately, either suppress the Rank column and use the existing rank-free score at line 294 for tokens whose rank is only a within-loaded-set ordinal, or stop feeding a 1-40 ordinal into a 20000-supply score.

survived.failure_scenario: User connects a wallet holding Nakamigos, opens /nakamigos/trade, selects one of their own NFTs on the left and searches any token on the right. (lines 467-473). It frames listingsError as a working failure signal that the sniper merely fails to receive; in fact listingsError (useListings.js:33) is dead for every consumer. fetchListings never rejects on an outage and never returns an `error` key — build() calls mergeListings, which returns only {listings, source}, and the `error:` returns elsewhere in api.js (662, 1044, 1090, 1106-1138, 1171-1208) belong to unrelated wallet/fulfillment functions. So `data?.error ?? (error ? "Listing data temporarily unavailable…" : null)` resolves to null in every outage case, which also makes the Listings.jsx:870-873 "Listing data for X temporarily unavailable" banner unreachable. Consequence for the fix: prop-passing listingsError into RaritySniper would change nothing; the per-source catches at api.js:795-798 and api.js:800-803 must surface a failure flag (e.g. return {listings, source, error}) before any consumer can distinguish "no listings" from "could not read listings". listingsLoading is genuinely live (react-query isLoading), so the cold-load false-empty half IS fixable by prop-passing alone. Severity high is appropriate and should stand: the sniper is a decision tool, and the failure renders a confident factual sentence about market state ("No Nakamigos listings available") that is exactly what a broken upstream produces — the defect class this sweep exists to close.

Maintainer defenses examined and rejected: (a) "the copy is hedged" — only the body sentence is; the title and summary are flat factual assertions identical for a real empty book and a dead upstream; (b) "per-source catches are intentional" — true and documented (api.js:789-793), but that is precisely what destroys the signal; (c) "the sniper is a derived view, presentation belongs to the owner" — the two siblings fed by the same hook do gate, so this is an omission, not a design.

FIRST, the cold-load window is understated, not overstated: Suspense at App.jsx:876-880 covers only the lazy chunk, and placeholderData:undefined (useListings.js:26) means no cache on a deep link; openseaGet retries maxRetries:3 baseDelay:1500 (api.js:80-82) with backoff 1500/3000/6000+jitter (withRetry:57), so against a 500 the false headline paints for ~10-15s, not "the first second." SECOND, the finding implies listingsError works for the tabs that receive it — it does not in this scenario. Because source resolves to "opensea", Listings.jsx:867 takes the FIRST branch and asserts "No active listings for Nakamigos right now.", never reaching the listingsError fallback at :869. listingsError is near-dead app-wide (only reachable if build() itself throws, e.g. a malformed price.current.value at api.js:689). Listings gets the cold-load half right and the outage half wrong; the sniper gets both wrong.

Severity corrected high -> medium: the defect is real and is squarely the failed-read-laundering class this project is closing, but no transaction is built, signed, or mispriced from it; it self-heals on the 5-minute poll (queryConfig.js:23) or the wired Refresh button (RaritySniper.jsx:368-385), and a hedged sentence sits under the false headline. Harm ceiling is a trader wrongly concluding the book is empty.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: RaritySniper (App.jsx:786-796) receives neither listingsLoading nor listingsError, and no failure signal exists to receive — api.js:795-804 swallows both listing sources, so a total outage resolves as a successful `{ listings: [], source: "opensea" }` and useListings.js:33 yields listingsError === null. The tab therefore renders three unqualified claims — "0 / 0 opportunities" (:366), "0 sniping opportunities found" (:392), and the title "No {collection} listings available" (:468) — that are byte-identical for a genuinely empty book, a dead OpenSea + dead native orderbook, and an unresolved cold load. Two amendments to the original write-up: (1) the cold-load window is ~10-15s, not ~1s, because openseaGet retries 3x with 1500/3000/6000ms backoff (api.js:80-82, withRetry:57) and Suspense (App.jsx:876) covers only the lazy chunk; (2) listingsError does not save the tabs that do receive it — with source==="opensea" Listings.jsx:867 takes the first branch and asserts "No active listings for Nakamigos right now.", never reaching the listingsError text at :869, so the same laundering also affects the Listings tab's outage path (its cold-load path is correctly gated). Severity medium, not high: information-integrity defect on a trading surface, self-healing, no money path touched.

survived.title: Top holders, owner count and concentration are computed from one unpaginated page of owners
survived.claim: fetchTopHolders issues a single alchemyGet('getOwnersForContract', { withTokenBalances: 'true' }) and never reads or follows `data.pageKey` (api.js:610-630). That the endpoint paginates is established in this same codebase: lib/marketIntegrity.js:535-560 loops on `data.pageKey` for up to 8 pages and returns a `truncated` flag for exactly this call. WhaleIntelligence then treats page 1 as the whole owner set: it prints '{totalOwners.toLocaleString()} unique owners' as a bare fact (WhaleIntelligence.jsx:554), sorts it into 'Top Holders' (lines 578-628), and derives Holder Concentration from it (lines 333-344 and the panel at 884-960).
survived.failure_scenario: Nakamigos has several thousand owners. Alchemy returns page 1 with a pageKey. The page renders 'Top 25 / 20,000' with '· 100 unique owners' beneath it, and a Holder Concentration bar reading e.g. 'Top 10 Holders 3.2%'. Both are wrong: the true owner count is an order of magnitude larger, and the wallets shown are the largest of page 1, not the largest in the collection — a genuine whale on page 3 never appears. No caveat is shown, and unlike the integrity tab there is no truncation notice.
survived.suggested_fix: Reuse fetchCollectionOwners from lib/marketIntegrity.js (it paginates and returns `truncated`), or add pageKey following to fetchTopHolders and surface the truncation the way MarketIntegrity.jsx:178 does.

verdicts.reasoning:
The code description is accurate but the user-visible defect does not exist and cannot be reached.

CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN (the mechanism):
- frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:610-630 — fetchTopHolders issues a single alchemyGet("getOwnersForContract", {contractAddress, withTokenBalances:"true"}) and never reads or follows data.pageKey. It returns totalOwners = allOwners.length from that one response.
- frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/marketIntegrity.js:535-560 — fetchCollectionOwners does loop on data.pageKey (maxPages=8) for the identical call and returns a `truncated` flag, surfaced to users at MarketIntegrity.jsx:178. The asymmetry the finding points at is real.
- frontend/src/nakamigos/components/WhaleIntelligence.jsx — line 181 calls fetchTopHolders({limit:25}); line 544 renders "Top {holders.length} / {SUPPLY}"; line 554 renders "{totalOwners.toLocaleString()} unique owners"; lines 333-344 compute top10Pct/top25Pct; the Holder Concentration panel is at 885-910. All render sites are exactly as described.

REFUTED (the harm):
The premise that "Alchemy returns page 1 with a pageKey" is false for every contract this app can query. I fetched the app's own production proxy for the largest reachable collection (Nakamigos, 20,000 supply):
  GET https://memetic.fun/api/alchemy?endpoint=getOwnersForContract&contractAddress=0xd774...c367&withTokenBalances=true
  -> HTTP 200, 1,088,757 bytes, response keys ["owners","pageKey"]
  -> pageKey: null
  -> owners.length: 5248
  -> sum of tokenBalances across all owners: 20000 (i.e. EXACTLY the full supply — the page is provably complete)
  -> top-10 holdings sum 3881, top-25 sum 5436

So page 1 IS the whole owner set. "5,248 unique owners" is correct, the Top Holders list is the true top holders, and Holder Concentration renders Top 10 = 3881/20000 = 19.4% and Top 25 = 27.2% — correct figures.

This is structural, not luck. frontend/api/alchemy.js:63-68 hard-allowlists exactly three contracts (Nakamigos 20,000; GNSS Art 9,696; Jungle Bay 5,555 — constants.js:34,55,71) and getOwnersForContract is in CONTRACT_REQUIRED_ENDPOINTS (alchemy.js:70-77), so an arbitrary contract 400s. Unique owners are bounded above by supply (max 20,000), far below the page size this endpoint actually serves (it returned 5,248 owners with balances in one page, and Alchemy's documented page size for this call is 50,000). pageKey can never be non-null on any user-reachable path.

Both concrete numbers in the scenario are invented: it claims "· 100 unique owners" (real: 5,248; also WhaleIntelligence passes limit:25, and totalOwners is the full page length, never 100) and "Top 10 Holders 3.2%" (real: 19.4%). The claimed "order of magnitude larger" true owner count does not exist.

Two secondary notes, neither a defect: (a) the same function is called with limit:100 by HolderAnalytics.jsx:62 and CollectionHealth.jsx:138 — same clean bill, same complete page. (b) The failure path is honest, not laundered: on error for the flagship contract fetchTopHolders returns FALLBACK_WHALES with fallback:true, WhaleIntelligence sets holdersLive=false and renders the banner "Showing cached example holders — live holder API unavailable" (lines 557-566), and totalOwners=0 is suppressed by the `totalOwners > 0 &&` guard at line 554 so no false owner count is printed.

ACCURATE RESIDUAL (severity info, not high): fetchTopHolders is a latent maintenance hazard — it has no pagination and no truncation signal, so it silently disagrees with its paginating sibling. If a fourth, much larger collection were ever added to ALLOWED_CONTRACTS (needing >50k owners, hence >50k supply), the whales tab would silently show a partial owner set while the integrity tab correctly flagged truncation. Today nothing renders wrong, so this is a code-hardening note for whoever expands the allowlist, not a shipping bug a user can hit.
verdicts.correction: Downgrade from high to info, and restate as a latent hazard rather than a live defect. Accurate version: "fetchTopHolders (api.js:610-630) does not follow `pageKey`, unlike its sibling fetchCollectionOwners (marketIntegrity.js:535-560), and emits no truncation signal. This is currently harmless: the Alchemy proxy allowlists only three contracts (alchemy.js:63-68) whose max supply is 20,000, and a live production read of the largest (Nakamigos) returns all 5,248 owners in one page with pageKey:null and tokenBalances summing to exactly 20,000 — so every rendered figure (5,248 unique owners; Top 10 = 19.4%; Top 25 = 27.2%) is correct. The gap only becomes user-visible if a collection with >50k owners is ever added to the allowlist." No user-facing copy or number is wrong today; no fix is required before expanding ALLOWED_CONTRACTS.

Finding confirmed and substantially accurate; two refinements.

(1) Direction of the error should be stated: page 1's top-10 is a strict SUBSET of the collection's true top-10, so `top10Pct`/`top25Pct` (WhaleIntelligence.jsx:333-344) are strict UNDER-estimates. The tab whose purpose is flagging whale/concentration risk systematically reports the collection as LESS concentrated than it is — the worst direction for this defect.

(2) Blast radius is larger than "whales". The same truncated `totalOwners` drives `components/HolderAnalytics.jsx:129` ("TOTAL HOLDERS" stat tile) and :152 ("Showing top X holders of Y total"). HolderAnalytics.jsx:62 and CollectionHealth.jsx:138 both request `limit: 100` from a page that is itself ~100 entries, so their "top 100 holders" is really "100 arbitrary owners". (CollectionHealth.jsx:138 additionally wraps the call in `.catch(() => ({ holders: [], totalOwners: 0, totalHeld: 0 }))` — separate failed-read-laundering issue, outside this finding.)

(3) Classification note: this is NOT failed-read laundering. The outright-failure path is handled honestly (api.js:631-644 sets `fallback: true`; WhaleIntelligence.jsx:557-565 renders "Showing cached example holders — live holder API unavailable"). It is the adjacent class: a SUCCESSFUL but silently truncated read presented as complete. The return shape at api.js:625-630 has no field capable of carrying a truncation signal.

Accurate one-line version: "fetchTopHolders (api.js:610-630) reads a single unpaginated page of getOwnersForContract and never follows `data.pageKey`, so owner count, holder ranking and concentration percentages describe page 1 rather than the collection — and concentration is under-reported. The correct paginated implementation of the identical call already ships in lib/marketIntegrity.js:535-560 with a `truncated` flag."

Severity high is correct: no transaction is built or signed, so not critical, but it is an unqualified factual claim about wallets and concentration on the tab users open specifically to judge whale risk, with no caveat and a working in-repo fix 80 lines away.
verdicts.reasoning:
I read all cited code rather than reasoning from the summary.

api.js:610-630 — fetchTopHolders issues exactly one `alchemyGet("getOwnersForContract", { contractAddress, withTokenBalances: "true" })`, maps `data.owners`, sorts, and returns `holders: slice(0, limit)`, `totalOwners: allOwners.length`. `data.pageKey` is never read. Confirmed verbatim.

The only defense that could save it is "this endpoint doesn't paginate at our size." That is refuted inside this repo: lib/marketIntegrity.js:535-560 makes the IDENTICAL call (same endpoint, same withTokenBalances flag, same alchemyGet helper) inside a `do { ... } while (pageKey)` loop with `maxPages = 8` and a `truncated` return flag, and its docstring (526-527) says it follows pageKey pagination. That loop is unreachable/pointless unless the call paginates.

I also verified the proxy is not silently aggregating: frontend/api/alchemy.js:344-347 builds the upstream URL by forwarding `params` verbatim and returns the raw upstream body; `pageKey` is not in the clamp list at 309-317 and is not stripped — which is precisely why marketIntegrity's loop functions. So the client gets exactly one Alchemy page.

Consumer side, WhaleIntelligence.jsx: :181 calls with limit 25; :184 stores `totalOwners`; :554 renders the bare factual sentence `· {totalOwners.toLocaleString()} unique owners`; :544 renders `Top {holders.length} / {SUPPLY}`; :578-631 renders a ranked list with rank badges and medal colours for ranks 1-3 (an implicit "biggest holders in the collection" claim); :333-344 computes top10Pct/top25Pct from that same truncated array; :884-960 renders them as `ConcentrationBar label="Top 10 Holders"`. All line references in the finding check out.

The "Top N" / "Based on top N holders vs. supply" labels disclose the denominator but not that the numerator is drawn from an arbitrary page, so they do not cure the claim. The fallback warning at :557-565 covers only total API failure, not truncation — and the return shape has no truncation field to surface anyway.

Corroborating intent: the comment at WhaleIntelligence.jsx:228-229 states "loadHolders pulls the full owner set every tick" — the team believed it was fetching the full set; it is not.

Only unverified detail: the exact Alchemy page size with withTokenBalances=true (I believe 100) could not be checked without hitting the live API. It does not affect the conclusion — the code never follows pageKey regardless of cap size, and the sibling implementation's maxPages=8 guard implies a small per-page cap.

Incidental non-finding: `apiTotalHeld` (WhaleIntelligence.jsx:169,185) is set but never rendered — dead state, not user-visible.

survived.title: Fabricated sample sales render with no disclosure, and the page then states facts about them

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED (core mechanic), with two mis-statements that reduce the blast radius.

Reproduced, file:line:
- api.js:551-556 — on the dual-failure path (`fetchOpenSeaActivity` throws at :536 → `primaryResult` stays null; `fetchAlchemyActivity` throws at :543) the catch returns `{ activities: FALLBACK_ACTIVITY, fallback: true }` when `contract.toLowerCase() === CONTRACT.toLowerCase()` (api.js:554). `CONTRACT` is Nakamigos (constants.js:98). Reachable: `openseaGet` throws on failure, so a provider outage lands here.
- constants.js:248-252 — four invented sales anchored to a fixed 2026-01-01 ref (`FALLBACK_ACTIVITY_REF = 1767225600000`, :247), each with `sample: true`.
- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:200 — `setActivityLive(!data.fallback)`. That flag is consumed at exactly three places: :352 (`isLive = holdersLive || activityLive`, feeding the page-level badge at :501), :967, :1161. It suppresses badges only.
- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:557-566 — the "Showing cached example holders — live holder API unavailable" banner is gated on `!holdersLive` and lives in the Top Holders panel. There is no activity-side equivalent anywhere in the file.

- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:1147-1155 — with `trend === null` (:305-306, null when `whaleTransactions` is empty) and `activities.length > 0`, the page renders "No Whale Activity for {collection.name} — None of the {activities.length} recent {collection.name} sales involved top {holders.length} holders." So during the outage `whaleTransactions` is deterministically `[]`, `activities.length` is 4, and the user is told a quantified negative finding about whale behaviour computed over four fabricated trades. The page-level LIVE badge (:501) still renders because holders loaded. That is the finding's scenario, and it holds.

MIS-STATED #1 — the line 1047 citation is wrong twice. Line 1047 ("No large holder activity detected in recent {collection.name} trades.") is not in Whale Alerts; it is inside the Accumulation Trends panel, in the `trend ?` TRUTHY branch opened at :971. It is guarded by `whaleTransactions.length === 0` (:1043), but `trend` is non-null only when `whaleTransactions.length > 0` (:306). The condition is unsatisfiable — that string is unreachable dead code and no user ever sees it. Only their COUNT leaks, via `activities.length` at :1153. (Whether ActivityFeed or another tab renders them as rows is outside this finding's file.)

SEVERITY: high → medium. The defect is genuine failed-read laundering of exactly the class this project has been closing, and the false sentence is user-visible. But it is confined to one integer in one empty-state sentence, requires a total dual-provider activity outage, touches no money/tx/price path, and the owning section's own LIVE badge is already correctly suppressed. The two loudest assertions in the original write-up (the Whale Alerts quote, the rendered fake sales) do not exist.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: During a dual outage of both activity sources (OpenSea events at api.js:536 and Alchemy getNFTSales at api.js:543), fetchActivity substitutes four fabricated sales (constants.js:248-252) for the Nakamigos contract (api.js:554). WhaleIntelligence records the substitution as `activityLive = false` (:200), which only suppresses LIVE badges (:352, :967, :1161) — and the page-level badge at :501 still renders anyway whenever holders loaded, since :352 ORs the two flags. No activity-side "cached example" warning exists; the only such banner (:557-566) is holders-only, and the `sample: true` marker on each fabricated row is read by no component (only by fallbackHonesty.test.js:32). The fabricated rows are then filtered out of `whaleTransactions` by :294-301 (their from/to are truncated placeholders absent from holderAddressSet), which forces `trend` to null (:306) and drops the Accumulation Trends panel into the empty state at :1147-1155, where line 1153 quantifies them: "None of the 4 recent Nakamigos sales involved top 25 holders." The user is handed a specific negative finding about whale behaviour manufactured entirely by an outage over four invented trades. The fake sales themselves are never displayed; only their count escapes. Line 1047 is not part of this — it sits in Accumulation Trends (not Whale Alerts) inside the `trend ?` truthy branch opened at :971, guarded by `whaleTransactions.length === 0`, a condition that branch makes unsatisfiable; it is unreachable dead code. Whale Alerts' real empty copy is :1190 and is honest. Corrected severity: medium.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED in substance, with two factual corrections that lower severity from high to medium.

VERIFIED AS CLAIMED:
- api.js:553-554: when both OpenSea and Alchemy activity fetches throw, fetchActivity returns { activities: FALLBACK_ACTIVITY, fallback: true } for the Nakamigos contract; for any other contract it returns { activities: [], fallback: true } (api.js:556).
- constants.js:248-253: four invented sales anchored to FALLBACK_ACTIVITY_REF = 1767225600000 (2026-01-01), each carrying sample: true.
- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:200 sets activityLive = !data.fallback. That flag feeds only SectionHeading live= props (967, 1161) and isLive (352). No written disclosure exists for activity.
- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:352 `const isLive = holdersLive || activityLive` and 501 `{isLive && <LiveBadge />}`: with holders healthy the page-level LIVE badge still renders during a total activity outage.
- WhaleIntelligence.jsx:557-566: an explicit written warning ("Showing cached example holders — live holder API unavailable") exists for HOLDERS only. The asymmetry is real.

Badge suppression is not a statement, and the header badge survives via the OR at 352. Two sibling consumers of the same fetchActivity already do it right — MarketIntegrity.jsx:318 discards fallback activities outright and sets salesUnavailable (347); ActivityFeed.jsx:342-352 renders "Activity data unavailable… The activity API returned an error." Requires a simultaneous double-API outage, and no fabricated trade data is ever shown — the user-visible harm is an unqualified LIVE badge plus one confident negative sentence about whale behaviour. verdicts.correction:

survived.title: 'in the last 30 days' can silently be the collection's entire history
survived.claim: MarketIntegrity requests a 30-day window (line 317, WINDOW_DAYS = 30) and labels the wash panel 'Self-dealing over sales in the last 30 days.' (line 194) and '{comparableSales} comparable sales (of {totalSales}) in the last 30 days.' (line 203). But fetchActivity's Alchemy fallback branch re-runs the query with daysBack 3650 when the 30-day query comes back empty (api.js:546-549) and returns that all-time result with no marker distinguishing it. Every downstream number — suspect volume, cluster internal sales, round-trip and rapid-retrade token counts — inherits the wider window under the 30-day caption.
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea's events API is unavailable so the Alchemy path is used. Nakamigos has had zero sales in the last 30 days, so the all-time retry fires and returns 100 sales spanning 2023-2026. The panel renders '100 comparable sales (of 100) in the last 30 days', flags coordinated wallet groups and a suspect-volume percentage, and the top-of-page confidence chip reads HIGH because comparableSales >= 20 (lib/marketIntegrity.js:495). A reader concludes a dead collection is being actively wash-traded right now.
survived.suggested_fix: Have fetchActivity return the window it actually used (e.g. `daysBackUsed`) and have MarketIntegrity render that value in the subtitle instead of the constant, or opt out of the all-time widening when a caller passes an explicit daysBack.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED against the files, end to end.

1. The caption is real and unconditional: MarketIntegrity.jsx:15 defines WINDOW_DAYS = 30; :317 requests fetchActivity({limit: 100, daysBack: WINDOW_DAYS}); :203 renders `${result.comparableSales} comparable sales (of ${result.totalSales}) in the last ${WINDOW_DAYS} days.` and :194 renders "Self-dealing over sales in the last 30 days."

2. The silent widening is real: api.js:545-549 — after the Alchemy fallback returns zero activities, `if (primaryResult.activities.length === 0 && !pageKey && daysBack < 365)` re-runs fetchAlchemyActivity with daysBack: 3650 and replaces primaryResult if that returns anything. Inside fetchAlchemyActivity (api.js:441-459), `isAllTime = daysBack >= 365` means **no fromBlock is sent at all**, so Alchemy returns the 100 most recent LIFETIME sales (order: "desc").

3. The marker genuinely does not exist: fetchAlchemyActivity returns only `{ activities, pageKey, empty }` — no `fallback`, no window field. MarketIntegrity.jsx:318 inspects only `res.fallback`, and :347 sets `salesUnavailable: !!(salesRes.fallback || salesRes._err)`. Both are false on the all-time retry, so the yellow "Live sales feed was unavailable" disclosure at :423-428 never renders.

4. Nothing downstream re-filters: computeMarketIntegrity (marketIntegrity.js:477-519) and analyzeWashTrading (:207+) do no time filtering whatsoever — grepping the whole 561-line file for cutoff/window/Days yields only comment prose and the per-sale `time` field, which is used solely to ORDER sales (:264), never to bound them. Suspect volume, cluster-internal sales, roundTripTokens and rapidRetradeTokens all inherit the wider set. The Ownership panel's "COORD. CLUSTER" tile (MarketIntegrity.jsx:140) inherits it too, since clusterOf comes from the same sales array.

survived.title: Every USD figure in the Portfolio tab is computed from a hardcoded $3,200/ETH that can never be overridden
survived.claim: PortfolioTracker reads the ETH/USD rate from useTOWELIPriceOptional(), but /nakamigos/* is routed OUTSIDE AppLayout (frontend/src/App.tsx:206 vs :219) and PriceProvider is mounted only inside AppLayout (frontend/src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:113). The hook is the non-throwing variant and returns null there, so line 127 destructures {} and ethUsd is always undefined. Lines 299-300 then evaluate `totalPnL * (ethUsd || 3200)` and `pnlData.currentValue * (ethUsd || 3200)` — the fallback is not a degraded path, it is the ONLY path on this mount. The results render as '~$X' (line 334) and '+$X' (line 342) with no staleness marker. The repo's own formatUsd helper documents the opposite rule in frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/formatPrice.js:29-38 ('this NEVER fabricates a rate'), and a real rate is available via frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useEthUsd.js.
survived.failure_scenario: A user holds 12 Nakamigos at a 0.10 ETH floor and opens /nakamigos/nakamigos/portfolio while ETH trades at $2,000. currentValueUsd = 1.2 * 3200 = $3,840, so PORTFOLIO VALUE renders 'Ξ 1.2000 / ~$3,840'. The truthful figure is $2,400. The TOTAL P&L dollar line under it is inflated by the same 60%. Nothing on screen indicates the rate is a constant, and no amount of waiting or clicking Refresh will change it, because the provider that would supply a live rate is not in this subtree at all.
survived.suggested_fix: Use the nakamigos-local useEthUsd() hook (which already fetches a real rate for this sub-app) instead of the out-of-tree PriceContext, and render USD via formatUsd(eth, rate) so a missing rate produces no dollar line rather than a fabricated one.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the files, every link in the chain. (1) PortfolioTracker.jsx:8 imports useTOWELIPriceOptional; :127 destructures `useTOWELIPriceOptional() ?? {}`. (2) PriceContext.tsx:61-63 — the optional variant is a bare `useContext(PriceContext)` against a context created with `null` default (:11), so it returns null outside a provider; its own doc at :54-58 says the Tradermigos mounts are "neither wrapped." (3) Repo-wide grep for `PriceProvider` yields exactly one mount: AppLayout.tsx:113 (closing :206). (4) App.tsx:206 routes `nakamigos/*` as a sibling of the AppLayout element route at :219, with an inline comment confirming it "renders outside AppLayout." (5) PortfolioTracker.jsx:299-300 therefore always evaluate `totalPnL * 3200` and `pnlData.currentValue * 3200`; :333 renders `~$X` and :342 renders `+$X` with no rate disclosure. (6) Single mount point — App.jsx:798-799, unconditional switch case "portfolio", no gate. (7) The claim that an honest rate is available also checks out: hooks/useEthUsd.js resolves context -> cached CoinGecko, clamps to 100..100,000, and returns 0 (render nothing) rather than inventing a rate; components/Usd.jsx wraps it and is already used by ShoppingCart.jsx, Modal.jsx, Listings.jsx, Hero.jsx and Gallery.jsx in the same directory. PortfolioTracker is the sole holdout — it does not import Usd (the grep hit in that file is only the local identifiers totalPnLUsd/currentValueUsd), and `3200` appears nowhere else under frontend/src/nakamigos. lib/formatPrice.js:29-38 states the opposite rule in prose ("this NEVER fabricates a rate"). The scenario's arithmetic is correct: 1.2 ETH * 3200 = $3,840 vs $2,400 at a real $2,000/ETH, a 60% overstatement, and the TOTAL P&L caption at :342 inherits the same multiplier. I could not refute any element of the claim. I attempted the strongest counterarguments and each failed: there is no second PortfolioTracker mount inside AppLayout that would make the fallback a genuine degraded path; the `?? {}` at :127 is not a crash guard that ever sees a populated object on this route; and the inline comment at :124-126 ("this tab renders outside the main app's PriceProvider ... the ?? path keeps USD math on the existing 3200 fallback") is an in-repo admission that the constant is the only path, not a fallback.
verdicts.correction: The technical claim needs no correction — file:line, the routing argument, the null-return mechanism, and the arithmetic all hold. I would grade it medium rather than high, on presentation weight only. Mitigating facts visible in the same render: the fabricated figure is a 9px dim caption (:332-334, :341-343) sitting beneath the primary ETH-denominated values (:330, :339), which are correct and are what this audience actually reads; it is prefixed "~"; and nothing on this surface builds, signs, prices, or gates a transaction off the USD number, so the worst outcome is a misinformed hold/sell judgement, not a mispriced or lost transaction. Aggravating facts that keep it above low: the error fires for 100% of visitors rather than only in a failure mode, it is unbounded and grows as ETH drifts from $3,200, and there is no correction path at all (the Refresh button at :309-319 re-runs loadPortfolio but cannot change the constant). Accurate one-line statement: "PortfolioTracker's USD captions (PortfolioTracker.jsx:299-300) always multiply by a hardcoded 3200 because the PriceProvider they read from is mounted only inside AppLayout (AppLayout.tsx:113) while /nakamigos/* routes outside it (App.tsx:206), so both the PORTFOLIO VALUE and TOTAL P&L dollar lines are fabricated on every visit; the fix already exists in-tree as hooks/useEthUsd.js + components/Usd.jsx, used by five sibling components." Also worth passing along to whoever fixes it: useEthUsd returns 0 when it has no real rate and formatUsd (lib/formatPrice.js:48-54) returns its empty fallback for a non-positive rate, so the correct fix renders no USD line at all rather than substituting another number.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED end to end by reading the files.

Chain verified:

- PriceContext.tsx:61-63 useTOWELIPriceOptional is a bare useContext -> returns null outside the provider. Its own doc comment (:53-58) states the Tradermigos sub-app has two mount points, "neither is wrapped".
- PortfolioTracker.jsx:127 `const { ethUsd } = useTOWELIPriceOptional() ?? {}` therefore yields undefined on EVERY render for EVERY user.
- Lines 299-300 `totalPnL * (ethUsd || 3200)` and `pnlData.currentValue * (ethUsd || 3200)` are consequently the only path, not a degraded path.
- Rendered at :333 as `~${Math.round(currentValueUsd).toLocaleString()}` and :342 as `{pnlSign}${...}` with no staleness marker.
- Tab reachability: constants.js:94 lists "portfolio"; App.jsx:798-799 renders PortfolioTracker from an unconditional switch, no flag.

At ETH $2,000 the truthful figure is $2,400 (60% overstatement), and the TOTAL P&L dollar line inherits the same multiplier.

MAINTAINER DEFENSE EVALUATED AND REJECTED (4 grounds):
1. "Documented deliberate fallback" (comment at :124-126 citing prod bug 2026-06-11) — a fallback that fires 100% of the time is a hardcoded constant. The comment misdescribes the runtime.
2. "It prevents a crash" — false. The crash guard is the `?? {}` at :127. `|| 3200` does zero defensive work; substituting 0 or useEthUsd() would not reintroduce the 06-11 bug.
3. "PriceContext sanctions caller fallbacks" — the repo's actual house rule is the opposite and is implemented three ways: hooks/useEthUsd.js:7-19 ("Returns 0 when no real rate is available... We NEVER hardcode a placeholder rate", CoinGecko fallback + 100..100_000 clamp, written explicitly FOR this unwrapped mount), lib/formatPrice.js:29-38 and :52 (`if (r <= 0) return fallback`), and components/Usd.jsx (renders null rather than a fake figure). PortfolioTracker imports none of them (:1-8).
4. "The ~ marks it approximate" — a tilde reads as rounding, not "rate is a constant"; Usd.jsx uses the same grammar for REAL rates, so it implies equivalent provenance.

Git corroborates it is an un-migrated straggler, not a considered exception: the 3200 line originates in 10d026d0 (2026-04-11), predating the useEthUsd honesty work (1d470333 "USD denomination across the trading surface F665/F556").
verdicts.correction:
Finding stands as written; severity high is correct. Three precision amendments, none of which change the verdict:

1. Scope quantified: "Every USD figure in the Portfolio tab" is literally true but there are exactly TWO such figures (:333 PORTFOLIO VALUE and :342 TOTAL P&L), and both are fabricated. The per-token breakdown rows (:484) render ETH only via formatPrice and are honest. The finding should say "both USD figures" rather than leaving the count open.

2. Blast radius: the fabricated rate is display-only. Grep confirms currentValueUsd/totalPnLUsd are consumed nowhere but :333 and :342 — no transaction build, quote, fee, or persisted snapshot uses them (saveSnapshot at :191 stores the ETH-denominated currentValue). So the harm is confident misinformation on a money surface, not fund loss. High is still right — permanently wrong by construction for every user, unbounded drift as ETH moves, no staleness marker, no in-app remedy, and a correct hook exists 40 lines away — but it is not critical.

3. Defect class: this is NOT a failed read being laundered; it is a read that is never attempted (the provider is absent from the subtree, so there is no upstream failure to swallow). Same user-visible outcome, but the fix differs and should be stated: import useEthUsd from ../hooks/useEthUsd and render via formatUsd/<Usd>, which returns "" for a 0 rate so the line disappears rather than lying. Do not add error handling around the context read.

survived.title: A swallowed Alchemy failure makes every held NFT read as a free mint and reports the whole portfolio as pure profit
survived.claim: calculatePnL wraps both getNFTSales calls in try/catch blocks that only console.warn in DEV (lines 145-147 and 157-159) and leave allSales/sellSales as []. purchaseMap is then empty, so line 186 gives every held token `costBasis = purchase?.costBasis ?? 0` and line 209 sets `isMint: !purchase` = true for all of them. unrealizedPnL (line 251) becomes totalCurrentValue - 0 = the entire portfolio value. The result is written to a 5-minute localStorage cache at line 265, and PortfolioTracker.jsx:190-194 feeds it into saveSnapshot, persisting it into the 90-day value chart. The UI renders it as a green TOTAL P&L (PortfolioTracker.jsx:338-343) and stamps a green 'MINT' badge on every row (PortfolioTracker.jsx:470-478). A 429 from the Alchemy proxy is the ordinary trigger — proxy.js:147 throws ApiError on any non-2xx, and this tab fires getNFTSales twice on top of fetchWalletNfts and fetchCollectionStats.
survived.failure_scenario: A user bought 10 Nakamigos at 1.0 ETH each; the floor is now 0.1. The Alchemy proxy returns 429 on both getNFTSales calls. The tab renders TOTAL P&L as '+Ξ 1.0000' in green (instead of the true -Ξ9.0), GAS (EST.) as Ξ0 (line 197 only charges gas when a purchase record exists), a 'MINT' badge on all 10 tokens the user actually paid for, and 'No gainers with known cost basis' / 'No losers with known cost basis' in both performer panels. The wrong number is cached for 5 minutes and written into the value-over-time chart permanently.
survived.suggested_fix: Have calculatePnL record that the sales lookups failed (e.g. return a salesUnavailable flag) instead of silently substituting an empty array, do not writeCache or saveSnapshot on that path, and have PortfolioTracker render the retryable error banner it already has at lines 264-276 rather than a P&L computed over no purchase history.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every load-bearing line reproduces verbatim in `frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/portfolio.js` and `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/PortfolioTracker.jsx` (note the finding's path is missing the `components/` segment; line numbers are correct).

- portfolio.js:137-147 and 150-160 — both `getNFTSales` calls sit in try/catch whose entire body is `if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.warn(...)`. In a production build that is a no-op; `allSales`/`sellSales` stay `[]` and NO error flag is attached to the returned object.

- portfolio.js:186 `const costBasis = purchase?.costBasis ?? 0` and :209 `isMint: !purchase` — every held token gets cost basis 0 and `isMint: true`.
- portfolio.js:197 `if (purchase) totalGasSpent += GAS_ESTIMATE` — gas totals 0.
- portfolio.js:251 `unrealizedPnL = totalCurrentValue - totalCostBasis` = full portfolio value.
- portfolio.js:265 `writeCache(key, result)` with the 5-min TTL at :11 — the fabricated result is cached (the Refresh button does bypass it via forceRefresh, portfolio.js:126-127).

The realized branch was hardened against precisely this; the unrealized branch does what the realized branch was fixed not to do. SEVERITY: high holds. User-visible, money-adjacent (P&L), silently wrong in the flattering direction, cached 5 minutes, no signal anywhere. Not critical — read-only display, signs nothing and moves no funds.

With every costBasis at 0, the line 213 filter (t.costBasis > 0) empties both arrays, so the whole section does not render — the user sees no panels at all, not two "no data" messages. Ξ0 (197 -> 348); MINT badge on all 10 paid-for tokens (209 -> 470-478); AVG COST Ξ0 in the collection breakdown (411); 5-minute cache (265).
