survived.title: Cancel sends the transaction to Seaport 1.5 while discarding the order's own protocol address, then reports success
survived.claim: fetchMyListings carries each order's real protocol address through to the caller (api-offers.js:659, `protocolAddress: o.protocol_address`), but cancelOrder ignores it and passes the hardcoded `seaportAddress: SEAPORT_ADDRESS` (Seaport 1.5, constants.js:113) into cancelSeaportOrder. lib/seaportCancel.js:73-78 pins the target to whatever it is handed, reads getCounter on THAT contract, and calls cancel() there. Seaport's cancel() does not revert for an order hash it has never seen, so the tx mines and returns true. MyCollection.jsx:182-184 then toasts 'Listing cancelled successfully!' and removes the row from ACTIVE LISTINGS. Note that lib/seaportCancel.js's own header docstring describes exactly this failure mode ('the UI toasted cancelled — but the real listing stayed 100% fillable'), and components/OrderBookPanel.jsx:70 is the only call site that correctly forwards the order's protocol_address.
survived.failure_scenario: A user lists a Nakamigo on opensea.io, where new orders are signed against Seaport 1.6 (0x0000000000000068F116a894984e2DB1123eB395 — already in the KNOWN_SEAPORT_ADDRESSES allowlist at constants.js:122). MyCollection's ACTIVE LISTINGS shows it. The floor rises and the user clicks Cancel to relist higher. The cancel is submitted to Seaport 1.5, mines, costs gas, and cancels nothing. The UI says 'Listing cancelled successfully!' and drops the row, so the user believes the NFT is delisted — while the 1.6 order is still fillable and anyone can buy the NFT at the old price.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass `seaportAddress: order.protocolAddress` (falling back to SEAPORT_ADDRESS only when the field is absent) exactly as OrderBookPanel.jsx:70 does; resolveSeaportTarget already fails closed on an unrecognised address. The same one-line defect exists in components/MyListings.jsx:386 and components/BidManager.jsx:286.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not — every link in the chain reproduces at the cited lines.

1. `frontend/src/nakamigos/api-offers.js:615-667` — `fetchMyListings` calls `openseaGet("orders/ethereum/seaport/listings", {maker, asset_contract_address, ...})`. That is the real OpenSea v2 API via `lib/proxy.js:61-63` (`/api/opensea?path=...`), queried by maker+contract, so it returns listings the user created on opensea.io, not just app-created ones. The `.map()` at :645-662 preserves `protocolAddress: o.protocol_address` (:659) and `rawOrder: o` (:660). The filter chain at :639-644 drops only cancelled/finalized/expired — there is no protocol-version filter, so a Seaport 1.6 row survives to the UI.

2. `api-offers.js:690` — `cancelOrder(order)` pulls `params` out of `order.rawOrder.protocol_data.parameters` (:683) but then calls `cancelSeaportOrder({ ..., seaportAddress: SEAPORT_ADDRESS })`. The order's own `protocolAddress`, carried all the way from :659, is never read. `SEAPORT_ADDRESS` is Seaport 1.5 (`constants.js:118`, `0x00000000000000ADc04C56Bf30aC9d3c0aAF14dC`), and `constants.js:117` even carries the stale comment "verify compatibility if OpenSea migrates to v1.6".

3. `lib/seaportCancel.js:67-79` — the helper builds the contract at whatever `resolveSeaportTarget(seaportAddress)` returns, reads `getCounter(params.offerer)` on that contract, and calls `cancel([components])` there. Seaport's `_cancel` requires only `msg.sender == offerer || zone`; an unseen order hash is simply marked cancelled and returns true, so the tx mines. The file's own header (:4-13) documents this exact failure mode from the F630 bug ("The tx mined ... and the UI toasted 'cancelled' — but the real listing/bid stayed 100% fillable").

4. `components/MyCollection.jsx:180-184` — `if (result.success)` toasts "Listing cancelled successfully!" and `setListings(prev => prev.filter(...))`, removing the row from ACTIVE LISTINGS. `result.success` is set at `api-offers.js:692` purely on `tx.wait()` resolving.

The one thing the finding states imprecisely: `seaportCancel.js:73-74` does not pin "the target to whatever it is handed" — it runs the value through `resolveSeaportTarget` (`constants.js:138-143`), which is a fail-closed allowlist. That guard just cannot help here, because the hardcoded 1.5 address is itself allowlisted (`constants.js:128`). Mechanism and outcome are unchanged; only the description of that line needs correcting.

The finding also UNDERSTATES breadth. `grep` for `cancelSeaportOrder` shows four call sites; only `components/OrderBookPanel.jsx:70` forwards the order's address. The other two hardcodes:
- `components/BidManager.jsx:286` — same defect class for BID cancels. `normalizeOrder` at :250 captures `protocolAddress: order.protocol_address` from OpenSea's `orders/ethereum/seaport/offers`, and :286 discards it for `SEAPORT_ADDRESS`. A WETH bid signed against 1.6 is "cancelled" against 1.5 and stays fillable — arguably worse, since a live stale bid can be hit against the user.
- `components/MyListings.jsx:386` — this one is effectively benign today: its rows come from the native orderbook (`:310-328`), and the app writes `protocol_address: SEAPORT_ADDRESS` when it creates them (`lib/orderbook.js:449, 651`) and signs against `SEAPORT_DOMAIN` version "1.5" (`constants.js:147-152`). It captures `protocolAddress` at :321 and discards it at :386, so it is latent, not live.

Exposure is therefore exclusively orders the user created on opensea.io (or anywhere signing against 1.6) and which the app surfaces in MyCollection's ACTIVE LISTINGS and BidManager's bids. Nothing the app signs itself is affected.

Severity high is right, not critical: no attacker input is needed and the loss is real (NFT sells at a stale floor price after the user was told it was delisted, plus wasted gas), but it requires the listing to have originated off-app against 1.6.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: `api-offers.js:690` discards the order's own `protocolAddress` (carried through at :659) and hardcodes Seaport 1.5 (`constants.js:118`). `lib/seaportCancel.js:73-74` does run the value through the fail-closed `resolveSeaportTarget` allowlist — it does not blindly trust its argument — but that guard is a no-op here because 1.5 is itself allowlisted (`constants.js:128`), so the cancel lands on 1.5 regardless. Seaport's `cancel()` does not revert on an unknown hash, so the tx mines, `api-offers.js:692` returns `{success:true}`, and `MyCollection.jsx:182-184` toasts "Listing cancelled successfully!" and drops the row while a 1.6 order stays fillable. Additionally, the same hardcode exists at `components/BidManager.jsx:286` for bid cancels (its `protocolAddress` is captured at :250 and discarded), which is live OpenSea-sourced and equally exposed; `components/MyListings.jsx:386` has the same hardcode but is latent only, since its rows are native-orderbook orders the app itself created against 1.5 (`lib/orderbook.js:449, 651`).

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed at source. fetchMyListings (frontend/src/nakamigos/api-offers.js:621-626) queries OpenSea with only {maker, asset_contract_address} — no protocol/source filter — so it returns every live listing that wallet has on the contract, including orders signed on opensea.io against Seaport 1.6. It computes protocolAddress: o.protocol_address at :659, and cancelOrder discards it at :690, passing the hardcoded seaportAddress: SEAPORT_ADDRESS (Seaport 1.5, constants.js:118). lib/seaportCancel.js:73-75 resolves the target from whatever it is handed and fails closed only on an UNKNOWN address; our own constant always resolves non-null, so the guard is unreachable on this path — it protects against a poisoned address, not against the real one never being supplied. Seaport cancel() requires only msg.sender == offerer, hashes the given components, marks that hash cancelled and returns true with no existence check, so the tx mines; cancelOrder returns {success:true} (:691-692) and MyCollection.jsx:182-184 toasts 'Listing cancelled successfully!' and removes the row while the 1.6 order stays fillable. The maintainer defenses all fail: (1) 'we are a 1.5-only client' is true for orders we SIGN (SEAPORT_DOMAIN version 1.5, constants.js:147-152) but false for orders we DISPLAY and offer a Cancel button on; (2) 'the sink is hardened by resolveSeaportTarget' is bypassed by construction; (3) 'F630 was about the counter slot, a different bug' is wrong at the level that matters — the docstring in lib/seaportCancel.js:1-14 describes the identical user-visible consequence (mined tx, toasted cancelled, order stays 100% fillable). The repo itself treats 1.6 orders as live reality: constants.js:127-130, api.js:1126, and frontend/api/orderbook.js:1550-1555 ('pin (1.6 only) DoS'd every fill that landed on Seaport 1.5'). Only limitation: I could not execute a live OpenSea query to exhibit a 1.6 protocol_address for this collection, so the 'orders in the wild are 1.6' link is inference from OpenSea's protocol migration plus the repo's own 1.6 handling; the source-level discard is unconditional regardless.
verdicts.correction: The finding is accurate as written; two corrections both widen it. (1) FREQUENCY understated: the scenario reads as an edge case, but since new OpenSea orders are signed against Seaport 1.6, any listing created outside this app is the COMMON case — the reliably-succeeding 1.5 cancel is the narrow one. (2) SCOPE understated: 'OrderBookPanel.jsx:70 is the only call site that correctly forwards protocol_address' is true, but the finding omits that components/BidManager.jsx:286 has the identical defect on the bids path — normalizeOffer carries protocolAddress at api-offers.js:190, cancelBid discards it for the hardcoded SEAPORT_ADDRESS, and BidManager.jsx:457 reports success, so a stale WETH bid the user believes cancelled remains acceptable by any holder. MyListings.jsx:386 also hardcodes, but that path reads the native orderbook where orders are our own 1.5 signatures, so it is latent rather than live. Severity stays high: silent false success on a money path where the user acts on the false statement (relists, or stops watching) and eats the delta between the stale ask and the current floor.

verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the mechanism end to end, but the finding overstates the consequence and the severity.

VERIFIED (the core claim is real):

REFUTED (the part that makes the title and severity wrong):
- "un-cancellable" is false. `my-listings` is a first-class production tab: `constants.js:90-95` (VALID_TABS), `App.jsx:95` + `:776-777`, and it is in both navs (`components/Header.jsx:147`, `components/MobileNav.jsx:28`). `components/MyListings.jsx:262-290` queries `/api/orderbook?action=query&maker=<wallet>&status=active` — i.e. exactly the native orders the wizard creates — and provides per-row Cancel plus Cancel All. Native listings are also visible and cancellable from the Floor/orderbook panel (`components/OrderBookPanel.jsx:125`, `:303`; `components/NativeListingsList.jsx:180-210`, which renders a Cancel `ActionButton` when `order.maker === wallet`).

MyCollection never renders a false factual sentence: when `listings` is empty the "· N listed" span is simply omitted (`:228`) and the ACTIVE LISTINGS block does not render at all (`:337`). There is no "0 listed" / "no active listings" claim on this tab. It is an absent view, not a laundered read. (The genuine swallow — `api-offers.js:663` `catch { return [] }` — has the same silent-absence consequence, not a false assertion.)

Net: real, reproducible defect (source mismatch between the tab's own write path and its read path), but it is a cross-tab UX/duplicate-listing hazard, not a loss of control over live orders. Medium, not high.

survived.title: A failed wallet read renders as 'Your wallet does not hold any NFTs to trade'
survived.claim: `fetchWalletNfts` never rejects — on any upstream failure it returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: 'Could not load wallet NFTs...' }` (api.js:660-663). NftCompare destructures only `{ tokens: owned }` (line 201) and drops the `error` field entirely, so an outage is indistinguishable from an empty wallet. The `.catch()` at line 211 is unreachable for this case. The empty branch at lines 328-333 then states as fact: 'No <collection> Found' / 'Your wallet does not hold any <collection> NFTs to trade.' PortfolioTracker.jsx:161 handles the same return value correctly and even carries a comment about it, so the honest pattern exists in-tree.
survived.failure_scenario: Alchemy is rate-limited or the /api/alchemy proxy 5xx's. A holder of 8 Nakamigos opens the trade tab. fetchWalletNfts resolves with tokens:[] and an error string that is thrown away. The left panel renders 'No Nakamigos Found — Your wallet does not hold any Nakamigos NFTs to trade.' The user is told a false fact about their own holdings, has no retry control, and the state never self-corrects (the effect only re-runs on wallet/tokens/contract change).
survived.suggested_fix: Read the `error` field from fetchWalletNfts and render an error-with-retry state instead of the 'you hold nothing' empty state, matching PortfolioTracker.jsx:151-165.

NftCompare.jsx:201 destructures only `({ tokens: owned })` and discards `error`. The `.catch()` at :211-216 is unreachable for this case. The empty branch at :328-333 then asserts as fact: "No {collection.name} Found" / "Your wallet does not hold any {collection.name} NFTs to trade." The only failure signal anywhere is a console.warn in api.js:661. There is no error state and no retry control in the panel.

CORRECTION to the scenario's last clause: "the state never self-corrects" is too strong. The effect deps [wallet, tokens, collection.contract] are stable (tokens = nfts.allTokens = rankedTokens, a useMemo at hooks/useNfts.js:148/:190), so it will not re-run in place — but App.jsx renders NftCompare only when tab === "trade" (App.jsx:90, :761), so switching tabs away and back remounts and refetches, as does a page reload. Accurate statement: the panel offers no error indication and no retry affordance, so nothing prompts the user to remount; they are simply told a false fact about their own holdings and left with the trade path unusable.

Severity high is correct: the false claim is about the user's own wallet contents, it sits on the P2P trade (money) path, and it is silent. The honest pattern exists in-tree at PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 with a comment referencing F724, so the fix is a two-line lift.

Breadth beyond the reported line (same swallow, unchecked callers): useProAccess.jsx:29-32 (`data?.totalCount || 0` -> false, currently masked by PRO_PASS_LIVE gate), useHolderStatus.jsx:83, MyCollection.jsx:116 and :154, OnChainProfile.jsx:137, WhaleIntelligence.jsx:254, BidManager.jsx:359, TradesPanel.jsx:83 and :449, TradeWindow.jsx:146. PortfolioTracker is the only caller that inspects `error`.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every cited line. api.js:648-664 returns the exact `{tokens:[], totalCount:0, error}` envelope claimed and never rejects. proxy.js:142-154 confirms the transport throws on outage and api.js withRetry rethrows, so the catch is genuinely exercised by a 5xx or rate limit rather than being dead code. NftCompare.jsx:201 discards `error`; the .catch at :211 cannot fire for that path; :328-333 renders the confident "Your wallet does not hold any ... NFTs to trade." copy with no error UI and no retry. App.jsx:90/:761 confirm the trade tab is unconditionally reachable. useNfts.js:148/:190 confirm the `tokens` prop is a stable useMemo so the effect will not re-run in place. PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 confirms the honest in-tree pattern and even names the prior finding ID. Only defect in the report: "never self-corrects" ignores that a tab remount or reload refetches; the substantive harm (silent false claim about the user's own holdings, no retry affordance, money path blocked) is unchanged, so severity stays high.

verdicts.correction:
The finding is correct on every mechanical point; only the severity needs adjusting from high to medium.

Accurate as written:
- `frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:648-664` — `fetchWalletNfts` wraps its entire body in try/catch and on failure returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs. Please check your connection and try again." }` (api.js:662). It never rejects. `alchemyGet` (api.js:66-70) is `withRetry(..., { maxRetries: 2 })`, so a sustained 429/5xx lands in that catch, not a transient one.
- `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/NftCompare.jsx:201` — `.then(({ tokens: owned }) => ...)` destructures only `tokens`. The `error` field is discarded at the destructuring site; no other code in the component references it.
- `NftCompare.jsx:211` — the `.catch()` is genuinely unreachable for the outage case (the only way in is a throw from inside the `.then` body itself).
- `NftCompare.jsx:328-333` — the empty branch renders "No {collection.name} Found" / "Your wallet does not hold any {collection.name} NFTs to trade." with no retry control, and because it is the `else if` arm of the ternary it *replaces* the `NftSlot` search input entirely (NftCompare.jsx:334-344), so the tab's only function is blocked.
- Effect deps are `[wallet, tokens, collection.contract]` (NftCompare.jsx:218) and `tokens` is `nfts.allTokens` = `rankedTokens`, a `useMemo` over loaded tokens (hooks/useNfts.js:147-150, 190). I checked for polling — there is no `setInterval` and no live refresh in useNfts.js. So once the collection has finished loading, the identity is stable and the false empty state is terminal until wallet change / collection switch / reload. The one nuance the finding omits: if the user opens the tab *while* the collection is still streaming pages, `allTokens` changes identity and the effect re-fires, which can incidentally self-heal. That is accidental, not a mitigation anyone designed.
- The honest pattern does exist in-tree: `components/PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167` explicitly checks `if (nftData.error && nftData.tokens.length === 0)` and sets a retryable error, with a comment referencing F724.

Severity: medium, not high. The defect class is real (failed-read laundering, a false factual sentence about the user's own assets, no retry), but the blast radius is bounded — it discourages an action rather than inducing a wrong one. No transaction is built, signed, or priced off this state; `handleSendTrade` (NftCompare.jsx:244-280) is unreachable without a selected `yourNft`. Contrast a scanner "no wash trading detected", which drives a buy. Fix is the PortfolioTracker pattern: destructure the full result, and when `error && tokens.length === 0` render a retryable error state instead of the "does not hold any" copy.

Breadth note for the sweep (not part of this finding): every other `fetchWalletNfts` consumer drops `error` the same way — MyCollection.jsx:116 and :154, BidManager.jsx:359, OnChainProfile.jsx:137, WhaleIntelligence.jsx:254, TradesPanel.jsx:83 and :449, TradeWindow.jsx:146, hooks/useHolderStatus.jsx:83, hooks/useProAccess.jsx:29. `useProAccess` is the one worth ranking above this finding: a failed read there resolves as "not a Pro Pass holder" and gates a paid feature shut.
verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to defend it and could not. The three arguments available to me all fail against the file.

(1) "The empty state is a UI affordance, not a claim — the trade tab is a picker, not an information surface." Does not hold. NftCompare.jsx:332 is a declarative sentence about the user's property: "Your wallet does not hold any Nakamigos NFTs to trade." That is a factual assertion, and it is exactly the sentence a broken upstream produces.

(2) "withRetry absorbs failures, so the catch only fires on genuinely dead connections." Does not hold. api.js:66-70 gives 2 retries; Alchemy rate-limiting and proxy 5xx routinely outlive 3 attempts. The `error` string at api.js:662 exists precisely because the author expected callers to hit it — and PortfolioTracker.jsx:161 proves the author expected callers to *handle* it.

(3) "It self-corrects on the next render / collection load." Does not hold once the collection has settled. I checked useNfts.js for polling and there is none; rankedTokens is a plain memo. A user who navigates to /nakamigos/trade after the gallery is loaded is stuck with the false statement and has no retry button.

The strongest thing I can say in the code's defense is that the failure is non-financial and self-limiting: the user can open the collection tab or a block explorer and see their NFTs. That is an argument about severity, not about correctness, and it is why I dropped high to medium rather than refuting.

survived.title: Incoming trade cards quote the final Dutch-leg amount as if it were the amount you get now
survived.claim: `TradeCard` computes `wethTopup = fmtEth(trade.weth_topup_wei)` and `ethTopup = fmtEth(trade.eth_topup_wei)` (lines 209-210) and renders them as the live cash legs (lines 271-285) and inside the accept button (line 300). Those DB columns store the MAX of each leg, not the current value — frontend/api/orderbook.js:1712-1717 defines `maxLeg` and the comment says 'Stored topup columns carry the MAX of each leg'. TradeChips.jsx:54-58 makes the same point from the display side ('the stored topup columns carry the max commitment, not the moment') and correctly uses `currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters)` instead. TradesPanel's own TradeCard never calls it. Rising sweeteners are reachable in production via the '📈 Auto-sweeten until accepted' checkbox in TradeWindow.jsx:401-421, which this same panel opens.
survived.failure_scenario: A maker posts a directed trade: NFT #123 plus a WETH sweetener starting at 0.05 and rising to 0.50 over a 3-day expiry. The recipient opens Trades > incoming an hour later. The card's YOU GET column reads '+ 0.5000 WETH'. They accept. Seaport interpolates and actually pays them ~0.056 WETH — roughly a tenth of what the card promised. The same trade viewed through TradeSummary (the board card, or the DM trade card) shows the correct '0.0560↗ WETH', so the app quotes two different prices for one order.
survived.suggested_fix: Have TradeCard derive its cash legs from `currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters)` exactly as TradeChips.jsx:56-58 does, keeping the ↗/↘ arrows, and reserve the stored max only for the msg.value the button actually escrows.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every link in the chain reproduces from the files.

1. The columns really are the MAX, not the moment. frontend/api/orderbook.js:1712-1717 defines `const maxLeg = (item) => { const a = parseAmt(item.startAmount); const b = parseAmt(item.endAmount); return a > b ? a : b; }` under the comment "Stored topup columns carry the MAX of each leg — the maker's full commitment." It is the only writer: `wethTopupWei += maxLeg(item)` (line ~1735, offer itemType 1) and `ethTopupWei += maxLeg(item)` (line ~1772, consideration itemType 0), persisted once at orderbook.js:1905-1906 (`eth_topup_wei`, `weth_topup_wei`). Nothing anywhere updates those columns after insert — grep for the column names returns only those two write sites.

2. TradesPanel's TradeCard really does render those raw columns as the live legs. TradesPanel.jsx:209-210 `const ethTopup = fmtEth(trade.eth_topup_wei); const wethTopup = fmtEth(trade.weth_topup_wei);` (`fmtEth` is `fmtEthWei` from TradeChips, imported at line 6 — a pure wei formatter, no interpolation). Rendered at 271, 274, 281, 284 as the YOU GIVE / YOU GET cash lines, and baked into the accept button at line 300 (`pay ${ethTopup} ETH`). `currentLegAmounts` is never imported into TradesPanel.jsx.

3. The correct helper exists and the sibling component uses it. TradeChips.jsx:54-58 — "the stored topup columns carry the max commitment, not the moment" — computes `const legs = trade.parameters ? currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters) : null` and falls back to the stored column only when `parameters` is absent, plus renders ↗/↘ arrows (lines 59-60). `currentLegAmounts` (lib/trades.js:685-709) linearly interpolates offer itemType-1 and consideration itemType-0 amounts over [startTime, endTime], exactly as Seaport does.

4. `trade.parameters` IS available to TradeCard, so this is a plain omission, not a data gap: the trade-query handler does `supabase.from("trade_offers").select("*")` (orderbook.js:385) and returns whole rows (line 414); TradesPanel passes the whole row down (line 641). OpenTradeAccept in the same file already reads `trade.parameters?.consideration` (line 69).

5. Rising sweeteners are reachable in production on the directed path that TradeCard renders. TradeWindow.jsx:401-408 is the "📈 Auto-sweeten until accepted" checkbox (`setWethEnd(e.target.checked ? (wethTopup || "0.01") : "")`), 409-421 the "rises to … by expiry" input; it is in the shared "Cash legs" block rendered in both directed and board mode. It flows to `wethTopupEndEth` (TradeWindow.jsx:243) → `buildTradeOrderParameters` (lib/trades.js:190, 217) which emits `startAmount: wethTopupWei, endAmount: wethEnd` on the WETH offer item. The API accepts it: `maxLeg` does not require start >= end, and only NFT legs are pinned static (`assertStaticNft`).

Arithmetic in the scenario checks out: 0.05 → 0.50 WETH over 3 days, viewed at t+1h → 0.05 + 0.45·(3600/259200) = 0.0563 WETH, against a card that says 0.5000 WETH. ~8.9x overstatement of what the acceptor receives, with the DM trade card (DirectMessages.jsx:97) and the board card (TradesPanel.jsx:616) quoting 0.0563↗ for the same order.

Nothing about the accept path compensates: acceptTrade (lib/trades.js:474 onward) passes `params` straight into the Seaport struct with the raw start/end amounts (lines 559-573), so the chain interpolates and the taker receives the ~0.056, not the 0.50 the card promised.

I found no counter-evidence. Severity high stands: a money-path misquote that a user acts on by clicking Accept.
verdicts.correction:
CONFIRMED as stated, with three additions that make it broader than the write-up.

(a) Both directions are wrong, not just the WETH one. The decaying-ETH-ask twin is reachable via the mirrored "THEY ADD (ETH)" decay checkbox at TradeWindow.jsx:437-441 (`ethEnd`), and `maxLeg` on a decaying leg stores the START amount. So the accept button at TradesPanel.jsx:300 says "Confirm — sign & pay 0.5000 ETH" when Seaport will interpolate down to, say, 0.1. That direction OVERSTATES the taker's cost (Seaport refunds the unused msg.value — lib/trades.js:539-550 deliberately sends max), so it is a deterrent/misquote rather than a loss, but it is the same defect and it makes the button copy wrong in both directions. Same for the YOU GIVE / YOU GET ETH lines at TradesPanel.jsx:271 and 284.

(b) The open/board accept modal contradicts ITSELF on screen. OpenTradeAccept computes `const ethTopup = fmtEth(trade.eth_topup_wei)` at TradesPanel.jsx:73 and puts it in the confirm button at line 177 — while line 106 of the same modal renders `<TradeSummary>`, which uses `currentLegAmounts` and shows the correct interpolated figure with a ↘ arrow. Two different ETH numbers, ~10cm apart, in one dialog.

(c) Adjacent and lower severity, worth fixing in the same patch: the counter prefill at TradesPanel.jsx:489-490 seeds the new order from `fmtEth(counterTrade.eth_topup_wei)` / `fmtEth(counterTrade.weth_topup_wei)` — also the max, so a counter to a Dutch trade silently starts at the original's ceiling rather than at its live value.

Fix shape: TradeCard and OpenTradeAccept should derive from `currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters)` with the stored column only as a fallback when `parameters` is missing — i.e. the exact pattern already in TradeChips.jsx:56-58 — and should carry the ↗/↘ arrows so the accept button and the board card agree.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced end-to-end. TradesPanel.jsx:209-210 reads the stored max columns; orderbook.js:1712-1717 defines maxLeg with the comment "Stored topup columns carry the MAX of each leg", and 1734/1775 accumulate into weth_topup_wei/eth_topup_wei written at 1908. TradeChips.jsx:56-60 uses currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters) and renders a rising arrow, its comment (54-55) explicitly stating the stored columns carry the max not the moment. TradeCard never calls it. Arithmetic checks out: 0.05->0.50 over 3 days, one hour in, interp = 0.05 + 0.45*(3600/259200) = 0.05625 vs a card reading 0.5000 (~8.9x, approaching 10x at t=0). Reachable in production: TradeWindow.jsx:401-408 checkbox -> line 243 wethTopupEndEth -> trades.js:196,216-217 startAmount/endAmount.

The three maintainer defenses fail. (1) "Max is the intended commitment view" is contradicted by the copy itself: line 281 renders a bare "+ 0.5000 WETH" with no "up to" and no arrow, while the sibling TradeSummary renders "+ 0.0560 arrow WETH" for the identical concept. (2) "TradeCard lacks parameters" is false: orderbook.js:385 is select("*") and parameters is a column, proven at runtime by TradesPanel.jsx:68-71 reading trade.parameters.consideration in the same file. (3) "msg.value really is max so the button is honest" is true only for the native ETH leg (trades.js:539-550 pays max and Seaport refunds) and does not touch the WETH leg, where an under-delivered ERC-20 offer item has no refund path.

The finding is under-scoped rather than mis-stated. Six sites: TradesPanel.jsx:281 (incoming YOU GET WETH - the harmful under-quote), 274 (outgoing YOU GIVE WETH), 271 and 284 (ETH legs), 300 (accept button), plus an unnamed second offender at 73+177 - OpenTradeAccept renders live TradeSummary at line 106 and a max-based confirm button at line 177 in the same modal, showing two different prices ~70px apart on the final screen before signing. Also note TradesPanel.jsx:616 uses the correct live TradeSummary for board cards, so the same file quotes one order two ways.

Direction nuance: the ETH legs over-quote (max = startAmount for a decaying ask) and msg.value genuinely is that max, so the ETH button misstates net cost rather than the wallet prompt - that portion is medium. The WETH under-quote at line 281 carries the high severity: irreversible money path, user accepts on a number up to ~10x what they receive.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: TradesPanel's TradeCard (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/TradesPanel.jsx:209-210) and OpenTradeAccept (line 73) both read the stored MAX topup columns and render them as live cash legs and inside accept buttons, while TradeChips.jsx TradeSummary correctly derives live Dutch-leg amounts via currentLegAmounts(trade.parameters). Affected render sites: TradesPanel.jsx:271, 274, 281, 284, 300 (TradeCard) and 73 -> 177 (OpenTradeAccept confirm button, which sits ~70px below a correct live TradeSummary at line 106 in the same modal). Worst case is line 281: a recipient of an auto-sweetened incoming trade is shown the final sweetener as the amount they get now, up to ~10x the interpolated value, and there is no refund mechanism for an under-delivered ERC-20 offer item. The ETH-side sites (271, 284, 300, 177) over-quote instead; msg.value genuinely is max(start,end) per trades.js:539-550 with Seaport refunding the remainder, so those misstate net cost and contradict the live figure shown elsewhere on the same screen - medium on their own. Overall severity high, driven by the WETH under-quote in an irreversible accept flow.

survived.title: Failed inventory read tells you 'You don't hold any <collection> — you can't fill this slot'
survived.claim: `OpenTradeAccept` loads the acceptor's inventory with `out[contract] = res?.tokens || []` (line 84) and a `catch { out[contract] = [] }` (line 85). fetchWalletNfts returns `{tokens: [], error}` rather than throwing (api.js:660-663), so the error is silently coerced to an empty inventory. Lines 120-123 then render, in red: "You don't hold any <collection> — you can't fill this slot." There is no retry and no distinction from a genuinely empty wallet.
survived.failure_scenario: A user holding 4 Jungle Bay NFTs clicks 'Accept this trade' on a board post asking for 'any Jungle Bay'. The Alchemy call 429s. The modal tells them, in error red, that they don't hold any Jungle Bay and can't fill the slot. They close the modal believing they are ineligible for a trade they can in fact settle, and the post may be filled by someone else.
survived.suggested_fix: Propagate the error field and render a 'couldn't read your inventory — retry' state instead of the eligibility verdict.

verdicts.reasoning:
I opened every file in the chain and the claim reproduces exactly.

1. TradesPanel.jsx:83-85 — confirmed verbatim. `out[contract] = res?.tokens || []` on line 84; `catch { out[contract] = []; }` on line 85. The `error` field of the response is never read anywhere in the component (grepped the file).

2. api.js:648-664 — confirmed. `fetchWalletNfts` swallows the throw and RETURNS `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "..." }`. So the empty-inventory path is reached by normal return, not by the catch. The claim's causal chain is right.

3. TradesPanel.jsx:120-123 — confirmed. `tokens.length === 0` renders the sentence "You don't hold any {c?.name || "tokens from this collection"} — you can't fill this slot." styled `color: "var(--red)"`. Grepped the string repo-wide: single occurrence, no hedge, no error branch, no "try again" affordance anywhere in the modal.

4. Reachability — confirmed, not hypothetical. `OpenTradeAccept` is rendered unconditionally at line 698-706 whenever `acceptTarget` is set, and `setAcceptTarget(t)` is wired to the plain "Accept this trade" button at line 622-624 on every board post the viewer does not own. No feature flag gates this path.

I actively tried to refute on four fronts and each attempt failed:
- Does fetchWalletNfts throw, making the catch the real path and the error envelope irrelevant? No — api.js:660 catches internally and returns the envelope. Confirms rather than refutes.
- Is there retry that makes this self-healing? Partially — alchemyGet wraps in withRetry maxRetries:2 (api.js:66-70). This refutes the claim's literal "no retry" wording but not its substance: after exhaustion the user still gets the false sentence with no error state. Corrected in the correction field.
- Is the error surfaced elsewhere in the modal, making the red text non-authoritative? No — nothing in OpenTradeAccept reads `res.error`; `loading` flips false unconditionally at line 87 regardless of outcome.
- Could a user proceed anyway, making it cosmetic? No — allPicked (line 94) is false and Confirm is disabled (line 160), so they are genuinely blocked.

The one place the finding overstates is severity. This is fail-closed: no transaction is built with bad data, nothing is signed, no money moves. The damage is a false assertion about the user's own holdings plus a lost trade opportunity, and it clears on remount. That is medium, not high.

The strongest evidence the finding is legitimate rather than a false positive: PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 guards this exact envelope with a comment citing a prior finding ID (F724) and the phrase "instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim". The project already ruled this pattern a defect and fixed it in a sibling component; TradesPanel is an unswept instance of the same bug.

verdicts.correction:
Finding is REAL and reproducible, with two corrections: (a) the laundering point is TradesPanel.jsx:84 `out[contract] = res?.tokens || []`, not the catch on :85 — fetchWalletNfts (api.js:648-663) returns `{tokens: [], error}` and never throws on API failure, so that catch is effectively dead code; the finding names it as if it were load-bearing. (b) Severity is medium, not high.

Verified chain: lib/proxy.js:144-147 throws ApiError on any non-ok response (429/5xx) -> api.js:66-69 retries at most 3 attempts -> api.js:660-663 swallows and returns `{tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs…"}` -> TradesPanel.jsx:84 discards `res.error` (it is referenced nowhere in the file) -> TradesPanel.jsx:114/120-123 renders in var(--red): "You don't hold any <collection> — you can't fill this slot."

The maintainer defense that this is intentional fail-closed design holds for the BEHAVIOUR but not the COPY. Refusing to offer unverifiable tokens is correct, and the Confirm button is gated on `allPicked` (:94, :160) so no transaction is ever built or signed — no funds at risk. But the string is a positive factual assertion about the contents of the user's own wallet, emitted by a read that failed. The "implicit retry on reopen" defense (effect deps [trade.id, wallet], modal unmounts on close) is self-defeating: a user told a definitive fact about their own holdings has no reason to reopen.

"Intentional" is not available as a defense because the codebase already settled this exact question elsewhere. PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 carries the comment "fetchWalletNfts returns { tokens:[], error } on an API outage — surface the retryable error state instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim (F724)" and branches on `nftData.error && nftData.tokens.length === 0`. TradesPanel was simply never brought in line with the house rule.

Worse than stated in the report: the board list runs its OWN independent holdings read (TradesPanel.jsx:447-453, cached per-wallet behind holdingsWalletRef), so the normal failure shape is a card badged green "✓ You can fill this — you hold 4" (:613) sitting behind a modal that says in red that the user holds none. The app visibly contradicts itself about the same wallet.

Sibling instance any fix must cover: TradeWindow.jsx:146-149 launders identically (`res?.tokens || []` plus an equally dead `catch { return [] }`), surfacing as emptyText at :323 "No NFTs from the supported collections in your wallet" and :380 "…in that wallet" — same class, same false claim about a wallet.

Severity medium rather than high: the harm is a false denial plus an abandoned trade (opportunity cost — the board post can be filled by someone else), not loss of funds, a wrong transaction, or an unrecoverable state; it requires a transient upstream failure and self-heals on the next open. It is squarely the failed-read-laundering class the project has been closing, and the fix is the F724 one-liner: thread `res.error` through and render "Couldn't check your wallet right now — try again" with a retry, instead of the ownership denial.
verdicts.reasoning: Read TradesPanel.jsx:61-182 (OpenTradeAccept), :438-473 (board holdings read), :585-627 (accept button), api.js:648-663 (fetchWalletNfts), api.js:66-69 (withRetry), lib/proxy.js:142-159 (throws ApiError), PortfolioTracker.jsx:145-176 (the F724 precedent that surfaces the same error field), TradeWindow.jsx:138-155 + :323/:380 (sibling instance). Confirmed the error field is discarded at line 84 and that the red ownership denial is what a 429 produces. Downgraded to medium because the Confirm button is disabled with zero selections so no money path is reachable and the failure is transient/self-healing on reopen.

survived.title: 'All listings are priced at or above their trait floors' is rendered when the listings read returned nothing
survived.claim: Deals concludes there are no deals whenever `listings` is empty (line 562) and then, once `hasMore` is false, states as fact: 'No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors.' (line 768). An empty `listings` is exactly what an upstream outage produces and nothing distinguishes the two: fetchListings catches the OpenSea page-1 failure into `{raw: [], next: null}` (api.js:795-798) and the native-orderbook failure into `{orders: []}` (api.js:800-803), then returns `mergeListings(...)` which only ever emits `{ listings, source }` — it has no error field at all (api.js:773-783). Because fetchListings resolves rather than throwing, `useListings` computes `listingsError = data?.error ?? (error ? ... : null)` = null (useListings.js:33). And App.jsx does not pass `listingsError` to Deals in any case (App.jsx:723-739), though it does pass it to Listings (App.jsx:741-744).
survived.failure_scenario: The /api/opensea proxy is rate-limited and the native orderbook is unreachable. A user opens /nakamigos/deals. Token metadata loads fine, so the loading state clears. The tab reports 'No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors. Deals auto-refresh every 60 seconds.' — a positive verdict about the state of the market derived from zero market data. A trader uses this to conclude the collection is efficiently priced.
survived.suggested_fix: Give mergeListings/fetchListings a real error field when both upstreams fail, pass listingsError into Deals, and render an outage banner instead of the 'all listings are fairly priced' verdict.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link at the cited file:line. api.js:794-805 catches the OpenSea page-1 failure into {raw:[],next:null} and the native-orderbook failure into {orders:[]}; mergeListings (api.js:773-783) returns only {listings, source} with no error field, and its source ternary yields "opensea" even when BOTH arrays are empty. Because fetchListings resolves rather than throwing, useListings.js:33 computes listingsError = data?.error ?? (error ? ... : null) = null — the error channel is dead for this failure mode, not merely unrouted. App.jsx:723-739 passes Deals only tokens/listings/listingsLoading/stats/onPick/wallet/onConnect/addToast/onAddToCart/onRefresh/loadAll/hasMore — no listingsError; Deals.jsx:444-457 confirms the prop is not even accepted, and the file contains zero occurrences of "unavailable"/"temporarily"/listingsSource, so there is no honesty banner. Tokens come from a separate endpoint (useNfts.js:29 fetchTokens), so with tokens healthy, Deals.jsx:467 isInitialLoading clears; Deals.jsx:562 returns deals:[] on empty listings; the empty-state gate at Deals.jsx:747 is only (deals.length===0 && !listingsLoading); and with hasMore false (token pagination, useNfts.js:57, and Deals.jsx:484-486 calls loadAll on mount so it reliably reaches false) Deals.jsx:768 renders "No deals found right now. (1) Severity high -> medium: the harm is a false NEGATIVE (user is told there is nothing to buy), so it cannot route anyone into a bad transaction; it produces a wrong inference about market efficiency and silently suppresses the tab. verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Every cited line checks out and the maintainer defenses all fail against the code.

Verified chain (worktree scanner-rebase @ 67d01e6b):
- api.js:794-805 — both sources are individually .catch()'d to empty: OpenSea page 1 -> {raw: [], next: null} (795-798), native orderbook -> {orders: []} (800-803). fetchListings then RESOLVES via build() at 834/839.

- useListings.js:33 — listingsError = data?.error ?? (error ? ... : null). data.error is permanently undefined (nothing ever sets it — dead code), and react-query's error is null because fetchListings resolved. Result: null.
- App.jsx:723-739 — the Deals case passes tokens, listings, listingsLoading, stats, onPick, wallet, onConnect, addToast, onAddToCart, onRefresh, loadAll, hasMore. No listingsError. Only Listings gets it (App.jsx:744).
- Deals.jsx:467 — isInitialLoading = listingsLoading || tokens.length === 0. Tokens come from a different endpoint (useNfts) and load fine, and the listings query resolved, so this is false; the 12s slowLoad notice (468-473) clears.
- Deals.jsx:562 — empty `listings` short-circuits to { deals: [], allListedNfts: [] }.
- Deals.jsx:484-486 — Deals calls loadAll() on mount, so hasMore reaches false.
- Deals.jsx:747 -> 766-773 — with deals.length === 0, !listingsLoading, and !hasMore, it renders: "No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors. Deals auto-refresh every 60 seconds. Check back soon!"

- useEffect at Deals.jsx:628-634 re-asserts the verdict every 60s for the whole outage.

1. "Listings tab owns error surfacing" — /nakamigos/deals is independently reachable, AND listingsError is null in this scenario anyway, so threading the prop alone would fix nothing.
2. "hasMore guard protects it" — only delays it; loadAll() drives hasMore to false.
3. "slowLoad notice covers outages" — clears on resolve; a fast 429 resolves fast.
4. "listingsSource distinguishes" — no; mergeListings emits "opensea" for the both-empty case. Same fallthrough makes Listings.jsx:868 print "No active listings for {collection} right now." in the identical outage (same root cause, corroborating rather than mitigating).

Severity: downgrading high -> medium on CONSEQUENCE only, not validity. The false statement is a negative claim about shopping information; no funds move, no price is misquoted, no transaction is built, and it self-heals when upstream recovers. survived.title: A total listings outage renders as a confident, success-styled "No active listings right now"
survived.claim: When BOTH listing sources fail, fetchListings resolves with `{ listings: [], source: "opensea" }` and no error field, so the Listings tab tells the user there are no listings — in green success styling — instead of admitting the read failed. The honest branch is unreachable dead code.
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea proxy is rate-limited (429) or the /api/opensea function is cold/erroring, and the native orderbook read also fails. api.js:795-798 catches the OpenSea rejection and substitutes `{raw: [], next: null}`; lib/orderbook.js:98-102 already resolves (never rejects) with `{orders: [], count: 0, error: "..."}` and mapNativeListings drops that `error`. mergeListings (api.js:780-782) then hits the final ternary and labels the empty result `source: "opensea"`. useListings.js:33 computes `listingsError = data?.error ?? (error ? ... : null)` — `data.error` is undefined and react-query's `error` is null because the queryFn resolved — so listingsError is null. Listings.jsx:865-868 therefore takes the `listingsSource === "opensea"` branch and renders, on a green rgba(74,222,128) background: "No active listings for Nakamigos right now." Listings.jsx:999-1006 adds "No Listings Available / There are currently no active listings for Nakamigos. Check back soon." A buyer concludes the collection is empty and leaves; a seller with a live listing concludes their listing vanished. Because fetchListings can no longer reject, the `listingsError ? "Listing data ... temporarily unavailable"` branch at Listings.jsx:869-870 can essentially never render.
survived.suggested_fix: Have fetchListings propagate per-source failure (e.g. `{ listings, source, osFailed, nativeFailed }`) and make mergeListings return `source: null` when both inputs are empty AND at least one source errored. Gate the "No active listings" sentence on a successful read; otherwise render the existing "temporarily unavailable" copy.

(error ? msg : null): data.error does not exist and react-query's error is null because the queryFn resolved, so listingsError is null. components/Listings.jsx:852-868 therefore renders "No active listings for {collection.name} right now.", and Listings.jsx:996-1006 renders "No Listings Available / There are currently no active listings for {collection.name}. Check back soon." The listingsError branch at Listings.jsx:869-870 is gated behind listingsSource !== "opensea", but source is exactly "opensea" whenever the set is empty, so it is unreachable for any outage — confirming the dead-code claim. Two mis-statements in the finding, neither of which changes the verdict: (1) the styling claim is overstated — the banner at Listings.jsx:853-863 is a 4%-opacity green tint with var(--text-dim) text and a chart-down icon, and the actual green "LIVE — Real active listings" pill at Listings.jsx:839-848 is gated on hasRealListings and does NOT render; the LISTED stat card at Listings.jsx:650 also honestly shows an em-dash rather than 0. (2) The trigger is broader, not narrower, than claimed: it does not need BOTH sources to fail. The native orderbook legitimately returning zero orders (its normal state) plus an OpenSea-only 429 already produces source "opensea", listings [], no error — the same false sentence. verdicts.correction: Accurate version: fetchListings (frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:785-840) cannot surface a read failure. Both source catches (api.js:795-798 for OpenSea, api.js:800-803 for the native orderbook) substitute empty results with no error marker, lib/orderbook.js:98-102 already returns a soft {orders: [], count: 0, error} whose `error` mapNativeListings (api.js:719-760) discards, and mergeListings (api.js:773-783) returns only {listings, source}, labelling the empty set source: "opensea" at api.js:780-781. Because the queryFn resolves, hooks/useListings.js:33 leaves listingsError null, so components/Listings.jsx:852-868 states "No active listings for {name} right now." and Listings.jsx:996-1006 states "No Listings Available … Check back soon." — factual denials produced by a broken upstream. Correction 1: the banner is not "success-styled"; it is a 4%-opacity green-tinted neutral banner with var(--text-dim) text and a chart-down icon (Listings.jsx:853-865), and the real green "LIVE — Real active listings" pill (Listings.jsx:839-848) is gated on hasRealListings and does not render; the LISTED stat card (Listings.jsx:650) correctly shows an em-dash, not 0. Correction 2: the trigger does not require a dual outage — an OpenSea-only failure while the native orderbook legitimately returns zero orders (its normal state) produces the identical false sentence, making this substantially more likely than stated. The honest branch at Listings.jsx:869-870 is dead for all outage cases because it is gated behind listingsSource !== "opensea" while an empty merge always labels itself "opensea". Severity: high.

verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED by reading the files. The chain reproduces exactly as described: api.js:795-798 substitutes `{raw: [], next: null}` for a rejected OpenSea page; lib/orderbook.js:98-102 resolves (never rejects) with `{orders: [], count: 0, error}` and mapNativeListings (api.js:719-765) drops that `error`; mergeListings (api.js:773-783) derives `source` purely from array lengths, so a substituted empty array is indistinguishable from a real empty page and gets labeled `source: "opensea"` with no `error` field. useListings.js:33 (`data?.error ?? (error ? ... : null)`) yields null because mergeListings sets no `error` and react-query's `error` is null (the queryFn resolved). Listings.jsx:867-868 then prints "No active listings for {collection} right now." and Listings.jsx:999-1006 prints "No Listings Available / There are currently no active listings ... Check back soon." The honest branch at Listings.jsx:869-870 requires `listingsSource !== "opensea"` AND truthy listingsError, so it is unreachable for any upstream outage (reachable only on an unexpected throw such as BigInt(priceWei) at api.js:689). No global degraded/offline banner exists anywhere in the surface (grepped lib/ and App.jsx). MAINTAINER DEFENSE EVALUATED AND REJECTED: (a) the per-source .catch() intent stated at api.js:792-793 ("one failing never blanks the other") justifies catching, but not discarding the failure fact — mergeListings has no vocabulary for "unknown"; (b) the "we already retried" defense (openseaGet withRetry maxRetries 3 / baseDelay 1500, api.js:80-82) covers blips only, and the resolve actively KILLS listingsQuery.retry:2 (queryConfig.js:26) plus react-query isError, so persistent outages (cold/500 /api/opensea function, missing key, un-allowlisted prod origin) render the false sentence permanently; (c) the "Browse on OpenSea" link (Listings.jsx:877-880, 1008-1016) is an out but does not correct the false factual claim.
verdicts.correction:
Two corrections to the finding, one narrowing and one widening.

1) PRECONDITION IS MIS-STATED, AND THE ACCURATE VERSION IS WORSE. The finding says "when BOTH listing sources fail." Accurate: OpenSea fails AND the native book contributes zero rows — which includes the perfectly ordinary case where the native orderbook is simply empty (its normal production state). Because `nativeListings.length > 0` is false in that state, api.js:780-782 collapses `source` to "opensea" for EVERY OpenSea outage. This is a single point of failure, not a double failure, so likelihood is materially higher than the finding implies.

2) STYLING IS OVERSTATED. The green "LIVE — Real active listings via {sourceLabel}" badge is Listings.jsx:839-848 and is gated on `hasRealListings` — it does NOT render in this state. What renders (Listings.jsx:855-865) is a 4%-opacity green tint with `color: var(--text-dim)` and a 📉 icon. "Success-styled" is too strong. Correct framing: the code selects the neutral/nothing-to-see-here variant instead of the blue informational-problem variant. The COPY is the defect, not the chrome.

3) ADJACENT ISSUE ON THE SAME PATH, NOT IN THE FINDING. If OpenSea fails while the native book IS non-empty, `source` becomes "native", `hasRealListings` is true, and Listings.jsx:847 DOES render the green "LIVE — Real active listings" badge — while `priceStats` (Listings.jsx:572-581), the LISTED count (Listings.jsx:650) and `listedPct` (Listings.jsx:624) are computed over the native subset alone. The user is shown a floor, median and listed-count presented as live market state with the OpenSea half silently missing and no disclosure. This is a quantitative claim the upstream does not back, and arguably more damaging than the empty-state copy.

ROOT CAUSE ANCHOR: the laundering originates at api.js:795-798 (rejection replaced by an empty page) and is cemented at api.js:780-782 (the `source` ternary cannot express "read failed"). useListings.js:33 is downstream and blameless — it has no error to read.

SEVERITY: high stands. Primary buy surface of the marketplace, high-likelihood trigger (the repo itself notes at api.js:79 that OpenSea 429s are common), permanent under a sustained outage, and it tells a buyer the collection is empty and a seller that their live listing vanished.

survived.title: "No offers received" is what a broken wallet-NFT read and a broken offers read both produce
survived.claim: fetchReceivedOffers discards the explicit `error` string that fetchWalletNfts returns on failure, and fetchTokenOffers swallows its own errors into `[]`. Either failure renders EmptyState "No offers received" with no error banner — the exact silent-revenue-loss outcome the code's own comment at lines 366-368 says it is guarding against.
survived.failure_scenario: Path A: the Alchemy proxy is down or rate-limited. api.js:660-663 returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs. Please check your connection and try again." }`. BidManager.jsx:359 destructures only `{ tokens: ownedNfts }`, throwing the error string away; lines 360-364 see length 0 and `setReceivedOffers([])` then `return` — note this returns BEFORE the catch block, so fetchError is never set. Line 653-654 renders EmptyState type="bidsReceived": "No offers received — When someone makes an offer on one of your NFTs it will appear here." Path B: the wallet NFTs load fine but OpenSea is throttled; api-offers.js:84-87 catches and returns `[]` for every token, so `results.flat()` is empty and nothing throws — same empty state, same absent banner. In both cases a holder sitting on a live 5 ETH offer is told nobody has bid, does not accept, and the offer expires. The 30s auto-refresh repaints the same false claim indefinitely.
survived.suggested_fix: Capture the `error` field from fetchWalletNfts and set fetchError instead of returning early with an empty list. Give fetchTokenOffers an out-of-band failure signal (e.g. return `{ offers, failed }` or let it reject and use Promise.allSettled) so BidManager can distinguish "zero offers" from "could not read offers" and show the banner it already has.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both paths from the actual files. Path A: api.js:660-663 returns {tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..."} on failure; BidManager.jsx:359 destructures only `{ tokens: ownedNfts }`, discarding `error`; :360-364 then setReceivedOffers([]) and early-return, so the catch at :391 that sets fetchError never runs, and fetchCurrentTab at :432 has already cleared fetchError to null. Render at :653-654 shows EmptyState type="bidsReceived", whose copy is confirmed at EmptyState.jsx:91-96 ("No offers received" / "When someone makes an offer on one of your NFTs it will appear here."). Path B: api-offers.js:84-87 catches and returns []; lib/proxy.js:89-97 confirms the proxy genuinely throws ApiError on network/timeout/non-2xx/non-JSON, and api-offers.js:62-64 retries 3x then rethrows, so a sustained 429 reliably lands in that catch. BidManager.jsx:376 awaits inside Promise.all so nothing rejects; results.flat() at :387 is empty; same EmptyState, no banner. The banner infrastructure exists and works (BidManager.jsx:562-566) and is used by fetchMyBids (:348) and fetchBidHistory (:416) — tab 1 is the only one of the three that fails silently, which confirms this is a gap rather than a deliberate design choice. The code's own comment at :366-369 explicitly names "see 'no offers received', and never accept it (silent revenue loss)" as the harm being guarded against.
verdicts.correction: Two corrections. (1) The finding understates Path B: the PARTIAL failure is worse than the total failure described. If 3 of a holder's 25 tokens hit a 429 while the rest succeed, api-offers.js:84-87 returns [] for just those three, the list at BidManager.jsx:656+ renders populated, and there is NO empty state and NO banner at all — the user sees a confident, complete-looking offer list silently missing offers, with zero signal anything was dropped. The all-empty case at least resembles a plausible "nobody bid." (2) Severity should be medium, not high: no funds are at risk, no wrong transaction is built or signed, the 30s tick (BidManager.jsx:447) self-heals as soon as upstream recovers, and Path A's empty state is ALSO the correct answer for the much more common case of a wallet holding zero NFTs in the collection — so the false claim only misleads an actual holder during an upstream-outage window overlapping a live offer. Fix is trivial: thread the `error` field through at :359 into setFetchError, and give the per-token fan-out at :372-381 a partial-failure count so a "some offers could not be loaded" banner renders alongside whatever did load.

verdicts.reasoning:
I took the maintainer's side first and tried four defenses. All four collapse against the file. DEFENSE 1 — "The empty state is the honest default; an offer book is a negative-space read. You can never prove 'no offers exist', only 'we found none', and every marketplace renders that as an empty state." COLLAPSES. The copy at EmptyState.jsx:91-96 is not "we found none" — it is `title: "No offers received"` plus `description: "When someone makes an offer on one of your NFTs it will appear here."` That second sentence is a forward-looking promise that the pipe is working. More damning: this component ALREADY has an error surface. BidManager.jsx:562-566 renders `
{fetchError}
`, and the two sibling fetchers set it — fetchMyBids at :348 ("Failed to load bids"), fetchBidHistory at :416, and fetchReceivedOffers' own catch at :393. The author's design intent is unambiguous: a failed read gets a banner. The Received-Offers path just never reaches it. DEFENSE 2 — "fetchTokenOffers returning `[]` per token is deliberate partial degradation. A holder with 100 NFTs shouldn't get a blank panel because one token 404s." HOLDS ONLY FOR PARTIAL FAILURE. The code cannot distinguish 1-of-100 failing from 100-of-100 failing — `results.flat()` is the same empty array either way, and because api-offers.js:75-87 never throws, the `Promise.all` at BidManager.jsx:374 never rejects and the catch at :391 never runs. Worse for the defense: openseaGet already wraps every call in `withRetry` (api-offers.js:60-62, maxRetries 3, exponential backoff, 429-aware via `err.retryAfter`). Transient single-token blips are already absorbed. What survives all three retries across all N tokens is precisely the systemic outage — the one case that must not be rendered as an answer. Counting failures and setting fetchError when the count equals N preserves 100% of the partial-degradation benefit and kills the false claim, so the two goals are not in tension. DEFENSE 3 — "fetchWalletNfts returns a graceful `{ tokens: [], error }` shape; callers who care check `error`." COLLAPSES, and it is self-refuting. The `error` field at api.js:662 exists for exactly one reason: so callers check it. A sibling component already does, with a comment naming this defect class by ID — PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167: "fetchWalletNfts returns { tokens:[], error } on an API outage — surface the retryable error state instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim (F724)", followed by `if (nftData.error && nftData.tokens.length === 0) { setError(...); return; }`. BidManager.jsx:359 destructures `const { tokens: ownedNfts } = await fetchWalletNfts(...)` and drops `error` on the floor. This is not an intentional divergence; it is an F724 migration that was applied to PortfolioTracker and never applied here. DEFENSE 4 — "It isn't silent, there's a console.warn." Not user-visible. api.js:661 and api-offers.js:85 both warn to console only. DEFENSE 5 (severity-only) — "Path A is mitigated: if only Alchemy is down, OfferPanel.jsx:25 still calls fetchTokenOffers per token, so the offer is visible on the NFT detail page." PARTIALLY HOLDS, FOR PATH A ONLY, AND DOES NOT LOWER SEVERITY. It requires the holder to click into each NFT individually — which is the exact task this tab exists to replace. It does nothing for Path B, where OpenSea itself is the failing dependency. And it makes the UX worse, not better: in Path A the user sees PortfolioTracker correctly say "Couldn't load this wallet's NFTs right now" while the Bids tab confidently says "No offers received" — two tabs, same outage, contradictory claims, and the confident one is the wrong one. VERIFIED MECHANICS, line by line: - BidManager.jsx:359 — `const { tokens: ownedNfts } = await fetchWalletNfts(...)`; `error` discarded. CONFIRMED. - BidManager.jsx:360-364 — `if (!ownedNfts || ownedNfts.length === 0) { setReceivedOffers([]); setLoadingReceived(false); return; }`. This `return` is inside the `try`, so it runs `finally` (:394-396) and skips the `catch` (:391-393). fetchError is never set. CONFIRMED exactly as the finding states. - api.js:662 — catch returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs. Please check your connection and try again." }`. CONFIRMED (finding cited 660-663; actual is 662 — immaterial). - api-offers.js:84-86 — catch `console.warn` then `return []`. CONFIRMED (finding cited 84-87 — immaterial). - BidManager.jsx:651-654 — `loadingReceived ? : receivedOffers.length === 0 ? : ...`. The ONLY discriminator is array length. CONFIRMED. - BidManager.jsx:17 + :445-449 — `REFRESH_INTERVAL = 30_000`, `setInterval(... if (!document.hidden) fetchCurrentTab(), REFRESH_INTERVAL)`. The 30s repaint claim is CONFIRMED. The finding is also mildly UNDER-stated in one respect worth adding: fetchCurrentTab at :431-432 begins with `setFetchError(null)` on every single tick. So even in a mixed session where the My-Bids tab had legitimately set a banner, switching to or refreshing Received Offers wipes it first. There is no path by which a banner and this empty state coexist. SEVERITY: "high" stands and I would not argue it down. This is a user-visible factual claim about money ("nobody has bid on your NFTs"), rendered from a read that failed, on a surface whose whole purpose is to trigger an Accept click, with zero error signal, repainting every 30 seconds, and with the correct fix already written and shipped in a sibling file. It is the same defect class as the four commits already on this branch (67d01e6b deployer, a4cc2ffa scanner, 67a67b32 price).
verdicts.correction:
The finding is accurate as written; only the line cites drift by 1-3 and one aggravating fact is missing. Accurate restatement:

TITLE: Received Offers renders "No offers received" from a wallet-NFT read that failed and from an offers read that failed — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty offer book.

FILES: frontend/src/nakamigos/components/BidManager.jsx:359 (primary), :360-364, :651-654; frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:648-663; frontend/src/nakamigos/api-offers.js:75-87; frontend/src/nakamigos/components/EmptyState.jsx:91-96.

PATH A (wallet-NFT read fails): api.js:662 returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..." }`. BidManager.jsx:359 destructures only `{ tokens: ownedNfts }` and discards `error`. Lines 360-364 then early-`return` from inside the `try`, bypassing the `catch` at :391-393, so `fetchError` is never set. Line 653 sees `receivedOffers.length === 0` and renders EmptyState "No offers received / When someone makes an offer on one of your NFTs it will appear here."

PATH B (offers read fails): api-offers.js:84-86 catches and returns `[]` per token, so `Promise.all` at :374 never rejects even when every token's fetch fails. `results.flat()` is empty, `catch` never runs, same empty state, same absent banner.

AGGRAVATOR NOT IN THE ORIGINAL: fetchCurrentTab at :431-432 calls `setFetchError(null)` on every invocation, including every 30s auto-refresh tick (:17, :445-449), so no stale banner can ever accompany the false empty state either.

PRECEDENT THAT SETTLES INTENT: PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 already implements the exact missing guard against the exact same API, with a comment citing the defect ID — "fetchWalletNfts returns { tokens:[], error } on an API outage — surface the retryable error state instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim (F724)". BidManager was never migrated. This is an incomplete fix, not a design choice.

USER HARM: a holder with a live offer is told nobody has bid, does not accept, and the offer expires. In Path A the app contradicts itself across tabs — PortfolioTracker correctly errors while Bids confidently claims no offers.

SHAPE OF THE FIX (not applied — read-only sweep): (1) capture `error` at :359 and, when `error && tokens.length === 0`, `setFetchError("Couldn't load your NFTs right now — offers may exist that aren't shown.")` and return without claiming emptiness; (2) have fetchTokenOffers signal failure to its caller (a sentinel or a thrown typed error) so BidManager can count failures and set fetchError when the failed count equals the token count — this preserves the intended partial-degradation behaviour for a 1-of-N failure while refusing to answer on a total failure.

ADJACENT, NOT AUDITED HERE: OfferPanel.jsx:25 consumes the same swallowing fetchTokenOffers and may launder it the same way; worth a separate look.

SEVERITY: high — unchanged.

survived.title: A failed OpenSea offers fetch renders as the factual claim "No trait offers"
survived.claim: fetchCollectionOffers swallows every error and returns [], so React Query never sees a failure. TraitBidPanel reads only isLoading (never isError), derives {} from the empty array, and falls through to EmptyState type="traitOffers" whose copy is "No trait offers / Trait-based offers will appear here."
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea's offers endpoint 429s (the app already retries 429s explicitly, so this is a known-frequent state) or the /api/opensea proxy is down. User opens Traits, clicks 'Gold Chain', and the TRAIT OFFERS panel states 'No trait offers'. In reality there is a standing 0.06 WETH trait bid. The user, believing there is no bid, either lists into a worse price or places a redundant undercutting offer.
