survived.title: Live OpenSea events are timestamped 1970 — event_timestamp (seconds) parsed as milliseconds
survived.claim: normalizeRestEvent does `new Date(event.event_timestamp).getTime()`. api.js:360-365 parses the SAME field from the SAME endpoint (`events/collection/{slug}` via the same proxy) and documents it: "OpenSea v2 returns Unix seconds (int)", converting with `ts * 1000`. Passing an integer like 1785000000 to new Date() is interpreted as milliseconds, yielding 1970-01-21.
survived.failure_scenario: A Nakamigos listing/sale/bid arrives on the 15s OpenSea poll. It flows useOpenSeaStream -> useCollection.allOpenSeaEvents -> useActivityWebSocket -> mergeEventStreams -> ActivityFeed. formatTimeAgo(1785000000) takes the >1-year branch and renders the literal date 'Jan 21, 1970' in the time column. Because the feed sorts newest-first (ActivityFeed.jsx:128), every live OpenSea event sinks below every other row and is cut off by the 100-row render cap — so the freshest marketplace data in the app is both mislabelled and effectively invisible. The same mis-parse at line 187-191 sets cursorRef to ~1785000 seconds, defeating the `after=` incremental-fetch optimisation.
survived.suggested_fix: Reuse api.js's parser: `const ts = Number(event.event_timestamp); timeMs = Number.isFinite(ts) ? ts * 1000 : Date.parse(event.event_timestamp) || Date.now();`. Same fix needed at useOpenSeaStream.js:187-191 for the cursor, and check lib/eventFeed.js:107-109 (Stream-SDK path) for the same shape.

verdicts.correction:
Accurate on the core defect; two sub-claims need trimming, and the severity is one notch high.

CONFIRMED — the mis-parse (frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useOpenSeaStream.js:108-112):
    time: event.event_timestamp
      ? new Date(event.event_timestamp).getTime()
      : ...
Same endpoint, same field, same proxy as api.js:363-365, which handles the int form defensively:
    const ts = Number(event.event_timestamp);
    timeMs = Number.isFinite(ts) ? ts * 1000 : Date.parse(event.event_timestamp) || Date.now();
with the comment at api.js:360 "OpenSea v2 returns Unix seconds (int) or occasionally ISO string". I confirmed the proxy does not transform the field: frontend/api/opensea.js sanitizeOpenseaResponse() (lines 64-79) only nulls URL fields and validates `price`; `event_timestamp` passes through raw, and the payload is returned verbatim at line 311. So both consumers see the identical value. `new Date(1785000000).getTime()` = 1785000000 ms = 1970-01-21. api.js is correct under BOTH wire formats; useOpenSeaStream is correct only under the ISO form — so it is the fragile one regardless of which format OpenSea actually emits.

CONFIRMED — the reach. All three collections have an openseaSlug (constants.js:33, 54, 70), so the hook always polls. Chain verified end to end: useCollection.js:30-42 -> useActivityWebSocket.js:212-216 (mergeEventStreams, sorts by time desc) -> useCollection.js:121-123 (sorts desc, cap 500) -> App.jsx:818 -> ActivityFeed.jsx:128 (sorts desc) and Header.jsx:60. Two user-visible surfaces, not one — the finding missed the Header ticker, which rotates every 4s across the same merged array on EVERY nakamigos tab and renders `${Math.floor(diff/86400)}d` (Header.jsx:66-72), i.e. a live listing shows as "20591d". That widens the blast radius beyond the activity tab.

CONFIRMED — cursor. useOpenSeaStream.js:189-191 computes Math.floor(new Date(1785000000).getTime()/1000) = ~1785000, sent as `after=1785000` (line 166). Harmless but a permanent no-op: the incremental-fetch optimisation never engages and every poll re-fetches the full 50.

OVERSTATED — "effectively invisible, cut off by the 100-row render cap". The cap is real (ActivityFeed.jsx:178-180, RENDER_CHUNK = 100) but it only bites once the merged list exceeds 100 rows. fetchActivity pulls limit 50; at low volume the 1970 rows DO render, at the bottom of the feed, literally labelled "Jan 21, 1970". So the guaranteed harm is mislabelling + wrong sort position; disappearance is the high-volume case only. Say "sinks to the bottom, and drops off entirely once the feed exceeds 100 rows".

OVERSTATED — implied uniqueness of the expression. eventFeed.js:107-108 has the byte-identical expression, but that one is CORRECT: it normalizes the @opensea/stream-js SDK payload, where event_timestamp is an ISO string. A fix must be scoped to the REST normalizer only; blind-patching both would break the Stream path.

WORTH ADDING (adjacent, same function): useOpenSeaStream.js:96-98 does `event.order_hash ?? event.transaction?.hash`, but OpenSea v2 returns `transaction` as a plain string hash — api.js:385 treats it as one (`hash: event.transaction`). So `.hash` on a string yields undefined and the hash collapses to the synthetic `os-rest-{type}-{id}-{ts}`. That key never matches api.js's, so ActivityFeed's dedup (lines 136-145) cannot collapse them: the 1970-stamped sale appears as an EXTRA row alongside the correctly-dated one rather than replacing it. Net user-visible state: the same sale listed twice, once "3m ago", once "Jan 21, 1970".

SEVERITY: medium, not high. It is confidently-wrong rendered data on the marketplace's flagship live feed plus the sitewide ticker, and it silently demotes live OpenSea events out of "newest first" — real and worth fixing. But no money path is touched, prices/addresses/token ids are unaffected, the correctly-timestamped sale data from the api.js path still renders, and a 1970 date is self-evidently broken rather than deceptive — no user acts on it believing it. It fails the "a broken upstream produces the same sentence" test for failed-read laundering: this is a live-read succeeding and being formatted wrong, not a failed read laundered into an answer.
verdicts.reasoning: Read useOpenSeaStream.js in full: line 108-112 does `new Date(event.event_timestamp).getTime()` with no Number()/seconds handling, while api.js:363-365 parses the same field from the same `events/collection/{slug}` path with `ts * 1000` and documents it as Unix seconds. Read frontend/api/opensea.js to rule out proxy-side normalization — sanitizeOpenseaResponse touches only URL fields and `price`, so the raw int reaches both consumers. Traced the render chain file by file (useCollection.js:30-42, 121-123; useActivityWebSocket.js:212-216; ActivityFeed.jsx:128, 178-180, 438; Header.jsx:60, 66-72) and confirmed all three collections carry an openseaSlug so the hook actually polls. The only refutation avenue was the wire format, and it fails both ways: api.js's form is correct whether the field is an int or an ISO string, while useOpenSeaStream's is correct only for ISO — and the repo's own comment plus the v2 `after=` seconds convention used at api.js:397 say int. Trimmed two overstated sub-claims (the 100-row cap is conditional; eventFeed.js:107 has the same expression but is correct for the Stream SDK), added the missed Header ticker surface and the adjacent `event.transaction?.hash` bug that turns these into duplicate rows rather than replacements, and downgraded high to medium since nothing about money, price, or a safety claim is affected.

CONFIRMED. The maintainer defense was constructed and it fails on three independent checks.

Defense 1 ("normalizeRestEvent deliberately handles both Stream-SDK ISO strings and REST shapes, so new Date() is correct") collapses on the call graph. normalizeRestEvent has exactly ONE caller: useOpenSeaStream.js:196 inside poll(), over data.asset_events from the REST proxy. The Stream-SDK normalizer is a separate function, normalizeOpenSeaEvent at lib/eventFeed.js:74, whose new Date(payload.event_timestamp) at 107-108 IS correct for ISO input — and `grep -rn "normalizeOpenSeaEvent" frontend/src` returns only its own definition, zero importers. It is dead code. There is no ISO-string caller anywhere in the app; the docblock at 59-63 describes an architecture replaced by REST polling.

Defense 2 ("the *1000 in api.js is the outlier; the field is polymorphic") collapses on the URL. frontend/api/opensea.js:244 hardcodes https://api.opensea.io/api/v2/${path}. api.js:402 and useOpenSeaStream.js:163 request the IDENTICAL path (events/collection/{slug}) through the IDENTICAL proxy, which is a pure pass-through (res.status(200).json(data) at line 311) — nothing transforms the field. The hook itself concedes the time domain is seconds: line 189 divides by 1000 to build `after`, and api.js:397 sets `after` to Math.floor(Date.now()/1000).

Defense 3 ("cosmetic") is where the finding is slightly overstated, corrected below.

Reproduced numerically with node: new Date(1785000000).getTime() = 1785000000 -> 1970-01-21T15:50:00.000Z; cursor = 1785000. ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47: diff ~1.78e9 s exceeds the 31536000 branch, so line 45-46 renders toLocaleDateString -> "Jan 21, 1970". Exactly as claimed.

Precondition (latency): frontend/api/opensea.js:250 attaches x-api-key only `if (OPENSEA_KEY)`. Without it v2 401s, poll() throws, isConnected goes false, zero live events, bug latent. But that same proxy is the primary source for the whole activity feed (api.js fetchOpenSeaActivity), so if activity data works at all, this fires on every live event.

Not verified from a live response: no test covers normalizeRestEvent and there is no captured OpenSea fixture in the repo. The "v2 emits int seconds" step rests on the in-repo comment at api.js:360, the seconds-valued `after` params, and the hardcoded /api/v2/ URL.
verdicts.correction:
Severity high HOLDS, but three corrections to the stated scenario:

1. OVERSTATED: "cut off by the 100-row render cap — effectively invisible." This is conditional, not automatic. Default feed is ~50 fetched sales (ActivityFeed.jsx:91, limit:50) plus a few live rows; RENDER_CHUNK is 100 (ActivityFeed.jsx:178). Under 100 total rows the 1970 events DO render — pinned to the very bottom below every real event, which is arguably worse than hidden because they read as ancient history. The binding cull is upstream of the render cap: mergeEventStreams(openSeaEvents, alchemyEvents, 200) at useActivityWebSocket.js:212 sorts newest-first and slices to 200, while the OpenSea reducer accumulates up to 100 PER CATEGORY across four categories (useOpenSeaStream.js:33) = up to 400. On a long session the 1970-stamped OpenSea events are the first thing that 200-cap discards, so genuine marketplace events are culled in favour of older Alchemy transfers.

2. MISSED SURFACE: Header.jsx:66-73's formatTimeAgo has no >1-year branch, so the same events render in the header ticker as "20670d".

3. SUB-CLAIM DOWNGRADE: the cursor defect at 189-191 is real (after=1785000 is Jan 1970, so the incremental filter never narrows and every poll refetches the full window) but it FAILS SAFE — a too-small `after` returns everything, dedup suppresses it, user sees nothing wrong. Wasted bandwidth, not a user-facing defect. Should not carry weight in the severity.

FIX WARNING: do not blanket-apply `* 1000` — lib/eventFeed.js:107-108 is correct for its own (ISO) input and must not be "fixed" the same way. The right fix mirrors api.js:363-365 (Number() the field, multiply by 1000 when finite, else Date.parse) at useOpenSeaStream.js:108-112, and drops the /1000 at 189-191.

survived.title: Failed Alchemy read locks real holders out of chat with "Own a Nakamigos to post" — and caches the false 0 for 5 minutes
survived.claim: The chat composer is gated on `holderTier` (CommunityChat.jsx:885/925). `holderTier` comes from useHolderStatus, which calls `fetchWalletNfts` (api.js:648). That function NEVER throws — its own catch at api.js:660-663 returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..." }`. So useHolderStatus's `catch` block (lines 93-99, the branch written to fall back to cache) is dead code, and the success path runs instead: `const c = data.totalCount || 0` (line 86) → `setTier(getHolderTier(0))` = null. Worse, lines 91-92 then WRITE that fabricated 0 to localStorage under `holder_cache_<contract>` with a 5-minute TTL. The `error` field returned by fetchWalletNfts is discarded and never reaches the UI.
survived.failure_scenario: Wallet 0xABC holds 12 Nakamigos. The /api/alchemy proxy returns 429 or 500 (or the user is briefly offline) while the chat tab mounts. `withRetry` exhausts 2 retries, alchemyGet throws, fetchWalletNfts swallows it and returns totalCount:0. The user is shown a gold "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE" pill and the sentence "Own a Nakamigos to post" (CommunityChat.jsx:931-932), and the textarea + Send button are removed entirely. The fabricated count:0 is persisted to localStorage, so reloading the page repeats the same false denial for 5 minutes even after the API recovers. Nothing anywhere tells the user a read failed.
survived.suggested_fix: Have fetchWalletNfts propagate failure distinguishably (return null, or keep the `error` field and check it in useHolderStatus). In useHolderStatus, do not call setTier/setCount and do NOT write the cache when `data.error` is present; expose an `error` flag so CommunityChat can render "Couldn't verify your holdings — retry" instead of a claim about ownership.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — every link in the chain reproduces from the files, and I could not find a refuting path.

1) `fetchWalletNfts` never throws. api.js:648-664: the whole body (including the `.map(normalizeToken)`) is inside `try`, and the `catch` at 660-663 returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..." }`. Nothing rethrows.

2) The retry wrapper does throw upward into that catch, so the catch is genuinely reachable: `alchemyGet` (api.js:66-70) = `withRetry(..., { maxRetries: 2 })`; `withRetry` (api.js:23-50) breaks out of the loop and rethrows `lastError` on 429/5xx/network after exhausting attempts, and breaks immediately on non-retryable 4xx.

3) `useHolderStatus`'s own catch is dead. useHolderStatus.jsx:82-99 — the only await in the `try` is `fetchWalletNfts`, which cannot reject; `setCount`/`setTier` don't throw; `saveCache` (lines 19-24) has its own internal try/catch. So the cache-fallback branch at 96-99 is unreachable and the success path always runs.

4) The fabricated 0 is produced and persisted. Line 86 `const c = data.totalCount || 0` → line 88 `setTier(getHolderTier(c))` → `getHolderTier(0)` returns `null` (line 30). Lines 91-92 then write `{ count: 0, ts: Date.now() }` to `localStorage["holder_cache_<contract>"]`, and line 72 honors it for `CACHE_TTL = 5 * 60 * 1000` (line 10).

5) The error field is discarded. Line 83-86 reads only `data.totalCount`; the hook returns `{ tier, count, loading }` (line 107). No error surface exists.

6) The UI consequence is exactly as described. App.jsx:396 `const { tier: holderTier, count: holderCount } = useHolderStatus(wallet, collection.contract)` → App.jsx:781 passes `holderTier` into `<CommunityChat>`. CommunityChat.jsx:885 renders the textarea + Send only when `wallet && holderTier`; :925-933 renders the gold "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE" pill and "Own a {collection.name} to post" when `wallet && !holderTier`. The composer is removed entirely. The gate is client-side only (`handleSend` at :526-559 does no holder check), so this is purely a false denial, not a mirror of a server rule. `HolderBadge` also disappears (useHolderStatus.jsx:115 `if (!tier) return null`).

Two corrections, both making it worse, not better:
- The persistence is understated. `check` only re-runs on `[address, check]`, and `check` is memoized on `[contract]` (lines 103, 105). There is no polling and no retry. So without a reload the false `tier: null` persists INDEFINITELY — until the user switches wallet or collection. The 5-minute TTL only bounds the reload path; it is a floor on recovery, not a cap on the damage.
- `loading` is computed (line 101) and returned (line 107) but App.jsx:396 destructures only `tier` and `count`, and CommunityChat never receives it. So on every fresh mount with a connected wallet and no warm cache, a genuine holder is shown "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE / Own a Nakamigos to post" during the normal in-flight window too — the same false sentence appears in the happy path, not only on failure.

Minor wording nits that do not affect validity: the copy is `Own a {collection.name} to post`, so the literal "Nakamigos" only appears for the default collection; and `maxRetries: 2` means 3 attempts, not "2 retries" after a first try (the finding's phrasing is ambiguous but not wrong in substance).

Severity: I'd downgrade high → medium. The technical claim is fully accurate and it is a textbook instance of the failed-read-laundering class this project has been closing (a failed read rendered as a factual assertion about the user's wallet, then cached). But the blast radius is access to a chat composer — no funds, no transaction, no irreversible action, and no misinformation about a token that a third party could trade on. What pulls it up from low is that it states something false about the USER ("Own a Nakamigos to post" to someone holding 12), surfaces no error at all, and — per the correction above — does not self-heal without a reload. Medium is the honest placement; the same pattern in `useProAccess` (hooks/useProAccess.jsx:29-37, identical `data?.totalCount || 0` over a never-throwing read) is currently inert only because `PRO_PASS_LIVE` is false.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written, with two amplifying corrections. (a) The false state is NOT bounded at 5 minutes in the live session: useHolderStatus.jsx:103/105 memoize `check` on `[contract]` and run it only on `[address, check]`, so there is no re-fetch or polling — the fabricated `tier: null` persists until the user changes wallet or collection. The 5-minute localStorage TTL (line 10, written at 91-92) only bounds the reload path. (b) The hook computes `loading` (line 101) and returns it (line 107), but App.jsx:396 destructures only `{ tier, count }` and never forwards it to CommunityChat, so the same "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE / Own a {collection.name} to post" denial (CommunityChat.jsx:925-933) also flashes during the normal in-flight window on every cold mount, not just on API failure. Also note the identical never-throwing-read pattern at hooks/useProAccess.jsx:29-37, currently inert only because PRO_PASS_LIVE is false. Severity medium rather than high: real false denial with no error surfaced, but scoped to chat posting — no funds, transaction, or irreversible action.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every mechanical claim reproduces against the files. fetchWalletNfts (frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:648-664) has its own catch returning {tokens:[], totalCount:0, error:"Could not load wallet NFTs..."} and therefore cannot reject, so useHolderStatus's catch (hooks/useHolderStatus.jsx:93-99) is unreachable from that call and the success path runs on an outage: line 86 `const c = data.totalCount || 0` -> setTier(getHolderTier(0)) -> null. Lines 91-92 then persist the fabricated {count:0} under holder_cache_<contract>, and the cache-hit early return at lines 71-76 skips any re-fetch, so the false denial survives reloads for the 5-minute TTL (line 10) and also clobbers a previously-good but expired count. `data.error` is never read by the hook. Downstream: App.jsx:396 -> App.jsx:781 -> CommunityChat.jsx:885/925, where !holderTier renders the gold "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE" pill plus "Own a {collection} to post" (lines 931-932) and removes the textarea and Send button entirely. withRetry via alchemyGet uses maxRetries:2 as stated (api.js:66-70).

The maintainer defenses do not survive. (a) "The catch handles it" is dead code, proven above. (b) "House convention" is refuted by our own code: PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 reads exactly this error field with a comment citing F724 -- "surface the retryable error state instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim" -- so the convention is the opposite. (c) "Fail closed for an entitlement gate" collapses because there is no server-side holdership enforcement anywhere: sendMessage (lib/supabase.js:191) routes through the SIWE proxy which only binds author to the JWT wallet, and no holder check exists in frontend/api/** or RLS. The gate is cosmetic, so failing closed protects nothing and only denies real holders. Even as a gate, "Own a Nakamigos to post" is a factual claim about the user's wallet rather than a verification-failure message. (d) The cache is not merely a perf measure -- it is what upgrades a transient 429 into 5 minutes of persistent false denial.

Two refinements to the report. First, it understates the blast radius: App.jsx:396 destructures only {tier, count} and discards `loading`, so holderTier is null during every normal in-flight read too -- a genuine holder sees "Own a {collection} to post" on every cold mount before the read resolves, not only on failure. Second, the cache overwrite only bites when the prior entry has already expired, since a fresh valid entry short-circuits the fetch at lines 71-76. A sibling instance of the same pattern exists at hooks/useProAccess.jsx:29-31 (`data?.totalCount || 0`), currently inert because PRO_PASS_LIVE is false.

Severity: downgrade high -> medium. The defect is real and is squarely the failed-read-laundering class, but no funds are at risk, nothing is irreversible, the gate is not a security boundary, and the state self-heals within 5 minutes without user action. It is a user-visible false factual statement about the user's own wallet produced by a broken upstream, which warrants a fix (thread data.error/loading into a "couldn't verify, retry" state and never cache a failed read), but not a high rating.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed as written, with two refinements. (1) Broader than reported: App.jsx:396 discards the hook's `loading` flag, so holderTier is null during every normal in-flight read -- real holders see "Own a {collection} to post" briefly on every cold mount, not only during an API failure. (2) The localStorage clobber of a good value only occurs when the prior cache entry has already expired; a fresh entry short-circuits the fetch at useHolderStatus.jsx:71-76. Also note the gate is purely cosmetic -- no server-side holdership check exists (sendMessage at lib/supabase.js:191 only binds author to the JWT wallet), so "fail closed" buys no protection. Same pattern sits inert at hooks/useProAccess.jsx:29-31 behind PRO_PASS_LIVE=false. Severity high -> medium: transient, self-healing, no funds or irreversible action.

survived.title: NftCompare's SEND TRADE always dead-ends — collection tokens never carry an owner
survived.claim: The 'THEIR NFT' panel searches `tokens` (App.jsx:761 passes `nfts.allTokens`), and every token from that source has `owner: null` — api.js:145 sets `owner` solely from `nft.owners`, and the only request made (api.js:151-163, `getNFTsForContract` with contractAddress/withMetadata/limit/startToken) never asks for and does not return per-token owner data. Nothing enriches it afterwards. So `theirNft.owner` is falsy for every token the right-hand search can return, and handleSendTrade aborts at line 248 before building anything.
survived.failure_scenario: A holder connects, picks one of their own NFTs on the left (that one DOES have an owner — fetchWalletNfts sets `owner: walletAddress` at api.js:651), searches '7762' on the right, selects it, optionally types an ETH sweetener, and clicks SEND TRADE. The button is enabled (canSubmit at line 238 only requires wallet + both slots + !submitting), so it looks live. They get the toast 'Target NFT owner unknown — pick a token with a known holder'. There is no token in that search that has a known holder, so the instruction is unfollowable and the entire tab is a dead end. The 'Owner: 0x…' line at line 100-104 also never renders for the right panel, removing the only clue.
survived.suggested_fix: Resolve the counterparty before enabling the button: call Alchemy getOwnersForNFT (or reuse the holders read) when a right-panel token is selected, show the resolved owner in the slot, and keep SEND TRADE disabled until it resolves — so the failure is visible at selection time instead of after the user has composed a whole offer.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED from the files. Full chain reproduced:

1. App.jsx:761 passes `nfts.allTokens` as NftCompare's `tokens`.
2. useNfts.js:190 -> `allTokens: rankedTokens` = `computeRarity(tokens, ...)` (useNfts.js:148-151). computeRarity (api.js:848-889) spreads `...token` and only adds `rank`/`rarityScore` — it never introduces `owner`.
3. `tokens` come from fetchTokens (api.js:154-172), mapped through normalizeToken (api.js:164). The ONLY owner assignment for a collection token is api.js:145: `owner: Array.isArray(nft.owners) ? nft.owners[0] : null`.
4. The request is `getNFTsForContract` with contractAddress/withMetadata/limit/startToken (api.js:156-162) against the Alchemy NFT **v3** root (frontend/api/alchemy.js:22-24). The proxy is a pure pass-through (frontend/api/alchemy.js:342-357) — no enrichment. v3 getNFTsForContract carries no per-token owner data, and Alchemy's per-token owner endpoint (getOwnersForNFT) is not even in the proxy allowlist (frontend/api/alchemy.js:51-62), so no code path could add it.
5. The fallback branch is no better: FALLBACK_NFTS (constants.js:211-224) has no `owner` key at all.
6. Nothing patches allTokens afterwards. The deep-link fetch (App.jsx:373-391) writes to `setSelected`, not into allTokens. Repo-wide there are exactly two `owner:` assignments in nakamigos/api.js (lines 145 and 651).
7. NftCompare.jsx:230-236: `theirResults` filters the `tokens` prop directly, and `theirNft` can only be set from those results (NftCompare.jsx:402). `onPick` is destructured at line 163 and never used, so there is no other way in.
8. canSubmit (NftCompare.jsx:238) and the button (line 380) ignore `owner`, so SEND TRADE renders fully enabled, then handleSendTrade hard-returns at line 248 with "Target NFT owner unknown — pick a token with a known holder". No token reachable by the right-hand search satisfies that instruction, so the tab's sole purpose is unreachable — and the header copy at line 311 ("Select your NFT, pick the one you want, and send a trade offer") describes behaviour the code does not have.

CORRECTIONS to the finding (they make it worse, not weaker):
- "fetchWalletNfts sets `owner: walletAddress` at api.js:651" is WRONG. Line 651 is the `owner` REQUEST parameter passed to Alchemy's getNFTsForOwner, not a field on the returned token. fetchWalletNfts returns `normalizeToken(nft, metadataBase)` at api.js:657 — the same line-145 rule — so the LEFT panel's tokens have `owner: null` too. Corroborated by two independent defensive fallbacks that would be pointless if Alchemy populated owners: MyCollection.jsx:69 (`owner: nft.owner || wallet`) and Listings.jsx:328 (`token?.owner || listing.maker`). Consequence: the "Owner: 0x..." line at NftCompare.jsx:100-104 never renders on EITHER panel, not just the right one.
- Minor: the cited range "api.js:151-163" is off by a line or two — line 151 closes normalizeToken; fetchTokens is 154-172 with the params at 156-162.
- The NftCompare enrichment at lines 204-206 also does not add owner (it only merges rank/rarityScore/attributes).

Residual uncertainty: this rests on Alchemy NFT v3 getNFTsForContract not returning a populated `owners` array, which I could not exercise live from here. Everything in the repo corroborates it (no per-token owner endpoint allowlisted; two call sites defensively substitute a different address for a missing token.owner). Even in the "field present but null" case, `Array.isArray(null)` is false and owner is still null.

Severity high is correct: the primary action of a production-reachable tab is a guaranteed dead end behind an enabled-looking button, and the error text instructs the user to do something no state of the app permits.
verdicts.correction: Keep the finding at high. Fix two statements before publishing it: (1) api.js:651 is the `owner` QUERY PARAMETER sent to Alchemy's getNFTsForOwner, not a token field — fetchWalletNfts maps its results through the same normalizeToken (api.js:657), so the left-panel ("YOUR NFT") tokens also have `owner: null`. The accurate version of the scenario is that NEITHER panel ever shows the "Owner: 0x..." line (NftCompare.jsx:100-104), and yourNft.owner is simply never read by handleSendTrade — only theirNft.owner is (lines 248-249, 257) — so the dead-end conclusion is unchanged. Corroborating evidence for the null owner: MyCollection.jsx:69 (`owner: nft.owner || wallet`) and Listings.jsx:328 (`token?.owner || listing.maker`) both defensively substitute an address for a missing token.owner. (2) Cite the request block as api.js:154-172 (params at 156-162); line 151 is the close of normalizeToken. Also worth adding: the proxy allowlist at frontend/api/alchemy.js:51-62 does not include getOwnersForNFT, so no client code could obtain a per-token holder even if it tried, and the header copy at NftCompare.jsx:311 advertises the send flow as working.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. The maintainer's best defense — that NftCompare.jsx:248 is a deliberate fail-closed guard preventing a Seaport order from being signed against an unknown/fabricated counterparty, consistent with the anti-laundering discipline elsewhere in this repo — is correct in principle but does not hold, because the guard fires on 100% of possible inputs. The feature it protects has never worked.

Chain verified end to end: App.jsx:761 passes `nfts.allTokens` -> useNfts.js:190 `rankedTokens` -> computeRarity (api.js:856 spreads `...token`, preserving null) -> fetchTokens (api.js:154-172) -> normalizeToken. normalizeToken sets `owner: Array.isArray(nft.owners) ? nft.owners[0] : null` (api.js:145). The only request issued is getNFTsForContract with contractAddress/withMetadata/limit/startToken (api.js:156-162); the serverless proxy forwards query params verbatim and injects nothing (frontend/api/alchemy.js:162, 257-271). No owner data is requested or returned. useNfts exposes no setter, so nothing enriches allTokens afterward. The API-failure fallback (api.js:170 -> FALLBACK_NFTS, constants.js:212+) has no `owner` key either. NftCompare is mounted exactly once (App.jsx:761) and `trade` is an unconditionally reachable tab (constants.js:92).

Result: theirNft.owner is falsy for every token the right-hand search can return. canSubmit (line 238) only requires wallet + both slots + !submitting, so the gold SEND TRADE button renders fully enabled, and every click aborts at line 248 with "Target NFT owner unknown — pick a token with a known holder" — an instruction no token in that search can satisfy.

Corroborating: MyCollection.jsx:69 explicitly patches `owner: nft.owner || wallet` before handing a token onward, which only makes sense because normalizeToken never produces an owner.

The dead-end is structural, not merely guard-induced. Deleting line 248 does not help: trades.js:279-284 rejects a null/malformed taker, and the only taker-less mode (`open: true`) is rejected at trades.js:274-277 unless every `get` slot is a wildcard, while NftCompare always sends a specific tokenId (line 256). A real fix requires an ownerOf read (pattern already present at trades.js:509-513) or a manual counterparty input as TradeWindow.jsx:236-246 uses.

Severity high is appropriate and unchanged: an entire headline, production-reachable tab, advertised in its own copy ("Select your NFT, pick the one you want, and send a trade offer", line 311), is 100% non-functional while presenting an enabled primary CTA. No funds are at risk — the failure is honest and fail-closed — so this is a dead-control defect (category 3), not a failed-read-laundering defect.
verdicts.correction:
One sub-claim in the finding is factually wrong and should be corrected before the report ships. The finding states the left panel is unaffected because "fetchWalletNfts sets `owner: walletAddress` at api.js:651". It does not. api.js:651 is the `owner` QUERY PARAMETER passed to Alchemy's getNFTsForOwner, not a field assigned to a returned token. The response is mapped through normalizeToken at api.js:657, so left-panel (owned) tokens also carry `owner: null`.

This does not change the verdict or severity — handleSendTrade only inspects theirNft.owner (line 248), yourNft.owner is never read — but it broadens the cosmetic symptom: the "Owner: 0x…" line at NftCompare.jsx:100-104 never renders on EITHER panel, not just the right one, so `owner` is effectively a dead field across this entire surface (the same reason Modal.jsx:311 and Modal.jsx:553's owner-gated LIST button never fire for tokens sourced from allTokens).

Accurate title: "NftCompare's SEND TRADE always dead-ends — no token from the collection feed ever carries an owner (and neither does the wallet feed)."

survived.title: Floor-price alerts trigger on the hardcoded fallback floor when the stats API is down
survived.claim: `fetchFloor` accepts `stats.floor` on the sole test `stats.floor != null` and discards the `fallback` flag that came back with it. When both Alchemy and OpenSea fail, api.js:277 returns `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}` — floor 0.1048 for Nakamigos — so a total read failure is indistinguishable from a live quote. checkAlerts (line 119-168) then evaluates user thresholds against that constant and fires a browser notification.
survived.failure_scenario: A user sets 'Below 0.11 ETH'. The stats proxy goes down (rate limit, key expiry, outage). Within 30s the panel shows 'Nakamigos floor: 0.1048' in confident gold with the caption '(alerts trigger based on floor price)', the alert flips to TRIGGERED with a pulsing green glow, and a push notification says 'Floor price has dropped below 0.11 ETH (now 0.1048 ETH)'. Nothing happened on-chain; the number is a 2023-era constant in constants.js:227. Worse, the 5% re-arm hysteresis at line 136-138 keeps it latched, so the user acts on a fabricated floor break.
survived.suggested_fix: Skip the update when the payload is flagged: `if (!cancelled && stats.floor != null && !stats.fallback) setFloorPrice(stats.floor)`, and render 'Floor unavailable' rather than a stale value so alerts pause instead of firing on a constant.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every link in the chain reproduces from the files.

1. `frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:277` — in `_fetchCollectionStatsUncached`, after the Alchemy block throws AND the OpenSea `collections/{slug}/stats` retry throws, the function returns `{ ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }` for the default contract. (Line 278 handles non-default collections and honestly returns `floor: null`.)
2. `frontend/src/nakamigos/constants.js:226-231` — `FALLBACK_STATS = { floor: 0.1048, volume: 52200, owners: 5238, supply: 20000 }`. A hardcoded constant, not a read.
3. `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/PriceAlerts.jsx:66-72` — `fetchFloor` does `const stats = await fetchCollectionStats(...); if (!cancelled && stats.floor != null) setFloorPrice(stats.floor)`. The sole test is `!= null`. `stats.fallback` is never read anywhere in the file (grep for "fallback" in PriceAlerts.jsx returns exactly one hit, and it is a code comment on line 417 about the local engine instance). So a total read failure is stored identically to a live quote, and it OVERWRITES a previously-good floor.
4. `PriceAlerts.jsx:119-168` — `checkAlerts` evaluates `price = floorPrice` against `alert.targetPrice`, and on `shouldTrigger && !alert.triggered` builds `Floor price has dropped below ${targetPrice} ETH (now ${price} ETH)`, calls `sendLocalNotification(...)` when `Notification.permission === "granted"` (149-156) and `addToast(body, "success")` unconditionally (158-160).
5. `PriceAlerts.jsx:135-141` — the re-arm requires `pctAway >= 0.05`. Since the fallback floor is a fixed constant it never moves, so the alert stays latched TRIGGERED for the whole outage.
6. Render at `PriceAlerts.jsx:539-547` — shows `{collection.name} floor: {floorPrice.toFixed(4)}` in `var(--gold)` bold with `(alerts trigger based on floor price)`. No fallback/cached badge. And `:290-301` gives the latched row a green border + `pulseGlow` animation; `:653-655` renders the `TRIGGERED` badge.

The decisive evidence that this is a defect and not a deliberate design choice: `frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useCollection.js:75` already consumes exactly this signal — `setIsLive(!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback)` — with the comment at :14-16 saying the flag exists "so the UI can badge it 'cached' instead of presenting stale numbers as live (F582)". The same flag arrives at PriceAlerts.jsx:69 and is thrown away.

Refutation attempts that failed:
- "The alerts tab may be unreachable / the engine inert." No: `App.jsx:686` instantiates `usePriceAlerts(nfts.allTokens, addToast)` unconditionally at app level (active defaults true), and `App.jsx:779` passes it into `PriceAlertPanel`. This makes the finding BROADER than stated — the 30s poller and `checkAlerts` run app-wide, so the fabricated toast/notification fires from any Tradermigos tab, not only "alerts".
- "Needs an improbable double outage." Both `alchemyGet` and `openseaGet` route through the same origin's serverless functions (`lib/proxy.js:63` `/api/opensea`, `:117` `/api/alchemy`) and both throw `ApiError` on network error, non-2xx, or non-JSON (`:88,93,100,142,147,154`). One proxy-layer fault — offline, expired key, rate limit, missing origin allowlist, function-cap deploy miss — fails both at once. This is a single common-mode failure, not two independent ones.
- "Maybe first paint is honest." It is: `floorPrice` starts null and renders "Loading ... floor price..." (:544-546). The dishonesty only appears after a failed fetch, which is the point.

Two small corrections to the write-up, neither of which weakens it:
- The browser push notification requires the user to have previously granted permission (:149-152). The in-app toast at :158-160 fires unconditionally, so the false factual claim always reaches the user.
- Only the default Nakamigos collection is affected; other collections take `api.js:278` (floor null) and stay honest.

Severity: high is correct and I'd keep it. This is not a passive stale number — it is a proactive, latched push/toast asserting a specific price event ("dropped below 0.11 ETH (now 0.1048 ETH)") that did not occur on-chain, delivered app-wide, with the exact flag needed to suppress it already present in the payload and already consumed correctly two files over.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written, with three refinements. (a) Scope is wider than "tab alerts": the engine is instantiated app-wide at frontend/src/nakamigos/App.jsx:686 and passed to the panel at :779, so the false toast/notification fires from any Tradermigos tab, not only when the alerts tab is open. (b) The browser push notification additionally requires Notification.permission === "granted" (PriceAlerts.jsx:149-152); the in-app toast (PriceAlerts.jsx:158-160) fires unconditionally, so the false claim always reaches the user regardless. (c) Only the default Nakamigos collection is affected — api.js:278 returns floor: null for other collections, so they stay honest. The fix is one line: PriceAlerts.jsx:69 should gate on `!stats.fallback && stats.floor != null`, matching the pattern already used at hooks/useCollection.js:75.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at frontend/src/nakamigos/components/PriceAlerts.jsx:69. `fetchFloor` tests only `stats.floor != null` and discards the `fallback` flag that api.js:277 attaches to `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}`. constants.js:226 hardcodes floor 0.1048, so a total dual-provider read failure is indistinguishable from a live quote. That constant is rendered as a confident gold figure at PriceAlerts.jsx:541 with the caption at :542 and NO `CachedTag` (contrast Hero.jsx:105-127, which uses the same `stats.fallback` flag for exactly this disclosure, as do ActivityFeed.jsx:104 and MarketIntegrity.jsx:347). checkAlerts (119-168) then compares it to the user threshold and sendLocalNotification (:155) pushes "Floor price has dropped below X ETH (now 0.1048 ETH)" — a factual market claim manufactured by a failed read. This is the failed-read-laundering class.

Two aggravators beyond the report: the engine is instantiated app-wide at App.jsx:686 (not gated on the alerts tab), so it polls and notifies regardless of where the user is; and constants.js:227 carries the comment "do not use for volume comparisons or alerts" on the sibling `volume` field — the hazard was recognized for one field of the same object and missed for the adjacent one.

Two sub-claims are overstated and should be corrected before this is written up:
(1) The hysteresis at :135-138 does NOT keep the alert latched. The fallback floor is a constant, so `shouldTrigger` stays true and the notification fires exactly once (guarded by `!alert.triggered` at :144). On API recovery the alert re-arms normally provided the real floor is >=5% away from target. The residual is narrower: if the recovered real floor lands WITHIN 5% of the threshold, the false TRIGGERED badge and its pulsing green glow (styles :296-300) persist against a price that never crossed.
(2) Blast radius is the default collection only. api.js:278 returns `floor: null` for every other collection, which the `!= null` guard correctly rejects — those collections honestly stay on "Loading ... floor price..." (:545).

Severity downgraded high -> medium: no transaction is built or signed, no funds at risk, no slippage/fee surface; it requires simultaneous Alchemy + OpenSea failure; it is scoped to one collection; and it self-corrects on recovery in most cases. It remains a genuine fabricated factual claim delivered by push notification and warrants a fix.

Fix is one line: `if (!cancelled && stats.floor != null && !stats.fallback) setFloorPrice(stats.floor);` — the panel then falls through to its existing honest loading state instead of evaluating thresholds against a 2023-era constant.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: PriceAlerts.jsx:69 discards the `fallback` flag, so when both stats providers fail for the DEFAULT collection only, the hardcoded 0.1048 from constants.js:226 renders as a live floor (no "cached" badge, unlike Hero.jsx:127) and fires a one-shot browser notification asserting a floor crossing that did not occur. Non-default collections are unaffected (api.js:278 returns floor: null, correctly rejected). The 5% hysteresis at :135-138 does NOT latch the alert indefinitely — it re-arms once the real floor returns >=5% from the target; the residual is a false TRIGGERED badge that persists only when the recovered real floor sits within 5% of the threshold. Severity medium, not high: informational harm, no money path.

survived.title: LIVE badge is OR'd across two independent reads, so failed stats/activity render under 'Connected to live APIs'
survived.claim: `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` combines two unrelated signals. `isLive` from useCollection (useCollection.js:75) means stats AND activity both came back live; `nfts.isLive` (useNfts.js:40) means only the token list came back live. A single successful token fetch therefore lights the badge even when the stats and activity reads both fell back.
survived.failure_scenario: The Alchemy token endpoint is healthy but the stats + activity endpoints fail. `nfts.isLive` is true, so Header.jsx:580-586 renders the green LIVE pill with tooltip 'Connected to live APIs'. Immediately to its right the Ticker (Header.jsx:589) rotates through activities that are FALLBACK_ACTIVITY (api.js:554) — four hardcoded synthetic sales such as '#11007 sold for 0.11 ETH' — each next to a pulsing live-dot. Meanwhile Hero shows the hardcoded 0.1048 floor. The user is told the app is on live APIs while every market number on screen is a constant.
survived.suggested_fix: Show LIVE only when every feed backing the visible surface is live (`isLive && nfts.isLive`), or split the badge into per-feed indicators so a failed stats/activity read cannot be masked by a successful token read.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at source. `frontend/src/nakamigos/App.jsx:820` reads `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}`. The left operand comes from `useCollection()` destructured at App.jsx:338; `useCollection.js:75` sets it as `setIsLive(!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback)` — i.e. stats AND activity both live. The right operand is `useNfts.js:40` `setIsLive(!data.fallback)` — token list only. They are genuinely independent reads: tokens come from Alchemy `getNFTsForContract` (api.js:161), stats from a 4-way `Promise.all` of `getFloorPrice`/`getOwnersForContract`/`getContractMetadata`/native-orderbook with an OpenSea second try (api.js:215-278), activity from OpenSea events then Alchemy `getNFTSales` (api.js:529-558). A rate-limited or partially-failing proxy can easily satisfy the single token call while the 3-call stats fan-out and the activity chain both exhaust their fallbacks, so `false || true` lights the badge.

Downstream render confirmed: `Header.jsx:579-586` prints the green `LIVE` pill with `title="Connected to live APIs"` on that OR'd prop, and `Header.jsx:589` renders `<Ticker activities={activities}/>` immediately beside it from the same `activities` array. When activity falls back, that array is `FALLBACK_ACTIVITY` (api.js:554 -> constants.js:248-253) — four hardcoded synthetic sales. `Ticker` (Header.jsx:9-64) does NOT read the `sample: true` flag those entries carry; grep shows `.sample` is consumed nowhere in the app except `fallbackHonesty.test.js:32`. So the Ticker is the one surface with zero fallback disclosure, and it is fed exactly the fabricated data, under a badge asserting live APIs.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the scenario as written:
1. - meta state (:307) has fields for truncated/salesUnavailable/ownersUnavailable only — no listings field.
- Yellow "feed unavailable" banner at :423-428 covers sales and owners only.

I ran a verbatim replication of the function body plus the three metrics primitives. With 60 priced listings and no makers: `{measured:true, attributedListings:0, unattributedListings:60, distinctSellers:0, effectiveSellers:0, hhi:0, topSellerShare:0, top3SellerShare:0, band:'well-distributed'}`. WHAT THE FINDING MISSES (strengthens it): `computeMarketIntegrity` only records a floor coverage gap when `!floor.measured` (marketIntegrity.js:497). An all-unattributed floor is `measured: true`, so it contributes NO gap — with sales and owners healthy, `dataConfidence.level` is "high" (:513) and the page header renders a green "DATA HIGH" chip (MarketIntegrity.jsx:400) above the green "Well distributed" chip, over zero seller evidence. The band is computed over `attributed` only, with no minimum-evidence floor. 8 attributed listings from 8 distinct sellers out of a 100-listing floor gives top=0.125 / top3=0.375 -> green "Well distributed" describing a floor that is 92% unmeasured. The mirror case is a false RED: I reproduced 1 attributed listing of 60 -> topSellerShare 1.0, band 'concentrated'. Neither direction is guarded.

WHY I'D DOWNGRADE TO LOW (reachability):
- OpenSea path (frontend\src\nakamigos\api.js:684-707): `maker` and `tokenId` are BOTH derived from `listing.protocol_data.parameters` (:687 offer[0].identifierOrCriteria, :697 offerer), and :707 filters out any row with `tokenId == null`. A payload missing protocol_data is dropped before it can reach the analyzer as an unattributed listing. It would take a Seaport order carrying `offer[0]` but no `offerer` — not a shape OpenSea v2 produces.
- Native path (api.js:739-760): `maker: order.maker` comes straight from the orderbook rows, and frontend\api\orderbook.js:437 selects `*`. Rows carry maker.
So the "listings payload shape changes" premise is a latent/defensive gap, not a state a user can hit against today's two adapters. The finding's own scenario is honest about being conditional.

MITIGATIONS THAT ARE REAL BUT SUBORDINATE (the finding already notes the first): `bandReason` "No attributable sellers on the floor." (:400) and, at MarketIntegrity.jsx:294-296, "60 listing(s) had no readable seller and were left out of the seller count." plus the "DISTINCT SELLERS 0 across 0 listings" tile (:278). All of it is 10px `--text-muted` beneath a colored verdict chip, so the disclosure exists but loses to the badge.

ACCURATE ONE-LINE VERSION: `analyzeFloorConcentration` computes its band from the attributed subset with no minimum-evidence guard, so an empty or near-empty seller set yields the green "well-distributed" initializer and does not register as a data-confidence gap. CONFIRMED (traced end to end): analyzeFloorConcentration (marketIntegrity.js:343-419) keeps a listing on price alone (line 346) and excludes makerless rows from `attributed` (line 358). With zero attributed rows: bySeller empty -> shares = [] (line 388-390) -> computeHHI([]) = 0 (metrics.ts:35-39) -> effectiveHolders(0) = 0 (metrics.ts:46-49) -> topSellerShare = shares[0] ?? 0 = 0 (line 392) -> topNShare([],3) = 0 -> both thresholds at lines 396-397 fail -> band stays "well-distributed" (line 395) -> MarketIntegrity.jsx:268 maps it to { label: "Well distributed", color: "var(--green)" } and renders it as the Section headline chip (line 273). No NaN: the .map over an empty bySeller never divides by attributed.length = 0.

THE MAINTAINER-INTENT DEFENSE DOES NOT HOLD. The code is visibly gap-aware (comment at 356-359, `unattributedListings` field at 409, the distinctSellers===0 bandReason at 398-400, UI disclosure at MarketIntegrity.jsx:294-296, test at marketIntegrity.test.js:157-167) and the module does have a refusal mode (measured:false at line 348) - so one can argue "well-distributed" is a null hypothesis with the caveat printed. Three things kill that: (1) the green chip is the panel's headline verdict while the caveat is 10px --text-muted prose below six stat tiles - assert in the headline, disclose in the footnote is precisely the failed-read-laundering pattern; (2) the discontinuity - ONE attributed listing gives topSellerShare = 1.0 -> red "Concentrated", ZERO gives green "Well distributed"; nothing monotone in evidence produces that jump, so it is a missing coverage gate, not a designed default; (3) there is no honest rendering path in the component anyway - BAND_META (MarketIntegrity.jsx:8-12) has no "unknown" key and line 268 falls back to BAND_META.mixed (yellow), so an "unmeasured" band would render as a different false verdict. The fix must live in the lib.

MIS-STATED #1 - NOT REACHABLE TODAY (this is the severity difference). OpenSea path (api.js:684-707): tokenId comes from listing.protocol_data?.parameters?.offer?.[0] and maker from listing.protocol_data?.parameters?.offerer - the SAME subtree - and line 707 drops rows with tokenId == null, so losing protocol_data removes the listing entirely -> empty list -> measured:false -> honest "No active listings to measure." Native path (api.js:746): `maker: order.maker` has no fallback and no filter, but the column is `maker text NOT NULL` (api/orderbook.js:269), the feed is select("*") (line 437), and inserts write the signature-recovered offerer (line 970). Also MarketIntegrity.jsx:325 catches a listings fetch failure into { listings: [] }, which self-gates. So no user sees this today; it is a latent robustness gap that fires on an upstream payload shape change.

MIS-STATED #2 - THE FINDING UNDER-STATES THE WIDER HALF. The same missing gate bites on PARTIAL attribution in the opposite direction: shares are computed over attributed.length (line 389), so 3 attributed rows out of a 100-deep floor yield topSellerShare between 0.33 and 1.0 -> a RED "Concentrated" chip, while the Section subtitle still reads "Bottom 100 of the active listings" (MarketIntegrity.jsx:272, depth = floor.length) and bandReason quotes "of the 3 cheapest listings" (line 401). Partial maker loss is a strictly wider trigger than total loss and produces a false ACCUSATION about a collection rather than a false reassurance.

ACCURATE VERSION: analyzeFloorConcentration has no attribution-coverage gate, so the band is computed over whatever fraction of the floor carries a maker - at zero coverage a green "Well distributed" headline from an empty set, at low-but-nonzero coverage a "Concentrated" headline from a handful of rows on a basis the subtitle misstates. Any fix should gate on attributed.length / floor.length (below a floor -> measured:false), which closes both directions; gating only on distinctSellers === 0 fixes the green badge and leaves the red one.
verdicts.reasoning: Read marketIntegrity.js:343-419, lib/detection/metrics.ts:35-57, MarketIntegrity.jsx:8-12/260-300/312-350, api.js:684-716/719-765/785-840, api/orderbook.js:425-490/940-986, and marketIntegrity.test.js:130-168. The described code path is exactly right and produces a green "Well distributed" headline chip from an empty seller set, with the only counter-evidence in 10px muted footnote text; the 0-vs-1 attributed-listing discontinuity (green vs red) proves it is a missing coverage gate rather than an intentional null hypothesis, and BAND_META's mixed fallback means the component has no honest rendering path either. However, neither live listings producer can currently emit priced-but-makerless rows (OpenSea derives tokenId and offerer from the same protocol_data subtree and drops rows lacking tokenId; native maker is NOT NULL and signature-recovered), so no user is misled today - latent, hence low rather than medium. The finding also omits the strictly-wider partial-coverage case, which produces a false red "Concentrated" verdict on a basis the panel subtitle misstates.

survived.title: 'TOP 10 OF SUPPLY' reports a share of counted-holder supply, not of supply
survived.claim: The tile labelled 'TOP 10 OF SUPPLY' renders a.metrics.topN.top10, which computeMetrics derives from includedSharesDesc(included, includedSupply) (lib/detection/metrics.ts:192 and 98-102) — the vector topNShares itself documents as 'of person-held supply' (metrics.ts:104). The adjacent tile 'TOP 1 OF SUPPLY' (line 137) uses top1ShareOfTotal, which genuinely divides by totalSupply (metrics.ts:200), so the two tiles use different denominators under identical labels. The divergence becomes large when fetchCollectionOwners stops at its 8-page cap and sets `truncated` (lib/marketIntegrity.js:553-556): includedSupply is then only the sampled owners' holdings while totalSupply is the full 20,000. NAKAMOTO COEFF. and GINI are computed from the same truncated vector.
survived.failure_scenario: The owner list is capped at 8 pages and covers 800 owners holding 2,000 of 20,000 Nakamigos. The top 10 sampled wallets hold 400 tokens. True top-10-of-supply is 2%, but the tile reads 'TOP 10 OF SUPPLY 20.0%' while 'TOP 1 OF SUPPLY' next to it reads 0.6%. The only disclosure is one bullet inside the collapsed confidence box: 'Owner list was paginated to a cap — a very large collection may be partially sampled.' A reader concludes the collection is far more concentrated than it is, on a page whose whole purpose is flagging concentration.
survived.suggested_fix: Relabel the tile 'TOP 10 OF COUNTED SUPPLY' (and likewise the Nakamoto/Gini tiles), or suppress the topN/Nakamoto/Gini tiles entirely when `truncated` is set rather than reporting them against a full-supply-sounding label.

verdicts.reasoning:
The MECHANISM is real and reproduces exactly as described; the FAILURE SCENARIO and the severity do not.

Confirmed at file:line (worktree scanner-rebase):
- frontend/src/nakamigos/components/MarketIntegrity.jsx:137 renders `pct(a.metrics.top1ShareOfTotal)` under label "TOP 1 OF SUPPLY"; :138 renders `pct(a.metrics.topN.top10)` under label "TOP 10 OF SUPPLY".
- frontend/src/lib/detection/metrics.ts:200 `top1ShareOfTotal: ratio(largestBalance(included), totalSupply)` — denominator is total supply.
- metrics.ts:192 `includedSharesDesc(included, includedSupply)` → :98-102 divides by `includedSupply`; :104 documents topNShares as "of person-held supply".
- score.ts:413 `includedSupply = sumBalances(included)`; MarketIntegrity.jsx:310 `totalSupply = stats?.supply ?? collection.supply` is an authoritative supply independent of the owner list, so the two denominators genuinely can diverge.

Why the filed scenario does NOT reproduce:

1. The 10x distortion requires `truncated`. fetchCollectionOwners (marketIntegrity.js:535, 553-556) caps at `maxPages = 8` over Alchemy `getOwnersForContract`. The tab only ever runs against three hardcoded collections (constants.js:31/52/68 — supplies 20000, 9696, 5555; CollectionContext.jsx falls back to a COLLECTIONS entry, there is no arbitrary-contract path). Even at Alchemy's smallest page size for this endpoint, 8 pages covers far more owners than a ≤20,000-token collection has. The filed scenario's own numbers ("8 pages = 800 owners", "2,000 of 20,000 sampled") are invented; nothing in the code produces a 100-owner page. `truncated` is effectively unreachable in the shipping app.

2. Without truncation the wedge between includedSupply and totalSupply is only the EXCLUDED holders, and on this path almost nothing is excluded. analyzeOwnershipConcentration (marketIntegrity.js:436-447) builds holders with `{address, balance, clusterId}` only — it never sets `isContract`, so the contract heuristic at exclusions.ts:165-174 cannot fire, and it passes no `labelSources`, so the label path (exclusions.ts:150-158) cannot fire either. The only live exclusion is the built-in burn registry (exclusions.ts:161-163). So in production includedSupply = totalSupply − burned, and the two tiles agree to within a rounding digit, not 20.0% vs 0.6%.

3. The claim that "NAKAMOTO COEFF. and GINI are computed from the same truncated vector" is wrong as a defect. Gini is scale-invariant by construction (metrics.ts:75-81: "Scale-invariant, so shares or balances give the same result") — the denominator choice cannot change it at all. Nakamoto coefficient (metrics.ts:64-71) is only meaningful over a vector that sums to 1, which is precisely what includedSupply normalization gives it; using totalSupply would break it (it could fail to cross 50% and silently return the holder count). Both are correctly denominated.

4. Partial disclosure already exists in the visible panel, not only in a collapsed box: the subtitle at MarketIntegrity.jsx:128 states "LP/burn/contract wallets excluded", and the headline rendered at :132 (score.ts:357) says the figure is over "the person-held supply".

Accurate residual: two adjacent tiles carry the identical suffix "OF SUPPLY" over different denominators — TOP 1 over total supply, TOP 10 over post-exclusion (person-held) supply. That is a real label-precision inconsistency and would be worth fixing (label the second "TOP 10 OF COUNTED SUPPLY", or denominate both the same way), but with the shipped configuration the numeric error a user sees is bounded by burned supply, i.e. sub-1% and usually zero. It is not failed-read laundering, and it does not mislead a reader about concentration.
verdicts.correction: Real but minor and mis-stated. Accurate version: "TOP 10 OF SUPPLY" (MarketIntegrity.jsx:138) is denominated over post-exclusion supply (metrics.ts:98-102, 192) while the adjacent "TOP 1 OF SUPPLY" (:137) is denominated over total supply (metrics.ts:200) — identical label suffix, different denominators. In the shipped app the gap is only burn-address holdings, because analyzeOwnershipConcentration (marketIntegrity.js:436-447) sets no `isContract` and passes no `labelSources`, disabling every exclusion path except the burn registry; and the 8-page cap (marketIntegrity.js:553) cannot be hit by any of the three fixed ≤20,000-supply collections, so `truncated` never fires. Drop the truncation scenario and the GINI/Nakamoto claims entirely — Gini is scale-invariant (metrics.ts:75-81) and Nakamoto REQUIRES the sum-to-1 normalization it has. Severity: low (label precision), not medium.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified against source. MarketIntegrity.jsx:137 renders a.metrics.top1ShareOfTotal (metrics.ts:200, denominator = totalSupply) and line 138 renders a.metrics.topN.top10 (metrics.ts:192 -> includedSharesDesc(included, includedSupply), metrics.ts:98-102), under identically formatted, identically worded 'OF SUPPLY' labels. MarketIntegrity.jsx:310 passes the AUTHORITATIVE supply (stats?.supply ?? collection.supply; Nakamigos = 20000 per constants.js:34) while fetchCollectionOwners (marketIntegrity.js:535-561) may return a SAMPLED holder list once the 8-page cap sets truncated at 553-556. score.ts:381 documents totalSupply as 'Authoritative on-chain total supply', so the caller is feeding the core an authoritative denominator with a partial numerator, which makes includedSupply no longer 'person-held supply' as metrics.ts:104 claims.

The maintainer defense is genuine but incomplete. Sharing one denominator across the concentration family is deliberate and correct (metrics.ts:176-180): effectiveHolders = 1/HHI only means 'effective number of equally-sized holders' if the share vector sums to 1, and top1ShareOfTotal is intentionally of-total because it feeds the single-holder-majority hard gate (score.ts:253-256). That justifies two denominators internally; it does not justify one shared user-facing label, and it does not survive a sampled input.

Three corrections/expansions to the finding as written:
(1) SCOPE IS UNDERSTATED. blendSoftSignals (score.ts:127-157) draws top1, top10, nakamoto and gini from the same sampled vector; only the hard gate uses top1ShareOfTotal. So the band chip at MarketIntegrity.jsx:129 -- the page's headline 'Well distributed / Mixed / Concentrated' verdict -- is itself computed over the sample, not just one tile.
(2) THE SAMPLE IS ARBITRARY, NOT TOP-N. marketIntegrity.js:559 sorts AFTER the pagination loop breaks, so the retained wallets are whatever order Alchemy's pageKey walked. The tile is unstable across reloads, not merely biased.
(3) NO GUARDRAIL EXISTS. analyzeDistribution computes includedSupplyShareOfTotal at score.ts:458; grep across all of src/nakamigos returns zero references, so it is never rendered. assessConfidence (score.ts:269-329) takes includedHolders, unclassified shares, token age, bundles and snipers -- never coverage -- so 800 sampled holders reads as a healthy holder count and nothing downgrades confidence.

Two factual errors in the finding itself: (a) the disclosure is NOT in a 'collapsed' box -- MarketIntegrity.jsx:169-180 renders unconditionally with no details/toggle; it is small (10px) and hedged ('may be partially sampled'), which is the real complaint. (b) 'True top-10-of-supply is 2%' is wrong: 400/20000 is the SAMPLED ten's share, but an arbitrary 800-wallet draw largely misses the collection's actual top ten, which hold more. The accurate statement is that the figure is inflated by roughly 1/includedSupplyShareOfTotal and is not measuring the quantity its label names.

One premise I could not verify from source: that Alchemy pages getOwnersForContract + withTokenBalances at 100 owners/page, making 8 pages ~800 of Nakamigos' ~2,900 owners. fetchCollectionOwners sends no pageSize and api/alchemy.js:315-317 only clamps a supplied value (never injects a default). If the real page size were ~1000, truncated would never fire for Nakamigos and the divergence would reduce to the exclusion set alone -- a few percent, and defensible. The existence of a purpose-written truncation disclosure implies the maintainers expect the cap to fire.

Severity medium is correct and I am not raising it: read-only analytics, no funds move, and a hedged disclosure does exist. It sits at the top of medium because the inflation lands on a red/green concentration verdict on the one page whose entire purpose is flagging concentration.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version: 'TOP 10 OF SUPPLY' (MarketIntegrity.jsx:138) renders topN.top10, whose denominator is includedSupply (metrics.ts:192, 98-102), while the adjacent 'TOP 1 OF SUPPLY' (line 137) divides by totalSupply (metrics.ts:200) -- two denominators under one label. The divergence is bounded by the exclusion set when the owner fetch is complete, but becomes unbounded when fetchCollectionOwners hits its 8-page cap (marketIntegrity.js:553-556): MarketIntegrity.jsx:310 still passes the full 20,000 as totalSupply, so includedSupply collapses to the sampled wallets' holdings.

Beyond the finding as filed: the inflation is not confined to one tile. blendSoftSignals (score.ts:127-157) feeds top1, top10, nakamoto and gini from the same sampled vector, so the band chip at MarketIntegrity.jsx:129 ('Well distributed' / 'Mixed' / 'Concentrated') is itself a function of the sample. The sample is also arbitrary rather than top-N, because marketIntegrity.js:559 sorts only after pagination breaks -- so the displayed concentration is unstable across reloads. And includedSupplyShareOfTotal, computed at score.ts:458, is never rendered anywhere in src/nakamigos and is not an input to assessConfidence (score.ts:269-329), so the one number that would quantify the coverage gap is discarded.

The two mis-statements in the original finding: the truncation disclosure is not collapsed (MarketIntegrity.jsx:169-180 always renders; it is merely 10px and hedged with 'may be partially sampled'), and 'true top-10-of-supply is 2%' is wrong because the sampled top ten are not the collection's top ten.

survived.title: A failed listings read renders as "you have no active listings" with no error and no retry
survived.claim: fetchMyListings catches every failure and returns [] (api-offers.js:663-666). MyCollection's own handler then swallows what is left: `.catch(() => { if (!mounted) return; setLoadingListings(false); })` at lines 134-137 (and identically at 169-172 in handleRetry) sets no error state. `listings` stays [], so the header's '· N listed' span (line 228) and the whole ACTIVE LISTINGS block (line 337) simply do not render — visually identical to genuinely having nothing listed. The `error` banner at line 380 is wired only to the wallet-NFT read, not to this one. Note the wallet-NFT read next to it does this correctly: fetchWalletNfts returns an explicit `error` field (api.js:662) and PortfolioTracker.jsx:163-167 surfaces it.
survived.failure_scenario: The OpenSea proxy is rate-limited (429) while a user with 3 live listings opens My NFTs. The page renders '0x1234…5678 · 12 Nakamigos owned' with no listed count and no ACTIVE LISTINGS panel. The user believes their listings expired or were never created, and re-lists NFTs that are already on sale — signing and paying for duplicate orders. handlePick (line 69) also resolves orderHash to null, so the detail modal offers 'List for sale' on an already-listed token.
survived.suggested_fix: Give fetchMyListings the same error-envelope shape as fetchWalletNfts and render a distinct 'Couldn't load your listings' banner with a retry, rather than letting an empty array speak for the wallet.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the full chain from the files. lib/proxy.js:89-92 throws ApiError on a non-ok OpenSea proxy response (e.g. 429); api-offers.js:62-64 retries 3x then rethrows; api-offers.js:663-666 catches and `return []`. MyCollection.jsx:130-137 then does `.catch(() => { if (!mounted) return; setLoadingListings(false); })` with no error state (identical at 169-172). `listings` stays [], so the `· N listed` span (line 228) and the entire ACTIVE LISTINGS block (line 337) — which contains the only Cancel button (363-373) — are gated on `listings.length > 0` and simply do not render. The error banner at line 380 reads `error`, set only at 124 and 161 (wallet-NFT paths). handlePick (line 69) resolves orderHash via `nft.orderHash || l?.orderHash || null`; normalizeToken (api.js:130-146) never emits orderHash, so it is null, and Modal.jsx:553 (`!nft.orderHash && wallet === nft.owner`) renders "List for sale" on an already-listed token. All line numbers in the finding are accurate.
verdicts.correction:
Confirmed, with three corrections and one material expansion.

(1) TITLE OVERSTATED: no sentence is rendered. Nothing says "you have no active listings" — the `· N listed` span (228) and the ACTIVE LISTINGS panel (337) silently vanish. It is absence-as-answer, visually identical to genuinely having nothing listed, which is still the defect class, but there is no false sentence in the listings path.

(2) THE .catch() IS DEAD CODE: fetchMyListings never rejects (api-offers.js:663-666 swallows internally and returns []), so the handlers at MyCollection.jsx:134-137 and 169-172 never run. The laundering is entirely at the API boundary; the fix belongs there — return an `error` field the way fetchWalletNfts does at api.js:661.

(3) "THE WALLET-NFT READ NEXT TO IT DOES THIS CORRECTLY" IS FALSE FOR THIS FILE. It is true of PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167, which checks `nftData.error`. MyCollection.jsx:116-120 does NOT — it reads only data.tokens/data.totalCount and ignores data.error. Because fetchWalletNfts never throws, the .catch at 121-126 is also dead and the error banner at 380 can never fire from the initial load. On an Alchemy outage MyCollection renders "0x1234…5678 · 0 Nakamigos owned" (227) plus the explicit false factual sentence "This wallet doesn't hold any {collection} NFTs." (393-399) with a "Browse on OpenSea" CTA and no retry path. That is a rendered false claim about the user's holdings — a strictly worse instance of the same defect class, in the same component, and should be folded into this finding.

(4) SCENARIO COST OVERSTATED: Seaport listings are gasless off-chain signatures, so the user does not "sign and pay for duplicate orders" (only a one-time approval if unset), and a duplicate cannot double-sell — the second order becomes unfillable once the NFT transfers. The accurate harm is loss of control: a user with live listings cannot see or CANCEL them (Cancel exists only inside the hidden panel) and may re-list below their existing price while a stale higher listing remains fillable.

Accurate scenario: OpenSea proxy returns 429 while a user with 3 live listings opens My NFTs. Header shows the owned count with no listed count, no ACTIVE LISTINGS panel, no error, no retry. The user cannot cancel listings they actually have, and the detail modal offers "List for sale" on tokens that are already listed. Severity medium holds.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by reading the full chain. Trace for a 429: lib/proxy.js:89-92 throws ApiError(status) -> api-offers.js:62-64 withRetry retries 3x on retryable (lines 31-59) -> still throws -> fetchMyListings catch at api-offers.js:663-666 logs and `return []`. MyCollection.jsx:130-133 therefore takes the SUCCESS branch with an empty array. `listings` stays [], so the `· N listed` clause (227-232) is omitted, the ACTIVE LISTINGS block (337) does not render, AnimatedCard's `listingPrice` (420) is undefined so per-card price badges vanish, and handlePick (69) resolves orderHash to null -> Modal.jsx:553 gates "List for sale" on `!nft.orderHash` and offers it on an already-listed token. All cited line numbers check out (134-137, 169-172, 228, 337, 380, 69).

The finding is real but mis-stated in three ways, and it UNDER-reports the damage.

(1) MECHANISM. "MyCollection's own handler then swallows what is left" is wrong. The `.catch` at 134-137 (and 169-172) is unreachable for the API-failure class, because fetchMyListings never rejects. Those catches only fire on a synchronous throw inside the .then. This matters for the fix: adding error state to those catches would do nothing. fetchMyListings must return an error envelope (as fetchWalletNfts does) and the caller must read it.

(2) THE COMPARISON IS BACKWARDS, AND HIDES A WORSE BUG. The finding says "the wallet-NFT read next to it does this correctly." False as applied to this file. fetchWalletNfts (api.js:647-663) also catches internally and RESOLVES with `{tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..." }` — it does not reject. MyCollection.jsx:116-120 reads only `data.tokens` and `data.totalCount` and never reads `data.error`, so the `.catch` at 121-126 never fires on an Alchemy outage. Consequences: `error` stays null, the banner at 380 never renders, handleRetry (142-173) is unreachable, and the page renders the empty state at 392-399 — "No Nakamigos Found / This wallet doesn't hold any Nakamigos NFTs" — a POSITIVE false factual sentence about the user's wallet, which is strictly worse than the listings omission. PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 is the component that handles this correctly, with an explicit F724 comment saying to surface the retryable error "instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim." MyCollection is the file that missed that fix.

(3) HARM OVERSTATED IN ONE DETAIL. "signing and paying for duplicate orders" — a Seaport listing is a free off-chain signature; no gas is paid unless the collection approval is missing. The real economic harm is that the original, still-fillable order remains live: a user who believes the listing vanished and re-lists at a higher price can still be filled at the old lower price.

SEVERITY: medium is correct for the listings read in isolation (silent omission + a wrong "List for sale" affordance on a money path). The sibling defect in (2) is arguably higher on its own because it prints a false sentence about the wallet AND removes the only retry control from the page; treated as one cluster, medium-to-high. I am leaving the reported severity at medium since that is the item under review, and flagging the wallet-NFT gap as a separate finding worth filing.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: On any upstream failure (429/5xx/network), fetchMyListings (frontend/src/nakamigos/api-offers.js:663-666) catches and returns [] — it never rejects, so MyCollection.jsx:130-133 takes the success branch. The `.catch` blocks at MyCollection.jsx:134-137 and 169-172 are unreachable for this failure class and are not where the swallowing happens; the fix belongs in fetchMyListings (return an error envelope) plus the caller. Failed-read symptoms: the `· N listed` clause (227-232) is omitted, the ACTIVE LISTINGS panel (337) does not render, per-card listing price badges (420) disappear, and handlePick (69) yields orderHash=null so Modal.jsx:553 offers "List for sale" on an already-listed token. Correction to the finding's framing: the adjacent wallet-NFT read does NOT do this correctly here. fetchWalletNfts (frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:647-663) likewise catches internally and resolves with {tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error}; MyCollection.jsx:116-120 ignores `data.error` entirely, so on an Alchemy outage `error` stays null, the banner and Retry at 380-385 never render (handleRetry is unreachable), and the page asserts "No Nakamigos Found / This wallet doesn't hold any Nakamigos NFTs" at 392-399 — a positive false claim. PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 is the correct reference implementation (F724). Finally, re-listing costs a signature, not gas; the economic harm is that the original lower-priced order stays fillable.

survived.title: FLOOR PRICE, EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE and the CSV export can all be the hardcoded 0.1048 fallback with no CACHED badge
survived.claim: The `stats` prop comes from useCollection, which seeds state with FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED — `{floor: 0.1048, volume: 52200, owners: 5238, ...}` plus `fallback: true` (hooks/useCollection.js:16,22 and constants.js:226-231) — and api.js:277 returns the same flagged object when both Alchemy and OpenSea stats fail. MyCollection reads `stats?.floor` at line 73 and renders it as 'FLOOR PRICE' (line 297) and as 'EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE' = floor × tokens.length (line 289), and writes it into the downloaded CSV as 'Est. Value (ETH)' (line 97) — never once checking `stats.fallback`. Hero.jsx:127,181 reads the identical object and appends a <CachedTag /> to exactly these labels, so the honest pattern exists and this tab is the one missing it.
survived.failure_scenario: Alchemy and OpenSea stats both fail (or the user simply looks at the page during first paint before the fetch resolves). A holder of 40 Nakamigos sees 'FLOOR PRICE Ξ 0.1048' and 'EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ 4.1920' presented as current on-chain data, clicks Export CSV, and walks away with a file listing 0.1048 as the per-token estimated value of every NFT. If the real floor has moved to 0.03, the user is off by 3.5x on a number they may use for tax or lending decisions.
survived.suggested_fix: Thread `stats.fallback` into these three stat cards (and suppress or annotate the CSV 'Est. Value' column) using the same CachedTag treatment Hero.jsx already applies.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced line-for-line. constants.js:226-231 defines FALLBACK_STATS with floor 0.1048; useCollection.js:16 wraps it as FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED (fallback:true) and seeds it as initial state (:22) and on every collection switch (:46); api.js:277 returns the same flagged object when both the Alchemy and OpenSea stats paths throw. App.jsx:338 destructures that stats object and App.jsx:765 passes it straight into MyCollection. MyCollection.jsx:73 reads stats?.floor with only a null/isFinite guard and never inspects stats.fallback — grep for "fallback" across MyCollection.jsx returns zero hits. That floorPrice is rendered as FLOOR PRICE (:297), multiplied by tokens.length into EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE (:83, rendered :289), and written into the CSV as "Est. Value (ETH)" (:97). Hero.jsx:126 derives isFallback from the identical object and appends CachedTag to FLOOR/ALL-TIME VOL/OWNERS (:181,:194,:204), so the honest pattern exists and this tab is the one missing it — exactly as claimed. The one candidate mitigation is defeated: Header.jsx:580-585 shows a DEMO badge when isLive is false, but App.jsx:820 passes isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive} and useNfts.js:40 sets nfts.isLive purely from the token-list fetch, so a successful token fetch plus failed stats renders "LIVE" in the header while the on-screen floor is the hardcoded constant.
verdicts.correction: Finding stands at medium; two scope corrections. (1) It affects only the default Nakamigos collection. useCollection.js:12,22,46 seed EMPTY_STATS ({floor:null,...}) for any non-default collection, and api.js:278 returns floor:null for them, so those tabs honestly render an em-dash. (2) The "first paint" half of the scenario is a race, not a certainty: the stats bar is gated on MyCollection's own !loading && tokens.length > 0 (:275), so on a warm tab the stats fetch has usually already resolved; the robust case is the persistent one where both Alchemy and OpenSea stats fail (api.js:277) and the tab shows Ξ0.1048 as FLOOR PRICE indefinitely with no badge. Also worth noting the header cannot be relied on as disclosure here — App.jsx:820 ORs in nfts.isLive (useNfts.js:40), so the badge can read "LIVE" while the floor is the hardcoded fallback. Adjacent same-class instance not covered by this finding: BulkListingWizard.jsx:487 does `stats?.floor != null && isFinite(stats.floor) ? stats.floor : 0` with no fallback check either, and that value feeds listing-price suggestion (a money path), so it is arguably the more serious sibling.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — every citation verified against the files.

VERIFIED CHAIN:
- constants.js:226-231 — FALLBACK_STATS = {floor: 0.1048, volume: 52200, owners: 5238, supply: 20000}. The volume field carries the comment "Historical total volume, not 24h — do not use for volume comparisons", i.e. the authors knew these are stale-by-construction figures.
- hooks/useCollection.js:16 — FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED = {...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}; :22 and :46 seed/reset state with it for the default collection.
- api.js:277 — `if (contract.toLowerCase() === CONTRACT.toLowerCase()) return { ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true };` on the both-Alchemy-and-OpenSea-failed path.
