- hooks/useCollection.js:66-69 — setStats spreads statsData, so `fallback: true` survives into the prop.
- App.jsx:765 — MyCollection receives that exact object as `stats`.
- MyCollection.jsx:73 — `stats?.floor != null && isFinite(stats.floor) ? stats.floor : null`. Guards ABSENCE, not staleness. 0.1048 is non-null and finite, so it passes through with full confidence. `stats.fallback` is never read anywhere in the 548-line file (grep confirms).
- Rendered at :297 as bare "FLOOR PRICE", at :289 as floor*tokens.length "EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE", written at :97 into the CSV column "Est. Value (ETH)".
- Hero.jsx:127 `const isFallback = !!stats.fallback` and :181/:194 append <CachedTag/> to the identical FLOOR and ALL-TIME VOL labels. The honest pattern exists; this tab is the outlier.

MAINTAINER DEFENSES EVALUATED — three of four fail:
1. "Line 73 is a defensive guard" — category error. It handles absence (null -> em-dash / "N/A"), not a present-but-stale constant. This is the laundering shape.
2. "Labels are hedged (EST.)" — half true. It hedges the DERIVATION, not the stale input, and FLOOR PRICE at :295 has no qualifier at all.
3. "Global DEMO badge covers it" — COLLAPSES. Header.jsx:579-585 shows LIVE/DEMO from App.jsx:820 `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}`. `nfts.isLive` comes from a DIFFERENT fetch (hooks/useNfts.js:40, `setIsLive(!data.fallback)` on the gallery token list). When collection stats fail but the token list succeeds — different endpoints, the common partial-outage case — the header reads LIVE while stats.floor is the hardcoded 0.1048. The mitigation is defeated in exactly the case it was meant to cover.
4. "Plausible cached figure" — true but irrelevant; plausibility is what makes it dangerous, and the constant has no timestamp so the code cannot know if it is still plausible.

SCENARIO CORRECTION: the reporter's "first paint" variant is real but narrow — the stats bar is gated on `!loading && tokens.length > 0` (:275), so it requires fetchWalletNfts to win a race against fetchCollectionStats (which makes Alchemy meta + owners + an OpenSea volume call). Plausible but transient. The DURABLE case is api.js:277 (both stats upstreams down), which persists until the next successful 60s/300s poll. The finding should lead with that.

SEVERITY: medium holds. Not high — no transaction is signed on this path, blast radius is the default collection only (other collections return floor:null and honestly show an em-dash), and the value is order-of-magnitude plausible. Not low — the CSV at :97 persists the number into a file that leaves the app, where no badge, tooltip or header state can follow it, and the FLOOR PRICE card is an unqualified factual market claim.

ADJACENT HIGHER-SEVERITY SIBLING (separate finding, same blast radius): MyCollection.jsx:542 passes the same `stats` object to BulkListingWizard, which at :487 applies the identical fallback-blind guard (`stats?.floor != null && isFinite(stats.floor) ? stats.floor : 0`) and at :127 computes suggested listing prices as `floor * multiplier`. That is a real money path pricing real listings off a possibly-stale constant. No test coverage exists for either (no test file references MyCollection or FALLBACK_STATS).

FIX: read `stats.fallback` at :73 and either render Hero's existing <CachedTag/> beside FLOOR PRICE / EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE, or emit "N/A (cached floor)" in the CSV column.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed as written, with two refinements. (1) The primary scenario should be the durable one — api.js:277, both Alchemy and OpenSea stats calls fail, so `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}` persists until the next successful poll. The "first paint" variant is real but transient and narrower than stated: the stats bar is gated on `!loading && tokens.length > 0` (MyCollection.jsx:275), so it only appears if fetchWalletNfts beats fetchCollectionStats. (2) The finding understates its own case by omitting the strongest evidence: the app-wide mitigation is broken. App.jsx:820 passes `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` to the Header, and `nfts.isLive` is set from the gallery token fetch (hooks/useNfts.js:40), not the stats fetch. So when stats fail but tokens load, the header badge reads LIVE while FLOOR PRICE shows the hardcoded 0.1048 — the user gets an affirmative "live data" signal alongside a stale constant. Also worth splitting out as its own finding: BulkListingWizard.jsx:487 (reached from MyCollection.jsx:542) repeats the identical fallback-blind guard and at :127 prices real listings at `floor * multiplier`, making this a money path and not only a display path.

survived.title: Portfolio value, unrealized P&L and the 90-day chart are computed from the same unbadged fallback floor
survived.claim: loadPortfolio calls fetchCollectionStats (line 152-156) and passes statsData.floor straight into calculatePnL as the valuation basis (line 182) without inspecting statsData.fallback. When both stats sources fail, api.js:277 returns FALLBACK_STATS with floor 0.1048. lib/portfolio.js:187 uses that for every token's currentValue, so PORTFOLIO VALUE (line 330), the FLOOR column (line 414), UNREAL. P&L (line 416) and every per-token VALUE/P&L cell are derived from a constant. Worse than the MyCollection case: line 190-194 then calls saveSnapshot, writing the fabricated value into the 90-day PORTFOLIO VALUE OVER TIME chart, where it persists in localStorage after the API recovers.
survived.failure_scenario: A user with 6 NFTs opens the Portfolio tab during an Alchemy + OpenSea outage. The tab shows 'PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ 0.6288', 'FLOOR Ξ 0.1048' and a green UNREAL. P&L, all from a constant. Tomorrow, with the API healthy and the real floor at 0.03, the value chart shows a fabricated cliff from 0.63 to 0.18 that no market event caused, and the user reads it as a 71% crash.
survived.suggested_fix: Check statsData.fallback: badge the floor-derived figures as cached, and skip saveSnapshot entirely when the floor did not come from a live read.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED in the code, with one materially wrong trigger condition in the scenario.

Mechanism reproduced end to end:
- PortfolioTracker.jsx:150-157 fetches wallet NFTs and stats in parallel; :169-170 stores both (`setStats(statsData)`).
- :179-183 passes `floorPrice: statsData.floor` straight into `calculatePnL`. `statsData.fallback` is never read anywhere in the file — I grepped it: `stats` appears only at :132 (useState), :170 (setStats), and is never referenced in the JSX. It is dead state; the fallback flag is discarded.
- api.js:275-278: when the Alchemy stats leg AND the OpenSea stats fallback both fail, and the contract is the main Nakamigos CONTRACT, it returns `{ ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }`. constants.js:226-231: `FALLBACK_STATS.floor = 0.1048` — a hardcoded constant.
- lib/portfolio.js:187 -> getCurrentValue (:108-112) returns that floor verbatim as each token's `currentValue`; :251 `unrealizedPnL = totalCurrentValue - totalCostBasis`; :262 `floorPrice: floorPrice || 0`.
- Render: PORTFOLIO VALUE (:330), FLOOR column (:414), UNREAL. P&L (:416), per-token VALUE (:484) and P&L/% (:487-491), TOP GAINERS/LOSERS percentages (:545, :577) all derive from the constant, with no badge or caveat.
- Snapshot poisoning is real: :190-194 calls `saveSnapshot(result.currentValue, ...)` whenever `currentValue > 0`, and 6 x 0.1048 = 0.6288 > 0. portfolio.js:286-305 writes it to localStorage under `portfolio_snapshots_<wallet>_<contract>`, retained up to 90 days (MAX_SNAPSHOTS), and it feeds PORTFOLIO VALUE OVER TIME (:597).

The finding is strengthened by a fact it did not cite: the app already has the badge convention and this tab is the one that skips it. Hero.jsx:127 sets `isFallback = !!stats.fallback` and Hero.jsx:181/195 render a `<CachedTag />` next to the FLOOR and ALL-TIME VOL values from the exact same FALLBACK_STATS. Same pattern at hooks/useCollection.js:75, hooks/useNfts.js:40, WhaleIntelligence.jsx:186/200, ActivityFeed.jsx:104, MarketIntegrity.jsx:347. PortfolioTracker is the outlier, and it is the one surface that also persists the value.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG — the stated trigger. "A user opens the Portfolio tab during an Alchemy + OpenSea outage" does NOT produce this render. On a full Alchemy outage `fetchWalletNfts` (api.js:660-663) returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: ... }`, and PortfolioTracker.jsx:163-167 correctly short-circuits to the retryable error banner (:264-276) — that path is honest and is exactly the F724 fix noted in the comment. Nothing renders and nothing is saved.

Reachability is therefore narrower but still real: it needs a PARTIAL failure where `getNFTsForOwner` succeeds while the stats call fails. That is plausible because the two calls are different endpoints issued concurrently, and inside `_fetchCollectionStatsUncached` (api.js:217-222) only two of the four legs can reject — `getFloorPrice` and `getOwnersForContract` (the `getContractMetadata` and native-listings legs have their own `.catch`). `getOwnersForContract` on a 20k-supply / ~5.2k-owner collection is the heavy call and can hit the proxy request timeout (lib/proxy.js:134-141 converts timeout/network into a thrown ApiError) while the small per-wallet query succeeds. The OpenSea secondary then has to fail too, which the codebase itself documents as routine — api.js:246-251 notes the per-collection OpenSea stats call "is the first to get throttled" by the app's own rate limiter.

One further caveat on persistence: portfolio.js:293-295 overwrites the same-date entry, so a later successful load ON THE SAME DAY self-corrects. The fabricated point only sticks permanently if the outage window covers the user's only visit that day — after which it sits in the chart for 90 days and the recovery reads as a crash the market never produced.

SECOND, UNREPORTED HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT (worth folding in): for every non-Nakamigos collection (gnssart at constants.js:52, the 0xd372... entry at :68, etc.), api.js:278 returns `floor: null` on the same failure. getCurrentValue then returns 0, so the tab renders "PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ 0.00" and a full-size red UNREAL. P&L equal to minus the entire cost basis — telling the user their holdings are worthless when the truth is only that the floor read failed. `saveSnapshot` is skipped there (currentValue is 0), so the chart is spared, but the hero stats are a confident falsehood. The root cause is identical: PortfolioTracker never distinguishes "floor unknown" from "floor is a real number", neither for `fallback: true` nor for `floor: null`.

Accurate restatement: PortfolioTracker discards the `fallback` flag returned by fetchCollectionStats and renders portfolio value, floor, unrealized P&L, per-token values and gainer/loser percentages from either the hardcoded 0.1048 constant (main collection) or from 0 (other collections / null floor), unbadged, while Hero.jsx badges the identical value as cached — and on the main-collection path it additionally writes the fabricated total into the 90-day localStorage snapshot series.

Severity medium is correct and I would not raise it: no money moves and no transaction is built off this number, but it is an unbadged, user-visible financial claim that outlives the outage in local storage. Triggering needs a partial-failure window rather than a clean outage, which is what keeps it below high.
verdicts.correction: The defect is real but the trigger in the scenario is wrong. A full "Alchemy + OpenSea outage" does NOT reach it: fetchWalletNfts (api.js:660-663) returns an error and PortfolioTracker.jsx:163-167 shows the retryable error banner instead — that path is honest. The finding is reachable only on a PARTIAL failure: getNFTsForOwner succeeds while getFloorPrice or getOwnersForContract fails (api.js:217-222 — the other two legs of the Promise.all have their own .catch) AND the OpenSea stats fallback also fails/throttles (api.js:266-279), which api.js:246-251 documents as a routine occurrence. Corrected scenario: a user holding 6 Nakamigos loads the tab while the heavy getOwnersForContract call times out and the OpenSea stats call is rate-limited. api.js:277 returns FALLBACK_STATS, and the tab renders PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ 0.6288, FLOOR Ξ 0.1048 and a per-token P&L derived entirely from the constant at constants.js:227 — with no badge, even though Hero.jsx:181 renders a <CachedTag /> next to that exact same value. PortfolioTracker.jsx:170 stores statsData but `stats` is never read in the render, so the fallback flag is simply thrown away. Line 190-194 then persists 0.6288 into the 90-day localStorage snapshot series (portfolio.js:286-305), which feeds the PORTFOLIO VALUE OVER TIME chart — caveat: portfolio.js:293-295 overwrites the same-date entry, so a later healthy load on the SAME day self-corrects; the fabricated point only sticks if the outage covers that day's only visit. Additionally, the finding under-reports the sibling case: for non-Nakamigos collections api.js:278 returns floor: null, getCurrentValue returns 0, and the tab shows "PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ 0.00" plus a full-cost-basis red UNREAL. P&L — telling the user their holdings are worthless when only the floor read failed. Root cause for both: PortfolioTracker never distinguishes "floor unknown" from a real floor. Severity medium is correct.

Defect confirmed; the trigger scenario is mis-stated and the fix scope is understated.

CONFIRMED CHAIN: PortfolioTracker.jsx:170 stores statsData (including `fallback: true`) into a `stats` state variable that is NEVER read in the JSX (declared :132, set :170, zero other references). :182 passes `statsData.floor` into calculatePnL with no `.fallback` inspection. api.js:277 returns `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}` (constants.js:226-231, floor 0.1048) for the main contract when both stats sources fail. portfolio.js:111/:187 uses it as every token's currentValue; :251 derives unrealizedPnL; :262 sets floorPrice. Rendered at PortfolioTracker.jsx:330 (PORTFOLIO VALUE), :414 (FLOOR), :416 (UNREAL. P&L), :484/:487 (per-token), and topGainers/topLosers :210-221. :190-194 then calls saveSnapshot -> portfolio.js:286-306 writes it to localStorage (90-day ring, no UI to clear), read back by ValueChart at :597. Persistence after recovery is real.

MIS-STATED TRIGGER (the one maintainer defense that holds): an "Alchemy + OpenSea outage" is SELF-BLOCKING. fetchWalletNfts (api.js:648-664, getNFTsForOwner) would also throw, returning `{tokens: [], error}`, and PortfolioTracker.jsx:163-167 short-circuits to the retryable error banner BEFORE calculatePnL runs (F724). The bug cannot fire on a total outage.

ACCURATE TRIGGER: a PARTIAL failure. getNFTsForOwner succeeds while _fetchCollectionStatsUncached loses both legs. The try block at api.js:217-222 fails if either getFloorPrice OR getOwnersForContract throws (the other two calls carry .catch() guards; these two do not), then the OpenSea rescue at :267 must also fail. The file documents this as live: the comment at :183-190 exists because page fan-out "trip[s] our own /api/opensea rate limiter", and :246-251 calls the OpenSea stats call "the first to get throttled". Ordinary 429 behaviour, not an outage.

MISSED SECOND VARIANT that changes the fix: api.js:256-261 returns stats with NO `fallback` key at all when the Alchemy path succeeds but `floorData.openSea?.floorPrice` and the native orderbook floor are both empty (:224-229) — routine for a collection with no live listings. floor is then null, getCurrentValue (portfolio.js:111) returns 0, and the user sees PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ0.0000, FLOOR Ξ0.0000 and a red TOTAL P&L of exactly -costBasis: a confident "your holdings are worthless" produced by an absent price. saveSnapshot's `result.currentValue > 0` guard (:190) spares the chart here, so this variant is display-only — but a fix gating solely on `statsData.fallback` misses it entirely. The gate must also cover `statsData.floor == null`.

PROJECT PRECEDENT defeats the "cached estimate is fine" defense: Hero.jsx:104-120 already ships a CachedTag() whose own comment says it is shown "when the numbers are the hardcoded fallback rather than a live fetch (F582) — honest disclosure, no number change", gated on `const isFallback = !!stats.fallback` (Hero.jsx:127). PortfolioTracker fetches the same object, holds the same flag, and applies neither. Worse than Hero: here the constant is multiplied by holding count and subtracted from real on-chain cost basis to produce a derived per-user financial claim with a green/red colour.

SEVERITY: medium stands. Holdings reads fail closed, no money path, no signing. What keeps it above low is that the `.fallback` variant is the one that persists into a 90-day localStorage chart with no user-facing way to clear it.

RESTATED SCENARIO THAT ACTUALLY REPRODUCES: user holding 6 Nakamigos opens Portfolio while getFloorPrice is rate-limited and the /api/opensea stats call is throttled, but getNFTsForOwner returns normally. Tab shows PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ0.6288, FLOOR Ξ0.1048, green UNREAL. P&L — all 6 × 0.1048 — with no `cached` tag, while Hero on the same page would show one. saveSnapshot records 0.6288 for today. Tomorrow, stats healthy and the real floor at 0.03, the chart draws a red cliff from 0.63 to 0.18 that no trade caused.
verdicts.reasoning: Read all four files. The laundering chain is exactly as claimed and verified line by line, including the snapshot persistence into localStorage. Two corrections. (1) The stated scenario is impossible: on a full Alchemy+OpenSea outage fetchWalletNfts also fails and PortfolioTracker.jsx:163-167 bails to an error banner before calculatePnL — the real trigger is a partial failure (getFloorPrice or getOwnersForContract 429 plus an OpenSea stats 429) while getNFTsForOwner succeeds, which api.js's own comments at :183-190 and :246-251 document as a live rate-limit condition. (2) The finding misses a second, more common unbadged state: api.js:256-261 returns floor:null with no fallback flag when no listings exist, producing PORTFOLIO VALUE Ξ0 and a red P&L of -costBasis — so a fix gating only on statsData.fallback is incomplete. The maintainer's "it's just a cached estimate" defense is defeated by the project's own F582 precedent: Hero.jsx:127 badges this exact object with CachedTag, and PortfolioTracker stores the identical flag in a `stats` state variable it never renders. Severity medium is correct: display/valuation honesty with durable localStorage contamination, no money path.

survived.title: Wallet NFTs are read as a single un-paginated 100-item page while the header reports the API's full totalCount
survived.claim: fetchWalletNfts issues one getNFTsForOwner call with pageSize 100 and never follows data.pageKey (api.js:648-659) — unlike fetchTokens, which threads a pageKey (api.js:154-165). It returns the truncated `tokens` array alongside the API's untruncated `totalCount`. MyCollection then renders totalCount in the header (line 227) and in the NFTs OWNED card (line 283) while deriving EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE from `tokens.length` (line 83), AVG RANK from `tokens` (line 77) and the CSV from `tokens` (line 92). PortfolioTracker has the same split: NFTs HELD is pnlData.nftCount = heldTokens.length (line 355), capped at 100.
survived.failure_scenario: A wallet holds 150 Nakamigos. My NFTs renders '0xabc…def · 150 Nakamigos owned' and 'NFTs OWNED 150', but EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE is floor × 100 — a third of the collection silently missing — the grid caps at 100 cards with the 'Show more' button vanishing at 100 rather than 150, and Export CSV produces 100 rows for a header that says 150. On the Portfolio tab the same wallet's P&L and NFTs HELD are computed over 100 of 150 tokens with nothing indicating truncation.
survived.suggested_fix: Follow data.pageKey in fetchWalletNfts until exhausted (or until a sane cap), and if a cap is kept, return a `truncated` flag and say so in the UI instead of pairing a full count with a partial set.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the files. `fetchWalletNfts` (frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:648-664) issues exactly one `getNFTsForOwner` with `pageSize: "100"` (line 654), never reads `data.pageKey`, and returns `tokens: (data.ownedNfts || []).map(...)` (656-657) next to `totalCount: data.totalCount || 0` (658). By contrast `fetchTokens` (api.js:154-172) does thread a page cursor (`if (pageKey) params.startToken = pageKey` at 161, `continuation: data.pageKey` at 165), so the asymmetry the finding describes is real and 100 is Alchemy's max page size — the truncation is not recoverable by bumping the number.

MyCollection.jsx consumes the split exactly as claimed: header `{totalCount} {collection.name} owned` (line 227), NFTs OWNED card `{totalCount}` (283), TOTAL HELD `{totalCount}` (490) — all from the untruncated API count — while EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE is `floorPrice * tokens.length` (83), the grid slices `tokens` (413) and the Show-more button is gated on `tokens.length > visibleCount` (424, +60 per press from 39), and Export CSV maps `tokens` (92). PortfolioTracker passes `nftData.tokens` into `calculatePnL` (151, 179), whose `nftCount: heldTokens.length` (lib/portfolio.js:261) renders as NFTs HELD — at PortfolioTracker.jsx:354, not 355, and also at 408/411 where it divides costBasis by it for AVG COST.

The load-bearing external assumption — that Alchemy's `totalCount` is the full owned count for the filtered contract, not the page count — is corroborated inside this codebase, which is what raises this above speculation: OnChainProfile.jsx:270 computes `portfolioValue = totalCount * floorPrice` (the correct basis), and useHolderStatus.jsx:86 / useProAccess.jsx:32 both treat `totalCount` as the true balance. MyCollection line 83 is the inconsistent one.

Two corrections to the finding as written. (1) The AVG RANK citation (MyCollection.jsx:77/84) is a red herring for truncation: wallet tokens come from `normalizeToken`, which hardcodes `rank: null` (api.js:149), and MyCollection never enriches ranks (`attachRanks` at api.js:851-897 is not applied here). So `avgRank` is `sum(0)/len = 0` and the card renders "#0" for every wallet regardless of page size — that is a separate, unconditional defect, not a consequence of the missing pageKey. (2) The reported line for NFTs HELD is off by one (354).

One same-class instance sits just outside the reported scope and is worth folding in: OnChainProfile.jsx:554-568 renders a "View all {totalCount} →" button gated on `totalCount > MAX_GRID`, which for a 150-NFT wallet promises 150 and can never reveal more than the 100 fetched.

Severity medium holds, at the low end. Nothing is mis-signed and no funds move, but a whale wallet sees two contradictory numbers side by side in the same stats bar (NFTs OWNED 150, EST. PORTFOLIO VALUE = floor × 100), gets a CSV whose row count disagrees with its own header, and gets P&L/cost-basis computed over two thirds of its holdings with no truncation indicator anywhere. It only bites wallets holding >100 of one collection — rare, but precisely the segment the app builds surfaces for (`isWhale = totalCount >= 10`, WhaleIntelligence).
verdicts.correction: Accurate in substance; three adjustments. (a) The AVG RANK claim (MyCollection.jsx:77) is wrong as a truncation harm — `normalizeToken` sets `rank: null` (api.js:149) and MyCollection never enriches ranks, so AVG RANK renders "#0" for every wallet independent of paging; that is a separate standalone defect. (b) NFTs HELD in PortfolioTracker is line 354, not 355 (also reused at 408 and as the AVG COST divisor at 411). (c) The strongest evidence is internal inconsistency, not just the missing pageKey: OnChainProfile.jsx:270 computes portfolio value as `totalCount * floorPrice` while MyCollection.jsx:83 uses `tokens.length`. Add the adjacent instance OnChainProfile.jsx:554-568, where "View all {totalCount} →" can never reveal more than the 100 fetched tokens.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Every cited line verifies exactly. api.js:648-659 issues one getNFTsForOwner with pageSize "100" and discards data.pageKey, while returning the API's untruncated data.totalCount. The same file paginates correctly elsewhere (fetchTokens api.js:154-165 threads startToken/pageKey; fetchActivity api.js:391-407, 441-479), so the capability exists and was not applied here.

The maintainer defenses I could construct all fail:
(1) "100 is Alchemy's max" — true, but that defends the parameter, not the missing loop; the function holds totalCount, the very value that proves its own answer is short, and never compares it to tokens.length.
(2) "Rendering totalCount in the header is the honest choice" — self-defeating. The harm is that totalCount and a tokens.length-derived number render in the SAME stat row from the SAME response: MyCollection.jsx:283 NFTs OWNED = totalCount (150) sits three cards from :289<-:83 portfolioValue = floorPrice * tokens.length (floor x 100), with FLOOR PRICE printed at :291. The user can divide card 2 by card 3, get 100, and read 150 on card 1. The screen falsifies itself with its own numbers.
(3) "EST. label covers it" — EST. discloses that floor-price-as-value is approximate; it does not cover undercounting the holdings by a third.
(4) "Pagination fan-out cost" — real (9 call sites; useProAccess/useHolderStatus only need totalCount; the file already needed in-flight de-duping per F516), but that argues for an opt-in paginate flag, not for capping every caller.

"Intentional" is refuted by history: git log -L 646,662 on api.js returns exactly one commit, b0fe56e3 (the original sub-app import), in current form — no comment, no test, never revisited. By contrast the deliberate honesty guards around it are all commented (PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 "F724", OnChainProfile.jsx:137-142, WhaleIntelligence.jsx:256). Deliberate decisions in this file leave marks; this one left none.

Severity medium holds: requires >100 of one collection and signs no wrong transaction (not high), but it fabricates a wallet-specific valuation the same screen disproves and degrades worst on the surface built for large wallets (not low).
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version, with three refinements:

1. "PortfolioTracker has the same split" is MIS-STATED. PortfolioTracker never renders totalCount — nftCount (:354, :408), costBasis/nftCount (:411), currentValue and unrealizedPnL are ALL derived from heldTokens.length (portfolio.js:261). The panel is internally consistent at 100, so there is no on-screen contradiction there — just a silent uniform undercount of a whale's entire P&L. The self-contradiction is MyCollection-only. Different defect shape: understatement vs. self-contradiction.

2. The "Show more" control is a MITIGATION, not an aggravator. Initial visibleCount is 60 (:39), and the counter reads tokens.length - visibleCount (:435), so it renders "(40 left)" once and disappears — it never advertises the missing 50.

3. Blast radius is UNDERSTATED. WhaleIntelligence.jsx:254 expands a top-holder row through the same call. A top-holders panel selects, by construction, exactly the wallets most likely to exceed 100 (the app's own sample data has a 156-holder, constants.js:240) — so the one surface built for large wallets is the one silently capped. `tokens` is also what's passed to BulkListingWizard and BundleListing, so a >100 holder physically cannot reach past their first 100 to bulk-list.

ADJACENT AND HIGHER SEVERITY, same call site, NOT in the original finding: MyCollection.jsx:116-121 is the only fetchWalletNfts caller that does not check data.error. fetchWalletNfts resolves (never rejects) with { tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error } on outage (api.js:658), so the .catch at :122 is unreachable and `error` stays null. The component falls through to :391 and renders "No Nakamigos Found — This wallet doesn't hold any Nakamigos NFTs." An upstream outage becomes a confident factual claim about the user's wallet with no retry affordance. PortfolioTracker (:161-167), OnChainProfile (:137-142) and WhaleIntelligence (:256) all guard this exact case with commented intent; MyCollection was missed. Textbook failed-read laundering — rate above the pagination issue.

survived.title: The Watchlist's price alerts can never fire — the tokens it is given always have price: null
survived.claim: Watchlist receives `tokens={nfts.allTokens}` (App.jsx:763). Those tokens come from normalizeToken, which hardcodes `price: null` (api.js:147), and computeRarity only adds rank/rarityScore (api.js:881-897). Listing prices live in a separate `listings` array and are merged onto a token only by enrichWithListing, which App.jsx applies solely to the modal selection and cart adds (App.jsx:395, 505) — never to allTokens. So in this component nft.price is always null: `belowTarget` at line 175 is permanently false, the price span at line 188 never renders, and the 'Below target price!' badge at lines 212-216 is unreachable. Meanwhile the header subtitle promises 'Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts' (line 127) and the empty state promises 'Add {collection} NFTs to track price changes and get alerts' (components/EmptyState.jsx:38).
survived.failure_scenario: A user adds 5 Nakamigos to the watchlist and sets TARGET PRICE 0.08 on each, expecting to be told when one lists at or below that. The values persist to localStorage and Supabase. One of those NFTs is subsequently listed at 0.05 ETH. The Watchlist card shows no price at all and no alert badge, now or ever, and the user misses the fill they set the target for.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass the `listings` array into Watchlist and merge it onto the watched tokens (reuse App.jsx's enrichWithListing), or — if the alerting genuinely lives in the PriceAlerts tab — remove the target-price input and the alert copy from this tab rather than shipping an input that is written to a database and never read against anything.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end from the files. (1) App.jsx:763 passes tokens={nfts.allTokens} to Watchlist. (2) useNfts.js:190 returns allTokens = rankedTokens = computeRarity(tokens), and tokens come only from fetchTokens -> normalizeToken (api.js:164); the hook never merges listings. (3) api.js:147 is literally `price: null,` inside normalizeToken's return object — line number exact. (4) computeRarity (api.js:881-897) only spreads {...t, rarityScore} then {...t, rank, rankApproximate}; it never sets price. (5) enrichWithListing (App.jsx:172-185) is the sole writer of price from the listings feed, and its only call sites are App.jsx:395 (selectedEnriched, the modal) and App.jsx:505 (addToCart) — both build new objects, allTokens is never rewritten. (6) The fallback path is no escape: constants.js:212-222 FALLBACK_NFTS also carry price: null. An in-repo comment at components/Gallery.jsx:35 independently confirms "normalizeToken hard-sets price:null, so the listings feed is the only source of a gallery card's price"; Gallery does its own local tokens.map() merge (Gallery.jsx:42-60), Watchlist does not. Therefore Watchlist.jsx:175 `data.targetPrice && nft.price && ...` is permanently falsy, the price span at :188 never renders, and the "Below target price!" badge at :212-216 is unreachable — while the subtitle at :127 says "set price alerts" and EmptyState.jsx:38 says "track price changes and get alerts". STRENGTHENING the finding: I traced targetPrice/target_price across frontend, api/ and supabase/ — Watchlist.jsx:175 is its ONLY consumer. It is persisted to localStorage (:103) and to Supabase watchlist.target_price (lib/userdata.js:274,293) and read back in syncWatchlist (:257) only to refill the input. There is no server-side job or notification path, so the alert cannot fire from anywhere, not merely "not in this component". LIMITING context (does not rescue it): a genuinely working alert engine exists on a different tab — components/PriceAlerts.jsx:31-160, wired once at App.jsx:686 — which polls fetchCollectionStats().floor every 30s and sends real notifications, and is honest about its basis (comment at PriceAlerts.jsx:28-30). A user in the Watchlist gets no hint that live alerting lives elsewhere under a different model (collection floor, not this token's list price). Severity medium stands: a dead, database-persisted control plus UI copy describing behaviour the code does not have, with no failure signal to the user. Minor scope note not claimed by the finding: watchedNfts = tokens.filter(...) (Watchlist.jsx:114) means a watched token that has not yet been paginated into allTokens does not render a card at all.
verdicts.correction: The finding is accurate as written, including every line number (App.jsx:763, api.js:147, api.js:881-897, App.jsx:395/505, Watchlist.jsx:127/175/188/212-216, EmptyState.jsx:38). Two refinements for the report: (a) it is stronger than stated — targetPrice has NO consumer anywhere in the repo other than Watchlist.jsx:175 (verified across frontend/, api/, supabase/), so no server-side job could fire it either, even though the value is written to Supabase watchlist.target_price via lib/userdata.js:274,293; (b) it should note that a separate, genuinely functional FLOOR-price alert engine does exist on the "alerts" tab (components/PriceAlerts.jsx:31-160, wired at App.jsx:686) — this does not make the Watchlist control work, but the fix is plausibly to route the Watchlist target into that engine, or to merge the listings feed onto allTokens the way Gallery.jsx:42-60 already does locally.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on the mechanics, with one part of the framing mis-aimed.

Chain verified end to end: App.jsx:763 passes tokens={nfts.allTokens}; useNfts.js:190 returns allTokens = rankedTokens; rankedTokens = computeRarity(tokens...) (useNfts.js:148-151); computeRarity (api.js:848-897) adds only rank/rarityScore/rankApproximate; tokens come from fetchTokens -> normalizeToken, which hardcodes price: null (api.js:147). The Alchemy-failure fallback is not an escape either: every FALLBACK_NFTS entry is price: null (constants.js:212-223). enrichWithListing (App.jsx:172-190) is applied only at App.jsx:395 (modal selection) and App.jsx:505 (cart add). No code anywhere assigns .price onto a token object (grep for `.price =` returns zero hits in the surface). So in Watchlist nft.price is always null: belowTarget (line 175) is permanently false, the price span (188) never renders, the "Below target price!" badge (212-216) is unreachable.

Corroborated by two in-repo comments that state the same fact: Gallery.jsx:35 ("normalizeToken hard-sets price:null, so the listings feed is the only source of a gallery card's price") — Gallery does the merge locally at 43-49, Watchlist never got it; and PriceAlerts.jsx:28-30 ("Individual token prices aren't available from the NFT metadata API, so alerts trigger based on floor price changes").

Maintainer defenses and why they fail:
(1) "The `nft.price &&` guard is correct failed-read honesty." This one HOLDS — omitting an unknown price is right, which is why the finding is slightly mis-aimed at line 188. It does not excuse the affirmative copy at line 127 and EmptyState.jsx:38, nor a labeled TARGET PRICE (ETH) input.
(2) "Alerts exist, in the Alerts tab; the Watchlist target is just an annotation." Fails on wiring. updateTarget (Watchlist.jsx:100-112) writes only to `${slug}_watchlist` localStorage and the user_watchlist Supabase table via addWatchlistRemote. Grepping every "watchlist" consumer outside the component yields only the tab registry (App.jsx:93/762, constants.js:93), nav labels (Header.jsx:144, MobileNav.jsx:19), EmptyState copy, and userdata.js persistence (240-303) — nothing reads targetPrice. usePriceAlerts().addAlert is never called from Watchlist, and PriceAlertPanel reads a different storage key (`${slug}_price_alerts`, PriceAlerts.jsx:11-13). The floor-based engine does not know Watchlist targets exist.
(3) "It self-heals when listings are merged." Dead-code-until-someday is the class being closed.

Verdict: not refuted. Scenario reproduces exactly as written.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate framing: the defect is the dead control plus the alert copy, not the missing price display. The absent price at line 188 is honest behaviour (an unknown price renders as nothing) and should not be cited as the bug. The real defect is that TARGET PRICE (ETH) (Watchlist.jsx:193-200) is a fully dead input — its value is persisted to localStorage AND to the user_watchlist Supabase table (userdata.js:290), then read by exactly one expression in the entire app, `belowTarget` at line 175, which can never be true because nft.price is structurally null on this prop — while the header (line 127, "Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts") and the empty state (EmptyState.jsx:38, "track price changes and get alerts") promise alerting twice.

Sharpening that strengthens the finding: even in the hypothetical where listings WERE merged onto allTokens, belowTarget is render-only. It toggles a CSS class and an inline badge visible solely while the Watchlist tab is mounted and on screen. There is no toast and no sendLocalNotification call anywhere in Watchlist.jsx, unlike PriceAlerts.jsx which does notify. So "get alerts" would remain overstated even after the price merge; a complete fix needs both the listings merge (mirroring Gallery.jsx:43-49 / App.jsx:172-190) and a notification path, or the copy and the input should be removed.

Severity stays medium: no false factual claim about a token is rendered (nothing is laundered into a confident number), but a feature the UI explicitly sells is a silent no-op, and the user harm in the scenario — a missed fill on a target they set and saw persist across devices — is real.

Adjacent defect found in the same file while verifying, worth reporting separately: watchedNfts = tokens.filter((t) => watchedIds.has(t.id)) at Watchlist.jsx:114 renders only watched tokens present in the currently loaded page set. Nakamigos is supply 20000 paginated at 40 per page, and useNfts.js:100-101 auto-loads further pages only when collection.supply < 1000. After a page reload the watchlist grid renders empty or partial even though localStorage and the Supabase user_watchlist row still hold every entry — the user's saved items appear to have been deleted, with no "loading" or "N items not yet loaded" indication.

survived.title: Watched NFTs outside the loaded token window silently vanish, and the add-search reports them as "No results found"
survived.claim: watchedNfts is `tokens.filter(t => watchedIds.has(t.id))` (line 114) over nfts.allTokens, which for Nakamigos is only what has been paged in — useNfts loads 40 at a time and auto-loads the rest only for collections under 1,000 supply (hooks/useNfts.js:101). Unlike Deals, Listings and TraitExplorer, Watchlist is given neither `loadAll` nor `hasMore` (App.jsx:763 vs 736/749/753). A watched token that has not been paged in is dropped from the grid with no message: the EmptyState only renders when watchlist.length === 0 (line 167), so the user gets a header over an empty grid. The add-search has the same blind spot and states it as fact — searching an unloaded token id yields 'No results found' (lines 144-150). Favorites.jsx:74-77 handles the identical situation honestly with an explicit '{n} favorited NFTs not yet loaded' note.
survived.failure_scenario: A user watchlists Nakamigos #14231 and #9902, closes the tab, and returns the next day landing directly on /nakamigos/nakamigos/watchlist. Only the first ~40 tokens are loaded, so the grid is blank and no empty state explains why — the watchlist appears to have been wiped. The user opens '+ Add to Watchlist', types 14231, and is told 'No results found', which reads as a statement that the token does not exist.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass loadAll/hasMore through and render Favorites' 'not yet loaded' notice for the shortfall; make the search fall back to a fetch-by-id (App.jsx already has a fetch-by-id path for deep links at ~line 452) before printing 'No results found'.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every load-bearing line in the claim was read and matches.

1. `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/Watchlist.jsx:114` — `const watchedNfts = useMemo(() => tokens.filter((t) => watchedIds.has(t.id)), [tokens, watchedIds]);`. `tokens` is `nfts.allTokens` (App.jsx:763), i.e. `rankedTokens` = only the pages fetched so far (useNfts.js:190). A watched id that has not been paged in is silently dropped from the grid.

2. `frontend/src/nakamigos/App.jsx:763` — `<Watchlist tokens={nfts.allTokens} onPick={...} addToast={...} setTab={...} wallet={wallet} />`. No `loadAll`, no `hasMore`, and also no `loading`. Contrast Listings (749) and TraitExplorer (753), which both receive `loadAll={nfts.loadAll} hasMore={nfts.hasMore}`. Grepping App.jsx for `loadAll` shows it is only ever passed as a prop (706/736/749/753) — never invoked at app level — so nothing pre-loads the full set for a user who lands directly on the watchlist route.

3. `frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useNfts.js:29-35` — `limit: 40` per page. `useNfts.js:101` — `const shouldAutoLoad = collection.supply && collection.supply < 1000;`. This is actually STRONGER than the finding states: every shipped collection is over 1,000 (constants.js:34 nakamigos supply 20000, :55 gnssart 9696, :71 junglebay 5555), so the auto-load branch is dead for all three collections, not just Nakamigos.

4. `Watchlist.jsx:167` — `{watchlist.length === 0 && !showSearch && (<EmptyState type="watchlist" .../>)}`. The gate is on the stored id list, not on the rendered set, so a non-empty watchlist whose members are all unloaded renders the header (`WATCHLIST` / "Track Nakamigos NFTs and set price alerts", lines 124-132) over a completely empty `.watchlist-grid`. No empty state, no loading note, no "not yet loaded" note.

5. `Watchlist.jsx:45-54` and `144-150` — `searchResults` filters the same partially-loaded `tokens` array, and when `search.length > 0 && searchResults.length === 0` it renders the literal string "No results found". Typing a token id that exists on-chain but has not been paged in produces that sentence as a statement of fact. This is the sweep's target defect class: an incomplete read rendered as a confident negative answer.

6. `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/Favorites.jsx:74-77` handles the identical situation honestly: `{favoriteNfts.length < safeFavorites.length && (... "{n} favorited NFTs not yet loaded. Scroll the gallery to load more." )}`. So the honest pattern already exists in this codebase, one component over.

7. Routing supports the direct-landing scenario: `constants.js:93` lists `"watchlist"` among valid tabs and App.jsx:108 documents the `/:collection/:tab` route mapping, so `/nakamigos/nakamigos/watchlist` is reachable cold.

Failure scenario confirmed end to end: cold load on the watchlist route → 40 of 20,000 tokens present → any watched id above ~40 is invisible → header over blank grid with no explanation (looks wiped) → "+ Add to Watchlist" → type the id → "No results found".

Severity medium is right, not higher: the underlying data is safe in localStorage/Supabase (loadWatchlist at :10-12, sync at :31-40), nothing is deleted, and no money moves. But two distinct user-visible harms exist and the second is the sharper one — "No results found" is an affirmative factual claim about the collection that a partial read produces. Not lower than medium because there is zero signal distinguishing "not loaded" from "not there": Watchlist isn't even given `loading` or `hasMore`, so it cannot say "still loading" either.

Two small refinements to the write-up: (a) the impact is not Nakamigos-specific — no configured collection is under the 1,000 auto-load threshold, so this affects gnssart and junglebay too; (b) the EmptyState gate is `watchlist.length === 0 && !showSearch`, so opening the add-search also suppresses it — immaterial to the outcome.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written, with the scope understated. Corrected version: Watchlist (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/Watchlist.jsx:114) renders only watched tokens present in the partially-paged `nfts.allTokens`, and App.jsx:763 gives it neither `loadAll`, `hasMore`, nor `loading` — unlike Listings (App.jsx:749) and TraitExplorer (App.jsx:753). Because useNfts.js:101 gates auto-pagination on `collection.supply < 1000` and NO configured collection qualifies (constants.js:34 = 20000, :55 = 9696, :71 = 5555), the auto-load path is dead for every collection, so this is not Nakamigos-specific. On a cold landing at /:collection/watchlist only 40 tokens exist, so watched tokens above that window disappear from the grid while the EmptyState stays suppressed (Watchlist.jsx:167 gates on `watchlist.length === 0`), leaving a "WATCHLIST" header over an empty grid that reads as a wiped list. The add-search (Watchlist.jsx:45-54, 144-150) searches the same partial array and prints "No results found" — an affirmative factual claim produced by an incomplete read. Favorites.jsx:74-77 already implements the honest counterpart ("{n} favorited NFTs not yet loaded. Scroll the gallery to load more."). Severity: medium.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every cited line checks out. Watchlist.jsx:114 filters `tokens` (App.jsx:763 passes only `nfts.allTokens` — no loadAll, no hasMore, no loading, unlike Deals :736 / Listings :749 / TraitExplorer :753). useNfts.js:29-35 pages 40 at a time; the auto-load-the-rest branch is gated on `collection.supply < 1000` (useNfts.js:101) and ALL THREE shipped collections fail that gate (constants.js:34 = 20000, :55 = 9696, :71 = 5555), so the partial window is this tab's default state, not an edge case. EmptyState is gated on `watchlist.length === 0` (line 167) so out-of-window entries produce a header over a blank grid with no message. searchResults (lines 45-54) shares the window and additionally excludes already-watched ids (line 50), so an unloaded watched id is filtered twice and renders the bare factual sentence 'No results found' (lines 144-150). Favorites.jsx:74-77 implements the honest disclosure for the identical situation in the same codebase, which defeats any 'that is just how the pattern works' defense.

The maintainer's strongest defense — that wiring loadAll would fire ~500 sequential paged requests through a rate-limited proxy to render 3 cards, which is why only the whole-set-computing tabs get it — is legitimate as an argument against loadAll, but does not justify silence, and does not even justify the missing data: App.jsx:388 already uses `fetchTokensByIds([id], ...)` to pull a single out-of-window token for deep links, so the correct fix is cheaper than the thing the defense argues against. The 'data is never lost' defense (localStorage line 14 + syncWatchlist lines 31-40) is true but irrelevant to what the user is shown.

Two aggravating facts the finding omitted: (1) an unloaded watched item is unmanageable, not merely invisible — remove (line 184), target price (line 199) and note (line 208) all live on the card, so the user cannot see it, cannot re-add it (search denies it exists), cannot delete it, and syncWatchlist resurrects it across devices; the 'Below target price!' badge (lines 175, 212-216) can never fire, so an alert the user believes they set is silently inert. (2) On upstream failure this becomes true failed-read laundering: api.js:170 returns FALLBACK_NFTS with `continuation: null` when Alchemy is down for Nakamigos — 12 hardcoded entries, ids '0'-'11', price null, image null, with invented hardcoded rank values (constants.js:211-224) — hasMore goes false so the window never grows, and 'No results found' is then produced directly by the failed read for every token in the collection, with no failure signal in this tab.

Severity medium is correct: no funds at risk and no data destroyed, but the user sees an empty grid where saved items should be, is told a token they watch does not exist, and holds an entry they cannot remove or alert on; under API failure the false statement is served with zero degradation signal.
verdicts.correction: Watchlist renders only the intersection of the user's saved ids with the ~40-token first page, with no disclosure and no way to widen it from this tab. Because the auto-load-remaining gate (`supply < 1000`, useNfts.js:101) excludes all three shipped collections (constants.js:34/55/71), this is the tab's default state rather than an edge case. Out-of-window entries are invisible (Watchlist.jsx:114 + empty-state gate at :167), unremovable and un-editable (remove/target/note controls only exist on the card, lines 184/199/208), and their target-price alerts never evaluate (line 175); the add-search reports them as 'No results found' (lines 144-150), which is doubly blind because line 50 also filters out already-watched ids. When the token API fails, allTokens collapses to 12 hardcoded fallback entries with continuation null / hasMore false (api.js:170, constants.js:211-224), and 'No results found' becomes a false factual statement generated directly by the failed read. Favorites.jsx:74-77 already implements the honest disclosure and App.jsx:388's fetchTokensByIds already implements the cheap targeted per-id fetch that fixes this without paging 20,000 tokens.

survived.title: Cross-device favorites and watchlist restore is blocked by RLS, and renders as "you have none"
survived.claim: syncFavorites (line 192-196) and syncWatchlist (line 239-243) read through the anon Supabase client. That client carries only the anon key — the SIWE JWT lives in an httpOnly cookie and is attached server-side only by proxyWrite, as lib/supabase.js:91-98 states explicitly ('The Supabase client uses the anon key for READ operations only'). But the live SELECT policies are owner-scoped: frontend/supabase/migrations/002_native_orders_trades_push.sql:156-163 defines 'Owner reads favorites' and 'Owner reads watchlist' as `wallet = lower(current_setting('request.jwt.claims',true)::json->>'wallet')`, which is NULL for the anon role, so the query returns zero rows. Both functions also destructure `const { data } = await ...`, discarding the error, so a genuine failure is indistinguishable. remoteIds/remoteMap are therefore always empty; merged collapses to the local list, and every visit re-UPSERTs the whole local set as 'local-only'.
survived.failure_scenario: A user favourites 30 Nakamigos and watchlists 8 on their desktop; both are pushed to Supabase successfully via proxyWrite. They open memetic.fun on their phone and connect the same wallet. The Favorites tab renders 'No Nakamigos favorites yet — Click the heart on any Nakamigos NFT to save it here' and the Watchlist renders 'Watchlist is empty', both stating as fact that the user has saved nothing, while their rows sit intact in the database. The writes keep succeeding, so the data accumulates in a store the app can never read back.
survived.suggested_fix: Route these two reads through /api/supabase-proxy (which already forwards the cookie JWT and satisfies the owner-scoped policy) instead of the anon client, and stop discarding the `error` so a failed read can be distinguished from an empty one.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at file:line. (1) userdata.js:192-196 (syncFavorites) and :239-243 (syncWatchlist) read user_favorites/user_watchlist through the module-scope anon client. (2) supabase.js:96-98 creates that client with only the anon key — no global headers, no auth.setSession; a grep for `supabase.auth|setSession|accessToken|persistSession` across frontend/src returns zero hits (only unrelated `sessionChecked` state in useSiweAuth.js). So the read carries claims {role:"anon"} with no `wallet`. (3) The live SELECT policy is owner-scoped: 004_security_hardening.sql:157-165 `lower(wallet) = lower(current_setting('request.jwt.claims',true)::json->>'wallet')` (supersedes the identical-intent 002_native_orders_trades_push.sql:155-163 cited in the finding). With no wallet claim the predicate is NULL and every row is filtered. (4) Independent in-repo confirmation: frontend/api/supabase-proxy.js:63-67 states "SELECT through the proxy exists ONLY for DMs: their RLS hides rows from the anon key… Every other table stays write-only here (public reads go straight to PostgREST with the anon key, as before)" with SELECT_TABLES = {"dm_messages"}. That "as before" holds for messages/user_profiles/votes (all FOR SELECT USING(true) at 002:150,153,166) but NOT for user_favorites/user_watchlist — the repo diagnosed this exact class for DMs and left these two tables behind. (5) User-visible copy confirmed: EmptyState.jsx:30-31 "No {collection} favorites yet" / "Click the heart on any {collection} NFT to save it here." and :37 "Watchlist is empty", rendered from the merged (local-only) list via App.jsx:623-633 and Watchlist.jsx:31-40. (6) No read-side test exists; frontend/api/__tests__/supabase-proxy.test.js and api/_lib/__tests__/proxy-schemas.test.js cover user_favorites INSERT only.

MIS-STATED DETAIL (mechanism, not conclusion): the finding blames `const { data } = await ...` discarding `error` for making failure indistinguishable. That discard is real but is NOT what produces the empty result. 008_grant_new_table_roles.sql:18 grants SELECT on all public tables to anon, so there is no 42501 — PostgREST returns HTTP 200 with [] and error === null. RLS filters the rows silently. Accurate version: this is a structurally impossible read that returns a well-formed empty success; adding `if (error)` handling would not surface it, only routing the read through the SIWE proxy (adding these tables to SELECT_TABLES) would.

Secondary effects confirmed: localOnly at :202 and :263 is the entire local set on every wallet-connect/collection-change, so the whole local set is re-UPSERTed each visit; and the watchlist merge at :257-258 means a remote-only target_price/note can never be restored. Nothing destructive occurs on the second device (removeFavoriteRemote is per-token; the merge never issues a remote delete), so data is stranded, not lost — severity medium is correct, not high.
verdicts.correction: Severity and conclusion stand; the mechanism should be restated. The reads do not fail with an error that gets swallowed — anon HAS the table GRANT (008_grant_new_table_roles.sql:18), so PostgREST returns HTTP 200 with an empty array and error === null. The owner-scoped SELECT policy (004_security_hardening.sql:157-165, superseding 002:155-163) silently filters every row because the anon key's JWT has no `wallet` claim. The discarded `error` in the `const { data } = await ...` destructure is a secondary robustness gap, not the cause: correct error handling would not detect this. Also cite frontend/api/supabase-proxy.js:63-67 — SELECT_TABLES = {"dm_messages"} with a comment explaining that owner-scoped RLS hides rows from the anon key and asserting "public reads go straight to PostgREST with the anon key, as before"; that assertion is true for messages/user_profiles/votes but false for user_favorites/user_watchlist, which is precisely the gap. The fix is to add these two tables to SELECT_TABLES and route syncFavorites/syncWatchlist reads through proxy SELECT, not to add error handling.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified every link at source. (1) The anon client is genuinely anon-only: frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/supabase.js:96-98 creates it with just the anon key, there is no setSession or global Authorization header anywhere in frontend/src/nakamigos/**, and siweAuth.js:119-123 getStoredToken() returns null unconditionally with the comment "It will be removed once Supabase queries go through a server proxy". (2) The live SELECT policies on user_favorites/user_watchlist are wallet-scoped — the finding cites 002:156-163, but those are dropped and recreated at 004_security_hardening.sql:157-165 as lower(wallet) = lower(current_setting('request.jwt.claims',true)::json->>'wallet'). For the anon role the claim is NULL, so the predicate is NULL, so zero rows. (3) anon does hold GRANT SELECT (008_grant_new_table_roles.sql:18), so this is a clean successful empty read, not a 42501 error. (4) There is no alternative read path: api/supabase-proxy.js:67 sets SELECT_TABLES = new Set(["dm_messages"]) and lines 157-159 reject SELECT on any other table with 400. DMs hit the identical RLS problem and got a proxy read; favorites/watchlist never did. (5) The write side genuinely lands — api/_lib/proxy-schemas.js:103 arrayable() exists specifically for this, its comment naming user_favorites/user_watchlist as the typical array-upsert writers. So remoteIds/remoteMap at userdata.js:198/245 are permanently empty, merged collapses to local, and localOnly at :202/:263 is always the whole local set, re-UPSERTed on every wallet connect (App.jsx:636-646) and collection switch (Watchlist.jsx:31-40). Empty-state copy is confirmed at components/EmptyState.jsx:30-31 and :37-38.

Three corrections to the write-up: (a) the live policy citation should be 004:157-165, not 002:156-163; (b) the "discarded error makes failure indistinguishable" point is true but nearly moot — the SUCCESS path already returns zero rows with error === null, so fixing error handling alone changes nothing, and the swallowed error is not the defect; (c) scope is narrower than implied — user_profiles and votes use USING (true) (002:152-153, :165-166) and do sync cross-device, so only user_favorites and user_watchlist are affected. Precondition worth noting: proxyWrite requires the siwe_jwt cookie, so the "rows sit in the DB" half only applies to users who completed a SIWE sign-in via chat/DMs/offers; a connect-only user writes nothing and simply gets no sync.

Severity medium stands but at the low end. A shipped feature that has never worked, with an empty state asserting "No {collection} favorites yet / Click the heart on any {collection} NFT to save it here" against a DB holding the user's rows, plus a docstring (userdata.js:10) promising persistence "across devices". No money path, no false claim about a token or third party, and no local data loss (the union-only merge never shrinks the local list). This is better classified as misleading control/copy than as failed-read laundering — the read does not fail, it is authorized to see nothing.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: cross-device restore of favorites and watchlist can never work, because the only read path is the anon Supabase client (lib/supabase.js:96-98; siweAuth.js:119-123 returns no token) while the live SELECT policies are wallet-scoped (004_security_hardening.sql:157-165, superseding 002:156-163), and the write proxy's SELECT allowlist covers only dm_messages (api/supabase-proxy.js:67, rejected at :157-159). The query succeeds with error === null and zero rows, so remoteIds/remoteMap (userdata.js:198/245) are always empty, merged collapses to the local list, and the entire local set is re-UPSERTed as "local-only" (userdata.js:202/:263) on every wallet connect and collection switch. Writes do land (proxy-schemas.js:103 arrayable() exists for exactly this), so rows accumulate in a store the app cannot read back. The discarded `error` is a secondary nit, not the cause. Scope is limited to user_favorites and user_watchlist; user_profiles and votes use USING (true) and sync fine. The "rows sit in the DB" half requires the user to have completed a SIWE sign-in (proxyWrite needs the siwe_jwt cookie); a connect-only user simply gets no sync at all. User impact: the Favorites and Watchlist tabs state "No {collection} favorites yet" / "Watchlist is empty" (EmptyState.jsx:30-31, :37-38) on a second device while the rows exist server-side, contradicting the module's own "across devices" promise (userdata.js:10).

survived.title: Realized P&L silently excludes sales it could not match to a purchase, and the count that explains it is never rendered
survived.claim: When a sale has no matching prior buy (truncated 100-record history, mint, or an off-contract acquisition), calculatePnL deliberately excludes it from realizedPnL and increments realizedUnmatchedSells instead — with the in-code comment 'surface the count separately' (lines 241-247). It is returned at line 255 and covered by lib/portfolio.test.js:68,78, but grep across the whole nakamigos tree shows the field is read nowhere in any component: PortfolioTracker.jsx:419-421 renders `pnlData.realizedPnL` under the header 'REAL. P&L' with no caveat and no footnote.
survived.failure_scenario: A user minted 20 Nakamigos and has since sold 15 of them for 30 ETH total. No buy record exists for any of them, so all 15 sales land in realizedUnmatchedSells and realizedPnL stays 0. The COLLECTION BREAKDOWN row renders 'REAL. P&L 0' — telling a user who realised 30 ETH that they have realised nothing, with no indication that 15 sales were dropped from the calculation.
survived.suggested_fix: Render the realizedUnmatchedSells count next to REAL. P&L (e.g. '0  ·  15 sales excluded — cost basis unknown'), which is what the library already computes it for.

verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED at every cited line; nothing to refute. (1) portfolio.js:241-247 — the else branch excludes an unmatchable sale from realizedPnL and only increments realizedUnmatchedSells, with the in-code comment "surface the count separately". (2) portfolio.js:255 returns the field. (3) Grep for `realizedUnmatchedSells` across all of frontend/src returns ONLY portfolio.js (lines 225, 246, 255) and portfolio.test.js (lines 68, 78) — zero component reads, so the "surface the count separately" comment describes work never done. (4) PortfolioTracker.jsx:397 renders header "REAL. P&L"; :419-421 renders pnlData.realizedPnL with no caveat, no footnote, no title attribute. The scenario reproduces: mints do not appear in Alchemy getNFTSales, so sortedBuys is empty, all 15 sells hit line 246, realizedPnL stays 0. The panel does render because the user still holds 5 tokens, so the tokens.length===0 early return at PortfolioTracker.jsx:279 is not hit. TWO WAYS THE FINDING UNDERSTATES SCOPE: (a) it cites only the breakdown row, but realizedPnL also feeds the headline hero card via PortfolioTracker.jsx:298 (totalPnL = unrealizedPnL + realizedPnL), rendered as "TOTAL P&L" at :337-343 WITH a USD conversion — so dropped proceeds corrupt the most prominent number on the page, not just a table cell. (b) The component demonstrably knows how to disclose this exact caveat: PortfolioTracker.jsx:345 is the ONLY title= tooltip in the file, reading "Estimated gas: ~0.003 ETH per purchased token (excludes mints/airdrops)" — the identical mint/airdrop caveat was written for the gas figure and omitted for realized P&L. ADJACENT, MORE SEVERE DEFECT NOT MENTIONED: portfolio.js:145-147 and :158-160 swallow failed Alchemy fetches leaving allSales/sellSales as [], and calculatePnL never rethrows, so the component error banner at PortfolioTracker.jsx:196-199 cannot fire for a sales-read failure. If the BUY fetch fails, every held token gets costBasis=0 (line 186) so unrealizedPnL equals the full floor value — a fabricated profit — and realizedPnL is 0 with every sale silently "unmatched". That is textbook failed-read laundering and warrants its own finding at higher severity. medium is correct for the finding as scoped.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written, but scoped too narrowly in two respects. First, the omission is not confined to the COLLECTION BREAKDOWN cell at PortfolioTracker.jsx:419-421: realizedPnL is also summed into the headline hero stat at PortfolioTracker.jsx:298 and rendered as "TOTAL P&L" at :337-343 together with a USD figure, so the excluded proceeds understate the single most prominent number on the page. Second, the codebase already knows how to disclose this caveat — PortfolioTracker.jsx:345 carries the only tooltip in the component, "Estimated gas: ~0.003 ETH per purchased token (excludes mints/airdrops)", i.e. the same mint/airdrop caveat was written for GAS (EST.) and omitted for REAL. P&L. Separately, a related and more severe defect should be filed against the same function: portfolio.js:145-147 and :158-160 catch a failed Alchemy sales fetch and leave allSales/sellSales as [], and calculatePnL never rethrows, so the error banner at PortfolioTracker.jsx:196-199 cannot fire. A failed BUY fetch therefore yields costBasis=0 for every held token (portfolio.js:186), making unrealizedPnL equal the entire floor value and presenting a broken upstream read as a large unrealized profit.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at file:line. frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/portfolio.js:241-247 increments realizedUnmatchedSells instead of adding the sale to realizedPnL, with the in-code comment "surface the count separately"; it is returned at line 255. Grep across all of frontend/src returns the identifier in only two files — portfolio.js (225, 246, 255) and portfolio.test.js (68, 78). It is read by ZERO components. PortfolioTracker.jsx:419-421 renders pnlData.realizedPnL under the header "REAL. P&L" (line 397) with no caveat, no tooltip, no footnote.

The strongest maintainer defense is that the exclusion is intentional and correct: it was added by F723 (test at portfolio.test.js:58-69) to stop a later rebuy being used as cost basis for an earlier sale, and counting unmatched proceeds as pure profit would be a worse lie than 0. That defense is sound — but it defends the COMPUTATION, not the PRESENTATION. The code's own comment promised a separate surface and that half was never built. The component already speaks this exact dialect elsewhere ("No gainers with known cost basis", PortfolioTracker.jsx:533 and 565; the gas tooltip at 345 that explicitly says "excludes mints/airdrops"), which proves the caveat idiom exists and was simply not applied here. So the argument does not hold as a defense of the finding.

The finding is real but UNDERSTATES its blast radius on two counts, and misses a same-function sibling defect.
verdicts.correction:
ACCURATE VERSION — three corrections, all widening the finding:

1. It is not only the breakdown row. PortfolioTracker.jsx:298 computes `totalPnL = pnlData.unrealizedPnL + pnlData.realizedPnL` and renders it as the hero "TOTAL P&L" card at lines 337-343, with a USD conversion at 299 (`totalPnL * (ethUsd || 3200)`). That is the single most prominent number on the tab. The silent exclusion propagates into it and into the dollar figure beneath it. The finding cites only 419-421.

2. The all-mints scenario (realizedPnL === 0) is the BENIGN case, not the worst one. A flat 0 at least looks suspicious to an attentive user. The dangerous case is MIXED: a user who sold 15 unmatched mints for 30 ETH plus one properly-matched token at +0.2 ETH sees "REAL. P&L +0.2" — a specific, plausible, non-zero number that carries no tell at all. There is nothing on screen to distinguish a complete answer from a 6%-complete one.

3. SIBLING DEFECT, same function, same render, arguably worse — portfolio.js:137-160. Both getNFTSales calls swallow their catch into `allSales = []` / `sellSales = []` (the only trace is a DEV-gated console.warn at 146 and 159). If the Alchemy sales endpoint 5xxs or the key is missing in prod, then: realizedPnL = 0, realizedUnmatchedSells = 0 (so even a wired-up count would report "nothing dropped"), purchaseMap is empty so every held token gets costBasis 0 (line 186), and unrealizedPnL becomes the FULL floor value of the portfolio as pure profit (line 251). A total upstream read failure therefore renders as "you are up your entire portfolio value and have realised nothing" — a confident, wholly fabricated answer. This means wiring up realizedUnmatchedSells alone does NOT make the tab honest; the fetch failures need to be distinguished from genuinely-empty results and surfaced as an error state.

4. Note the asymmetry the design has not reconciled: an unmatched SELL is excluded (conservative), but an unmatched HOLD gets costBasis 0 and is booked as a full-floor unrealized GAIN. Held mints do at least get a "MINT" badge in the expanded per-token view (PortfolioTracker.jsx:470-476), so there is partial disclosure there — but the hero TOTAL P&L absorbs it with none.

SEVERITY: medium is correct, hold it. It is a factual, uncaveated claim about the user's own money feeding the tab's headline figure, but it is informational only — no transaction is built, signed, or priced off it, and nothing is irreversible. Item 3 alone would justify medium independently.

MINIMAL HONEST FIX (not applied — this was read-only): render the unmatched count next to REAL. P&L (e.g. "REAL. P&L +0.2 · 15 sales excluded (cost basis unknown)"), and give calculatePnL a distinct failure signal for the two catches at 145 and 158 so an unreadable upstream renders as "could not load" rather than as zeros.

survived.title: Trade builder asserts the counterparty holds nothing when their inventory read failed
survived.claim: `loadInventory` collapses every failure to an empty array (`res?.tokens || []` at line 147, `catch { return [] }` at line 148), again losing fetchWalletNfts's error field. The YOU GET panel's emptyText then states 'No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet' (line 380), and YOU GIVE states 'No NFTs from the supported collections in your wallet' (line 323). This modal is opened from the Trades tab's '+ New trade offer', '+ Post to board', and Counter buttons (TradesPanel.jsx:681-715).
survived.failure_scenario: A user pastes a counterparty address into '+ New trade offer' during an Alchemy outage. The right panel reports the counterparty owns nothing from any supported collection. The user concludes the address is wrong or the holder sold out, and abandons a trade with a wallet that actually holds the tokens.
survived.suggested_fix: Track a per-side load error and render 'Couldn't read this wallet's inventory — retry' rather than a factual claim about holdings.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the files. api.js:648-663 shows fetchWalletNfts does NOT throw on API failure; it catches internally and returns {tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..."}. TradeWindow.jsx:144-150 reads only `res?.tokens || []` (line 147) and discards the .error field, with `catch { return [] }` (line 148) as a secondary net. SidePanel (TradeWindow.jsx:23-86) has only three branches — loading skeleton / tokens.length === 0 -> emptyText / grid — with no error state. `grep -n "error" TradeWindow.jsx` returns only lines 252-253 (trade-submit toast), confirming zero inventory-error handling in the component. Empty-state strings confirmed verbatim at :380 ("No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet") and :323 ("...in your wallet"). Entry points confirmed at TradesPanel.jsx:681 (builder), :690 (board builder), :705 (counter). Corroboration that this is a recognized defect class rather than a design choice: PortfolioTracker.jsx:161-167 handles the identical envelope with the comment "fetchWalletNfts returns { tokens:[], error } on an API outage — surface the retryable error state instead of a confident '0 NFTs' claim (F724)". TradeWindow was missed by that fix.
verdicts.correction: Two refinements. (1) Mechanism precision: the laundering happens at TradeWindow.jsx:147 (`res?.tokens || []` swallowing the error envelope) — that is the path an actual Alchemy outage takes, since fetchWalletNfts never throws for API failures. The `catch { return [] }` at :148 only covers unexpected throws (e.g. normalizeToken). The finding names both lines so the claim stands, but :147 is the operative line. (2) The finding understates scope in two ways. First, the YOU GIVE side (:323, loaded unconditionally at :156) is the more damaging half: if the user's OWN inventory read fails they are told they hold nothing from the supported collections, and because `give` stays empty the trade cannot be built at all — a false statement about their own holdings plus a hard dead-end. Second, partial failure is silent: Promise.all over COLLECTION_LIST with a per-collection catch (:144-149) means one failing collection renders a partial inventory as a complete one, with no empty state and no warning — a user can sign a trade believing their unshown tokens were ineligible. Accurate title: "Trade builder renders a failed inventory read as 'this wallet holds nothing' on both sides, and renders partial reads as complete." Severity medium is correct — a false factual assertion about wallet contents on a money-adjacent path, but it misleads rather than constructing a wrong-value transaction.

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed at source. api.js:660-663 shows fetchWalletNfts does NOT throw on an API outage — it returns {tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..."}. TradeWindow.jsx:147 does `res?.tokens || []`, reading tokens and discarding the error field; the `catch { return [] }` on line 148 is a near-dead secondary guard for this scenario. setTokens(batches.flat()) at line 150 yields [], and SidePanel (line 39) renders emptyText, which at line 380 is the flat factual sentence "No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet" and at line 323 "...in your wallet". Nothing in TradeWindow ever reads an error field; addToast is used only for submit results (lines 249-253).

The maintainer defense — that the per-collection try/catch is deliberate partial-failure tolerance so one bad collection doesn't blank the picker — is legitimate as far as it goes, but it only justifies not throwing, not discarding the error. The same codebase does it correctly for the identical return shape: PortfolioTracker.jsx:160-167 checks `if (nftData.error && nftData.tokens.length === 0)` and shows a retryable error instead of a confident zero, with a comment citing the prior fix. So "intentional" does not hold.

Two corrections to the finding as filed:
(1) The "+ Post to board" entry point does NOT reach line 380 — boardMode replaces the YOU GET SidePanel with the wildcard branch (TradeWindow.jsx:325-371). The "that wallet" copy reaches users via "+ New trade offer" (TradesPanel.jsx:683) and Counter (TradesPanel.jsx:706) only. Line 323's "in your wallet" does fire on all three.
(2) The finding understates the counter path. Counter mode seeds the `get` map from initialRequested (line 103), independent of theirTokens. SidePanel renders its header count from selected.size (line 27) but its body from tokens (line 39), so on a failed read the user sees a self-contradiction: "YOU GET (2/5)" above "No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet", and can still submit a trade for items the UI says don't exist.

Adjacent same-class defect, outside this finding's scope: OpenTradeAccept at TradesPanel.jsx:83-85 uses the identical `res?.tokens || []` / `catch {}` pair for wildcard slot inventory; on an outage `allPicked` (line 93) can never be satisfied, so accepting an open trade is silently impossible with no error shown.

Severity medium is correct — no funds move incorrectly and no wrong signature is produced from the bad read; the harm is user abandonment of a valid trade plus a contradictory UI.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: TradeWindow.jsx:147 (`return (res?.tokens || [])...`) silently discards the `error` field that api.js:660-663 returns on an Alchemy outage — fetchWalletNfts does not throw, so the `catch { return [] }` on line 148 is not the operative path. The resulting empty array makes SidePanel render emptyText as a factual claim: "No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet" (line 380, non-board mode) and "...in your wallet" (line 323, all modes). Entry points for line 380 are TradesPanel.jsx:683 ("+ New trade offer") and 706 (Counter); "+ Post to board" (690) uses boardMode, which renders the wildcard branch (325-371) instead. Additional user-visible symptom in the Counter path: the panel header count comes from `selected.size` (line 27) while the body comes from `tokens` (line 39), so a failed read produces "YOU GET (2/5)" directly above "No NFTs from the supported collections in that wallet". Fix is the PortfolioTracker.jsx:160-167 pattern: track a per-batch error and show a retryable message instead of the empty-state sentence when nothing loaded. Same defect also present at TradesPanel.jsx:83-85 (OpenTradeAccept), where it silently makes accepting an open trade impossible.

survived.title: Deals 'Buy' has no max-spend bound and the success toast asserts the displayed price was paid
survived.claim: `handleBuy` calls `fulfillSeaportOrder(nft)` which builds the transaction entirely from OpenSea's fulfillment_data response. `buildSeaportFulfillCall` validates that the value parses as a non-negative BigInt (api.js:1115-1121), pins the target to known Seaport addresses (api.js:1124-1130) and allowlists the function name (api.js:1136-1139) — but never compares `txValue` to the `listing.price` the row quoted, and returns it unbounded (api.js:1161). The user then signs whatever amount came back. On success the toast asserts `Purchased #<id> for <deal.price> ETH` (line 690) using the feed price, not the value actually sent, and recordTransaction persists that same unverified number into the History tab (lines 691-698).
survived.failure_scenario: A Deals row quotes 0.0850 ETH. Between the listings feed snapshot and the click, the order the feed points at is different (stale cache, re-listed at a higher price, or a manipulated/incorrect fulfillment_data payload). The wallet prompt shows a larger value that no longer matches the 0.0850 the user was looking at, and if they confirm, the toast and the History tab both still record 0.0850 ETH — the app tells them they paid the quoted price when they did not.
survived.suggested_fix: Reject the built call when `txValue` exceeds the quoted `listing.price` by more than a small tolerance (the same guard is missing on the shared path used by Listings and the cart), and report the actual sent value in the toast and in recordTransaction.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at every cited line, with two corrections (mechanism and scope).

Reproduced exactly:
- Deals.jsx:688 `fulfillSeaportOrder(nft)` (non-native rows); Deals.jsx:690 toast is verbatim `Purchased #${nft.id} for ${(nft.price ?? 0).toFixed(4)} ETH`; Deals.jsx:691-698 persists `price: nft.price` via recordTransaction.
- api.js:1115-1121 BigInt/non-negative check; api.js:1124-1130 Seaport address pin; api.js:1136-1139 function-name allowlist; api.js:1161 `return { to: txData.to, value: txValue, data: encoded }`.
- No amount bound exists repo-wide: grep for maxSpend|expectedPrice|maxValue|priceTolerance returns zero hits. fulfillSeaportOrder (api.js:1247-1256) passes call.value straight to sendTransaction.

CORRECTION 1 - the scenario's headline mechanism does not work. "Stale cache / re-listed at a higher price" cannot cause a silent overpay on the OpenSea path: fulfillment data is requested keyed by listing.orderHash (api.js:1099), and a Seaport order hash commits to the consideration amounts, so a re-listing at a different price is a different hash -> failed fulfillment data or a reverting tx, not a larger charge. The mechanisms that DO work are: (a) a tampered/compromised fulfillment_data response - exactly the threat the file's own comment at api.js:1132-1135 names to justify the function allowlist, leaving `value` as the one field it reasoned about and left unvalidated; (b) the NATIVE path, needing no tampering at all - displayed price comes from server column order.price_eth (api.js:741) while the charged amount is independently recomputed as the consideration sum (lib/orderbook.js:191-194). Two independent server fields, never reconciled.

CORRECTION 2 - scope understated ~5x. Not Deals-specific. Identical unbounded-value + feed-price-toast pattern at Listings.jsx:543-546, Modal.jsx:499-501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284 and :312-315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339 and :358-362. All six share buildSeaportFulfillCall.
