STRONGEST POINT, understated in the original: fulfillSeaportOrder returns `tx` (api.js:1256), so the ACTUAL value sent is in the caller's hand when the toast fires - every caller displays the unverified feed number instead. Deals.jsx also drops priceWei when building the row (copies orderHash/orderData/protocolAddress at :607-609 but not priceWei, which normalizeOpenSeaListings populates at api.js:692), discarding the exact quoted wei before the buy.

Severity stays medium, not higher: the wallet confirmation prompt displays the real value, so no silent drain - MetaMask is the backstop on the money half. Unmitigated is the reporting half: the History tab records a purchase price the app never verified and demonstrably could have. That is the failed/unverified-read-laundered-into-a-confident-fact class this sweep targets.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version: "All six Tradermigos buy surfaces sign an unbounded ETH amount and then report the feed's quoted price as the price paid."

buildSeaportFulfillCall (api.js:1089-1161) validates the tx value is a non-negative BigInt (1115-1121), pins the target to Seaport 1.5/1.6 (1124-1130) and allowlists the fulfillment function (1136-1139) — but never compares txValue to the listing price it was built for, returning it unbounded at 1161. The file's own comment at 1132-1135 reasons explicitly about a tampered API response encoding an arbitrary Seaport call; `value` is the field that reasoning skipped.

After the tx confirms, fulfillSeaportOrder returns `tx` (api.js:1256) — the actual value sent is available — yet Deals.jsx:690 toasts the feed price and Deals.jsx:691-698 persists it to the History tab. Same pattern at Listings.jsx:543-546, Modal.jsx:499-501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284/312-315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339/358-362.

Corrected failure scenario (the original's "re-listed at a higher price" is not viable — the Seaport order hash commits to the consideration amounts, so a re-list is a different hash and fails rather than overcharging):

NATIVE path, no attacker required. A native-orderbook row has price_eth = 0.0850 (api.js:741, what the Deals row displays) but a `parameters.consideration` blob summing to a different total. fulfillNativeOrder recomputes msg.value from the consideration sum (lib/orderbook.js:191-194) and never checks it against price_eth. The user sees 0.0850, signs the consideration total, and the toast plus the History tab both record 0.0850 ETH.

OPENSEA path, tampered/compromised proxy response. openseaPost returns fulfillment_data with an inflated `value`; target and function name pass their allowlists, amount is unchecked, and the user is prompted to sign it. If confirmed, History again records the quoted price.

Severity: medium (unchanged). The wallet prompt shows the true value, so this is not a silent drain — that caps it below high. The unmitigated half is the persisted false record: the app holds the verified amount in `result.tx` and writes the unverified one instead.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified against source. The code facts in the finding are accurate: buildSeaportFulfillCall (api.js:1089-1162) validates txValue only as a non-negative BigInt (1114-1121), pins the target to Seaport 1.5/1.6 (1124-1130) and allowlists the function name (1136-1139), then returns value unbounded (1161). No caller anywhere in frontend/src/nakamigos compares it to the quoted listing price (grepped maxValue|expectedPrice|maxSpend|priceWei across the surface). Deals.jsx:690 asserts "Purchased #<id> for <nft.price> ETH" from the feed snapshot, and 691-698 persists that same number via recordTransaction into localStorage (lib/transactions.js:14-36), which the History tab renders as the user's trade record. Deals' enriched row (Deals.jsx:600-614) copies orderHash/orderData/protocolAddress but drops priceWei, so it has no wei-exact price of its own. However the finding's severity rests on an overspend framing that does not survive scrutiny: (a) the wallet confirmation prompt displays the exact value and is the real max-spend bound; (b) Seaport refunds unused msg.value to the caller, so an inflated value over-reserves rather than overpays; (c) what actually determines the amount paid is the seller-signed order struct in input_data, not the value field. So no reproducible path to unbounded loss. What IS real and cheap to fix is the honesty half: fulfillSeaportOrder returns { success, hash, tx } (api.js:1262) and tx.value is the amount actually sent, but handleBuy destructures only success and hash and discards it, then makes a factual claim about a completed on-chain event sourced from a 60s-stale feed instead. Realistic trigger is a re-listed/stale order, not an attacker, and drift is typically small with a local-only record. Same pattern at Listings.jsx:546 (its toast at 547 is honest — it omits the number), so this is not Deals-specific. Accurate statement: "the Deals success toast and local History record the feed-quoted price rather than the value actually sent, which the returned tx object already carries." Severity low, not medium.
verdicts.correction: Retitle to "Deals success toast and History record the feed-quoted price, not the value actually sent". Drop the max-spend/overspend framing: the wallet prompt bounds the spend, Seaport refunds excess msg.value, and the amount paid is fixed by the seller-signed order struct in input_data rather than by the unbounded value field — so there is no reproducible loss path from the missing txValue-vs-listing.price comparison. The surviving defect is Deals.jsx:690-698 asserting a factual purchase amount from the 60s-refreshed listings snapshot when fulfillSeaportOrder already returns the real one (api.js:1262 returns { success, hash, tx }; tx.value is discarded). Realistic trigger is a stale/re-listed order rather than a manipulated fulfillment_data payload. Note Deals.jsx:600-614 drops priceWei from the row, so the fix should read result.tx.value, not the feed. Same pattern at Listings.jsx:546. Severity: low.

survived.title: Deals computes Fair Value and Key Traits from synthetic fallback tokens with no on-tab signal
survived.claim: When the Alchemy token read fails for Nakamigos, fetchTokens returns the 12 hardcoded FALLBACK_NFTS with `fallback: true` (api.js:168-170; constants.js:211-224). Those entries carry invented traits — 'Robot', 'Zombie', 'Antenna', 'Circuit Board' — that do not exist in the collection. Deals receives them as `tokens`, `tokens.length` is 12 so `isInitialLoading` clears (line 467), `hasMore` is false (continuation null), and the trait-floor engine runs over fabricated attributes (lines 504-533, 578-621), rendering them in the 'Key Traits' column (lines 987-1003) and using them to derive the 'Fair Value' and '% below' columns. Deals is passed no isLive/fallback flag (App.jsx:723-739). The global header badge is the only signal and it is OR'd — `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` (App.jsx:820) — so it still reads LIVE whenever the activity feed is healthy even though the token set fell back.
survived.failure_scenario: Alchemy's NFT API is down but the activity feed is fine. A user opens Deals. The header says LIVE. The tab either lists 'deals' whose Key Traits column shows trait values that do not exist in Nakamigos, with a Fair Value derived from them, or falls through to the 'All listings are priced at or above their trait floors' verdict computed over 12 fake tokens. Either way the user is shown a market analysis of synthetic data with no indication.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass the fallback flag through to Deals and refuse to compute deals from a fallback token set (or badge the tab as DEMO); at minimum make the header badge require both feeds to be live rather than either.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced the plumbing exactly as claimed, but the finding's headline mechanism is wrong. CONFIRMED: api.js:170 returns the 12 FALLBACK_NFTS with fallback:true for Nakamigos (constants.js:211-224); useNfts.js:40/57 sets isLive=false and hasMore=false; Deals.jsx:467 isInitialLoading=listingsLoading||tokens.length===0 clears at 12 tokens; App.jsx:720-736 passes Deals no isLive/fallback/listingsError prop; App.jsx:820 isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive} feeds Header.jsx:580-585, so the badge still reads LIVE when only the token read fell back. REFUTED: the claim that 'Robot'/'Zombie'/'Antenna'/'Circuit Board' render in Key Traits and drive Fair Value. Deals.jsx:544 (`if (d.count < 3) return null`) gates every trait floor at >=3 listed tokens sharing that trait. Across the 12 fallback entries those four values (plus 'Ape', 'LED', and EVERY Hair and Shirt/Jacket value) occur exactly once, so they can never produce a floor, never enter keyTraits (lines 588-598), and never set maxTraitFloor. Only Type::Human Pale (4), Mouth::Smile (4), Mouth::Flat (4) and Type::Human Tan (3) are even candidates, and only if >=3 of token IDs 0-11 out of 20,000 happen to be listed simultaneously. The fabricated-traits table is effectively unreachable. What survives is only the finding's second branch.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: when the Alchemy token read fails for Nakamigos, fetchTokens (api.js:170) substitutes 12 hardcoded synthetic tokens. Deals.jsx:467 treats that as a successful load (tokens.length===12), the trait-floor engine finds nothing usable because Deals.jsx:544 requires >=3 listed tokens per trait, so deals=[] and — with hasMore false (continuation null, useNfts.js:57) — Deals.jsx:768 renders the unhedged sentence "No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors." That is a factual market verdict produced by a failed read, and the header still shows LIVE because App.jsx:820 ORs the token-read liveness with the stats/activity liveness. Deals receives no fallback signal (App.jsx:720-736). The finding's specific claim about 'Robot'/'Zombie'/'Antenna'/'Circuit Board' appearing in the Key Traits column, and about Fair Value being derived from them, is wrong and should be dropped. Two related facts found while verifying, worth separate findings rather than folding in here: (1) data/rarity.json has totalTokens:0, so computeRarity falls to the runtime branch (api.js:862-895) and Deals.jsx:1006-1008 renders a fabricated rank 1-12 for the synthetic set while ignoring rankApproximate; (2) the same false verdict sentence fires on a much likelier path — fetchListings .catch()es both sources (api.js:795-804) and returns listings:[] with no error field, and useListings.js:33 only surfaces data.error/query error, so a full listings outage yields "All listings are priced at or above their trait floors." over the real token set with no error shown.

verdicts.reasoning: Partially refuted: the stated mechanism is wrong, the underlying defect is real via a different (and more likely) code path. REFUTED HALF: 'Key Traits shows Robot/Zombie/Antenna/Circuit Board and Fair Value is derived from them' cannot happen. Deals.jsx:544 (`if (d.count < 3) return null`) requires >=3 LISTED tokens sharing a trait before a trait floor is trusted. Across the 12 FALLBACK_NFTS (constants.js:211-223) every exotic value cited appears exactly once (Robot=1, Zombie=1, Ape=1, LED=1, Antenna=1, Circuit Board=1; all Hair and Shirt/Jacket values are unique), so getTraitFloorExcluding returns null for each, they never enter keyTraits (Deals.jsx:576-584) and never contribute to maxTraitFloor. Only Human Pale(4)/Human Tan(3)/Smile(4)/Flat(4) could ever reach count 3, and count only increments for tokens that also carry a real listing, so it additionally requires >=3 of token ids {0,4,8,11}/{2,6,10}/{0,2,6,10}/{1,4,8,11} to be listed at the same moment out of 20,000. The finding's separate implication about invented ranks is also refuted: computeRarity overwrites rank on every token (useNfts.js:147, api.js:848-897), so the hardcoded 8420/6230/... never render. CONFIRMED HALF (the real finding): with 12 fallback tokens, fetchTokens returns continuation null (api.js:170) so hasMore is false, and tokens.length=12 clears isInitialLoading (Deals.jsx:467). deals is then empty, Deals.jsx:747 takes the empty state, and because hasMore is false the ternary at :756 selects the confident arm at :768 - 'No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors.' That is a factual market verdict rendered from a token read that FAILED, over 12 synthetic entries; the hasMore hedge that exists specifically to soften that sentence is defeated because the fallback reports the set as complete. Deals receives no fallback/isLive prop (App.jsx:723-739), and the only global signal is OR'd - App.jsx:820 `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` with useCollection.js:75 deriving its isLive from stats+activity only - so with Alchemy down and the feeds healthy the header still reads LIVE (Header.jsx:580-585). WIDER SIBLING, same defect class, larger trigger: fetchListings catches the OpenSea failure and returns an empty set with no error marker (api.js:795-798), so useListings reports listingsError null; Deals is never passed listingsError regardless. Deals calls loadAll (Deals.jsx:481-483), so on real tokens hasMore eventually goes false and the identical :768 sentence renders while the listings read has failed outright. FAILURE SCENARIO (accurate version): Alchemy getNFTsForContract fails for the Nakamigos contract while stats/activity are healthy. User opens Deals. Header reads LIVE. Within ~1s the tab states 'No deals found right now. All listings are priced at or above their trait floors.' - a market-wide claim computed over 12 hardcoded placeholder tokens, with no on-tab indication that the collection was never read. Severity stays medium: one misleading declarative sentence on a whole-tab outage state, no money moved, but it is exactly the failed-read-laundering class this branch has been closing.
verdicts.correction: Title should be: 'Deals states "All listings are priced at or above their trait floors" when the token read failed'. The trait-floor engine does NOT render fabricated traits or a Fair Value derived from them - Deals.jsx:544 (count < 3 -> null) blocks every once-occurring fallback attribute, which is all of the invented ones, and computeRarity (useNfts.js:147) overwrites the invented ranks. The real defect is the empty-state verdict: FALLBACK_NFTS give continuation=null -> hasMore=false, so Deals.jsx:756 picks the confident arm at :768 instead of the hedged 'Scanning for deals...' arm, asserting a complete market analysis over 12 placeholder tokens. Compounding signals: Deals gets no fallback/isLive prop (App.jsx:723-739) and the header badge is OR'd so it still reads LIVE (App.jsx:820, useCollection.js:75, Header.jsx:580-585). The same :768 sentence also fires on fully-real tokens whenever the listings read fails, because fetchListings swallows the OpenSea error into an empty set with no error field (api.js:795-798) and Deals is never passed listingsError. Fix direction: pass the fallback/error state into Deals and gate the :768 sentence on a known-good tokens AND listings read.

survived.title: Empty state tells sellers to list on OpenSea, but this page only reads the native orderbook
survived.claim: The myListings empty state says "List your NFTs on OpenSea to see them here", but MyListings fetches exclusively from /api/orderbook (the native book) and never queries OpenSea — so following the instruction guarantees the page stays empty. The app's only listing-creation surface is native anyway.
survived.failure_scenario: A seller opens My Listings with no native listings. They see "No active listings — You don't have any active listings for this collection. List your NFTs on OpenSea to see them here." They go to OpenSea, list three NFTs, come back, and the page still says they have no listings — because MyListings.jsx:263-337 only ever calls `fetch('/api/orderbook?action=query&...')` and hardcodes `source: "native"` at line 323 (each row is labelled "Native" at line 656); `fetchMyListings` (the OpenSea reader in api-offers.js:615) is imported only by MyCollection.jsx, never here. Conversely, a seller who already has OpenSea listings is told they have none. The instruction is also pointing at the wrong product: the only listing path in the app is BulkListingWizard.jsx:9 → createNativeListing, so the correct guidance is the in-app listing flow.
survived.suggested_fix: Either scope the copy to this page's actual data source ("You have no active listings on the Tradermigos orderbook — list from Bulk List") with a link to the wizard, or additionally fetch OpenSea listings here via the existing fetchMyListings and label each row by source.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the files. EmptyState.jsx:82 defines the myListings empty state as "You don't have any active listings for this collection. List your NFTs on OpenSea to see them here." — the only OpenSea string in that file. It is consumed at exactly one call site, MyListings.jsx:611, rendered whenever activeListings.length === 0. MyListings.jsx reads only the native orderbook: fetch('/api/orderbook?...') at lines 290 and 292, every row stamped source: "native" at line 322 (finding said 323 — off by one), every row labelled "Native" at line 656. There is no OpenSea call in the file. The OpenSea reader fetchMyListings (api-offers.js:615, hitting orders/ethereum/seaport/listings) is imported only by MyCollection.jsx:5 and used at 130/165/521/536 — never by MyListings. There is also no OpenSea listing-creation path anywhere in frontend/src/nakamigos/ (grep for createListing|postListing|seaport.createOrder|listings/create returns nothing); the only creation path is BulkListingWizard.jsx:9 -> createNativeListing (lib/orderbook.js:313, bundle variant at 495). The page header at MyListings.jsx:543 is the unqualified "My Listings", so nothing signals the native-only scope. So both halves of the scenario hold: following the instruction cannot ever populate this page, and a seller with live OpenSea listings is told on an unqualified "My Listings" page that they have none. Severity lowered from medium to low: the finding overstates the blast radius by implying the seller's OpenSea listings are invisible app-wide — MyCollection does fetch and display them — so this is a single stale sentence of misdirecting copy on one page, with no money path, no signing, and no data loss. Adjacent (not part of this finding): the Cancel All tooltip at MyListings.jsx:594 says it increments the Seaport counter invalidating ALL open orders, which would also nuke the seller's OpenSea listings from a page that otherwise never acknowledges OpenSea.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: the myListings empty state (EmptyState.jsx:82) instructs sellers to list on OpenSea, but its sole consumer MyListings.jsx:611 reads only the native orderbook (fetch '/api/orderbook' at 290/292, source: "native" at 322 — not 323 — rows labelled "Native" at 656), so following the instruction can never populate the page, and a seller with active OpenSea listings is told under an unqualified "My Listings" header (543) that they have none. The app has no OpenSea listing-creation path at all; the only listing flow is BulkListingWizard.jsx:9 -> createNativeListing, which is the guidance the copy should point at. Scope correction: the seller's OpenSea listings are not invisible app-wide — MyCollection.jsx (via fetchMyListings, api-offers.js:615) does show them — so this is one page's stale copy, not a total blind spot. Severity low, not medium: misleading copy only, no transaction, fee, or fund-loss path.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by reading the files. frontend/src/nakamigos/components/EmptyState.jsx:79-82 defines the `myListings` empty state with description "You don't have any active listings for this collection. List your NFTs on OpenSea to see them here." That key is consumed at exactly one site: frontend/src/nakamigos/components/MyListings.jsx:611 (`<EmptyState type="myListings" />`).

MyListings reads the native book only. `fetchListings` (MyListings.jsx:263-337) issues only `fetch('/api/orderbook?...')` (plus an optional `bundles=true` variant gated by BUNDLE_LISTING_ENABLED) and hardcodes `source: "native"` at line 322; every rendered row is labelled "Native" at line 656. The OpenSea reader `fetchMyListings` (frontend/src/nakamigos/api-offers.js:615, which calls `openseaGet("orders/ethereum/seaport/listings", ...)`) is imported only by MyCollection.jsx:5 and called at MyCollection.jsx:130/165/521/536 — never by MyListings.

The two books are disjoint in both directions. frontend/api/orderbook.js action=query reads one Supabase table with `.eq("order_type","listing")` (line 448) and `.eq("contract_address", lc)` (line 483); the file mentions OpenSea only in comments (lines 231, 499) and there is no job ingesting OpenSea orders into that table. Conversely `createNativeListing` (frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/orderbook.js:313+) never posts the signed order to OpenSea (no "opensea" reference in that file). So an OpenSea listing can never reach /api/orderbook, and the instruction's outcome is a guaranteed dead end.

The guidance also points at the wrong product: the app's only listing-creation path is MyCollection.jsx:246 "Bulk List" -> BulkListingWizard.jsx:9 `createNativeListing`, which is also the only path that applies PLATFORM_FEE_BPS (BulkListingWizard.jsx:5). The copy routes sellers off the only fee-bearing rail.

Maintainer defenses examined and rejected: (a) "the app does read OpenSea, so the copy is fine" — true of MyCollection, false of this page, and the sentence says "to see them HERE"; (b) "the Native label discloses scope" — the label only exists on rows, and in the empty state there are zero rows, so scope is disclosed exactly nowhere at the moment it matters.

One clause of the finding is overstated and should be softened: "a seller who already has OpenSea listings is told they have none" is true on this page but not app-wide, since MyCollection does read the OpenSea book and will show those tokens as listed. The defect is a scoping mismatch phrased as a universal claim about the user's state, not a total blind spot.

Adjacent asymmetry observed while verifying (not a separate finding, but worth recording): the read here is native-only while the write is cross-venue — Cancel All (MyListings.jsx:592) increments the Seaport counter and its own tooltip says it invalidates "ALL open orders (listings + bids)", which includes OpenSea orders this page never displayed.

Severity medium holds: no funds at risk and no failed-read laundering (the degraded-read handling at MyListings.jsx:299-302 is actually correct — it keeps the screen and shows "Listings temporarily unavailable"), but it is user-visible copy stating a false universal plus an instruction whose only possible outcome is the emptiness it purports to resolve.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: the `myListings` empty state (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/EmptyState.jsx:82) instructs sellers to list on OpenSea, but MyListings.jsx renders exclusively from the native orderbook (`fetch('/api/orderbook?action=query&...')` at MyListings.jsx:263-337, `source: "native"` hardcoded at line 322), and /api/orderbook's query action reads only the native Supabase orders table with no OpenSea ingestion (frontend/api/orderbook.js:440-483). Following the instruction therefore cannot ever populate this page. The correct guidance is the in-app native flow: MyCollection.jsx:246 "Bulk List" -> BulkListingWizard.jsx:9 `createNativeListing`, which is also the only fee-bearing listing path. Soften one clause of the original: a seller with OpenSea listings is told "you don't have any active listings" ON THIS PAGE only — MyCollection.jsx:130/165 does read the OpenSea book via api-offers.js:615 `fetchMyListings` and will show those tokens as listed, so this is a page-scoped false universal rather than an app-wide blind spot. Severity: medium (unchanged).

survived.title: Hardcoded FALLBACK_STATS floor/owners/supply render as live market data with no cached badge
survived.claim: stats can be `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}` — a hardcoded floor of 0.1048 ETH, 5238 owners, 20000 supply. useCollection flags it precisely so the UI can badge it "cached", and Hero.jsx:127 does; Listings.jsx, MyListings.jsx and BidManager.jsx never read the flag and present the constants as live numbers.
survived.failure_scenario: Both the Alchemy stats call and the OpenSea stats fallback fail (api.js:277 returns `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true}` for the default collection); the same object is also the initial state on every mount (useCollection.js:17,22). The Listings FLOOR PRICE card (Listings.jsx:643-645) then shows a gold "0.1048" identical to a live read, OWNERS shows 5,238 (line 672-675) and SUPPLY 20,000 (line 677-681); unlisted cards show "Floor: 0.1048 ETH" (line 180); SweepCalculator receives it as the basis for its floor-estimate mode. The same constant propagates into MyListings.jsx:246 → the "Floor Price" summary tile (line 582-589), the "+X% from floor" chip (line 638-640) and the Near Floor/Above Floor/High badge, and into BidManager.jsx:681-685 where a received offer is stamped green "112% of floor". A seller reading "112% of floor" accepts an offer that may be far below the real floor; a buyer reads a fabricated floor as the market price. FALLBACK_STATS.floor of 0.1048 has no timestamp and no on-chain backing at all.
survived.suggested_fix: Thread `stats.fallback` into these three components and either suppress the floor-derived chips/badges or render the same "cached" treatment Hero.jsx:127 already uses. The floor-relative verdicts ("% of floor", "Near Floor", "At floor") should be hidden entirely when the floor is a fallback.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the files. constants.js:226-231 defines FALLBACK_STATS {floor:0.1048, volume:52200, owners:5238, supply:20000}. useCollection.js:16 builds FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED with fallback:true and uses it as the initial state (:22) and collection-switch reset (:46) for DEFAULT_COLLECTION="nakamigos" (constants.js:85); api.js:277 returns the same flagged object when both the Alchemy and OpenSea stats calls fail for the default contract. useCollection.js:68-71 spreads statsData, so the flag survives into `stats`. Hero.jsx:127 reads `stats.fallback` and renders <CachedTag/> at :181/:194/:204 — the comment at Hero.jsx:104-105 states the flag exists exactly for this disclosure (F582). grep for "fallback" in Listings.jsx / MyListings.jsx / BidManager.jsx returns only unrelated image-CDN fallbacks: none of the three reads the flag. Confirmed render sites: Listings.jsx:569 (`const floor = stats?.floor || null`) -> :643-645 gold FLOOR PRICE "0.1048" with no badge, :674 OWNERS "5,238", :680 SUPPLY "20,000", :180 per-card "Floor: 0.1048 ETH"; Listings.jsx:1058 passes stats to SweepCalculator, which at SweepCalculator.jsx:164,252-255 uses it as avgPrice/maxPrice and totalEth = floor*count under the label "Floor estimate"; MyListings.jsx:246 (`stats?.floor || 0`) -> :582-586 "Floor Price" tile, :638-639/:658 "+X% from floor", :634 + :208-215 Near Floor/Above Floor badge, :668-670 "N% above floor"; BidManager.jsx:681-683 renders `Math.round((offer.price/stats.floor)*100)}% of floor` colored green when offer.price >= stats.floor. Props threading confirmed at App.jsx:743 (Listings), :775 (BidManager), :777 (MyListings), all from useCollection() at :338. No global demo banner mitigates it: isLive is consumed only at App.jsx:757 (ActivityFeed) and :820. Severity medium is accurate — the number is advisory (offers still execute at the offer price, sweeps still buy real listings), so it misinforms a seller's accept/decline decision rather than mis-executing a transaction.
verdicts.correction: Two corrections, neither weakening the finding. (1) Line numbers: the flagged constant is defined at useCollection.js:16, not :17, and is applied at :22 and :46. (2) The finding understates the blast radius by crediting Hero.jsx as correct. api.js:253 injects FALLBACK_STATS.volume (52,200) on the SUCCESS path and returns it WITHOUT `fallback: true`, so Hero's CachedTag (gated on stats.fallback at Hero.jsx:127/:194) does not fire — Hero renders the hardcoded 52,200 as a live "ALL-TIME VOL" whenever the OpenSea volume sub-call is throttled or unavailable. That is the same laundering class in the one component the finding treats as the good example, and any fix should cover it (per-field provenance, not a single object-level flag). Accurate framing: the `fallback` flag exists and is honored in exactly one of four consumers, and even there it is bypassed by the per-field volume fallback at api.js:253.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at every cited line; the maintainer defense collapses on one decisive fact.

Steelman attempted: FALLBACK_STATS is a cached snapshot of a real collection, not a fabrication, and the team already solved the honesty problem — useCollection.js:14-16 carries an explicit F582 comment, wraps the constant as FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED, api.js:277 propagates `fallback: true`, and Hero.jsx:106-118 renders a CachedTag ("Cached estimate — live stats unavailable right now") on FLOOR (181), ALL-TIME VOL (194) and OWNERS (204). Secondary surfaces echoing the same figure could be argued as covered by that one disclosure, and MyListings/BidManager show absolute ETH alongside the derived chips.

Why it fails:
1. DECISIVE — Hero renders ONLY inside `case "gallery"` (App.jsx:694-697). `listings` (App.jsx:741-742), `my-listings` (777) and `bids` (775) are SEPARATE tabs in the same switch. The one surface that discloses is never co-rendered with the three that don't. The badge does not travel; a user on the listings tab never sees it.
2. Verified by grep: `fallback` appears zero times as a read in Listings.jsx, MyListings.jsx, BidManager.jsx. Listings.jsx:569 `const floor = stats?.floor || null` -> :644 gold floor value, :672-675 OWNERS, :677-681 SUPPLY, :180 "Floor: 0.1048 ETH" on unlisted cards. MyListings.jsx:246 `const floorPrice = stats?.floor || 0` -> :582-589 "Floor Price" tile, :634 getHealthBadge (Near Floor/Above Floor/High, defined :208-218), :638-640 distFromFloor chip. BidManager.jsx:681-685 "% of floor" green/red chip. All as claimed.
3. Listings.jsx:636 renders the literal subtitle "Live floor price and recent market activity for {collection.name}" — and that branch fires when `!hasRealListings`, exactly the degraded state where the fallback is most likely. The copy explicitly asserts "live" over a hardcoded constant.
4. The "transient placeholder" defense is false in the failure case: useCollection.js:75-78 catches and does nothing (leaves prior stats), and api.js:277 returns `{...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback:true}` on EVERY subsequent poll while both Alchemy and OpenSea are down. It persists indefinitely.
5. SweepCalculator.jsx:164 `stats?.floor ?? null` -> :252-255 "Floor estimate" mode uses it as avgPrice/maxPrice/totalEth basis. It labels the mode an estimate (:650) but never that the floor itself is a constant.

Money-path harm is real and one-sided: FALLBACK_STATS.floor of 0.1048 is LOW, so offers render as a HIGH percentage of floor. BidManager.jsx:682 colors it green whenever `offer.price >= stats.floor`, on the exact row carrying the Accept button (:690-696). A seller is nudged to accept below true market.
verdicts.correction:
Finding is substantively accurate; nothing material is misstated. Three refinements, two of which BROADEN it:

(a) UNDERSTATED EXPOSURE. The finding presents the double-API-failure path (api.js:277) as primary and the initial-state path as secondary. It is the reverse: useCollection.js:21-22 seeds FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED as initial state for DEFAULT_COLLECTION on every mount, and useCollection is mounted app-wide at App.jsx:338. So a direct load of /nakamigos?tab=listings paints floor 0.1048 / owners 5,238 / supply 20,000 with NO upstream failure at all, on 100% of sessions, for the duration of the first fetch. useCollection.js:46 re-seeds it on every collection switch too.

(b) MISSED, AND IT DEFEATS THE FIX ON HERO ITSELF. api.js:252-254 injects `FALLBACK_STATS.volume` (52,200) into an OTHERWISE-SUCCESSFUL stats read and returns it WITHOUT `fallback: true` (the success return at api.js:256-261 has no fallback key). The OpenSea volume call is the throttle-prone one (per the comment at :250-251, the landing fans out several collections at once). So when only volume is rate-limited, Hero.jsx:194 renders ALL-TIME VOL = 52,200 with NO cached tag — the F582 mechanism is bypassed on the single surface that implements it. constants.js:228 even warns the figure is historical-total, not 24h. This is a distinct, additional leak the finding did not catch.

(c) MINOR WORDING. "no on-chain backing at all" is imprecise — a floor is an orderbook figure and never has on-chain backing on any surface. The accurate complaint is no timestamp, no provenance, and no disclosure.

Severity MEDIUM is correct and should stand. It is a stale-cached-value disclosure gap, not a number invented from nothing; the absolute ETH price is shown adjacent in MyListings/BidManager; and the sustained-wrong state needs a degraded upstream (though the first-paint window needs nothing). The BidManager.jsx:681-685 accept-offer chip is the sharpest edge and is what keeps this from being low.

Correct fix shape (do not change any number): thread the existing `stats.fallback` flag into Listings.jsx, MyListings.jsx, BidManager.jsx and SweepCalculator.jsx and reuse Hero's CachedTag (promote it out of Hero.jsx into a shared component); change the Listings.jsx:636 subtitle so it stops saying "Live" when stats.fallback is set; and set `fallback: true` on the api.js:252-254 volume-substitution path so the one working badge stops being bypassed.

survived.title: Fabricated FALLBACK_ACTIVITY sales render unlabelled as "RECENT SALES"
survived.claim: When the activity APIs fail, api.js:554 substitutes four hand-written sample sales carrying `sample: true`. Nothing in the codebase reads that flag, and Listings renders them as a RECENT SALES grid plus a RECENT SALES count stat card, with specific token ids, ETH prices, and a time-ago string.
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea events and Alchemy getNFTSales both fail. api.js:552-556 sets `primaryResult = { activities: FALLBACK_ACTIVITY, fallback: true }`; useCollection.js passes `activities` straight through (only `isLive` records the fallback, and Listings is never given `isLive` — see App.jsx:743-746). Listings.jsx:378-412 builds recentSales from them, dropping the `sample: true` marker (constants.js:249-252) entirely. With no listings, the page renders the header "RECENT SALES (4)" (line 968), a stat card "RECENT SALES 4" (line 683-690), and four cards reading e.g. "#11007 — 0.1100 ETH sold" with a formatTimeAgo string. Every one of those trades is invented: `hash: null`, addresses truncated placeholders. A user reads fabricated trade prints as this collection's real sales history and prices their bid or listing against them. Grep confirms no consumer of the `sample` field exists anywhere in components/, hooks/ or lib/.
survived.suggested_fix: Filter `a.sample` out of Listings' recentSales, or propagate the flag onto the card and render an explicit "sample data — live sales unavailable" treatment (the FALLBACK_WHALES comment at constants.js:233-235 shows the intended pattern of visibly marking synthetic data).

Header.jsx:579-586 renders an `api-badge` reading LIVE or DEMO from `isLive`, and App.css:4397-4400 explicitly calls it "the only disclosure that the data is sample/fallback ... (F540)". BUT that disclosure is defeated in exactly this scenario: App.jsx:820 passes `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}`, and useNfts.js:40 sets its own `isLive` to `!data.fallback` purely from the NFT-metadata fetch. When only the two activity sources fail (OpenSea events + Alchemy getNFTSales) while token metadata still loads, `nfts.isLive` is true, the header reads "LIVE", and the fabricated sales render under a LIVE badge. So the correct statement is "the one disclosure the code has is OR-ed away on this exact path", not "nothing labels it".

Listings.jsx:871-872 renders an affirmative factual sentence next to the fabricated grid: `Showing recent ${collection.name} sales from the blockchain below.` (branch taken when listings are empty, listingsSource !== "opensea", no listingsError, and hasRecentSales). verdicts.correction: Accurate version: "Fabricated FALLBACK_ACTIVITY sales render as real trade history, under a header badge that still reads LIVE and copy claiming they came from the blockchain." verdicts.reasoning:
MAINTAINER'S CASE (the strongest version I can build):

This is not laundering — it is a deliberately hardened demo path that was already audited once under F540. (a) It only fires for the canonical Nakamigos contract and only when BOTH activity providers throw (api.js:552-556; the non-canonical branch correctly returns `activities: []`). (b) F540 already stripped the deceptive parts: timestamps are anchored to a fixed 2026-01-01 reference (constants.js:245-247) precisely so the sales cannot masquerade as fresh, addresses are obviously-truncated non-persons, and `sample: true` was added as a marker. (c) There is a test pinning that hardening (fallbackHonesty.test.js:23-34). (d) The app carries a global provenance chip: Header.jsx:583-585 renders `LIVE`/`DEMO` with the tooltip "Using demo/fallback data — some features may be limited", and constants.js:242-244 explicitly names that badge as the safety property ("shown ONLY when live endpoints are unavailable (the DEMO badge is up)"). (e) Listings' own banner already tells the user the listing feed is broken (Listings.jsx:870). Nothing here builds a transaction — the sale cards render no Buy button (Listings.jsx:187 requires `nft.orderHash && nft.price`, and sale items carry `salePrice`, not `price`), only an OpenSea link.

WHETHER IT HOLDS: it does not. Four checks, and the load-bearing one fails outright.

1. THE DEMO BADGE IS NOT GUARANTEED TO BE UP. This is the defense's keystone and it breaks. App.jsx:820 passes `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}`. `isLive` from useCollection.js:75 is `!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback` — false in this state. But `nfts.isLive` is set independently at useNfts.js:40 from `!data.fallback` on `fetchTokens`, which calls a DIFFERENT endpoint (`alchemyGet("getNFTsForContract")`, api.js:151). The activity fallback fires when `fetchOpenSeaActivity` (api.js:391, OpenSea `events/collection/...`) and `fetchAlchemyActivity` (`getNFTSales`) both throw. Those three endpoints fail independently in ordinary operation — a missing/expired OpenSea key, a plan-gated `getNFTSales`, or a per-endpoint 429 takes out the two activity sources while `getNFTsForContract` keeps serving. The `||` then makes the header read **LIVE** over four invented sales. The comment at constants.js:242-244 asserts a property the wiring does not provide.

2. THE TEAM'S OWN STANDARD IS AN IN-PANEL BANNER, AND LISTINGS CANNOT MEET IT. ActivityFeed.jsx:262-271 renders "⚠ Showing cached example data — live API unavailable" gated on `isLive === false && activities?.length > 0`, and App.jsx:757 passes it `isLive`. The Listings case (App.jsx:740-751) passes `activities` but not `isLive`; the component signature at Listings.jsx:236 has no such prop. Same data, same fallback, one tab warns and the other cannot. That asymmetry is the defect, not a style gap.

3. LISTINGS ACTIVELY ASSERTS PROVENANCE IT DOES NOT HAVE — and this is stronger than the finding stated. Listings.jsx:872 renders `Showing recent ${collection.name} sales from the blockchain below.` over records whose `hash` is `null` and which never touched a chain. Listings.jsx:636 subtitles the page `Live floor price and recent market activity`. So the page does not merely omit a caveat, it affirmatively attributes the four prints to the blockchain.

4. `sample: true` IS DEAD. Grep across the whole surface: the only reader is fallbackHonesty.test.js:32. The flag is asserted by a test and consumed by nothing — recentSales (Listings.jsx:378-411) projects each activity into a new object and drops it. The test passes while the honesty property it stands for is unenforced in the render path, which is exactly the "green ≠ checked" pattern.

Reproduction is deterministic: with both activity providers throwing on the Nakamigos contract and no live listings, `hasRealListings=false` / `hasRecentSales=true` selects `gridItems = displaySales` (Listings.jsx:652), the stat card at Listings.jsx:683-690 prints "RECENT SALES 4", the section header at Listings.jsx:968 prints "RECENT SALES (4)", and Listings.jsx:167-178 renders four cards reading e.g. "◆ 0.1100 sold 213d ago".
verdicts.correction:
CONFIRMED, with two corrections and one escalation of the claim.

Correction 1 — the time string is NOT a freshness lie. The finding says the cards carry "a time-ago string", implying they read as fresh. They do not. `formatTimeAgo` at Listings.jsx:95-103 caps at whole days, and the fixed reference (constants.js:247, 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) puts every sample sale ~213 days back as of 2026-08-02, so cards read "213d ago". F540 genuinely closed the freshness masquerade. The residual deception is narrower and should be stated accurately: the user is told these are REAL BUT STALE prints, not that they just happened. That still does the damage — when a collection shows zero listings, a tight historical band (0.1099 / 0.11 / 0.1101 / 0.1123 ETH) is exactly the anchor a user prices a bid or a listing against, and the page tells them it came from the chain.

Correction 2 — line reference. The Listings case is App.jsx:740-751 in this worktree, not 743-746. The claim about it (no `isLive` prop) is correct; confirmed against the component signature at Listings.jsx:236.

Escalation — the finding understates the copy. It describes the sales as rendering "unlabelled". They are worse than unlabelled: Listings.jsx:872 states `Showing recent <collection> sales from the blockchain below.` and Listings.jsx:636 states `Live floor price and recent market activity`. Cite those two lines, not just the missing badge.

Also correct the finding's implicit assumption that the DEMO chip is a mitigation. Because of `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` at App.jsx:820, the header can read LIVE in exactly this state. That divergence is the real root cause and should be named in the fix.

SEVERITY: medium stands, at the top of the band. It is not high — reaching the state needs a dual-provider failure, no transaction is built or signed from these cards (Listings.jsx:187 gates the Buy button on `nft.orderHash && nft.price`, and sale items carry only `salePrice`), and the OpenSea link resolves to a real token. It is not low — it is a factual, priced, provenance-attributed market claim over invented data, on the tab whose entire job is telling a user what this collection trades for.

MINIMAL HONEST FIX (for whoever picks this up): pass `isLive` into Listings from App.jsx:740-751 and gate the "from the blockchain" / "Live ... market activity" copy plus the RECENT SALES grid on it, mirroring ActivityFeed.jsx:262. Independently, `isLive || nfts.isLive` at App.jsx:820 should be `&&` — an OR cannot express "everything on this page is live."

BREADTH (same defect class, same prop omission, worth checking in this sweep): App.jsx:755 passes `activities` to `Analytics` with no `isLive` either, so any chart or aggregate Analytics computes over FALLBACK_ACTIVITY inherits the identical problem. I did not audit Analytics' consumption in this pass — flagging it, not asserting it.

survived.title: "Counter" button on a received offer silently does nothing
survived.claim: handleCounter resolves the token only from the 40-token gallery page passed in as `tokens`; for a token not in that page it computes null and returns without calling onPick and without any toast, so the button is inert.
survived.failure_scenario: A holder receives an offer on Nakamigos #14892. BidManager.jsx:318-324 builds tokenMap from the `tokens` prop, which is `nfts.allTokens` from useNfts — loaded 40 at a time (hooks/useNfts.js:33 `limit: 40`) and never force-loaded by this component. Out of a 20,000 supply, #14892 is almost certainly absent, so resolveToken returns null (line 328) and handleCounter's `if (token && onPick)` guard (line 494) is false: no modal opens, no error, no toast — the click is swallowed. The button at lines 699-704 is styled as an active primary-ish action with a pointer cursor. The user clicks repeatedly and concludes the app is broken. The NFT thumbnails in all three tabs have the same dead guard (`onClick={() => token && onPick?.(token)}`, lines 617, 669, 738), as does MyListings.jsx:647.
survived.suggested_fix: Fall back to a synthesized token object (`{ id: offer.tokenId, name, image }`) — the component already builds exactly that as `nftForImage` on line 661 — or fetch the single token via fetchTokensByIds on click. At minimum, disable the button or toast when the token cannot be resolved.

verdicts.correction:
The finding is accurate as written; every cited line reproduces. Two refinements worth recording.

(1) The finding says #14892 is "almost certainly absent" from tokenMap. The stronger and more accurate statement is that a miss is the DEFAULT case, not a probabilistic one: received offers are derived from fetchWalletNfts(wallet, ...) at BidManager.jsx:359 (the holder's own arbitrary token IDs out of 20,000), while tokenMap is built from nfts.allTokens, which is the first 40 tokens in fetchTokens page order (useNfts.js:33 limit:40, :190 allTokens). There is no mechanism that would make those two sets intersect. Nakamigos supply is 20000 (constants.js:34), so the <1000 auto-pagination gate at useNfts.js:101 never fires, and grep confirms loadAll has no caller on the bids path (only Deals.jsx:485, Gallery.jsx:148, Listings.jsx:450, TraitExplorer.jsx:380).

(2) Undstated in the finding, and it makes the defect worse: the failure is nondeterministic across sessions. If the user visited Deals or Trait Explorer earlier in the session, those force loadAll, the full 20k loads into the shared useNfts state in App.jsx:351, and Counter begins working. Same button, same offer, opposite outcome depending on tab history, with no signal to the user in either direction.

Severity stays medium — correctly scoped. No funds at risk, no false factual claim rendered about a token or wallet, so this is not the failed-read-laundering class; it is a dead control on a revenue-adjacent path. It does not warrant escalation to high.

Also confirmed as stated: the card still renders a correct name and image via the offer.tokenName / offer.tokenImage fallbacks at BidManager.jsx:658-661, so the user sees a complete, healthy-looking card whose Counter button is inert — which is exactly why the user concludes the app is broken rather than that the token is unknown. The button is never disabled (BidManager.jsx:699-704) and styles.btnCounter (:135-146) gives it cursor:pointer and the same minHeight/padding as the working Accept button beside it. The secondary thumbnail guards at :617, :669, :738 and MyListings.jsx:647 (tokenMap/resolveToken at MyListings.jsx:249-260, :614) all reproduce.

Note the fix is trivial and the codebase already demonstrates it: App.jsx:457 opens the same modal from a synthetic token object, setSelected({ id: deepLinkTokenId, name: `#${deepLinkTokenId}`, attributes: [], image: null }), and the offer already carries tokenId, tokenName, and tokenImage.
verdicts.reasoning:
Read the actual files rather than reasoning from the claim. handleCounter at BidManager.jsx:491-495 is verbatim `const token = resolveToken(offer.tokenId); if (token && onPick) onPick(token);` — no else branch, no toast, no console warning, so a null resolve swallows the click entirely. resolveToken (:326-329) returns null on a tokenMap miss, and tokenMap (:318-324) is built solely from the `tokens` prop, which App.jsx:775 supplies as nfts.allTokens.

Traced allTokens to useNfts.js:190 (rankedTokens over accumulated pages) fed by fetchTokens at limit:40 (:33). The only paths that expand it beyond 40 are the <1000-supply auto-loader at :101 — dead for Nakamigos at supply 20000 (constants.js:34) — and loadAll, whose callers I enumerated by grep: Deals.jsx:485, Gallery.jsx:148 (filters only), Listings.jsx:450 (trait filter / value sort), TraitExplorer.jsx:380. None on the bids path. So a user landing directly on Bids has exactly 40 tokens in the map.

Confirmed the button presents as live: not disabled at :699-704, and styles.btnCounter at :135-146 carries cursor:pointer plus the same minHeight:36 and padding as the adjacent working Accept button.

Confirmed the secondary claims: dead thumbnail guards at :617, :669, :738 and MyListings.jsx:647, backed by the same tokenMap/resolveToken pattern at MyListings.jsx:249-260.

Could not refute any element of the claim. The only inaccuracy is understatement — the finding frames the tokenMap miss as probabilistic when the two token sets are structurally unrelated, and it omits that prior visits to Deals/TraitExplorer make the button intermittently work.

Confirmed at source. handleCounter (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/BidManager.jsx:491-495) resolves the token only from tokenMap (318-324), built from the `tokens` prop, which App.jsx:775 supplies as `nfts.allTokens`. resolveToken returns null for anything outside that set (line 328), and the guard `if (token && onPick)` at 494 then returns with no toast despite addToast being in scope (line 300) and used at 453/455/460/465/472/481/486. The button (699-704, styles.btnCounter 135-146) has cursor:pointer and no disabled state, so it reads as live.

The maintainer defenses fail on this repo's own code:

(a) "Guard prevents a confidently-empty modal" — refuted by App.jsx:451-460 (F583), the /nft/:id deep link, which handles the identical not-in-window case by synthesizing {id, name:"#id", attributes:[], image:null}, opening the modal, then enriching via fetchTokensByIds (api.js:909). The repo's own standard is synthesize+fetch, not no-op. BidManager already holds richer data than that stub: offer.tokenName / offer.tokenImage are attached at line 377.

(b) "allTokens accumulates as the user browses" — collapses on this tab specifically. Received offers are on tokens the wallet OWNS (fetchWalletNfts, line 359), scattered across a 20,000 supply (constants.js:34). Gallery pages at limit:40 in tokenId order (hooks/useNfts.js:33) and auto-pagination is gated to supply < 1000 (useNfts.js:101), so Nakamigos never auto-fills. BidManager is not passed loadAll at all (contrast App.jsx:775 with 749/753). On a fresh load of the bids tab allTokens is IDs ~0-39 of 20,000, so Counter is dead essentially always, not "almost certainly".

(c) "Only a convenience" — the same card renders the red "% of floor" badge (681-685) that exists to flag a lowball, so the UI actively steers the seller toward the one control that cannot fire.

Severity medium holds: real negotiation friction on a money-adjacent tab, but no fund loss and no false factual claim (images fall back correctly via 659-661).

One mis-statement to correct: the finding equates the thumbnail clicks (617, 669, 738) and MyListings.jsx:647 with the Counter button. Same root cause, lower impact — a thumbnail is not labelled as a control (only affordance is cursor:pointer, styles.nftThumb:76), so those are low, not medium.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: BidManager.jsx:493-494 — the "Counter" button on a received offer is inert for any offer whose token is outside the 40-token gallery window, which on the Received Offers tab is the normal case rather than an edge case (offers are on wallet-OWNED tokens scattered across 20,000 supply; useNfts.js:33 pages at 40 and useNfts.js:101 disables auto-load above 1000 supply; BidManager is never passed loadAll). No modal, no toast, no disabled state. The repo already solved this exact case for deep links at App.jsx:451-460 using a synthesized token plus fetchTokensByIds (api.js:909), and BidManager has offer.tokenName/tokenImage (line 377) available to build a better stub than the deep-link path uses. Severity medium. Downgrade the associated thumbnail click-throughs (BidManager.jsx:617, 669, 738 and MyListings.jsx:647) to low — same root cause, but a thumbnail has no button affordance beyond cursor:pointer (styles.nftThumb:76).

survived.title: Green "Near Floor" / "At floor" badge on a listing priced far BELOW the floor
survived.claim: getHealthBadge tests only the upper bound (`pctAbove <= 10` → green "Near Floor"), so any listing below the floor — including one priced by two orders of magnitude too low — gets the healthiest badge, and line 670 additionally prints "At floor".
survived.failure_scenario: Floor is 0.10 ETH. A seller fat-fingers a listing at 0.01 ETH (or lists an old order that the floor has since risen far above). MyListings.jsx:210 computes pctAbove = -90; line 211 matches `pctAbove <= 10` and returns `{ label: "Near Floor", color: green }`, rendered as a green badge at line 660-662. Line 668-671 separately evaluates `listing.price <= floorPrice` and renders the green word "At floor". The seller scans a page of green reassurance and never cancels; the listing is swept at a 90% discount. The only counter-signal is a small "-90.0% from floor" chip (line 657-659) sitting beside two green badges that say the price is healthy.
survived.suggested_fix: Add a below-floor tier before the `<= 10` check (e.g. `pctAbove < -5` → red "Below Floor"), and change the line 670 text to distinguish "At floor" from "Below floor".

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly from frontend/src/nakamigos/components/MyListings.jsx. getHealthBadge (lines 208-218) computes pctAbove = ((price - floorPrice) / floorPrice) * 100 and then tests only `if (pctAbove <= 10)` — there is no lower bound, so any below-floor price at any depth returns { label: "Near Floor", color: "var(--green, #4ade80)" }, rendered as a green badge at lines 660-662. Independently, lines 668-671 evaluate `listing.price <= floorPrice` and render the literal word "At floor" in var(--green), which is factually false for a listing 90% under floor. Both line anchors in the finding are correct. The bug is confirmed as an inconsistency rather than a design choice, because the same codebase contains the correct implementation in a sibling component: NativeListingsList.jsx:51-58, where floorDelta() only emits "At floor" when Math.abs(pct) < 1 and otherwise emits "N% below floor" with a `below` flag. No test pins the current behaviour (grep over **/*.test.* for getHealthBadge/Near Floor/MyListings returns nothing). Verified the tab is genuinely reachable: App.jsx:95 lazy map, App.jsx:776-777 unconditional switch case passing stats, constants.js:93 valid-tab list, Header.jsx:147 and MobileNav.jsx:28 nav entries. floorPrice derives from stats?.floor (MyListings.jsx:246, App.jsx:904), so the badge only renders when a real floor exists. Where I downgrade the finding: the scenario claims the seller sees only "green reassurance" with the sole counter-signal being "a small -90.0% from floor chip". That is not what the file renders. The floor-delta chip at 657-659 uses styles.cardMeta (fontSize 10) while the misleading badge at 660-662 uses styles.badge (fontSize 8) — the truthful chip is larger than the false label, not smaller. Line 680 also prints "Listed: 0.0100" and lines 582-589 print the floor in the summary bar. So no numeric claim on the page is wrong; two text labels are miscategorized and visibly contradict adjacent correct numbers. That is a copy/classification defect, not a case of a user being told a false fact with no counter-signal, so medium overstates it. I also checked the string-coercion edge: distFromFloor is a string from toFixed(1), and `"-90.0" > 0` coerces to -90 > 0 = false, so the negative form renders correctly — that part is not additionally broken.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: getHealthBadge at MyListings.jsx:208-218 is upper-bounded only (`pctAbove <= 10`), so every below-floor listing — at any depth — receives the healthiest green "Near Floor" badge (rendered 660-662), and lines 668-671 separately label it green "At floor". A listing 90% under floor is badged identically to one at parity, directly contradicting the "-90.0% from floor" chip rendered in the same row at 657-659. The scenario's framing that the seller has almost no counter-signal is wrong: the signed floor-delta chip (fontSize 10) is larger than the badge (fontSize 8), the raw listed price is shown at line 680, and the floor is shown in the summary bar at 582-589. The defect is therefore misleading labels contradicting correct adjacent numbers, not a fabricated fact — severity low. Fix already exists in-repo: mirror NativeListingsList.jsx:51-58, which reserves "At floor" for Math.abs(pct) < 1 and otherwise renders "N% below floor".

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by reading the file; every line cite in the report is accurate.

Reproduction (floor 0.10, listing 0.01):
- MyListings.jsx:210 -> pctAbove = ((0.01 - 0.10)/0.10)*100 = -90
- :211 `if (pctAbove <= 10)` matches (no lower bound) -> returns { label: "Near Floor", color: "var(--green, #4ade80)" }
- :660-662 renders it via styles.badge(green)
- :668-671 independently evaluates `listing.price <= floorPrice` -> true -> renders the literal word "At floor" in `var(--green)`
- :657-659 renders "-90.0% from floor" (the string/number coercion `"-90.0" > 0` resolves false correctly, so the sign does print)

MAINTAINER'S BEST DEFENCE, and why it does not hold:
1. "It is a sellability ladder, not a fairness ladder — below floor IS maximally sellable, so green is correct." The ladder (Near Floor green / Above Floor yellow / High red) does read as a will-it-move scale. But the audience inverts it: NativeListingsList (order book, colors below-floor green at :76-77) is viewed by a BUYER, for whom below-floor is a bargain. MyListings is the seller's own management screen (per-wallet, with Cancel buttons, 30s refresh at :17). Identical color, opposite party, opposite meaning.
2. "The repo is consistent." It is not — it is consistent in the buyer surface only. The correct helper already exists 600 lines away: floorDelta (NativeListingsList.jsx:51-58) preserves the sign, gates "At floor" behind `Math.abs(pct) < 1`, and otherwise emits "90% below floor". getHealthBadge:210-211 throws the sign away, merging two opposite states into one positive verdict. useSmartAlerts.js:312-327 also fires an "Underpriced Listing" alert on exactly this condition, so the app already classifies it as an event — just never on the screen of the party losing money.
3. "The raw number is on screen, a chip is allowed to be lossy." Strongest defence, defeated by visual weight per the styles I read: styles.cardMeta (:116-119) gives the "-90.0%" text fontSize 10 / `var(--text-dim)` with NO conditional coloring (identical at +2% and -90%), while styles.badge (:159-178) is a filled chip with green background AND green border, plus a third green string at :669. Two of three signals are affirmatively green and the only disconfirming one is the uncolored one.
4. Line 670 is not a color problem at all — it is a false sentence. "At floor" is printed as literal English for any price at or below floor, so 0.01 against a 0.10 floor is described as being AT the floor.

NOT the failed-read-laundering class: `floorPrice = stats?.floor || 0` (:246) fails CLOSED — a broken stats read zeroes the floor and both the badge guard (:209 `!floorPrice || floorPrice <= 0`) and the render guard (:668 `floorPrice > 0`) suppress the verdict entirely. Both inputs are genuine reads. This is a display/semantics defect, not a fabricated fact.

verdicts.correction:
The finding is real but its headline scenario leans on the weaker of two legs, and it understates the worst line.

WEAKER LEG (as reported): "seller fat-fingers 0.01 instead of 0.10." Real but low-yield — the seller typed the price seconds earlier, the listing form is the proper guard, and the large price is rendered at :676-681. The badge is not what protects them there.

MyListings is precisely the review-and-cancel-your-stale-orders screen, it re-polls every 30s (REFRESH_INTERVAL, :17), and on each poll it affirmatively tells the seller the stale order is healthy. This is the ordinary stale-listing sniping loss, and the screen built to catch it is instead reassuring the seller out of cancelling.

UNDERSTATED: the report treats :670 as an additional green badge. It is worse than that — it is a false factual sentence rather than a mis-chosen color. `listing.price <= floorPrice ? "At floor" : ...` prints the words "At floor" for a listing 90% BELOW floor. Even rendered in plain gray it would still be wrong. The repo's own floorDelta (NativeListingsList.jsx:56) already requires `Math.abs(pct) < 1` before saying "At floor" and otherwise says "N% below floor" — the correct string exists in this codebase.

survived.title: Collection/trait bids render as a bid on one specific token
survived.claim: normalizeOrder finds the NFT consideration item with `Number(c.itemType) >= 2`, which also matches ERC721_WITH_CRITERIA (4) and ERC1155_WITH_CRITERIA (5). For those, identifierOrCriteria is a merkle root or "0", not a token id — so a collection-wide bid is displayed as a bid on a concrete NFT.
survived.failure_scenario: If a criteria offer appears in the `orders/ethereum/seaport/offers` feed for the connected maker (the component anticipates this — it has a "Collection Offer" label at lines 600 and 727 for the tokenId===null case), line 241 sets `tokenId = String(identifierOrCriteria)`. For an any-token criteria offer that value is the string "0", which is truthy, so the card renders "Nakamigos #0" and loads token #0's artwork; for a merkle-rooted trait offer it renders "Nakamigos #<78-digit number>" with a broken image. The user believes they have an open bid on a single NFT they never bid on, and cannot tell which of their bids is the collection-wide one they need to cancel. The "Collection Offer" fallback is unreachable for these orders because itemType 4/5 always satisfy the `>= 2` test.
survived.suggested_fix: Narrow the predicate to `itemType === 2 || itemType === 3` for token-id extraction and treat itemType 4/5 as a criteria order — render the existing "Collection Offer" (or "Trait Offer") label and suppress the thumbnail.

The finding is accurate as written, with two refinements.

(1) CODE PATH — reproduced verbatim. C:/Users/jimbo/OneDrive/Desktop/tegriddy farms/.claude/worktrees/scanner-rebase/frontend/src/nakamigos/components/BidManager.jsx:240-241:
  const nftItem = (params?.consideration || []).find(c => Number(c.itemType) >= 2);
  const tokenId = nftItem?.identifierOrCriteria ? String(nftItem.identifierOrCriteria) : null;
Seaport ItemType is 0 NATIVE / 1 ERC20 / 2 ERC721 / 3 ERC1155 / 4 ERC721_WITH_CRITERIA / 5 ERC1155_WITH_CRITERIA, so `>= 2` does match 4 and 5. The repo itself confirms the 4-means-criteria reading at frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/trades.js:228-230 ("itemType: any ? 4 : 2 // ERC721_WITH_CRITERIA : ERC721", "identifierOrCriteria: any ? '0' : String(tokenId)") and trades.test.js:88 ("builds wildcard slots as itemType 4 with criteria 0"). The string "0" is truthy, so the null branch is skipped and tokenId becomes "0". For a merkle-rooted trait offer it renders the root as a decimal token id with a broken image.

(2) THE FEATURE IS REACHABLE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The app creates exactly these orders for exactly this wallet+contract: CollectionOffersPanel.jsx:60-66 ("Collection Offer" button) -> MakeOfferModal.jsx:92-105 -> api-offers.js createCollectionOffer (line 341, POSTs `criteria_offers` at :431) and createTraitOffer (line 456, POSTs at :547). Both build their consideration straight from OpenSea's `offers/build` partialParameters (api-offers.js:407-411 and :523-527), i.e. the itemType-4 criteria item verbatim. My Bids then reads those back through the maker-filtered feed at BidManager.jsx:336-341 (`orders/ethereum/seaport/offers` with maker + asset_contract_address). Same defect exists in the shared normalizer at api-offers.js:187 (identical expression), which feeds Received Offers via fetchTokenOffers — there it is masked because BidManager.jsx:377 overwrites tokenId with the owned nft.id.

REFINEMENT A (mis-statement): "the Collection Offer fallback is unreachable" is too absolute. It is unreachable for well-formed criteria orders, but still reachable when consideration contains no itemType>=2 item at all (malformed/partial protocol_data) or if identifierOrCriteria arrives as numeric 0 rather than the string "0". So the fallback is not dead code; it is just never hit by the case it was written for.

REFINEMENT B (impact bound): cancellation is not broken. handleCancel -> cancelBid (BidManager.jsx:272-296) uses bid.rawOrder.protocol_data.parameters and cancelSeaportOrder, so each card cancels its own real order hash regardless of the mislabel. The harm is purely identification: the user is told they hold a bid on a specific NFT they never bid on, two different bids can render under the same "#0" title, and a collection-wide bid is indistinguishable from an item bid in the list. No funds are misdirected. Medium is still the right severity for an honesty-class defect on a money surface, but it is a display/labeling bug, not a fund-loss bug.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (why confidence is medium, not high): I cannot prove offline that OpenSea's `GET orders/ethereum/seaport/offers` actually returns criteria orders in the maker-filtered feed — that requires a live API call. The Order model for that endpoint carries a criteria_proof field and an order_type of "criteria", and BidManager's own author clearly expected collection offers there (the tokenId===null branch at :600/:727 exists for no other reason), which is why I did not refute. But note the fork: if that feed does NOT return criteria offers, the finding as stated is unreachable and is replaced by a strictly worse one — the app lets a user place a collection/trait offer that never appears in Bid Manager at all, so they cannot see or cancel it there. Either branch is a real user-visible defect on this tab; only the wording changes. One live GET with a maker that has an open collection bid settles which.

Line 240 is literally `find(c => Number(c.itemType) >= 2)` and line 241 is a truthiness gate on identifierOrCriteria, so Seaport itemTypes 4/5 pass the NFT test and their criteria value ("0" for collection-wide, a merkle root for trait offers) is rendered as a concrete token id at lines 600 and 727. Reproduced against the file. verdicts.correction: Finding is real and correctly reasoned; medium is the right severity. Two refinements. (a) Harm is understated for the collection-offer case: tokenId "0" flows through resolveToken (:599), so the card can render a REAL token's name and artwork, and the thumbnail's onClick calls onPick(token) at :617 — clicking navigates the user into an NFT they never bid on. (b) Scope is two tabs: the identical mislabel is in Bid History at BidManager.jsx:727, not only My Bids at :600. Not lower than medium because a live, WETH-funded, any-token-fillable obligation is presented to its owner as a bid on one specific NFT.
