That caveat does not clear the code — if criteria orders do not arrive, the "Collection Offer" copy at :600/:727 is unreachable dead code instead, so one of the two branches is wrong either way.

survived.title: Live transfer timestamps are a hardcoded 12.000 s/block extrapolation with unbounded drift
survived.claim: blockToTimestamp = MERGE_TIME + (block - 15537393) * 12000. Post-merge slots are exactly 12s but some slots are MISSED (no block), so real seconds-per-block is strictly greater than 12.000 and the estimate lags real time monotonically — currently on the order of days. This estimate is rendered by formatTimeAgo as an exact relative time ('12s ago', '3h ago') with no indication it is computed rather than read from the chain. Same estimator at api.js:290-296 for the Alchemy sale path.
survived.failure_scenario: The poller detects a Transfer log in the block it just fetched — by construction that transfer happened within the last ~12 seconds. parseTransferLog stamps it with the 12.000s extrapolation, so the row renders as several days ago, sits below week-old OpenSea sales in the newest-first sort, and contradicts the green LIVE badge two inches above it whose aria-label reads 'Live transfer feed active, refreshed every 12 seconds' (ActivityFeed.jsx:213, 240-242). Separately, `if (!blockHex) return Date.now()` (line 14) and the identical `if (!blockNumber) return Date.now()` at api.js:291 turn an UNKNOWN block into the confident claim 'just now', which then sorts to the top of the feed.
survived.suggested_fix: Read the real block timestamp — eth_getBlockByNumber for the (usually one) new block per poll, or eth_getLogs already gives you blockNumber to batch-resolve. At minimum, stop defaulting an unknown block to Date.now(): return null and render an em dash.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, and empirically measured rather than argued.

THE CODE IS AS DESCRIBED
- frontend/src/nakamigos/hooks/useActivityWebSocket.js:10-17 — `const MERGE_BLOCK = 15537393; const MERGE_TIME = 1663224162000; function blockToTimestamp(blockHex) { if (!blockHex) return Date.now(); const blockNumber = parseInt(blockHex, 16); return MERGE_TIME + (blockNumber - MERGE_BLOCK) * 12000; }`
- Applied to every live transfer at useActivityWebSocket.js:51 — `time: blockToTimestamp(log.blockNumber)`.
- Duplicated at frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:285-296 with `POST_MERGE_MS_PER_BLOCK = 12000`, and the comment on api.js:284 asserts the false premise outright: "Post-merge: exactly 12s/slot."

MEASURED DRIFT (live mainnet read, ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, this session)
- latest block 25665635, real header timestamp 2026-08-02T07:13:59Z
- estimator output for that same block: 2026-07-22T23:31:06Z
- drift = 10.32 days, estimate LAGGING reality
- real seconds/block since merge = 12.08805, not 12.000
The mechanism in the claim is right: missed slots make real s/block strictly > 12.000, and the error is cumulative in block count, so it grows ~0.088s per block ≈ 10.5 min/day and never self-corrects.

THE RENDER PATH IS LIVE AND UNGATED
useCollection.js:39-42 calls the hook -> App.jsx:757 `<ActivityFeed activities={activities} ... isWebSocketConnected={isWebSocketConnected} />` (unconditional switch case "activity") -> ActivityFeed.jsx:438 `{formatTimeAgo(a.time)}`. formatTimeAgo (ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47) emits a bare "10d ago" with no "~", no "est.", no tooltip.

THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL
- ActivityFeed.jsx:213 aria-label "Live transfer feed active, refreshed every 12 seconds"; ActivityFeed.jsx:240-242 subtitle "Live on-chain transfers — refreshed every ~12s".
- A transfer the poller just found in the head block (by construction <=12s old) renders "10d ago" directly beneath that green LIVE badge.

THE SORT CONSEQUENCE IS REAL
ActivityFeed.jsx:128 `[...combined].sort((a, b) => (b.time || 0) - (a.time || 0))` and eventFeed.js:180 both sort newest-first. OpenSea sales carry REAL timestamps (api.js:360-371, from `event_timestamp`). Since drift (10.3d) currently exceeds a week, a brand-new on-chain transfer sorts BELOW every OpenSea sale from the last 10 days — the "newest-first" live feed puts its newest row in the middle of the list. The claim's "sits below week-old OpenSea sales" is correct at today's drift.

BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THE FINDING STATED (3 surfaces, not 2)
1. api.js:433 in `parseSales` — the Alchemy activity fallback. Conditional (only when the OpenSea events primary fails), but when it fires with the "24h" date-range button selected, EVERY row reads "10d ago" under a 24-hour filter.
2. api.js:596 in `fetchTokenSalesHistory` — NOT a fallback. It is the sole source for the per-NFT price-history chart in the detail modal (Modal.jsx:13, :61). That chart's x-axis is unconditionally ~10 days off for every token.
3. Bonus, minor and not worth its own finding: api.js:453 `const blocksBack = Math.floor(daysBack * 86400 / 12)` reuses the same 12s assumption to size the fromBlock window, so each range over-fetches ~0.7%. Harmless.

WHAT I WOULD DOWNGRADE
The `if (!blockHex) return Date.now()` sub-claim (useActivityWebSocket.js:14) is weak on that path. `eth_getLogs` over an explicit numeric fromBlock/toBlock range returns only mined logs, which always carry a blockNumber — a null blockNumber is a pending-log property. The branch is effectively unreachable there, and the framing is backwards on impact: `Date.now()` is the MORE accurate answer for a log just pulled from the head block, not the less. The sub-claim does survive at api.js:291, where Alchemy's `getNFTSales` omitting `blockNumber` on a sale object would stamp an arbitrarily old sale as "just now" and float it to the top of both the feed and the price chart. Keep it as a narrow note, not as co-equal evidence.

CLASSIFICATION: this is category 2 (a claim the chain does not back — a user-facing fact computed from a hardcoded constant and presented with no hedge), not category 1 failed-read laundering. No read fails here; the read succeeds and is then discarded in favour of arithmetic.

SEVERITY: medium is correct. No funds at risk, no irreversible action, nothing signed — but it defeats the stated purpose of the flagship "LIVE" feature, misstates a fact on three surfaces, and silently worsens every day.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate restatement:

`blockToTimestamp` (useActivityWebSocket.js:13-17, duplicated api.js:290-296) converts block numbers to wall-clock time with a hardcoded 12,000 ms/block, on the stated but false premise that post-merge slots are "exactly 12s/slot" (api.js:284). Missed slots make the true average 12.088 s/block, measured against mainnet block 25665635 this session. The estimator therefore lags real time by 10.32 days as of 2026-08-02, growing ~10.5 minutes per day, with no correction mechanism.

Three user-visible consequences, all verified to a render site:

1. ActivityFeed "activity" tab (App.jsx:757, unconditional). A transfer the poller finds in the block it just fetched — at most ~12 seconds old — is stamped 10 days in the past and rendered by formatTimeAgo (ActivityFeed.jsx:438) as a bare "10d ago", two inches below a green LIVE badge whose aria-label reads "Live transfer feed active, refreshed every 12 seconds" (ActivityFeed.jsx:213) and a subtitle reading "Live on-chain transfers — refreshed every ~12s" (ActivityFeed.jsx:240-242). No "~", no "estimated", no tooltip distinguishes it from the OpenSea rows beside it, which DO carry real chain timestamps (api.js:360-371).

2. Sort corruption. Both merge points sort strictly newest-first (ActivityFeed.jsx:128; eventFeed.js:180). Because drift now exceeds one week, the newest real event on the page sorts beneath every OpenSea sale from the past ten days. The live feed's newest row is not at the top.

3. Per-NFT price-history chart (api.js:596 -> Modal.jsx:61). Unlike the api.js:433 activity fallback, this path has no alternative source, so every token's price chart is unconditionally ~10 days off on the x-axis.

Downgrade one sub-claim: `if (!blockHex) return Date.now()` (useActivityWebSocket.js:14) is effectively unreachable, since eth_getLogs over a numeric block range returns only mined logs, which always carry blockNumber. It is also backwards on impact — Date.now() is the more accurate value for a head-block log. The concern is real only at api.js:291, where a `getNFTSales` row missing `blockNumber` would render an arbitrarily old sale as "just now" and float it to the top of the feed and the chart.

Severity: medium, unchanged. Not a money path and nothing signed, but a headline "LIVE" feature states a wrong fact on three surfaces and degrades daily. The honest fix is to read block timestamps (batch eth_getBlockByNumber for the block range the poller already fetched) or, failing that, hedge the copy so a computed age is never presented as a read one.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct measurement, not inference. The mechanism stated in the finding is exactly right: post-merge slots are 12s but slots are MISSED, so blocks-per-second is strictly slower than 12.000 and MERGE_TIME + (block - 15537393) * 12000 lags real time monotonically.

Empirical proof (live eth_getBlockByNumber against ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, 2026-08-02):
  latest block  = 25,665,633
  real timestamp= 2026-08-02 07:13:35 UTC
  estimator     = 2026-07-22 23:30:42 UTC
  DRIFT         = 891,773 s = 10.32 days ; effective 12.088 s/block since merge
So the finding's "on the order of days" is precisely 10.3 days today, and it widens ~2.6 days/year.

Code chain verified end to end:
- useActivityWebSocket.js:13-17 blockToTimestamp; :51 stamps every parsed Transfer log; :126 the logs come from a range the poller just fetched, i.e. the event is <=12s old by construction.
- useActivityWebSocket.js:208-217 -> useCollection.js:39-42, 121-123 -> App.jsx:757 -> ActivityFeed.jsx:128 (sort by a.time desc) -> :438 formatTimeAgo -> :37-47 renders "10d ago" as an exact relative time with no "approx" marker.
- LIVE badge + aria-label "Live transfer feed active, refreshed every 12 seconds" at ActivityFeed.jsx:213 and subtitle "Live on-chain transfers - refreshed every ~12s" at :240-242 sit directly above the mislabeled row. Confirmed verbatim.
- api.js:290-296 is the same estimator (plus a 13,500 ms pre-merge constant), used at api.js:433 (parseSales, Alchemy getNFTSales fallback path, reached at api.js:545 when OpenSea events fail) and api.js:596 (fetchTokenSalesHistory).

MAINTAINER DEFENSES AND WHY THEY FAIL:
(1) "12s is the consensus slot time, and eth_getLogs returns no timestamp, so estimating avoids a second RPC per block on a rate-limited 12s poller (the jitter at :177-180 shows the budget is tight)." Fails: measured error is 10.3 days, not a rounding error, and for LIVE rows the correct value costs zero RPC - Date.now() at receipt is accurate to +/-12s because the poller only ever fetches the block range it just learned about.
(2) "The estimator is strictly increasing in block number, so relative ordering is preserved." Fails because the feed is multi-source with real clocks on the other sources: OpenSea stream (eventFeed.js:107-109), OpenSea events API (api.js:360-369), native orderbook fills (api.js:520). They are merged and sorted against the estimate at eventFeed.js:180, useCollection.js:121-123, ActivityFeed.jsx:128. Two clocks 10 days apart in one newest-first sort: a just-detected transfer sinks below every OpenSea sale of the last 10 days and can fall outside the visibleCount=100 slice (ActivityFeed.jsx:178-180) entirely.
(3) "The Date.now() fallbacks are unreachable defensive code." This one HOLDS. eth_getLogs with concrete hex fromBlock/toBlock never returns pending logs, so log.blockNumber is always present (useActivityWebSocket.js:14), and Alchemy getNFTSales always returns blockNumber (api.js:291). It is a latent failed-read-laundering pattern (unknown block -> confident "just now" -> sorts to the top), worth a note, but the finding presents it at par with the drift and that part is overstated.

SEVERITY: medium is correct and I would not move it. It is a user-visible claim the chain does not back, it directly contradicts adjacent LIVE copy, and it is unbounded and worsening - but it is informational, not a money path, and it neither loses funds nor mis-signs a transaction.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate restatement: "Live transfer rows are timestamped by a 12.000 s/block extrapolation from the merge block; because slots are missed, the estimate now lags real time by 10.3 days (measured 2026-08-02: block 25,665,633 real 07:13:35 UTC vs estimate 2026-07-22 23:30:42 UTC; effective 12.088 s/block) and the gap widens ~2.6 days/year. A Transfer detected in the block range the poller just fetched - provably <=12s old - renders as '10d ago' (useActivityWebSocket.js:13-17, :51 -> ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47, :438) directly beneath a LIVE badge promising 12-second freshness (ActivityFeed.jsx:213, 240-242). Worse than the label alone: the same estimate is the SORT KEY (eventFeed.js:180, useCollection.js:121-123, ActivityFeed.jsx:128) in a feed whose other sources carry REAL timestamps (OpenSea stream eventFeed.js:107-109, OpenSea events api.js:360-369, native fills api.js:520), so the new transfer sorts below 10 days of real sales and can be pushed out of the 100-row visible slice (ActivityFeed.jsx:178-180) - the LIVE feed shows nothing new arriving. Blast radius is wider than the activity tab: Header.jsx:60 renders the same a.time in the site-wide ticker next to a live-dot, and api.js:596 (fetchTokenSalesHistory -> Modal.jsx:61) shifts the per-NFT price-history chart x-axis by the same ~10 days; api.js:433 applies it to Alchemy-fallback sale rows (api.js:545)."

Two corrections to the finding as filed:
1. The `if (!blockHex) return Date.now()` / `if (!blockNumber) return Date.now()` sub-claim (useActivityWebSocket.js:14, api.js:291) is effectively UNREACHABLE - eth_getLogs with concrete block bounds returns no pending logs, and Alchemy getNFTSales always includes blockNumber. Keep it as a low-severity latent note, not as a co-equal half of the finding.
2. The finding under-states blast radius: add Header.jsx:60 (ticker on every nakamigos page) and api.js:596 / Modal.jsx:61 (price-history chart).

Correct fix, for the record (not applied - read-only sweep): stamp live rows with Date.now() at receipt (accurate to +/-12s, zero extra RPC), or batch one eth_getBlockByNumber per distinct block in the poll and cache it; and drop the estimator from parseSales/fetchTokenSalesHistory in favour of the real block timestamp. If an estimate must remain anywhere, the rendered string must be marked approximate rather than printed as an exact relative time.

survived.title: SALES and VOLUME are computed over one 50-row API page but presented as stats for the selected time window
survived.claim: totalVolume and salesCount reduce over statsSource = fetchedActivities, which is whatever fetchActivity({limit: 50}) returned for the current page (ActivityFeed.jsx:91, 186-204). They are rendered as bare 'SALES' and 'VOLUME' figures (lines 245-258) directly beside the 24h/7d/30d/All Time selector, with no scoping qualifier.
survived.failure_scenario: User selects '30d' on Nakamigos. OpenSea returns the first 50 sale events in that window; the header reads e.g. 'SALES 50 / VOLUME 5.6 ETH'. The real 30-day figures are several times larger. The user reads this as the collection's 30-day volume. Clicking 'Load More' appends a second page into fetchedActivities, so the same 'SALES'/'VOLUME' numbers visibly jump — proving they were never a window total. 'All Time' is the worst case: it reports a page of 50 as the collection's lifetime volume.
survived.suggested_fix: Either label them for what they are ('IN VIEW' / 'SALES SHOWN'), or source the aggregate from the collection stats endpoint that already powers useCollection rather than from the paged event list.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED against the actual files; every line reference in the finding checks out.

Chain of evidence:
1. ActivityFeed.jsx:91 — `fetchActivity({ contract, limit: 50, daysBack: days, pageKey })`.
2. api.js:391-410 (`fetchOpenSeaActivity`) — sends `{ event_type: "sale", limit }` plus `after = now - daysBack*86400` and returns `{ activities: parseOpenSeaEvents(events), pageKey: data.next || null }`. So `limit: 50` is a PAGE size, not a window total, and the presence of `pageKey`/`data.next` proves more rows exist beyond it. The Alchemy fallback (api.js:441-482) behaves the same: `limit: String(limit)` + `pageKey: data.pageKey`.
3. ActivityFeed.jsx:102 — a fresh (non-paged) fetch does `setFetchedActivities(data.activities || [])`, i.e. exactly one page.
4. ActivityFeed.jsx:186-190 — `statsSource` is `fetchedActivities` whenever it is non-empty (the merged list is only a fallback).
5. ActivityFeed.jsx:196-204 — `totalVolume` reduces `statsSource` sales prices; `salesCount` counts them.
6. ActivityFeed.jsx:245-258 — rendered as bare `SALES` and `VOLUME` with no window qualifier, no `title` attribute. Confirmed in App.css:2044-2049 and 4278 that no CSS pseudo-element adds one. The only nearby copy is the subtitle "Recent trades and transfers" (line 242), which does not scope a number to 24h/7d/30d/All Time. The 24h/7d/30d/All Time selector (lines 284-304) is the very next control block under the header.

The "All Time" case is the strongest: at daysBack=3650, `isAllTime` is true so the `after` param is omitted entirely (api.js:393-399) — the request is simply the 50 most recent sales, rendered as the collection's lifetime VOLUME. For any collection with more than 50 lifetime sales (i.e. all of them) this figure is wrong by orders of magnitude.

The "numbers visibly jump" claim also reproduces: Load More (lines 460-465) calls `loadActivities(daysBack, nextPageKey)` when `filtered.length <= visibleCount` (initially 50-ish rows vs visibleCount 100, so it fires on the first click), and the paged branch at lines 93-100 APPENDS into `fetchedActivities`, which is `statsSource` — so SALES/VOLUME grow on click. A genuine window total would not move.

Two corrections to the wording, neither of which changes the verdict:
(a) It is "one page" plus a little, not strictly 50: on a fresh fetch, native-orderbook fills are merged in (api.js:531, 562-573) after the page is assembled, so the count can read slightly above 50. Also `statsSource` deliberately ignores live WebSocket/prop sales while a page is loaded, so recent sales in the window are additionally omitted.
(b) The mis-statement is a systematic UNDERSTATEMENT that scales with the window: 24h is usually honest (fewer than 50 sales/day for most collections), 7d borderline, 30d and All Time are the broken cases. The finding's framing as uniformly wrong across the selector is slightly too strong.

Severity: hold at medium, as filed. These are headline, factual-sounding figures with no qualifier, they change with the window selector so a user reasonably reads them as window totals, and they are silently truncated. Not high: the underlying data is real (this is truncation, not the failed-read-laundering class), the direction of error is always downward, and nothing spends money on it.

RELATED, HIGHER-SEVERITY DEFECT IN THE SAME STAT (separate from this finding, worth its own report): when both OpenSea and Alchemy fail for the canonical Nakamigos contract, api.js:553-554 sets `primaryResult = { activities: FALLBACK_ACTIVITY, fallback: true }`. Those are hardcoded fake sales (constants.js:248-252, each tagged `sample: true`, prices ~0.11 ETH). They land in `fetchedActivities` and therefore in `statsSource`, so the header renders SALES/VOLUME computed entirely from fabricated data. The "Showing cached example data — live API unavailable" banner at ActivityFeed.jsx:262 is gated on the `isLive === false` PROP, not on the `apiFallback` state the component already tracks (line 104) — so in that path the fake stats render with no warning at all. That IS the failed-read-laundering class this sweep is hunting.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: SALES and VOLUME (ActivityFeed.jsx:196-204, rendered 245-258) are computed over `fetchedActivities`, which holds a single 50-row API page (api.js:391-410) plus any native-orderbook fills merged in on a fresh fetch (api.js:562-573) — not the selected time window. They are labelled with no scoping qualifier directly above the 24h/7d/30d/All Time selector. 24h is usually accurate; 30d and especially All Time are systematically understated, and All Time is guaranteed wrong for any collection with more than 50 lifetime sales because api.js:393-399 drops the time filter entirely and just returns the 50 most recent sales. Clicking Load More appends another page into the same `statsSource` (ActivityFeed.jsx:93-100, 462-464), making the figures grow on click — which a real window total would not do. Severity confirmed at medium.

CONFIRMED, with three factual corrections to the write-up.

Corrections:
1. `fetchedActivities` is CUMULATIVE across loaded pages, not "whatever the current page returned" — ActivityFeed.jsx:93-100 appends page N+1 onto prior rows. It is also not strictly capped at 50: native orderbook sales are merged into the same result server-side (api.js:562-572), and when `fetchedActivities` is empty, `statsSource` falls back to the merged prop/WebSocket/P2P-trade list (ActivityFeed.jsx:186-190) — a third, differently-scoped population.
2. Not "the first 50 sale events in that window" — OpenSea events return newest-first, so it is the 50 MOST RECENT sales in the window. Same for All Time: `isAllTime` (api.js:393) drops the `after` param entirely (api.js:396-399), so the figure is the 50 most recent sales ever, rendered as lifetime volume.
3. The Load-More jump is real and arrives sooner than described: RENDER_CHUNK is 100 (ActivityFeed.jsx:178) while an API page is 50, so `filtered.length <= visibleCount` is true on the very first click and it immediately pages the API (ActivityFeed.jsx:462-464), roughly doubling both headline figures in one click.

Sharper reproduction than the one given: every event `parseOpenSeaEvents` emits is `type: "sale"` (api.js:373), and `fetchOpenSeaActivity` requests `event_type: "sale"` with `limit` (api.js:395). Therefore `salesCount` is effectively the page size. On any liquid collection, 7d / 30d / All Time all render "SALES 50" — the headline barely moves across windows that differ by orders of magnitude in real volume. Precise characterization: the stat is CORRECT for any window containing fewer than 50 sales and silently SATURATES at ~50 above that.

Additional aggravator not in the finding: `statsSource` is not a summary of the rows shown either. `visible` derives from `filtered`, which applies the type filter and the search box (ActivityFeed.jsx:156-173), while `statsSource` ignores both. Typing a token ID into search collapses the list to one row while SALES/VOLUME sit unchanged — so the summarized population is labelled nowhere in the UI.

Accurate statement of the defect: totalVolume (ActivityFeed.jsx:196-200) and salesCount (:202-204) reduce over `statsSource` — the pages of activity loaded so far, page size 50 (:91) — and are rendered as unqualified "SALES" and "VOLUME" (:245-258) directly adjacent to a 24h/7d/30d/All Time selector (:284-304) that re-computes them. The server filters the window correctly (`after` param) and then truncates; the component treats the truncated page as the window total. The author's own comment at :182-185 ("server-filtered to the chosen time range") states the mistaken assumption explicitly, so this is a mis-statement of intent, not an intentional page-scoped stat.

Severity: medium is correct. Not the failed-read-laundering class — every summand is a real parsed on-chain sale, nothing is fabricated, and no money path, signing, or quote depends on it. But it is a correct measurement of the wrong population presented with zero qualifier, understating 30d/All Time volume by orders of magnitude, which materially misleads a user sizing up collection liquidity.

Fix direction (not applied; read-only sweep): either label the figures for the sample they actually are ("last 50 sales" / "SALES (LOADED)") or source them from a real window-scoped aggregate endpoint.

Adjacent issue found in the same block, deserves its own finding: the "Showing cached example data" banner (ActivityFeed.jsx:262) is gated on the `isLive` prop rather than on `apiFallback` (set at :104). When both activity APIs fail for the canonical contract, `fetchActivity` returns the hardcoded FALLBACK_ACTIVITY demo rows (api.js:553-554; constants.js:248), so SALES/VOLUME compute over sample data while the banner stays hidden unless `isLive === false` is passed. App.jsx:757 passes the live `isLive`, so the banner can be absent while demo data drives the stats.
verdicts.reasoning:
Read ActivityFeed.jsx in full and traced the data path through api.js.

Verified chain:
- ActivityFeed.jsx:91 calls fetchActivity with a hardcoded `limit: 50`.
- api.js:391-409 (fetchOpenSeaActivity) sends `{ event_type: "sale", limit }` plus `after = now - daysBack*86400`, and returns `pageKey: data.next`. So the server applies the time window and THEN truncates to the page size. `limit` is a page size, not a window bound.
- api.js:393,396-399: for daysBack >= 365 ("All Time" = 3650) the `after` param is omitted entirely, so the response is simply the 50 most recent sales ever.
- ActivityFeed.jsx:186-190 sets statsSource = fetchedActivities when non-empty.
- ActivityFeed.jsx:196-204 reduces statsSource into totalVolume and salesCount.
- ActivityFeed.jsx:245-258 renders them as bare "SALES" and "VOLUME", with the 24h/7d/30d/All Time selector at :284-304 immediately adjacent and re-triggering the fetch via :117-119.

So the finding reproduces: a page of at most ~50 sales is rendered as the time-window total, with no scoping qualifier, beside a control that implies scoping.

Maintainer defences considered and weighed:
(a) "It's a feed widget summarizing the rows below, not an analytics panel." Fails on two grounds — the stat is coupled to a time-window control that changes it, and it is not a summary of the rows below either, since `visible` flows through `filtered` (type filter + search, :156-173) while statsSource ignores both. The summarized population is labelled nowhere.
(b) "Nothing is fabricated; every summand is a real sale." True, and this is why severity stays at medium rather than high — it is not the failed-read-laundering class, it is a correct measurement of the wrong population.
(c) "The author was deliberate." Self-incriminating: the comment at :182-185 says stats prefer fetchedActivities because it is "server-filtered to the chosen time range." The intent was a window total, so the page truncation is an unrecognized bug, not a deliberate page-scoped design.

Sharpest tell, stronger than the one in the finding: parseOpenSeaEvents (api.js:350-388) types every event as "sale", and the request already filters event_type=sale, so salesCount is essentially the page size. 7d/30d/All Time all read ~50 on a liquid collection. The stat is accurate below 50 sales in the window and saturates above it.

Load-More jump confirmed and sooner than claimed: RENDER_CHUNK=100 (:178) exceeds the 50-row page, so `filtered.length <= visibleCount` holds on the first click and :462-464 pages the API immediately, roughly doubling both figures.

Corrections needed to the write-up: fetchedActivities is cumulative across pages (:93-100), not a single page; native orderbook sales merge in (api.js:562-572) so it is not strictly 50; statsSource can fall back to the merged prop/trade list (:186-190); and OpenSea returns newest-first, so it is the 50 most recent, not "the first 50."

Confidence high — every claim is anchored to read source; no runtime execution was needed because the truncation is structural (page size passed straight into a server `limit` param).

survived.title: When the selected date range has no Alchemy sales, all-time results are silently substituted
survived.claim: `if (primaryResult.activities.length === 0 && !pageKey && daysBack < 365) { const allTimeResult = await fetchAlchemyActivity({ ..., daysBack: 3650 }); if (allTimeResult.activities.length > 0) primaryResult = allTimeResult; }`. The returned object carries no marker that the requested window was replaced. A second instance at api.js:461-467 retries getNFTSales with the fromBlock lower bound DELETED when the bounded call errors, again returning all-time data for a bounded request.
survived.failure_scenario: OpenSea is unavailable so the Alchemy fallback is in play. User clicks '24h'. There genuinely were zero sales in 24h — the honest answer. Instead the app re-queries 3650 days and renders years-old sales while the '24h' button stays highlighted, and the SALES/VOLUME header computes over them. The user is told '24h: 18 SALES, 2.1 ETH' when the true 24h answer is zero. The empty flag is also false, so the honest 'No indexed sales' empty state can never fire.
survived.suggested_fix: Keep the substitution if it is useful, but return a marker (e.g. rangeWidened: true) and have ActivityFeed render 'No sales in the last 24h — showing all-time instead' above the list, and suppress or relabel the header stats.

verdicts.correction:
CONFIRMED with three corrections and one expansion.

VERBATIM AT api.js:546-549 — the all-time substitution is exactly as quoted. The substituted object carries empty:false (set at api.js:480) and no marker of the swap. Secondary instance is real but mis-cited: claim says 461-467; the actual try/catch spans 462-474 with `delete params.fromBlock` at line 469.

UI DOES NOT RE-FILTER (ActivityFeed.jsx): `filtered` (156-173) filters only by type and search, no time predicate. `statsSource` (186-190) prefers fetchedActivities outright; totalVolume (196-200) and salesCount (202-204) reduce over it. Range button highlight is `daysBack === opt.value` (296-297) and daysBack state is untouched by the substitution, so the selected button stays lit. DATE_RANGE_OPTIONS (30-35) = [24h:1, 7d:7, 30d:30, All Time:3650], so 1/7/30 all satisfy `daysBack < 365`.

CORRECTION 1 — "the honest 'No indexed sales' empty state can never fire" is overstated. It still fires when all-time is also empty (primaryResult stays the bounded result with empty:true, rendered at ActivityFeed.jsx:340-341). Accurate version: it cannot fire for a genuinely-empty WINDOW on a collection that has older sales — precisely the case it exists to report.

CORRECTION 2 — the header does not literally print "24h: 18 SALES". The stats block (245-258) prints bare SALES/VOLUME; the window is conveyed only by the adjacent highlighted range button. Same defect, weaker copy than claimed.

CORRECTION 3 — the precondition is stated as a given. This requires the OpenSea primary to throw (api.js:535-540). That is routine rather than exotic (openseaGet throws after retries on 429; slugFor at api.js:334-340 returns null for an unconfigured contract so fetchOpenSeaActivity queries the hardcoded COLLECTION_SLUG and 404s every time for that collection), but it IS a precondition, so the defect is conditional, not always-on.

EXPANSION (strengthens the finding) — blast radius exceeds the activity tab. MarketIntegrity.jsx:317 calls the same fetchActivity with daysBack: WINDOW_DAYS (30) and renders explicit prose over the result: "Self-dealing over sales in the last 30 days." (line 194) and `${result.comparableSales} comparable sales (of ${result.totalSales}) in the last ${WINDOW_DAYS} days.` (line 203). When the substitution fires, that sentence is a literal false factual statement about the window — a stronger instance than ActivityFeed's merely-implied one. ComparableSales.jsx:34 (daysBack: 90) is exposed identically.

Severity medium is correct: real user-visible false aggregate, but gated behind an OpenSea failure, individual rows still carry honest timestamps (formatTimeAgo at ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47 renders an absolute date past ~1yr), and no money path depends on it.
verdicts.reasoning: Read frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:441-576 and frontend/src/nakamigos/components/ActivityFeed.jsx:30-405, plus MarketIntegrity.jsx:194-203,317. The quoted substitution block at api.js:546-549 is verbatim. Confirmed no client-side time filtering exists downstream: ActivityFeed's `filtered` memo filters only on type and search, and `statsSource` feeds salesCount/totalVolume directly from fetchedActivities, so the header aggregates do compute over substituted all-time rows while the selected range button remains highlighted (highlight is driven by unchanged `daysBack` state). DATE_RANGE_OPTIONS confirms 24h/7d/30d all fall under the `daysBack < 365` trigger. The second instance is real (delete params.fromBlock at api.js:469) though the cited line range is slightly off. Three details in the claim are overstated: the empty state can still fire when all-time is also empty; the header never literally prints the range label; and the OpenSea failure is a genuine precondition rather than the steady state. Offsetting this, the defect propagates to MarketIntegrity, which prints explicit "in the last 30 days" prose over the same possibly-substituted set — a stronger, more explicit false claim than the one reported. Net: not refuted, severity medium stands.

Code confirmed at frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:546-549 — when OpenSea throws (535-540), the Alchemy fallback returns zero rows, pageKey is null and daysBack < 365, the function silently re-queries with daysBack: 3650 and substitutes the result. The returned object ({activities, pageKey, empty}) carries no marker of the substitution. Second instance confirmed at api.js:465-473: on an Alchemy error the fromBlock lower bound is deleted and the call retried unbounded.

The maintainer defense partially holds on details but fails on substance. Holds: the gate is tight (only after OpenSea failure, only page 1, only on a genuine zero); api.js:440 documents Alchemy as "may be stale for some collections"; the fromBlock-delete retry is real resilience because getCurrentBlock() can return an estimated block (api.js:328-329) that overshoots and makes Alchemy reject the request. Two finding specifics are mis-stated: no "24h:" prefix is ever rendered (ActivityFeed.jsx:245-258 shows bare SALES/VOLUME), and rows self-disclose age via formatTimeAgo (ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47, prints "300d ago" or an absolute date past a year).

Fails: the range selector stays highlighted on 24h (ActivityFeed.jsx:296-297) and is the only control governing the list, so the unlabeled aggregate reads as window-scoped regardless of the missing prefix.

The finding also UNDER-scoped the blast radius, and that is what defeats the defense. fetchActivity has five other callers; two consume the window as an explicit user-visible sentence and never re-filter by time:
- MarketIntegrity.jsx:317 requests daysBack: WINDOW_DAYS (30), filters only on a.type === "sale" (line 334), and renders "Self-dealing over sales in the last 30 days." (:194) and "N comparable sales (of M) in the last 30 days." (:203). Under widening those sentences are false — the wash-trading verdict is computed over up to 3650 days on a trust surface.
- ComparableSales.jsx:34 requests daysBack: 90, never re-filters, renders an unqualified "Avg: X ETH" (:96), and its empty branch claims "No comparable sales in the last 90 days" (:80). That average feeds listing-price decisions.

Condemning contrast: useSmartAlerts.js:230 requests daysBack: 1 then re-filters a.time >= cutoff (line 235) before firing alerts — immune. The codebase already treats the returned window as untrustworthy in one place; the two labeled consumers did not get the memo.

Severity stays medium (requires the degraded OpenSea-down state), but the accurate framing is broader than "the activity tab substitutes all-time results": it is an unmarked window substitution at the API layer that makes two literal window claims false downstream. The fix is at the source — the widened/unbounded results should carry the window they actually cover (e.g. windowDays / widened: true) so consumers can re-filter or disclose. Between the two instances, api.js:546 is the significant one; api.js:465-473 is the same class but lower impact since order:"desc" makes the unbounded result most-recent-first, so it only launders on a dead collection.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version: "Alchemy fallback silently widens the requested time window to 3650 days with no marker on the result, making downstream window labels false." Confirmed at api.js:546-549 (zero-result widening) and api.js:465-473 (fromBlock deleted on error, never restored). The result object exposes no windowDays/widened flag, so callers cannot detect or disclose the substitution.

Corrections to the original finding: (1) No "24h: 18 SALES" string is rendered — ActivityFeed.jsx:245-258 shows unqualified SALES/VOLUME; the misleading part is that the range button stays highlighted (ActivityFeed.jsx:296-297) while the aggregate silently covers a different window. (2) Rows do disclose age (ActivityFeed.jsx:37-47 renders "300d ago" / absolute dates), so the feed itself is only partly misleading — the header aggregate is the dishonest surface. (3) The "empty flag stays false so the honest empty state can never fire" point is technically true but redundant: with rows present the empty state would not render anyway.

Material omission the finding missed — the strongest evidence: MarketIntegrity.jsx:317 (daysBack: 30) does not re-filter by time (line 334 filters type only) yet renders the literal sentences "Self-dealing over sales in the last 30 days." (:194) and "N comparable sales (of M) in the last 30 days." (:203). ComparableSales.jsx:34 (daysBack: 90) likewise never re-filters, renders an unqualified "Avg: X ETH" (:96), and claims "No comparable sales in the last 90 days" in its empty branch (:80). By contrast useSmartAlerts.js:230 re-filters a.time >= cutoff (line 235) and is immune — proving the returned window is already known to be unreliable.

survived.title: Fabricated FALLBACK_ACTIVITY sales can render unbadged as real activity
survived.claim: For the canonical contract, fetchActivity returns FALLBACK_ACTIVITY (4 hand-written sales with prices 0.11/0.1101/0.1123/0.1099 ETH and fake truncated addresses) when both live sources fail (api.js:553-554). ActivityFeed stores that in apiFallback, but apiFallback is only consulted for the EMPTY state (line 342) — and the list is not empty, it has 4 rows. The 'Showing cached example data' banner is gated on the separate `isLive` PROP, which comes from useCollection's own independent fetchActivity call. Each fallback row carries `sample: true` (constants.js:249-252) and nothing in components/ reads that field.
survived.failure_scenario: useCollection's poll succeeded a moment ago so isLive === true. The user then clicks '7d', which fires ActivityFeed's own fetchActivity; that call hits the transient outage and returns FALLBACK_ACTIVITY. Result: four invented Nakamigos sales render as ordinary rows, with no banner, and the header reads SALES 4 / VOLUME 0.4323 ETH. fallbackHonesty.test.js:32 asserts `a.sample === true` "for any inline watermark consumer" — there is no such consumer.
survived.suggested_fix: Drive the banner from the component's own apiFallback state (OR it with the isLive prop), and render the per-row `sample` flag as a visible SAMPLE chip in the activity-row, the same way the wash badge is rendered at lines 389-408.

verdicts.correction:
Finding is CONFIRMED with two corrections.

CORRECTION 1 (arithmetic): fabricated volume is 0.4423 ETH, not 0.4323 (0.11 + 0.1101 + 0.1123 + 0.1099 = 0.4423).

CORRECTION 2 (finding understates the harm): the finding implies the fabricated header stats fill an otherwise-empty header. In fact ActivityFeed.jsx:186-190 sets `statsSource = (fetchedActivities.length > 0) ? fetchedActivities : activities`, so the 4 fabricated rows DISPLACE a real count. Even when `propActivities` from useCollection holds genuine live sales, the header reads SALES 4 / VOLUME 0.4423 ETH because fetchedActivities wins the ternary. Separately, `mergeBase` (ActivityFeed.jsx:131-147) dedupes by `hash`, and the fallback rows carry `hash: null`, so all four are unconditionally appended into the rendered list next to the real rows.

ACCURATE VERSION: ActivityFeed keeps the rows from a failed read but drops the flag that says they are not real.
- api.js:553-554 returns `{ activities: FALLBACK_ACTIVITY, fallback: true }` when both OpenSea and Alchemy throw for the canonical contract. Reachable: lib/proxy.js:90-94 and :148-152 raise ApiError on !res.ok and on network/timeout, so both fetchers genuinely throw.
- constants.js:248-252 defines 4 invented sales (0.11/0.1101/0.1123/0.1099), hash: null, sample: true.
- ActivityFeed.jsx:104 stores the flag in `apiFallback`; ActivityFeed.jsx:338-353 reads it ONLY inside the `filtered.length === 0` empty state, which cannot fire with 4 rows present.
- ActivityFeed.jsx:262 gates the "Showing cached example data" banner on the `isLive` PROP, written solely by hooks/useCollection.js:75 from that hook's own independent fetchActivity (useCollection.js:62). loadActivities never touches it.
- No component reads `a.sample`. A grep of frontend/src/nakamigos/** finds only constants.js:249-252 (the definition) and fallbackHonesty.test.js:32. The test comment "for any inline watermark consumer" describes a consumer that does not exist.
- The row renderer (ActivityFeed.jsx:377-453) applies only the POSSIBLE WASH badge, and lib/washTrade.js:39-41 rejects truncated display strings, so isSelfSale is false for these rows and they render as ordinary sales.

PROOF THIS IS AN OMISSION, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE: MarketIntegrity.jsx:318 handles the identical envelope correctly with `.then((res) => (res && res.fallback ? { activities: [], fallback: true } : res))`, discarding the fabricated rows. WhaleIntelligence.jsx:186,200 derives its live badge from `!data.fallback`. ActivityFeed is the sole consumer that keeps the rows and discards the flag.

SEVERITY stays medium. Aggravating: a user is shown four invented Nakamigos sales as real, with the header LIVE badge still lit (Header.jsx:585, same isLive), and headline SALES/VOLUME computed entirely from invented prices. Mitigating: the fixed FALLBACK_ACTIVITY_REF makes rows read ~"213d ago" rather than fresh; hash: null suppresses the Etherscan link (ActivityFeed.jsx:440); and the divergence requires one source to succeed while the other fails at a different moment (useCollection polls on a 60s/300s interval, loadActivities refires on the daysBack button) — a total proxy outage fails both and correctly shows the banner.
verdicts.reasoning:
I read every file in the chain and could not refute any link.

1. api.js:548-556 — the FALLBACK_ACTIVITY branch is inside `catch` around fetchAlchemyActivity, itself inside `if (!primaryResult)` after fetchOpenSeaActivity's catch. I verified both fetchers throw rather than returning an empty envelope: fetchOpenSeaActivity (api.js:391-409) awaits openseaGet with no internal catch, and fetchAlchemyActivity (api.js:441-478) rethrows when the no-fromBlock retry also fails. lib/proxy.js:80-94 and :140-152 throw ApiError on both network failure and !res.ok. So the fallback path is live code, not dead.

2. ActivityFeed.jsx:104 sets apiFallback. I grepped every use of apiFallback in the repo: lines 61, 104, 342, 351 only. 342 and 351 are both inside the `{!loadingFresh && filtered.length === 0 && (...)}` block opened at line 334. With 4 rows, filtered.length is 4, so neither renders.

3. ActivityFeed.jsx:262 is `{isLive === false && activities?.length > 0 && (` — the banner. I traced isLive: it is a prop (line 49), passed from App.jsx:757 out of useCollection() (App.jsx:338). useCollection.js:27 declares it, and the only writes are :50 (reset to false on collection change) and :75 `setIsLive(!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback)` from the hook's own fetchActivity at :62. ActivityFeed's loadActivities (:84-114) never writes it. Confirmed independent.

4. I grepped `sample` across frontend/src/nakamigos/**. Every hit is either an unrelated statistical-sampling use (TraitExplorer, FilterSidebar, Gallery, Deals, MarketIntegrity, TraitBidPanel, useSound), the constants definition, or the test. No component reads the `sample` field. The finding's claim about fallbackHonesty.test.js:32 asserting an invariant with no consumer is exactly right — I read lines 23-34 and the comment literally says "for any inline watermark consumer."

5. I checked whether the wash badge might incidentally mark them: lib/washTrade.js normalizeAddr requires /^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$/, and the fallback rows carry only truncated `from`/`to` like "0xd5a1...c442" with no fromFull/toFull, so isSelfSale returns false. No badge.

6. I recomputed the volume and got 0.4423, not the finding's 0.4323.

7. I found the finding understated the stats impact by reading ActivityFeed.jsx:186-190, where statsSource prefers fetchedActivities over the merged list — meaning fabricated rows override a real count rather than merely filling an empty one.

8. The strongest evidence against "this is intentional": MarketIntegrity.jsx:318 in the same directory does the correct thing with the same envelope, converting a fallback response to an empty list plus a flag. That establishes the project's own convention and shows ActivityFeed diverges from it.

Nothing I found supports refutation. The scenario the finding describes is reproducible from the source as written.

CONFIRMED by reading the full chain.

Maintainer's defense (and why it fails): the intended design is that `isLive` is a single global honesty signal — useCollection.js:62 fetches the same endpoint at the same default range (daysBack defaults to 30, matching ActivityFeed's initial state) and sets isLive = !statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback (line 75), polling every 60s/300s. FALLBACK_ACTIVITY is also deliberately defanged: fixed past timestamp (constants.js:246-247), synthetic truncated addresses, hash:null so no Etherscan link renders (ActivityFeed.jsx:440). That defense does not hold, because ActivityFeed issues its OWN independent fetchActivity (ActivityFeed.jsx:91) and never feeds the outcome back into isLive — it has no setter for it. The banner at ActivityFeed.jsx:262 is therefore gated on the result of a DIFFERENT network call than the one that produced the rows on screen.

survived.title: Trait and character-type floor prices are computed over the loaded token subset and rendered with no qualifier
survived.claim: traitFloors takes the minimum listing price across tokens present in the `tokens` array only. That array is paged 40 at a time (useNfts.js:33, loadAll pages every 200ms) so for a 20,000-supply collection it is a partial sample for minutes. The resulting price is rendered in green at line 806-809 with no '~', no tooltip, and no sample note — even though the very same component prefixes every rarity percentage with '~' when isSampled is true. CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:389-393 is worse: it labels the same sample-derived minimum literally 'Floor: 0.118 ETH'.
survived.failure_scenario: 20 seconds after opening Traits, ~800 of 20,000 tokens are loaded. A 'Gold Chain' row shows 0.25 ETH. The user treats that as the cheapest listed Gold Chain and bids/buys accordingly. A Gold Chain is in fact listed at 0.09 ETH — its token simply had not been paged in yet. Unlike the percentages, nothing on screen signals the number is provisional, and it silently drops as more pages arrive.
survived.suggested_fix: Gate the price cell on !isSampled, or prefix it with the same '~' / 'from loaded' marker used for the percentages, and change CharacterTypeExplorer's literal 'Floor:' label to 'Cheapest loaded:' while sampled.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the files. TraitExplorer.jsx:427-449 computes traitFloors by iterating `tokens` (line 438) and joining to a listings price map, so each trait floor is a minimum over listings-intersect-loaded-tokens. TraitExplorer.jsx:806-809 renders that value in green as `{floorPrice.toFixed(...)} ETH` with no `~`, no tooltip, no sample note — while the same component's rarity percentage on line 800 and its row title on line 794 both add `~`/" loaded" when `isSampled`. CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:279-305 does the identical tokens-side join and renders it at :389-393 as the literal `Floor: 0.118 ETH`, inside a section whose subtitle (:349) says "12 distinct character types across 20,000 Nakamigos" — full-collection framing with no sample indicator anywhere in that section.

Paging premise verified: useNfts.js:33 (`limit: 40`) and useNfts.js:135-137 (loadAll paces pages 200ms apart). Nakamigos supply is 20000 (constants.js:34), so 500 pages, minutes of partial data; TraitExplorer.jsx:611 renders the main view as soon as tokens.length > 0, so floors paint from the first 40 tokens. App.jsx:753 passes `nfts.allTokens` (unfiltered), so load progress is the only gap. Error direction confirmed: a minimum over a subset is monotonically >= the true minimum, so the displayed floor is always too HIGH and drifts downward as pages arrive — the user over-bids/overpays. useListings.js:17-20 fetches the cheapest listings first, so the cheap comparable is almost certainly already in `listings` and is missing only because its token row has not been paged in — this makes the scenario more likely, not less.

Two corrections. (1) "nothing on screen signals the number is provisional" is overstated for TraitExplorer: TraitExplorer.jsx:674-682 shows a "Tokens Loaded — N of 20,000 supply" card. But its parenthetical reads "(trait % from loaded sample)", explicitly scoping the caveat to percentages, which invites the reader to assume the floor is not sampled. The claim is fully accurate for CharacterTypeExplorer, which has no such card. (2) Strengthening detail the finding missed: TraitExplorer receives no `error` prop (App.jsx:753) and useNfts.js:126 halts loadAll permanently on the first failed page, so a mid-load fetch failure freezes the sample indefinitely — the floor never converges and the user is never told loading stopped.

Severity medium stands: a money-relevant number, styled as settled fact, wrong in the direction that costs the user, with no qualifier on the CharacterTypeExplorer half at all.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written for CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:389-393 ("Floor: X ETH", no sample signal in that section, subtitle at :349 frames it as "across 20,000 Nakamigos"). For TraitExplorer, amend "nothing on screen signals the number is provisional": a "Tokens Loaded — N of 20,000 supply" card does exist at TraitExplorer.jsx:674-682, but its parenthetical says "(trait % from loaded sample)", scoping the caveat to percentages only and implying the floor is not sampled. Add: TraitExplorer is passed no `error` prop (App.jsx:753) and useNfts.js:126 halts loadAll on the first failed page, so a fetch failure mid-load freezes the sample permanently — the floor stays wrong indefinitely with no error surfaced.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced against the source. TraitExplorer.jsx:427-449 builds traitFloors by iterating `tokens` (the loaded subset; App.jsx:740 passes nfts.allTokens) and looking each token up in a tokenId->price map built from `listings`. Because the trait association comes from the token side, a genuinely cheaper listing is invisible until its token pages in, even though `listings` is collection-wide and sorted cheapest-first (api.js:724, 788). Paging is 40 per request (useNfts.js:33) at 200ms intervals (useNfts.js:137), so 20,000 supply is a partial sample for minutes. The result renders at 806-809 in green with no qualifier, while the same component prefixes pct with "~" at 689, 700, 800 and appends " loaded" at 554 and 794. CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:391 prints it as a flat "Floor: X ETH" and is not even passed isSampled (line 275), so it cannot qualify it.

The maintainer defenses do not survive: (a) the only on-screen caveat, line 679-680, reads "(trait % from loaded sample)" — it scopes sampling to the percentage and thereby implies the floor is exact, which is worse than silence; (b) "overstated floor is the safe direction" fails because the null-floor branch renders a Make Offer button whose modal, when opened from the grid row (813 -> 862-869), receives no `sampled` prop (unlike TraitBidPanel at 570), so a too-high sample floor anchors a real offer amount.

The finding is also understated in two ways worth recording. First, the missing-floor case is a stronger false claim than the wrong number: a trait whose listed tokens have not paged in shows "Offer", indistinguishable from a genuine no-listings state. Second, the window is not necessarily transient — loadAll halts permanently on one failed page (useNfts.js:126) and TraitExplorer's trigger effect (379-381) depends on stable [loadAll, hasMore] so it never re-fires; App.jsx wires error/onRetry only to Gallery (690, 694), not to Traits (740), so a frozen sample is completely silent on this tab.

One correct concession to the maintainer: this is not the failed-read-laundering class. traitFloors returns {} on empty listings and every displayed price is a real listing for a real matching token. It should be classified as an unqualified sample-derived estimate on a money-adjacent path. Severity stays medium (no funds move automatically, happy path self-heals), at the top of the band.
verdicts.correction: Accurate restatement: trait and character-type floors are the minimum listing price over the intersection of (loaded tokens) x (collection listings). Because trait membership is read from the token side, cheap listings for un-paged tokens are invisible, so during the paging window the displayed floor is too high — or absent entirely, in which case the row renders a "Make Offer" button that reads as "nothing listed". Neither state is qualified: TraitExplorer.jsx:806-809 shows a bare green ETH figure and CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:391 asserts "Floor: 0.118 ETH", even though the same TraitExplorer prefixes every sampled percentage with "~" (689, 700, 800). Two aggravating factors the original finding omits: (1) the one caveat on screen, TraitExplorer.jsx:679-680, says "(trait % from loaded sample)", explicitly scoping sampling to percentages and implying the floor is exact; (2) the window is not bounded — loadAll stops permanently after any failed page (useNfts.js:126) and TraitExplorer's trigger effect (379-381) never re-fires, while App.jsx wires `error`/`onRetry` only into Gallery (690, 694) and not Traits (740), so a frozen partial sample produces a permanently wrong floor with no banner and no retry. Money impact is via anchoring: MakeOfferModal opened from the grid row (813 -> 862) gets no `sampled` prop, unlike TraitBidPanel (570). Severity: medium, top of band.

survived.title: "Rarest Trait" names a specific trait as the collection's rarest from a partial first page
survived.claim: summaryStats scans the loaded-sample trait map for min/max pct and renders the winners in headline stat cards labelled 'Rarest Trait' and 'Most Common' (lines 683-704). The '~' prefix qualifies the PERCENTAGE but not the RANKING — the card asserts which trait is rarest, and with a 40-token first page every trait seen once ties at 2.5% and the winner is whichever the object-key iteration happened to reach first.
survived.failure_scenario: User opens Traits on Nakamigos. Before loadAll finishes (500 pages at 200ms+latency, i.e. minutes), the card reads 'Rarest Trait: Bucket Hat ~2.5% · Hat/Helmet'. Nakamigos' actual rarest type is Ghost at 0.045% — the app's own constants.js:360 says so. The named trait is simply wrong, not merely imprecise, and it reshuffles as pages arrive. rarityColor() (line 358) also paints nearly every trait gold 'ultra rare' at small sample sizes because sample percentages are inflated.
survived.suggested_fix: Suppress the Rarest/Most Common cards while isSampled is true (or until a minimum sample fraction is reached), or label them 'Rarest so far (partial load)'.

verdicts.reasoning: Mechanism reproduces exactly at the cited lines. TraitExplorer.jsx:683-693 renders a stat card labelled "Rarest Trait" whose gold value is summaryStats.rarest.value; the isSampled "~" at line 689 is attached to the percentage string only, not to the label or the trait name. summaryStats (452-464) picks the min pct with strict `<` over traitMap, whose categories come from Object.entries insertion order and whose values are pre-sorted count-DESC (421), so ties are broken purely by iteration order. The sample really is tiny at first paint: useNfts.js:33 fetches limit:40; Nakamigos supply is 20000 (constants.js:34); the auto-paginator at useNfts.js:100-115 is gated to collection.supply < 1000 so it never fires for Nakamigos; only loadAll (TraitExplorer.jsx:379-381) paginates at 200ms/page = 500 pages; and TraitExplorer.jsx:611 only blocks render when tokens.length === 0, so the panel paints at 40 tokens where every singleton is exactly 2.5%. Stronger than the finding stated: useNfts.js:126 halts loadAll permanently on any fetch error with no retry on this tab, freezing the sample. THREE CORRECTIONS. (1) The "Ghost at 0.045%" counterfactual is not supported: constants.js:360 exists but CHARACTER_TYPES is itself a hardcoded array and Ghost is the rarest character TYPE, not established as the rarest trait value across all categories, which is what this card compares. (2) The "ultra rare" label does not exist in TraitExplorer.jsx; rarityColor (358) returns only a CSS colour, and the string lives in CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:5 and Modal.jsx:614. Also 2/40 = 5.0% fails `pct < 5`, so only singletons go gold, not "nearly every trait". (3) The finding omits the mitigation in the SAME panel: TraitExplorer.jsx:674-682 renders "Tokens Loaded / 40 / of 20,000 supply (trait % from loaded sample)", and the sampling choice is documented at 398-402. Severity drops to low: no money path, sampling is disclosed adjacent, and it self-corrects as pages arrive. Separately discovered and worth its own finding: api.js:167-170 returns FALLBACK_NFTS (~30 hardcoded mock tokens with fabricated attribute values, constants.js:211-242) with continuation null on any Alchemy failure for the Nakamigos contract, so hasMore goes false, loadAll never runs, and the "Rarest Trait" card names a trait computed entirely from mock data with no error state shown - that is the real failed-read-laundering instance on this tab.
verdicts.correction: TraitExplorer.jsx:683-693 labels a stat card "Rarest Trait" and names a specific trait value. The ranking is computed over the loaded sample only (452-464, strict `<` over insertion-ordered keys), so at the 40-token first page (useNfts.js:33; Nakamigos supply 20,000; auto-load gated to supply < 1000 at useNfts.js:101) every singleton ties at 2.5% and the winner is decided by object-key iteration order rather than rarity. The "~" at line 689 qualifies the percentage, not the ranking. Partially mitigated by the adjacent card at 674-682 reading "of 20,000 supply (trait % from loaded sample)", and it self-corrects as loadAll paginates - except loadAll halts permanently on a single fetch error (useNfts.js:126) with no retry on this tab. The claim that the true answer is "Ghost at 0.045%" is not supported by the code (constants.js:360 is a hardcoded character-TYPE table, a different comparison set), and rarityColor (line 358) applies only a gold colour, not an "ultra rare" label - that string is in CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:5 and Modal.jsx:614, not this file. Severity: low. Separate, more serious sibling on the same card: api.js:170 substitutes ~30 hardcoded FALLBACK_NFTS (constants.js:211-242) with fabricated attribute values on Alchemy failure, so the "Rarest Trait" card confidently names a trait derived from mock data with no error indication.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on the core claim, with the rarityColor half REFUTED and the framing too narrow.

Maintainer steelman (real, and partly holds): the sample-incidence choice is deliberate and documented at TraitExplorer.jsx:396-402; every percentage carries a "~" while sampled (:689, :700, :794, :800); a disclosure card renders "Tokens Loaded 40 / of 20,000 supply (trait % from loaded sample)" at :674-682; loadAll() fires on mount (:379-381) so the state self-corrects at full load. That argument fully covers the PERCENTAGE.

It does not cover the NAME, and it collapses on two failure paths:
1. :687 renders summaryStats.rarest.value (the trait name) in gold headline position under the label "Rarest Trait". The "~" sits on the line below, bound to pct. The identity/ranking claim is unhedged.
2. :459 uses strict `<`, so the first minimum wins. Iteration order is Object.entries(map) from the token scan (:405-412) = order of first appearance; within a category values are count-DESC sorted (:421, stable). At limit:40 (useNfts.js:33) every singleton ties at exactly 2.5%, so the displayed winner is decided by which token Alchemy returned first, not by rarity. Same for "Most Common" (:460). A noisy estimate is defensible; a superlative resolved by insertion order is not an estimate at all.
3. NOT reliably transient. (a) useNfts.js:126 halts loadAll permanently on any fetch error, and App.jsx:753 passes TraitExplorer no error and no loading prop, so a rate-limit at page 12 freezes "Rarest Trait: X" over 480/20,000 tokens with UI identical to a converged read. (b) api.js:170 returns FALLBACK_NFTS on total failure with continuation:null -> hasMore false -> loadAll never fires; those are 12 hardcoded tokens (constants.js:211-224) with invented values (Zombie, Ape, Robot, Human Pale) that are not real Nakamigos traits, so the card states "Rarest Trait: Robot ~8.3% · Type" as fact. Header DEMO badge is the only mitigation and App.jsx:820 passes `isLive || nfts.isLive`, so a live stats fetch keeps it reading LIVE over fabricated tokens. That is the failed-read-laundering class in its purest form.
4. Window: 20000/40 = 500 pages at 200ms throttle plus round-trip (useNfts.js:135-137) = minutes, above the fold.

REFUTED sub-claim: "rarityColor() paints nearly every trait gold 'ultra rare' at small sample sizes because sample percentages are inflated." The mechanism is backwards — inflated sample percentages push values ABOVE the 5% cutoff (:359), not below. At n=40 a value must be a singleton (2.5%) to go gold; count 2 = 5.0% -> blue. Small samples make gold RARER on that card. The residual real issue is milder: a 1-observation estimate gets a confident tier color whose true incidence spans 0.005% to several percent. The "ultra rare" label is invented — grep for ultra|legend in TraitExplorer.jsx returns zero hits; gold=ULTRA_RARE lives in the sibling CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:5-11 rendered below it for Nakamigos only (adjacency, not the claimed mechanism).

VERIFIED: constants.js:360 Ghost count 9, percentage 0.045. Minor precision note — that is a curated character-TYPE table, not necessarily the literal attribute key/value the API returns, so the scenario's apples-to-apples framing is loose, but the point survives (9-of-20,000 will essentially never land in a 40-token page).

Severity holds at medium: display-only, no money path, and partial disclosure genuinely exists — but the two stuck states put the worst case squarely in the failed-read class this project has been closing.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version — "Rarest Trait"/"Most Common" cards assert a winning trait BY NAME from the loaded sample; the "~" qualifies only the percentage, not the ranking (TraitExplorer.jsx:683-704, name rendered at :687/:698).

Two distinct defects:
(a) TIE-BREAK BY ARRIVAL ORDER. summaryStats (:452-464) uses strict `<` at :459, so among values tied at the sample minimum the winner is the first reached. Iteration order = Object.entries insertion order from the token scan (:405-412), values count-DESC within a category (:421, stable). At limit:40 (useNfts.js:33) every singleton ties at exactly 2.5%, so the named "Rarest Trait" is chosen by which token the API returned first and reshuffles every page. Not a noisy estimate — an arbitrary pick.

(b) THE WRONG NAME CAN PERSIST INDEFINITELY. loadAll halts permanently on any fetch error (useNfts.js:126; loadMore likewise gated at :86) and TraitExplorer receives neither `error` nor `loading` (App.jsx:753), so it renders no banner and no progress — a stalled 480/20,000 load is visually identical to a converged one. On total fetch failure api.js:170 substitutes 12 hardcoded FALLBACK_NFTS (constants.js:211-224) with continuation:null, so hasMore is false, loadAll never runs, and the card reports a "Rarest Trait" over invented values (Zombie/Ape/Robot/Human Pale) that do not exist in the collection. The header DEMO badge is OR'd (App.jsx:820 `isLive || nfts.isLive`) so it can still read LIVE.

DROP from the finding: the rarityColor claim. Small samples make gold rarer, not universal (inflated pct clears the 5% cutoff at :359), and no "ultra rare" string exists in this file — that label is in CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:5-11.

Minimal honest fix (not applied — read-only sweep): while isSampled, either suppress the name and show only a range, or label the card "Rarest in loaded sample" and stop resolving ties silently (e.g. render "N traits tied at ~2.5%"); and pass loading/error through App.jsx:753 so a halted or fallback load renders as unknown rather than as an answer.

survived.title: Character-type and ninja "filter the gallery" controls use hardcoded, admittedly guessed attribute keys
survived.claim: handleTypeClick always calls onFilterGallery('Type', typeName) with the key hardcoded — while typeFloors ten lines earlier hedges across three spellings, `a.key === "Type" || a.key === "type" || a.key === "Character Type"` (line 295-297), which is the code admitting it does not know the real key. handleNinjaView (line 319-333) maps display names to invented values ('Midnight Ninja' -> 'Ninja Midnight') under the comment "Ninja subtypes are TYPICALLY a 'Hat/Helmet' or 'Type' trait value", and TRAIT_LORE describes these as "community-discovered" variants — i.e. not distinct metadata values. useNfts.js:156-161 filters on exact key AND exact value.
survived.failure_scenario: User clicks the 'Ghost' card (or 'View in Gallery' on Midnight Ninja, advertised as '319 exist'). App navigates to the gallery with activeFilters {Hat/Helmet: ['Ninja Midnight']}, no token matches the literal value, and the gallery renders empty. The user concludes the collection has no Midnight Ninjas listed, or that the app is broken. Every one of the 12 type cards plus 3 ninja buttons rides on this — 15 controls, all of them advertised as clickable ('Click to filter the gallery', line 349).
survived.suggested_fix: Derive the key from the loaded tokens (find the attribute key whose value set matches CHARACTER_TYPES names) instead of hardcoding it, and drop or disable the ninja buttons unless the mapped value is actually present in the loaded attribute set.

verdicts.reasoning:
All quoted code facts reproduce verbatim: CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:312 hardcodes onFilterGallery("Type", typeName); :295-297 hedges three key spellings in typeFloors; :319-333 maps display names to invented values under a "typically" comment; useNfts.js:157-161 matches exact key AND exact value; App.jsx:753 wires changeFilter + tab switch; TraitExplorer.jsx:707-713 mounts the component for nakamigos only.

But the load-bearing step of the scenario -- "no token matches the literal value" -- is asserted, not demonstrated. No ground-truth Nakamigos metadata exists anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep for Boba / Pumpkin Spice / Ninja returns only constants.js and prose in About.jsx). Nothing in the files establishes the gallery goes empty.

The "Type" key is NOT guessed: Modal.jsx:605, RarityPriceScatter.jsx:630, and api-offers.test.js:35 all use a.key === "Type" unconditionally. The typeFloors hedge is one defensive lookup, not an admission. Calling the 12 type cards "admittedly guessed" overstates it.

The scenario is internally garbled: clicking the Ghost card sets {Type:['Ghost']}, not {Hat/Helmet:['Ninja Midnight']}. Two separate handlers were merged into one narrative.

The user-visible outcome is softer than claimed. Gallery.jsx:323-341 renders "No Nakamigos Match These Filters" / "Try removing some filters or adjusting the price range" with an active-filter chip count (Gallery.jsx:169). The user is told a filter matched nothing, not that the collection has no Midnight Ninjas -- this is a dead control, not failed-read laundering.

A confound the finding never mentions independently produces the identical symptom: useNfts.js:154-163 filters client-side over only tokens loaded so far, auto-load is gated to supply < 1000 (useNfts.js:101), and Nakamigos is 20,000 loaded 40 at a time. TraitExplorer.jsx:380 fires loadAll but that is ~500 pages at 200ms (useNfts.js:135-137). Clicking "Ghost" (9 of 20,000) yields an empty gallery for minutes even with a perfectly correct key and value. So an empty gallery is not evidence of the diagnosed cause.

What survives is narrow but real: the 3 ninja buttons. Their values exist only in this repo's own prose; the inline comment says "typically"; constants.js:429-431 and :525 label them "community-discovered". That is the one place a guess is documented in-code. Also worth noting: CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:2 imports TRAIT_LORE and never uses it -- the NINJA_SUBTYPES and RARE_COMBOS arrays are local hardcoded copies.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version, severity LOW: Three "View in Gallery" buttons in the Ninja Subtypes block (CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:413-429 -> handleNinjaView at :319-333) navigate to the gallery with a filter value that exists nowhere except this repo's own prose. The mapping "Midnight Ninja" -> "Ninja Midnight" is written under the comment "Ninja subtypes are typically a 'Hat/Helmet' or 'Type' trait value" (:322) -- "typically" is the author guessing -- and constants.js:429-431 / :525 describe these as "community-discovered" variants, i.e. possibly visual distinctions with no distinct metadata value. Since useNfts.js:157-161 requires an exact key+value match, a wrong value silently yields Gallery.jsx:329-341 "No Nakamigos Match These Filters". Failure scenario: user clicks "View in Gallery" on Midnight Ninja (advertised "319 exist"), lands on the gallery with {Hat/Helmet:['Ninja Midnight']} and an empty grid, and has no way to tell a bad filter value from a slow load.

NOT part of the finding: the 12 character-type cards. "Type" is used unconditionally by Modal.jsx:605, RarityPriceScatter.jsx:630 and api-offers.test.js:35, so it is the codebase's consistent key, not a guess. There is a separate unproven risk on the VALUES -- Modal.jsx:608 matches CHARACTER_TYPES with `typeAttr === t.name || typeAttr.endsWith(t.name) || typeAttr.startsWith(t.name)`, i.e. it tolerates a prefix/suffix, while the gallery filter demands exact equality. If real Type values are prefixed (the repo's own fallback data at constants.js:212-223 uses "Human Latte", "Human Pale"), the 12 cards would also filter to nothing. That is a real inconsistency worth a one-line check against live metadata, but it cannot be confirmed from the files.

Also not stated by the finding and independently material: the empty result is confounded by partial loading (useNfts.js:101/154-163) -- rare types like Ghost (9/20,000) render an empty gallery for minutes regardless of filter correctness.

Suggested fix framing: gate each of the 15 controls on the value actually being present in the loaded trait set (api.js:954-968 extractTraitFilters already produces it) -- hide or disable the control when it is not, the way TraitExplorer.jsx:558 already does by filtering on live-extracted selected.key/selected.value.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified against live on-chain metadata (1,500 tokens sampled from the collection's real IPFS CID at constants.js:35, https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmaN1jRPtmzeqhp6s3mR1SRK4q1xWPvFvwqW1jyN6trir9/N).

The defect is REAL and user-visible, but the finding's diagnosis is wrong in its central claim and overstated in blast radius.

REFUTED — "hardcoded, admittedly guessed attribute keys": the key "Type" at CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:312 is CORRECT. Every one of 1,500 sampled tokens carries {"trait_type":"Type",...}. The three-way hedge at lines 295-297 is defensive multi-collection coding, not an admission of ignorance. The finding built its title on the wrong half of the (key, value) pair.
