survived.title: Transaction History empty state promises offers and bids that nothing ever records
survived.claim: The empty state reads "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here." Every recordTransaction call site in the codebase passes `type: "buy"` — Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284 and :315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339 and :362, Deals.jsx:691, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170. No offer, bid, listing, cancel or transfer is ever written, even though TYPE_LABELS (lines 38-42) defines all seven labels as if they were.
survived.failure_scenario: User places a 0.05 WETH trait offer from the Traits tab, gets the 'Trait offer placed' toast, then opens History to check it. They see 'No Nakamigos transactions yet' together with a sentence stating that offers they make will appear there. They reasonably conclude the offer did not go through, and place it again — a second live WETH commitment against the same balance.
survived.suggested_fix: Either record offers/bids at the MakeOfferModal success branch (MakeOfferModal.jsx:120-129), or cut 'offers, and bids' from the copy so it reads 'Purchases you make for this collection will appear here.'

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED ON FACTS, OVERSTATED ON HARM.

Reproduced every factual assertion:
- frontend/src/nakamigos/components/TransactionHistory.jsx:103 renders exactly "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here." when walletHistory.length === 0 (guard at :89).
- TYPE_COLORS (:33-37) and TYPE_LABELS (:38-42) define seven types: buy, sale, offer, bid, list, cancel, transfer.
- The ONLY writer of the `${slug}_tx_history` localStorage key is recordTransaction at frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/transactions.js:34 (grep for `_tx_history` across frontend/src returns only TransactionHistory.jsx:11 read, transactions.js:8 read, transactions.js:34 write; HistoryPage.tsx uses an unrelated `tegridy_tx_history_` key outside this surface).
- All eight recordTransaction call sites pass a literal `type: "buy"`: Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284 and :315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339 and :362, Deals.jsx:691, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170. The finding's file:line list is exact.
- MakeOfferModal.jsx:120-129 fires the "Trait offer placed"/"Collection offer placed"/"Offer placed" toasts and calls onSuccess?.() with no recordTransaction call anywhere in the file. MyCollection.jsx's listing and cancelOrder flows likewise record nothing.

So six of the seven TYPE_LABELS entries (sale, offer, bid, list, cancel, transfer) are unreachable, and the sentence at :103 is a factual promise the code cannot keep. That is a real instance of the sweep's category 3 (copy describing behaviour the code does not have).

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG — the scenario. It claims the user "reasonably concludes the offer did not go through, and places it again — a second live WETH commitment." Three things in the actual files break that chain:
1. Placed offers ARE visible in this app, one nav item away. App.jsx:775 routes tab "bids" to BidManager; BidManager.fetchMyBids (BidManager.jsx:332-345) queries `orders/ethereum/seaport/offers` with `maker: wallet` and renders the user's live, non-cancelled, non-expired outgoing offers. Header.jsx:146 ("bids" -> "Bids") and :150 ("history" -> "History") place the two tabs adjacent in the nav.
2. Notably, BidManager does NOT launder a failed read: its catch sets `setFetchError("Failed to load bids. Check your connection.")` rather than rendering an empty list as "no bids" — so the surface that actually owns this data is honest.
3. MakeOfferModal.jsx:34 tracks activeOfferTotal from fetchMyOffers and :319-330 renders a "Warning: Your active offers (X WETH) plus this offer..." guard, so a re-open of the offer modal surfaces the existing commitment before a duplicate signs.
The user also received an explicit success toast naming the amount and trait.

ONE THING THE FINDING UNDER-STATES: the defect is not confined to the empty state. A wallet that has ever bought sees the populated list at :124-165, which silently omits their offers with no copy at all to explain the omission — same false impression, no sentence to blame. The empty-state string is just the one place the app writes the claim down.

ACCURATE VERSION: TransactionHistory only ever records purchases, so its empty-state copy at :103 promising offers and bids is false and misdirects the user away from the Bids tab that actually holds that data; six of seven TYPE_LABELS are dead. This is honest-copy drift, not a money-loss path — the offer succeeds, the toast confirms it, and BidManager displays it. Fix is one of: correct the sentence to "Purchases you make ... will appear here" plus a pointer to the Bids tab, or add recordTransaction calls with the offer/bid/list/cancel types the labels already anticipate. Severity low, not medium.
verdicts.correction: TransactionHistory.jsx:103's empty state promises "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here", but every one of the eight recordTransaction call sites passes type: "buy" (Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284/:315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339/:362, Deals.jsx:691, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170), and lib/transactions.js:34 is the only writer of the `${slug}_tx_history` key. MakeOfferModal.jsx:120-129 and MyCollection's list/cancel flows record nothing, so six of the seven TYPE_LABELS (sale, offer, bid, list, cancel, transfer) are unreachable. The populated list view (:124-165) has the same gap with no copy at all. The claimed duplicate-WETH-offer harm does not follow, however: the "bids" tab (App.jsx:775 -> BidManager.fetchMyBids at BidManager.jsx:332-345, queried with maker: wallet) does list the user's live outgoing offers and is adjacent to History in the nav (Header.jsx:146, :150); it surfaces a fetchError instead of an empty list on failure; the offer flow shows a success toast; and MakeOfferModal.jsx:319-330 warns on cumulative committed WETH before a second offer is signed. This is honest-copy drift that misdirects the user to the wrong tab, not a money-loss path — severity low.

verdicts.reasoning:
Core fact CONFIRMED and exhaustively verified. TransactionHistory.jsx:103 reads "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here." frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/transactions.js:34 is the ONLY writer to `${slug}_tx_history` (grep for `_tx_history` across frontend/src returns just transactions.js:8/:34, TransactionHistory.jsx:11, and an unrelated HistoryPage.tsx key). Every one of the 8 `recordTransaction` call sites passes `type: "buy"`: Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284 and :315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339 and :362, Deals.jsx:691-692, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170-171. So no offer, bid, list, cancel, sale or transfer is ever recorded, and the sentence states a present-tense behaviour the code does not have.

The maintainer defense (History = local purchase receipt log; offers are transient Seaport orders that belong on the live Bids tab) is coherent as an architecture, and it is real: App.jsx:774-775 routes "bids" to BidManager, whose fetchMyBids (BidManager.jsx:332-352) pulls the user's live outgoing Seaport offers from OpenSea, with Received Offers and Bid History panes alongside; MobileNav.jsx:20 ("Bids") and :25 ("History") both sit in MORE_TABS. But that defense convicts the copy rather than excusing it — if offers deliberately live on Bids, History must not claim them.

Where the finding is mis-stated: (1) The claimed harm "a second live WETH commitment against the same balance" is mechanically wrong. A WETH offer is a non-custodial signed Seaport order (MakeOfferModal.jsx:90-118 via api-offers createItemOffer/createTraitOffer/createCollectionOffer); nothing is debited at placement. Duplicating it yields a second fillable order, not a double-spend. (2) That exact hazard is already guarded: MakeOfferModal.jsx:67 loads the real active offer total via fetchMyOffers, and :316-338 renders a red role="alert" warning when active offers + this offer exceed WETH+ETH minus a gas buffer. (3) The scenario requires ignoring the full-screen confirmation at MakeOfferModal.jsx:228-239 ("Offer Submitted! / Your offer is now live on OpenSea") plus the success toast at :126, and missing a nav entry labeled "Bids". (4) The TYPE_LABELS (lines 38-42) point is filler — an unused enum branch in a render map is not a user-visible claim; the empty-state sentence is the whole defect.

Accurate version: TransactionHistory's empty state tells the user offers and bids will appear on this tab, but recordTransaction is only ever invoked with type "buy" and is the sole writer to the store — offers/bids surface on the Bids tab instead. A user who trusts the sentence may re-place an already-live offer, creating a duplicate fillable Seaport order. Severity low: genuine copy-vs-behaviour mismatch, narrow residual risk, materially mitigated by an explicit success screen, a live Bids tab, and an existing over-commitment guard.
verdicts.correction:
Real but mis-stated. Keep the finding, narrow it to the copy defect and drop the double-spend framing.

Accurate statement: TransactionHistory.jsx:103 tells the user that "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here," but frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/transactions.js:34 is the sole writer to `${slug}_tx_history` and all 8 recordTransaction call sites pass type: "buy" (Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284/:315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339/:362, Deals.jsx:691-692, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170-171). Offers and bids are never written there; they live on the Bids tab (App.jsx:774-775 -> BidManager.jsx:332-352, which fetches live Seaport offers from OpenSea).

Corrected failure scenario: user places a trait offer, sees the success toast, opens History and reads a sentence saying offers appear there, sees none, and re-places the offer — creating a second live, independently fillable Seaport order for the same intent. No balance is debited at placement (WETH offers are non-custodial), so this is duplicate-order risk, not a double spend.

Mitigations that cap the severity: MakeOfferModal.jsx:228-239 shows a full-screen "Offer Submitted! / Your offer is now live on OpenSea" confirmation; MakeOfferModal.jsx:316-338 already renders an over-commitment warning computed from the user's real active offer total (fetchMyOffers at :67); and the "Bids" nav entry (MobileNav.jsx:20) sits in the same menu as "History" (:25).

Severity: medium -> low. Fix is a copy change at line 103 (e.g. "Purchases you make through Tradermigos will appear here. Track live offers and bids on the Bids tab."), not a code change. The TYPE_LABELS/TYPE_COLORS observation (lines 33-42) should be dropped from the finding — unused render-map entries are not a user-visible claim.

survived.title: A browser-local log is presented as the user's transaction history with no device scoping
survived.claim: The only data source is `localStorage.getItem(`${slug}_tx_history`)`, wrapped in `catch { return [] }`. It is rendered under the unqualified heading 'Transaction History' (line 115) with the empty state 'No {collection} transactions yet' (line 100) — a factual statement about the user, produced by an empty or unreadable local cache. Nothing on the page says local-only, this-device-only, or last-50-only (lib/transactions.js:32 trims to 50).
survived.failure_scenario: A user who bought three Nakamigos through this very app on their desktop opens it on their phone (or in a private window, or after a browser storage clear, or after localStorage quota eviction). Connected to the same wallet, the History tab tells them 'No Nakamigos transactions yet'. The same sentence is produced by corrupted JSON, which the catch silently turns into []. A user checking whether a purchase actually landed gets a false negative from a cache miss.
survived.suggested_fix: Add a one-line qualifier under the heading ('Recorded on this device') and, for the empty state, offer an Etherscan/OpenSea link for the connected wallet the way the Activity tab does for OpenSea (ActivityFeed.jsx:355-374). Distinguish a JSON parse failure from a genuine empty log.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the files; could not refute. TransactionHistory.jsx:9-15 confirms the sole data source is JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(`${slug}_tx_history`) || "[]") inside try/catch { return [] } — there is no API, RPC, or indexer call anywhere in the 169-line component. Line 100 confirms the empty state "No {collectionName} transactions yet". lib/transactions.js:32 confirms the 50-item trim. A case-insensitive grep of the component for local|device|browser|stored returns only localStorage (line 11) and toLocaleString (line 26), both code — so the claim that no UI copy discloses local-only/this-device-only/last-50-only is verified. The tab is labeled bare "History" (Header.jsx:150, MobileNav.jsx:25) and the switch at App.jsx:782-783 is unconditional, so it ships to all users.

ONE MIS-STATEMENT: the "Transaction History" heading at line 115 and the empty state at lines 89-107 are mutually exclusive branches — the heading never renders alongside "No transactions yet", so it is not the unqualified frame at the moment of the false statement. The accurate frame is the nav label "History" plus TransactionHistory.jsx:77, "Connect your wallet to view your {collectionName} transaction history", which ties the view to the WALLET while the data is keyed only to the BROWSER.

TWO VECTORS THE FINDING MISSED, both strengthening it: (1) lib/transactions.js:33-35 has catch { /* quota */ } on setItem, so an on-chain purchase can silently fail to record on the SAME device — the false negative does not require a device switch; (2) localStorage.getItem throws SecurityError when storage is blocked (Chrome "block all cookies", embedded contexts), and the line-12 catch converts that failed read into "No transactions yet" rather than "can't read your history" — this is precisely the failed-read-laundering class.

SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to low: the empty-state subtext at line 103 ("Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here") partially scopes the view to in-app actions rather than a chain query; no transaction is built, signed, or priced on this screen; and genuinely on-chain surfaces exist for verification (portfolio -> PortfolioTracker and collection -> "My NFTs", App.jsx:798). A user misled into thinking a buy failed cannot readily double-buy, since they now own the token and it is no longer listed. Real honesty defect on a convenience log, not a money path.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: TransactionHistory (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/TransactionHistory.jsx) sources its entire content from browser localStorage (line 9-15, key `${slug}_tx_history`), with a catch that converts any read failure — corrupted JSON, or a SecurityError when storage is blocked — into an empty array. It renders under the bare nav label "History" (Header.jsx:150, MobileNav.jsx:25) and tells the user "No {collection} transactions yet" (line 100), a factual-sounding statement about the user produced by a cache miss. The connect prompt at line 77 ("Connect your wallet to view your {collection} transaction history") reinforces a wallet-scoped reading of data that is actually device-scoped. No UI copy discloses local-only, this-device-only, or last-50-only (lib/transactions.js:32 trims to 50). Note the "Transaction History" heading at line 115 is in the non-empty branch and never co-renders with the empty state, so the original finding's citation of line 115 as the unqualified heading over the false statement is incorrect. Additionally, lib/transactions.js:33-35 swallows setItem quota errors, so a completed on-chain purchase can go unrecorded on the same device, producing the same false negative without any device switch. Severity low, not medium: no money path on this screen, the line-103 subtext partially scopes the log to in-app actions, and on-chain verification exists in the portfolio and collection tabs.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced against the files. frontend/src/nakamigos/components/TransactionHistory.jsx:9-15 is the only data source: JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(`${slug}_tx_history`) || "[]") inside try/catch returning []. Rendered under the bare heading "Transaction History" (:115), a bare count (:121), and the empty state "No {collection} transactions yet" (:100). Nothing on the page says local-only, this-device-only, or last-50-only; lib/transactions.js:32 does slice(0,50).

The strongest maintainer defense — "localStorage is local and synchronous, so there is no upstream that can fail, and [] is indistinguishable from a legitimately fresh browser" — does not hold. Two concrete failure paths, one of which the original finding missed:

(a) SAME-DEVICE, SAME-SESSION false negative. lib/transactions.js:33-35 wraps setItem in `catch { /* quota */ }` and swallows the failure with no user signal. When site-data storage is blocked or partitioned for the origin, setItem throws and getItem also throws SecurityError (caught at TransactionHistory.jsx:12 -> []). Meanwhile the purchase is genuinely on-chain: api.js:1257-1260 awaits tx.wait() and rejects receipt.status === 0 before returning success, and Listings.jsx:545-547 only calls recordTransaction on that confirmed success. So the user gets "Successfully purchased #N!" and, seconds later on the same device, "No Nakamigos transactions yet." This is stronger than the cross-device scenario in the original claim, which is also valid (phone, private window, storage clear, ITP 7-day script-storage eviction).

(b) SILENT TRUNCATION. lib/transactions.js:32 keeps only 50 per collection; TransactionHistory.jsx:121 then renders "{collectionName} · N transaction{s}" as an unqualified count. A wallet with 60 recorded buys is told it has 50.

DEFECT THE FINDING MISSED (raises confidence that the framing, not the catch, is the real problem): the empty state at :103 reads "Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here." All eight recordTransaction call sites pass type: "buy" — Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284 and :315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339 and :362, Deals.jsx:691, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170. Grep for type: "offer"|"bid"|"list"|"cancel"|"transfer"|"sale" across frontend/src/nakamigos returns zero writes into this store (only api.js/eventFeed.js/constants.js activity-feed shapes). TYPE_LABELS at :38-42 advertises Offer/Bid/Listed/Cancelled/Transfer/Sale, none of which any code path can ever produce. So a user who places offers or bids sees the empty state promising those will appear, permanently.

WHERE THE FINDING IS MIS-STATED: it files this under failed-read laundering with the `catch { return [] }` as the mechanism. The catch is a minor contributor. The dominant defect is unqualified framing — a device-local, app-only, 50-entry receipt log presented under an unscoped "Transaction History" heading whose empty state makes a factual claim about the user's activity that a routine, invisible storage condition also produces.

The defense that no better source exists is half-refuted: OnChainProfile.jsx:212-221 already does a wallet-filtered chain read on this same surface (fetchActivity collection-wide, filtered client-side on fromFull/toFull), with an inline note that fetchActivity has no address-filter param. Imperfect (collection-wide last 50), but the pattern is present and unused here.

Severity stays MEDIUM, not high: no money path reads this store, nothing is built or signed from it, rows link out to Etherscan behind a strict /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/ guard (:153-163), the wallet filter at :62 is correct so no cross-wallet leakage, and a duplicate re-purchase of the same token is largely prevented because bought tokens are removed from the grid (Listings.jsx:549). Not low, because "Transaction History" is precisely the surface a user consults to confirm a purchase landed, and it answers with a definite negative.
verdicts.correction:
Accurate version, tab "history", frontend/src/nakamigos/components/TransactionHistory.jsx — severity medium, two defects:

1. Unscoped presentation of a device-local, 50-entry, app-only log. Sole source is localStorage `${slug}_tx_history` (:9-15). Heading "Transaction History" (:115), count "{collection} · N transactions" (:121), and empty state "No {collection} transactions yet" (:100) carry no local-only / this-device-only / last-50-only qualifier. Failure scenario (sharpest form, stronger than the cross-device one originally cited): with site-data storage blocked or partitioned for the origin, lib/transactions.js:33-35 swallows the failed setItem and TransactionHistory.jsx:12 swallows the throwing getItem. The user completes a receipt-confirmed purchase (api.js:1257-1260 awaits tx.wait() and rejects status 0), is toasted "Successfully purchased", opens History in the same session on the same device, and is told "No Nakamigos transactions yet." Cross-device / private-window / storage-clear / ITP-eviction produce the identical sentence. Truncation variant: 60 recorded buys renders as "50 transactions" (lib/transactions.js:32 -> :121).

2. Empty-state copy promises behaviour the code does not have. ":103 — 'Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here.'" All eight recordTransaction call sites pass type: "buy" (Listings.jsx:546, Modal.jsx:501, ShoppingCart.jsx:284,:315, SweepCalculator.jsx:339,:362, Deals.jsx:691, OrderBookPanel.jsx:170); no code path writes offer, bid, list, cancel, transfer, or sale, though TYPE_LABELS (:38-42) advertises all of them. A user who places offers and bids through the app is told they will appear here and they never will.

Framing note for whoever fixes it: the `catch { return [] }` is not the root cause and patching it alone changes nothing user-visible. The fix is (a) qualify the heading/empty state/count as this-device, app-recorded, last 50 — or back the view with the wallet-filtered chain read already used at OnChainProfile.jsx:214-221; (b) surface a distinct state when storage read/write is unavailable instead of rendering it as "no transactions"; (c) either drop offers/bids from the :103 copy or record them.

survived.title: Perk list and "perks light up automatically for holders" describe features that have no implementation anywhere in the app
survived.claim: PERKS (lines 7-13) promises "A Pro badge on your profile, chat handle, and listings", "A share of the platform fee on every buyer you refer", "Automation, smarter alerts, and Pro-only analytics first", and "Mint proceeds are ETH to the treasury → staker yield". Line 86 then states "The Pro Pass drops with the next wave — perks light up automatically for holders." Verified by grep over all of frontend/src: `useProAccess` is imported by exactly one file — ProMembership.jsx itself. No component anywhere reads `isPro` to render a badge (the only badge component, HolderBadge in useHolderStatus.jsx:113, is keyed on NFT count, not Pro). Grep for referral/referrer inside frontend/src/nakamigos/ returns ONLY ProMembership's own marketing copy plus `rel="noopener noreferrer"` — there is no referral-fee split in the marketplace (REFERRAL_SPLITTER_ADDRESS is the farm's, unrelated). TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS is 0x000…000 (lib/constants.ts:70), so no contract exists to route mint proceeds anywhere.
survived.failure_scenario: A user reads the page, believes flair/referral-cut/early-access are already implemented and gated only on a not-yet-deployed NFT, and buys a Pass the moment one exists (or waits for it as an investment). Even with the Pass in hand and PRO_PASS_LIVE flipped on, literally nothing in the app changes: no badge appears on their profile, chat handle, or listings; no referral fee accrues; no Pro-only tool unlocks. The word "automatically" is the load-bearing falsehood — there is no code that would activate.
survived.suggested_fix: Reword to forward-looking intent ("planned perks") until at least one perk has a consumer of `isPro`, or gate the perk rows on the features actually shipping.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every factual claim reproduces verbatim from the files; the only thing I would change is the severity, because current user-visible impact is exactly zero.

WHAT REPRODUCES (all confirmed):

- ProMembership.jsx:32-35 — the comment does state the in-app primary mint is wired "once the DropV2 Pro Pass is deployed", and that post-launch the button "opens the live collection so the funnel works the moment the address is set." Deliberate, documented, staged — not an oversight.
- The arming chain is a single constant, as claimed: constants.ts:70 `TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS = 0x000…0`; constants.ts:177-179 `isDeployed(a) { return a !== ZERO_ADDRESS }`; useProAccess.jsx:9 `PRO_PASS_LIVE = isDeployed(TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS)`. Setting one address simultaneously flips: the button's `disabled` (line 78), the label (41-43), the status pill from "MINTING SOON" to "NOT YET A MEMBER" (16-21), and swaps the honest pre-launch note (83-87) for "One mint, lifetime access — and it's yours to resell on the native book" (88-92). The hook's own comment at lines 5-8 states this auto-activation as the design intent.
- Reachability confirmed: `pro` is in the valid-tab list at nakamigos/constants.js:94 and rendered unconditionally at App.jsx:768-769.
- "No mint transaction" is stronger than stated: a real DropV2 mint path exists in this repo (frontend/src/hooks/useNFTDropV2.ts, used by components/launchpad/CollectionDetailV2.tsx) and this CTA does not use it. So the gap is a wiring gap, not a capability gap.

WHY I DOWNGRADE TO LOW, NOT REFUTE:
No user can currently see or suffer any of this. The button renders `disabled` at 0.55 opacity, reads "Minting soon", and the sub-copy honestly says the Pass "drops with the next wave." The scenario is entirely contingent on an operator action that has not happened. Under the sweep's own rule ("only report what a USER would see or suffer"), that is a latent pre-launch checklist item, not a shipped defect — hence low rather than medium. The precedent cited (the date-gated "+10% NFT boost" banner) is apt as a reason to track it, but that one was actually rendering; this one is not.

ONE CORRECTION / SHARPENING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:
The same single constant also arms a failed-read launder in the same feature. useProAccess.jsx:29-36 does `fetchWalletNfts(...).then(d => setIsPro((d?.totalCount || 0) > 0)).catch(() => setIsPro(false))`. Once live, an NFT-API outage makes a genuine Pass holder render "NOT YET A MEMBER" (line 21) and get a primary CTA reading "Mint Pro Pass" — i.e. the app invites a holder to buy a lifetime membership they already own. Both the `|| 0` and the `catch → false` collapse "read failed" into a confident negative claim about the user's wallet. That is the exact defect class this sweep targets, and it is armed by the same one-line change, which is the real argument for treating the whole Pro tab as needing review before the address is set — a stronger argument than the CTA mislabel alone.

ALSO NOTED (unconditional, live today, separate from this finding): the PERKS list at lines 7-13 renders regardless of the flag, asserting concrete mechanics — "A share of the platform fee on every buyer you refer" and "Mint proceeds are ETH to the treasury → staker yield" — for which no implementation exists (a repo-wide grep for referral logic in nakamigos/ hits only this file's copy string). The "MINTING SOON" pill and "drops with the next wave" framing make it read as roadmap rather than a live claim, which is why I do not treat it as a defect here, but it is the part of this page a user actually sees today.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written; severity should be low, not medium. Today the CTA is `disabled` (ProMembership.jsx:78) and reads "Minting soon" with honest pre-launch copy (83-87), so zero users are currently affected — this is a latent pre-launch trap, not a shipped defect. Two sharpenings: (1) the app does contain a working DropV2 mint path (frontend/src/hooks/useNFTDropV2.ts, used by components/launchpad/CollectionDetailV2.tsx) that this CTA simply does not call, so it is a wiring gap rather than a missing capability; (2) the more damaging thing the same constant arms is a failed-read launder at useProAccess.jsx:29-36 — `(data?.totalCount || 0) > 0` plus `.catch(() => setIsPro(false))` means an NFT-API outage renders a real Pass holder as "NOT YET A MEMBER" (line 21) and shows them a "Mint Pro Pass" button for a lifetime membership they already own. Both defects flip on together when TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS (constants.ts:70) is set, with no separate gate.

CONFIRMED, and the accurate scope is broader than reported — raise medium -> high.

Verified exactly as claimed:
- ProMembership.jsx:36-40 `onCta` does `window.open("https://etherscan.io/address/" + TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS)`. No transaction is built, signed or sent.
- ProMembership.jsx:41-43 label is "Mint Pro Pass" (connected non-holder) / "Manage your Pass" (holder) / "Connect to mint" / "Minting soon".

TWO MIS-STATEMENTS IN THE FINDING, both worth correcting:
1. "Currently unreachable" is imprecise. The tab IS reachable in production today (nakamigos/constants.js:94 lists "pro"; App.jsx:768-769 switches unconditionally). What is gated is the armed CTA. The PERKS block (lines 7-13, rendered at lines 57-72) has NO gate and is on screen right now.
2. "Arms itself the moment the operator sets the address" implies a runtime toggle. It is a compile-time `as const` in lib/constants.ts:70 — it takes a source edit, PR, build and redeploy. This is genuinely mitigating, but not protective: the arming diff is a single address literal whose review surface shows nothing about a CTA, a price, or perk copy. That is exactly the "+10% NFT boost" pattern — the gate defers the failure rather than preventing it.

WHY SEVERITY SHOULD BE HIGHER — the unbacked perk claims, which the finding did not catch:
I grepped all of frontend/src for `useProAccess` and `isPro`. useProAccess has exactly ONE consumer: ProMembership.jsx itself. The only other `isPro` hits are TradingModeContext.jsx:50/62-63, an unrelated lite/pro UI-mode flag. There is no `flair` implementation anywhere (the sole other "flair" hit, nakamigos/constants.js:350, is an NFT trait description). Therefore of the five perks advertised unconditionally today:
- "Pro flair across the app - A Pro badge on your profile, chat handle, and listings" (line 8) has no consumer anywhere.
- "Earn on who you bring - A share of the platform fee on every buyer you refer" (line 9) has no wiring from Pass ownership to any referral path.
Setting the address activates the StatusPill and the CTA and nothing else.

Compounding this, the comment at useProAccess.jsx:5-8 is itself false: it claims "every Pro perk + the mint funnel stay in their pre-launch state ... the whole feature auto-activates the moment TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS is set, no code change." There are no other perk consumers to auto-activate. That comment is precisely what would lead a future operator to set the address believing the product is complete.

CORRECTED FAILURE SCENARIO: Operator sets TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS to the deployed clone and redeploys. The page now presents a paid membership: five concrete perks (two of which have no implementation in the codebase), a "NOT YET A MEMBER" pill, "One mint, lifetime access", and a primary CTA reading "Mint Pro Pass". Clicking opens a raw Etherscan address page — no wallet prompt, no price, and for an unverified clone no Write tab at all. A user who perseveres must guess the payable value. A holder clicking "Manage your Pass" gets the same page with no manage capability of any kind; that label is false under every reading. Users who do mint receive none of the flair or referral revenue the page sold them.

MAINTAINER-SIDE DEFENSE THAT DOES HOLD: the staged rollout is documented (lines 32-35), the pre-live state is honestly labeled "MINTING SOON", and the button is genuinely inert today. The defense that "Etherscan is the real mint surface" does not hold — without a displayed price it is not a usable mint path, and it is not a manage path at all.
verdicts.reasoning: Read ProMembership.jsx in full, useProAccess.jsx in full, lib/constants.ts:66-70 and :177-179, and App.jsx:73/92/768-769 plus nakamigos/constants.js:94. Every mechanical claim in the finding reproduces at the cited lines: the CTA is a window.open to an Etherscan address page, the labels promise mint and manage, there is no price and no transaction, and the only thing standing between that copy and production is one zero-address constant. The maintainer case rests on three legs. Two are true but insufficient: the behaviour is documented in-code, and the trigger is a source commit rather than a runtime flag (the finding mis-stated this). The third — that Etherscan is a legitimate mint destination — fails, because no price is rendered anywhere, and it fails outright for the "Manage your Pass" branch, which has no corresponding capability. The deploy-gate argument also fails as a protection: the arming diff is a bare address literal that gives a reviewer no signal about the CTA or copy behind it, which is the same shape as the previously shipped date-gated banner incident. Investigating further raised the severity rather than lowering it: a grep of all of frontend/src shows useProAccess has exactly one consumer (this file), the other isPro hits being an unrelated trading-mode flag, and no flair implementation exists. So the unconditionally rendered PERKS list is advertising at least two perks with zero backing code, and the useProAccess comment asserting that every perk auto-activates is factually wrong — which is the mechanism by which an operator would ship this believing it complete. Not refuted; corrected to high with the perk-backing scope added and the two wording errors fixed.

survived.title: Chat loads the OLDEST 100 messages, not the newest — recent history silently disappears on reload
survived.claim: `fetchMessages` (JSDoc line 147: "Fetch recent messages.") queries `.order("created_at", { ascending: true }).range(offset, offset + limit - 1)` with offset=0, limit=100. Ascending order + range(0,99) returns the 100 OLDEST rows for the slug. CommunityChat.jsx:404 is the only caller and never passes an offset, and there is no load-more / pagination control anywhere in the component.
survived.failure_scenario: The nakamigos room accumulates 150 messages. A user opens the Chat tab and sees messages 1-100 — conversations from weeks ago — while the 50 most recent, including anything they posted yesterday, are absent with no indication. They post a message (it appears via the optimistic add), reload, and their message is gone: indistinguishable from being deleted or moderated. The MAX_RENDERED_MESSAGES=200 cap and its "Showing the latest 200 messages" notice (CommunityChat.jsx:519-730) can never fire because the fetch caps at 100.
survived.suggested_fix: Order descending with range(0, limit-1) and reverse client-side (or use a keyset on created_at), so the newest 100 load; add a load-older control if history depth matters.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the files. All load-bearing parts of the claim check out:

1. supabase.js:164-169 — `supabase.from("messages").select("*").eq("slug", slug).order("created_at", { ascending: true }).range(offset, offset + limit - 1)`. Defaults at line 151 are `limit = 100, offset = 0`, so the query is ORDER BY created_at ASC with `Range: 0-99` → the 100 OLDEST rows for the slug. The JSDoc at line 147 does say "Fetch recent messages." That is the opposite of what it does.

2. CommunityChat.jsx:404 is the ONLY caller in the whole tree (grep for `fetchMessages` across frontend/src returns only supabase.js definition/logging plus CommunityChat.jsx:5 import and :404 call). It passes only `tokenId` and `slug` — never `offset` or `limit`.

3. No pagination exists. A case-insensitive grep for `offset|load.?more` in CommunityChat.jsx returns zero hits other than the DM signal prop. There is no "load older/newer" control and no second page fetch. The only other message source is the realtime subscription (lines 424-444), which appends INSERTs that arrive AFTER subscribe — it never backfills the gap.

4. The tab is live and unconditional: App.jsx:97 lazy map, App.jsx:780-781 `case "chat": return <CommunityChat .../>`, no flag gate.

Failure scenario is real and as described: once a slug's room passes 100 rows, every fresh mount renders messages 1-100 (the oldest) as the whole chat. A user posts (optimistic add at CommunityChat.jsx:550-554 + realtime echo), reloads, and their message is absent with no indicator — the UI shows a normal, populated chat, not an error. Note the failure is specifically silent because the honest-failure path already exists and does NOT fire here: `fetchMessages` returns `null` on error (lines 176-182) and the component renders "Couldn't load messages right now" (CommunityChat.jsx:700). A truncated-window read returns a successful, well-formed `[]`-of-100, so it renders as if it were the full history. That is the same laundering shape the project has been closing, just via a wrong window rather than a caught error.

ONE SUB-CLAIM IS WRONG, and it should be struck from the writeup. "The MAX_RENDERED_MESSAGES=200 cap ... can never fire because the fetch caps at 100" is false. `visibleMessages` (CommunityChat.jsx:498-515) is derived from `messages`, which grows unbounded from realtime INSERTs — the code comment at lines 517-518 says exactly that ("realtime INSERTs grow the list unbounded over a long session"). A session that receives 100+ live messages crosses 200 and the "Showing the latest 200 messages" notice at line 729 fires normally. The cap is unrelated to this bug.

Also worth flagging for whoever fixes it: the ascending order is load-bearing for token mode. Non-token mode re-sorts by timestamp at line 504, but the `isTokenMode` branch (lines 501-502) only filters and relies on the fetch's ascending order for display sequence. A naive flip to `ascending: false` would render per-NFT comments newest-first/backwards. The correct fix is to fetch descending (newest 100) and reverse client-side before setState, or to switch to a keyset/"load older" pagination.

Impact is conditional on a room exceeding 100 messages, which I could not verify against production data from the repo (no retention/prune job found under supabase/). Medium is the right severity: silent, indistinguishable from moderation/deletion, but bounded to high-volume rooms and non-financial.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: `fetchMessages` (frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/supabase.js:151, query at :164-169) is documented as "Fetch recent messages" but orders `created_at` ASCENDING with `range(0, 99)`, returning the 100 OLDEST messages for the slug. Its sole caller, CommunityChat.jsx:404, passes no offset, and the component has no pagination control; the realtime subscription (CommunityChat.jsx:424-444) only appends messages arriving after mount and never backfills. Once a room exceeds 100 messages, every page load silently presents weeks-old history as the complete chat, and a user's own recent post vanishes on reload — indistinguishable from deletion or moderation. Because the fetch succeeds, the existing honest-failure path (null return at supabase.js:176-182 → "Couldn't load messages right now" at CommunityChat.jsx:700) never fires. STRIKE the claim that the MAX_RENDERED_MESSAGES=200 cap "can never fire": `messages` grows unbounded from realtime INSERTs (see the comment at CommunityChat.jsx:517-518), so the cap and its "Showing the latest 200 messages" notice do fire in long sessions and are unrelated to this defect. Fix note: token mode (CommunityChat.jsx:501-502) does not re-sort and depends on the ascending fetch order, so flipping to `ascending: false` requires reversing client-side. Severity: medium (unchanged).

verdicts.reasoning:
Confirmed at frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/supabase.js:151-184. `fetchMessages` defaults to limit=100, offset=0 and issues `.order("created_at", { ascending: true }).range(offset, offset + limit - 1)`. PostgREST applies range after ORDER BY, so this returns the 100 OLDEST rows for the slug, not the newest. The only caller is CommunityChat.jsx:404 (imported line 5), which never passes an offset, and there is no load-more / pagination control anywhere in the component (verified by grep: `hiddenCount` at line 523 is a render cap, not a fetch control).

Maintainer defenses considered and rejected:
1. "Ascending is intentional" — true but irrelevant. CommunityChat.jsx:504 re-sorts client-side (`[...list].sort((a,b)=>a.timestamp-b.timestamp)`), so a descending fetch would render identically. The sort cannot recover rows never fetched. This actually makes the fix contained and safe.
2. "Realtime covers it" — CommunityChat.jsx:424-444 only delivers INSERTs occurring after mount. Rows 101..N (N = row count at load time) are permanently unreachable on every reload.
3. "The failed-read path is handled" — it is, and correctly (supabase.js:176-182 returns null not [], so CommunityChat.jsx:408 renders "Couldn't load messages right now. The history is still there." at line 700 instead of the be-the-first empty state). But that machinery is bypassed here because the read SUCCEEDS — it just returns the wrong window. No error, no notice, no empty state.

Two aggravating factors beyond the report: (a) the scroll-to-bottom effect (lines 485-495) parks the user at the bottom of the oldest-100 list, so the newest visible message carries a formatTimeAgo stamp reading weeks old — the user reads "dead chat," not "truncated history"; (b) in room mode tokenId is null so supabase.js:171-173 never applies `.eq("token_id", ...)`, and room mode (lines 503-508) does not filter token-scoped rows back out — per-NFT comments consume the same 100-row budget, so exhaustion arrives sooner than a room-message count suggests.

One sub-claim is mis-stated and should be dropped: "the MAX_RENDERED_MESSAGES=200 notice can never fire" is false. visibleMessages grows via realtime INSERTs (lines 429-433), so a session receiving 100+ live inserts after mount crosses 200 and the line 729 notice renders. Rare, but reachable. Not load-bearing to the finding.

Local-mode note: the CHAT_ENABLED=false path (supabase.js:161) has the same oldest-100 slice, but is unreachable — CommunityChat.jsx:402 returns early and the local path uses loadMessages() (line 23) which reads all local rows. The bug is Supabase-mode-only, which is the live production mode (CHAT_ENABLED = !!(VITE_SUPABASE_URL && VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY), supabase.js:89).

Severity medium holds: not a money path, not failed-read laundering (the read succeeds), but silent permanent-feeling data loss that a user reads as moderation/deletion of their own post, with zero indication, degrading monotonically as the feature gains adoption.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: `fetchMessages` (supabase.js:151-184) selects the 100 OLDEST rows per slug rather than the newest, because `.order("created_at", { ascending: true })` is combined with `.range(0, 99)`. Once a room exceeds 100 rows — a budget shared between room messages and per-NFT comments, since room mode never applies the token_id filter — every page load renders a frozen archive of the earliest conversations. Newly posted messages appear via the optimistic add at CommunityChat.jsx:552 and then vanish on reload, indistinguishable from moderation or deletion. The visible tell is stale formatTimeAgo stamps at the bottom of the list, which reads as a dead chat rather than truncated history. Fix: fetch descending with `.range(0, limit-1)` and reverse client-side; the existing sort at CommunityChat.jsx:504 already normalizes render order. Drop the report's sentence claiming the MAX_RENDERED_MESSAGES=200 notice "can never fire" — realtime INSERTs (CommunityChat.jsx:429-433) can push visibleMessages past 200 within a session, so it is reachable, just rare. Severity remains medium.

survived.title: Liking a message silently does nothing when the backend call fails
survived.claim: `handleLike` (lines 586-592) only updates state when `toggleLike` returns a truthy row. `toggleLike` (supabase.js:266-274) catches every non-401 error — network failure, PostgREST 5xx, RLS rejection, missing RPC — and returns null. In that case handleLike takes no branch at all: no state change, no toast, no logging outside DEV. The heart glyph never fills and the count never moves.
survived.failure_scenario: User taps the ♡ on a message while the Supabase proxy is returning 500s (or their SIWE cookie's wallet no longer matches the connected wallet, so the RPC is rejected). The button visibly scales on hover and is clickable, but nothing happens — no error, no explanation, no retry affordance. The user concludes likes are broken/fake. Note handleReaction on the adjacent buttons at least toasts; likes don't.
survived.suggested_fix: Toast on a null return ("Couldn't save your like — try again"), mirroring the send path.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from the files, line for line.

CommunityChat.jsx:579-611 — `handleLike`. The `CHAT_ENABLED` branch is exactly:
  586  if (CHAT_ENABLED) {
  587    const updated = await runAuthed(() => toggleLike({ messageId: msgId, wallet, slug: collection.slug }));
  588    if (updated) {
  589      setMessages((prev) => prev.map((m) => (m.id === updated.id ? updated : m)));
  591    }
  592  }
There is no `else`. On a null return the handler falls off the end: no state change, no toast, no disabled/pending affordance.

lib/supabase.js:243-275 — `toggleLike`. The proxy path is 266-274: `proxyRpc("toggle_like", ...)`, and the catch rethrows ONLY `err.needsAuth`, logs behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, and `return null`. Per lib/supabaseProxy.js:22-32, `needsAuth` is set only on HTTP 401; every other outcome — fetch/network throw, 403 RLS rejection, 404 missing RPC, 5xx — becomes a plain Error and is swallowed to null. So a broken upstream is indistinguishable from "nothing happened", and in production builds nothing is even logged.

The button is a live, hover-animated control: CommunityChat.jsx:765-777, `onClick={() => handleLike(msg.id)}` with `onMouseEnter` scaling to 1.2. The glyph is derived from `liked` at line 735 (`msg.likes.some(...) === wallet`), i.e. purely from state that never changed, so the heart stays ♡ and the count at line 778-780 never moves.

The contrast asserted in the finding is also real, and is the strongest evidence this is an oversight rather than a decision:
- `handleReaction` (464-473) has `else if (CHAT_ENABLED) addToast?.("Reactions aren't enabled yet", "info")` on the identical null.
- `handleSend` (543-559) has `else { addToast("Failed to send message...", "error") }` on the identical null.
- The initial load (401-421) explicitly distinguishes null from [] and renders a "Chat Unreachable" empty state (694-699).
Likes are the one write in this component with no failure branch.

CHAT_ENABLED is `!!(SUPABASE_URL && SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)` (supabase.js:89), true in production, so the swallowing branch is the live one.

Two corrections to the finding as written:

1. Severity. I'd downgrade medium -> low. Nothing false is asserted to the user, no money or data is at risk, and no factual claim about a token/wallet is laundered — this is a silent no-op on a cosmetic social control, not the failed-read-laundering class. The user's inference ("likes are broken") is in fact correct at that moment, which is the opposite of the laundering defect. It is a genuine dead-control/missing-feedback bug, worth fixing with a one-line else, but it is the mildest kind.

2. One clause of the scenario is wrong. "their SIWE cookie's wallet no longer matches the connected wallet, so the RPC is rejected" does not happen: the proxy injects the cookie's verified wallet into the RPC args (supabaseProxy.js:42-44), so a mismatched cookie makes the like SUCCEED as the cookie wallet. That path is separately interesting — the returned row's `likes` will not contain the connected wallet, so `liked` at line 735 stays false and the heart still does not fill even though the write landed — but it is a different bug from the one claimed. The reproducible trigger for the claimed bug is a non-401 failure: proxy/PostgREST 5xx, offline/network throw, a 403, or `toggle_like` missing.

The accurate statement: on any non-401 failure of the toggle_like RPC, the like button is a completely silent no-op — no toast, no logging outside DEV, no visual state — while the adjacent reaction and send buttons both surface an error on the identical failure.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed at CommunityChat.jsx:586-592 and supabase.js:266-274, but restate as: "On any non-401 failure of the toggle_like RPC (proxy/PostgREST 5xx, network throw, 403, missing RPC), toggleLike swallows the error and returns null, and handleLike has no else branch — so the like button is a fully silent no-op: heart never fills, count never moves, no toast, no production logging. The adjacent handleReaction (:470-472) and handleSend (:557-559) both toast on the identical null." Drop the "SIWE cookie wallet mismatch" clause: the proxy injects the cookie's wallet server-side (supabaseProxy.js:42-44), so a mismatch makes the write succeed as the wrong wallet rather than be rejected — a related but distinct defect, where `liked` (line 735) is computed against the connected wallet and so still renders unfilled after a successful like. Severity medium -> low: no false factual claim, no money path, cosmetic social control only.

Core defect CONFIRMED, but two parts of the write-up are wrong and the severity is one notch too high.

(a) The claimed mechanism is right. CommunityChat.jsx:586-592 — `const updated = await runAuthed(() => toggleLike(...)); if (updated) { setMessages(...) }` with no `else`. supabase.js:266-275 — `try { proxyRpc("toggle_like", ...) } catch (err) { if (err.needsAuth) throw err; if (DEV) console.error(...); return null; }`. supabaseProxy.js:22-32 flags ONLY HTTP 401 as `needsAuth`; a PostgREST 5xx is mapped to 502 (api/supabase-proxy.js:380-382), an RLS reject to 403 (384-386), and a dead network rejects the fetch outright — all three become a plain throw, get swallowed into `null`, and reach `handleLike` as a no-op. Heart glyph (line 776) and count (line 778-780) both stay put, no toast, no console outside DEV. It is the only write path in this component with no failure branch: send toasts at :558, reactions toast at :471, sign-in failure toasts at :369.

(b) The 401 case is NOT silent, and the write-up implies the whole surface is. Signed-out or expired cookie -> 401 -> `needsAuth` -> runAuthed (:360-379) toasts "Sign in to chat — check your wallet to sign.", prompts SIWE, and retries once. That is the everyday failure mode and it is handled. The silent set is strictly: network down, 5xx/502, 403, or a 200 with no row.

(c) The second half of the scenario — "their SIWE cookie's wallet no longer matches the connected wallet, so the RPC is rejected" — is REFUTED. The proxy overwrites whatever wallet the client sent with the JWT-verified one: `const rpcArgs = { ...(req.body?.args || {}), wallet: verifiedWallet }` (api/supabase-proxy.js:347), and migration 006 rewrote `toggle_like` to ignore the arg and trust the JWT entirely ("the old signature is kept as a compatibility wrapper that ignores the parameter"). So a cookie/connected-wallet mismatch never produces a rejection. It produces a SUCCESS under the cookie's wallet: `updated` is truthy, setMessages runs, the count increments by one — but `liked` at line 735 is computed against the *connected* `wallet`, so the heart still does not fill. Same visible symptom, opposite cause, and the count does move. The finding conflates two distinct bugs; only the first is the silent one.

Accurate version: "A failed like (network error, 502 from a Supabase 5xx, or a 403 RLS reject) produces no feedback at all — CommunityChat.jsx:588 has no else branch, and supabase.js:270-274 swallows every non-401 error into null. The 401/signed-out case is handled with a toast and a SIWE retry; the server-error cases are not."

Severity low, not medium: nothing false is rendered. The UI is pessimistic by design — state moves only when the server returns the canonical row — so a failed like shows an unliked message, which is the truthful state. No money, no data loss, no factual sentence asserted from a failed read. The harm is a missing error affordance on a cosmetic social action, and the user can retry freely.
verdicts.reasoning:
MAINTAINER'S CASE (the strongest version): This is deliberate and it is the *correct* side of the very defect class this sweep exists to close. handleLike refuses to move state on anything but a server-returned canonical row. The alternative — an optimistic heart-fill — is exactly failed-write laundering: a filled heart and an incremented count for a like that never persisted, which the realtime UPDATE subscription (:434-437) would then silently contradict or, worse, never correct. The pessimistic branch means the rendered state is always a true statement about the database. Further, the dominant real-world failure (no SIWE cookie) is fully handled at :360-379 with a toast, a sign-in prompt, and a single retry — the F711/F713/F714 comment block shows this path was built on purpose after chat writes were found failing silently. And the asymmetry with handleReaction is principled, not an oversight: that toast reads "Reactions aren't enabled yet" because toggle_reaction may genuinely not exist (migration 007 unapplied) — a permanent, actionable condition. toggle_like has shipped since migration 001, so a null there is infrastructure noise, and toasting every transient blip in a live chat room is spam.

DOES IT HOLD? The first half does; the second half does not. "The display is honest" survives scrutiny — nothing false is shown, and that is why this is not a laundering finding and why medium is too high. But "therefore silence is correct" collapses on inspection. The user cannot distinguish "nothing happened because I misclicked" from "nothing happened because the server refused" — silence is honest to the database and opaque to the human. The "transient blip" justification is post-hoc: a 403 RLS rejection and a 502 from a PostgREST 5xx are not blips, and both land in the identical silent null because supabaseProxy.js:22 special-cases 401 alone. And the component's own conventions refute the maintainer: every sibling write (send :558, reaction :471, sign-in :369) tells the user when it fails. Likes are the lone exception, which reads as an omission rather than a decision. So: real defect, correctly located, mis-scenarioed in its second half (the wallet-mismatch case is refuted outright by the proxy's wallet injection at api/supabase-proxy.js:347 plus migration 006), and correctly fixed by adding an else branch with a toast — not by adding an optimistic update.

survived.title: A transient reaction failure is reported to the user as "Reactions aren't enabled yet"
survived.claim: `handleReaction` (lines 464-473): when `toggleReaction` returns null and CHAT_ENABLED, it toasts "Reactions aren't enabled yet". But `toggleReaction` (supabase.js:307-315) returns null for EVERY non-401 failure — offline, 429, 500, RLS reject, malformed response — not only for "migration 007/010/011 not applied". The comment at supabase.js:283-284 anticipates only the migration case; the catch is far broader.
survived.failure_scenario: Reactions are fully deployed and working. The user is on flaky mobile data and taps 🔥. The proxy POST fails at the network layer, proxyRpc throws, toggleReaction returns null, and the app tells them a shipped feature "isn't enabled yet" — a definitive product statement produced by a one-off network blip. They stop trying to react.
survived.suggested_fix: Distinguish err.status (4xx with a missing-function body → not enabled) from network/5xx (→ "Couldn't save your reaction, try again"), the same way DirectMessages.jsx:172-178 `classify()` already does.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified against the files. CommunityChat.jsx:467-472 toasts "Reactions aren't enabled yet" on any falsy return from runAuthed(toggleReaction(...)). supabase.js:307-315 returns null for every failure except 401 (which rethrows via err.needsAuth). supabaseProxy.js:15-34 confirms only res.status===401 sets needsAuth; every other non-OK status throws a plain Error with err.status, and a network-layer fetch rejection never reaches a status at all. Both classes land in the catch at supabase.js:311 and become null. firstRow (supabaseProxy.js:47-48) additionally returns null for a 200 with an empty array, so a successful-but-empty RPC produces the same toast. The migration-007 case documented in the comment at supabase.js:283-284 is only one subcase of a much broader catch, exactly as the finding states. The one null path the finding names that is NOT user-reachable is the REACTION_EMOJIS allowlist check at supabase.js:287 — the picker only renders REACTION_EMOJIS (CommunityChat.jsx:815-818), so no out-of-allowlist emoji can be tapped. The sibling handleLike (CommunityChat.jsx:586-592) has the correct shape: updates on success, silent on null, makes no product claim.
verdicts.correction: The finding is accurate but understates the defect: it misses two additional null paths in runAuthed (CommunityChat.jsx:360-379) that produce a self-contradicting double toast. When the user rejects the SIWE signature, runAuthed toasts "Sign-in is required to post in chat." and returns null at line 370; when the post-sign-in retry still throws needsAuth it returns null at line 375. Both fall through to the else-if at line 470, so a user who declines a signature sees "Sign-in is required to post in chat." immediately followed by "Reactions aren't enabled yet" — two mutually inconsistent explanations for one tap. That is the most concrete user-visible symptom and is more reliably reproducible than the flaky-network scenario in the original writeup. Severity should be low rather than medium: the failure is confined to a single dismissible toast on a cosmetic action, with no funds, no persisted state, and no false factual claim about a token, wallet, or user. The optimistic state is never written, so nothing desyncs — the reaction simply does not apply. The correct fix shape is the one handleLike already uses (silent on null), or distinguishing err.status to toast an accurate transient-failure message.

verdicts.reasoning:
Verified end to end against the source. CommunityChat.jsx:464-473: handleReaction awaits runAuthed(() => toggleReaction(...)) and, when the result is falsy and CHAT_ENABLED, toasts "Reactions aren't enabled yet". supabase.js:307-315: toggleReaction rethrows only err.needsAuth and returns null for every other throw. supabaseProxy.js:15-34 (proxyCall) sets needsAuth on status 401 ONLY; every other non-ok status throws a plain Error with err.status, and a network-layer fetch rejection throws too. So 429, 500, 503, RLS rejects and offline all collapse to null and render as a definitive "feature not shipped" statement.

The maintainer's defense (the toast exists so a pre-migration 007/010/011 state is not a silent no-op, consistent with the F711/F713/F714 anti-silent-failure work, and the else-if CHAT_ENABLED guard keeps it out of local mode) justifies having a message but not this message: the code has no way to distinguish the migration case from a transient one, and the CHAT_ENABLED guard actually restricts the toast to deployments where Supabase IS configured, i.e. exactly where "not enabled" is least likely to be true.

Two corrections to the finding. (1) The realistic trigger is not a flaky-mobile blip but the proxy's own rate limit: api/supabase-proxy.js:246-249 is a 20-write/60s bucket keyed on the verified wallet and api/_lib/ratelimit.js:219 returns 429; each reaction toggle is one write and DM polling shares the same wallet bucket. The project already booked this exact interaction for the sibling copy as F717 ("DMs aren't enabled yet", rated high) in plan/g13_naka_analytics_social.md:76 and DirectMessages.jsx:405. api/_lib/ratelimit.js:328 adds a 503 load-shed path with the same outcome. (2) The finding missed a contradictory double-toast that needs no infrastructure failure: if the user declines the SIWE signature, runAuthed (CommunityChat.jsx:366-371) toasts "Sign-in is required to post in chat." and returns null, then line 470 immediately toasts "Reactions aren't enabled yet" — two mutually exclusive explanations for one tap.

Severity medium is correct: no money path and no false factual claim about a token or wallet, but it is the same failed-read-laundering class this sweep targets and it tells users a live feature does not exist. Note handleLike (CommunityChat.jsx:586-592) has the same null-flattening but fails silently, so reactions is the only surface emitting the wrong sentence.
verdicts.correction: Accurate version: handleReaction (frontend/src/nakamigos/components/CommunityChat.jsx:464-473) reports EVERY non-401 reaction failure as "Reactions aren't enabled yet", because proxyCall (lib/supabaseProxy.js:22-31) tags only HTTP 401 with needsAuth and toggleReaction (lib/supabase.js:311-315) returns null for all other throws. The dominant real-world trigger is the proxy's own 20-writes-per-60s-per-wallet limiter (api/supabase-proxy.js:246-249 returning 429 via api/_lib/ratelimit.js:219), a bucket shared with DM polling — the same interaction already filed as F717 for the DM copy — plus 503 load-shed (ratelimit.js:328), 500s, RLS rejects and offline. Additionally, declining the SIWE signature makes runAuthed toast "Sign-in is required to post in chat." and return null (CommunityChat.jsx:366-371), after which line 470 fires a second, contradictory "Reactions aren't enabled yet" for the same tap. Fix: branch on err.status (429 -> slow-down copy, missing-RPC -> "not enabled yet", other -> "Couldn't save that reaction, try again") and suppress the toast when runAuthed already surfaced a message. Severity: medium.

survived.title: Analytics tab has no nav entry on desktop, and none at all for the default Lite user
survived.claim: 'analytics' is in VALID_TABS (constants.js:90-95), has a renderTab case (App.jsx:754) and a prefetch entry (App.jsx:84), but appears in neither PRIMARY_NAV (Header.jsx:129-137) nor MORE_NAV (Header.jsx:139-154). Header is the only nav rendered above 768px — App.css:1374/1388 hides .desktop-nav and shows .mobile-nav only at max-width 768, and .mobile-bottom-nav is display:none inline, flipped to flex only inside the same max-width:768 block (App.css:3774-3777). MobileNav.MORE_TABS is the sole nav that lists it. Separately, LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY (TradingModeContext.jsx:15) contains 'analytics' and the default mode is 'lite' (line 32), so MobileNav filters it out too and App.jsx:423-434 bounces any deep link.
survived.failure_scenario: A desktop visitor cannot reach Analytics by any click — it is in no menu. The documented '1–6 Switch tabs' shortcut (lib/shortcuts.js:17, rendered on the About page and the ? overlay) maps 4 to analytics (App.jsx:157); a default Lite user who presses 4 is redirected straight back to Gallery with the toast 'Analytics is a Pro feature'. For the default user on every viewport, an entire shipped tab — depth chart, rarity-vs-price scatter, collection health, holder distribution, CSV export — is unreachable. navRouting.test.jsx:13-23 cannot catch this because it only asserts nav ⊆ VALID_TABS, never the reverse.
survived.suggested_fix: Add ['analytics','Analytics'] to Header.MORE_NAV, and add the inverse assertion to navRouting.test.jsx: every VALID_TABS entry must appear in at least one nav list.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every claim reproduces from the files; I could not refute any of it.

VERIFIED:
- constants.js:90-95 VALID_TABS includes "analytics". App.jsx:84 prefetch, App.jsx:157 TAB_KEYS "4": "analytics", App.jsx:754 `case "analytics":` renders <Analytics/>. The tab is fully built (Analytics.jsx: depth chart, price distribution, sales stats, rarity-vs-price scatter, CollectionHealth, HolderAnalytics, CSV export at line 244).
- Header.jsx:129-137 PRIMARY_NAV = listings/gallery/deals/traits/activity/collection/portfolio — no analytics. Header.jsx:139-154 MORE_NAV = 14 entries — no analytics.
- Header.jsx:336-344 defines visiblePrimary/visibleMore/visibleAll purely from PRIMARY_NAV/MORE_NAV; they are the only sources for the desktop nav (line 499), the More dropdown (line 548), and the hamburger drawer (line 747). So no Header surface can ever offer analytics.
- Desktop-only claim holds: App.css:1374+1388 hides .desktop-nav at max-width 768; App.css:1390 shows .mobile-nav there; App.css:1454-1457 @media (min-width:768px) sets .mobile-nav display:none !important; MobileNav.jsx:127 hardcodes inline display:"none", flipped to flex only by App.css:3774-3777 @media (max-width:768px). The one other .mobile-bottom-nav rule (App.css:4342) is inside @media print. MobileNav is mounted unconditionally at App.jsx:1002 but is CSS-dead above 768px.
- MobileNav.jsx:17 { key: "analytics", label: "Analytics" } is the ONLY nav entry for the tab anywhere.
- TradingModeContext.jsx:15 LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY contains "analytics"; :22 LITE_HIDDEN_ALL unions PRIMARY+MORE; :32 getInitialMode returns "lite" by default. MobileNav.jsx:41 filters MORE_TABS by LITE_HIDDEN_ALL, so Lite users lose it on mobile too.
- App.jsx:420-433 lite redirect: if (isLite && LITE_HIDDEN_ALL.has(tab)) -> addToast(`${label} is a Pro feature — switch to Pro in the header to view it`) then navigate to the collection root. App.jsx:531-534 fires handleTabChange(TAB_KEYS[e.key]) for "4", which is then bounced by that effect.
- lib/shortcuts.js:17 documents ["1–6", "Switch tabs"], rendered by the ? overlay and the About panel.
- navRouting.test.jsx:13-23 only asserts nav ⊆ VALID_TABS; 25-37 asserts each VALID_TABS entry has a renderTab case. Neither direction catches "routable but in no menu".
- Exhaustive search of frontend/src/nakamigos for the literal "analytics" finds no setTab/handleTabChange/link/command-palette entry point outside those four sites; all other hits are CSS class names and an EmptyState config key (EmptyState.jsx:116).

EXTRA CORROBORATION the finding did not cite (strengthens that this is drift, not a deliberate gate): LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY's filter over PRIMARY_NAV is a no-op for "analytics" — the other two members, "deals" and "portfolio", ARE in PRIMARY_NAV. And App.jsx:152's comment claims TAB_KEYS "matches PRIMARY_NAV in Header", which it does not (TAB_KEYS = gallery/listings/traits/analytics/activity/collection vs a 7-item PRIMARY_NAV in a different order). Both artifacts imply analytics was once in the desktop primary nav and was dropped without updating the shortcut map, the Lite set, or the docs.

ACCURACY NIT: "A desktop visitor cannot reach Analytics by any click" is correct, but a desktop user who has switched to Pro can still reach it via the documented "4" shortcut or a typed /nakamigos/<slug>/analytics URL. Complete unreachability (no click, no key, no deep link) applies to the DEFAULT Lite user on every viewport.

Severity medium is right: no money path and no false factual claim about chain data, but a fully-built shipped tab has zero click affordance on desktop in either mode, is entirely unreachable for the default user, and a keyboard shortcut the app advertises to that default user silently bounces them with a Pro-upsell toast — a dead/misleading control, not a cosmetic issue.
verdicts.correction:
CONFIRMED as written, with one scope correction to the scenario. Accurate statement:

(a) DESKTOP (>768px), BOTH modes: there is no click path to Analytics. Header.jsx:499/548 render only PRIMARY_NAV (Header.jsx:129-137) and MORE_NAV (Header.jsx:139-154), neither of which contains "analytics"; MobileNav — the only nav that lists it (MobileNav.jsx:17) — is CSS-dead above 768px (MobileNav.jsx:127 inline display:none, flipped only by App.css:3774-3777 max-width:768). A desktop user who deliberately switches to Pro still never sees the tab appear.

(b) DESKTOP + PRO: still reachable via the "4" keyboard shortcut (App.jsx:157, 531-534) or a typed URL — so the tab is not literally unreachable there, only unclickable. The original scenario slightly overstates this.

(c) DEFAULT LITE USER (TradingModeContext.jsx:32), ALL viewports: unreachable by every path. MobileNav.jsx:41 filters it out of the mobile More menu via LITE_HIDDEN_ALL, and App.jsx:420-433 redirects both the "4" shortcut and any deep link back to the collection root with the toast "Analytics is a Pro feature — switch to Pro in the header to view it".

Supporting evidence that (a) is accidental drift rather than an intentional gate: LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY (TradingModeContext.jsx:15) lists "analytics" alongside "deals" and "portfolio", but only those latter two actually exist in PRIMARY_NAV, so the filter entry for analytics is a no-op; and App.jsx:152's comment asserts TAB_KEYS "matches PRIMARY_NAV in Header" when the two lists no longer correspond at all.

Test-gap claim is also accurate: navRouting.test.jsx:13-23 checks nav ⊆ VALID_TABS and :25-37 checks each VALID_TABS entry has a renderTab case, but nothing asserts VALID_TABS ⊆ (some nav), which is exactly the direction that would have caught this.

Severity stays medium.

verdicts.reasoning:
MAINTAINER'S CASE (the strongest version I can build):

"This is deliberate Pro-gating, not a bug. `analytics` sits in LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY (contexts/TradingModeContext.jsx:15) on purpose; the default mode is `lite` (line 32) because we want a simple first-run surface. App.jsx:421-434 doesn't silently swallow the deep link — it fires an explicit toast telling the user exactly why and how to fix it. Pro users get the tab in the bottom-nav More sheet (MobileNav.jsx:17), and power users on desktop have the documented `4` hotkey (App.jsx:157). navRouting.test.jsx deliberately asserts nav ⊆ VALID_TABS and not the reverse, because VALID_TABS is a superset by design — it must also cover deep-link-only routes."

WHY THAT ARGUMENT DOES NOT HOLD — checked file by file:

1. The Pro-gating defense explains hiding it from Lite. It does not explain the absence from the nav in Pro mode. Header.jsx:499 renders `visiblePrimary` (PRIMARY_NAV filtered by LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY) and :548 renders `visibleMore` (MORE_NAV filtered by LITE_HIDDEN_MORE). `analytics` is in neither source array (Header.jsx:129-137, 139-154), so the filter never even gets a chance to run on it. A Pro-mode desktop user has exactly the same zero click paths as a Lite one.

2. The strongest evidence it is an accidental drop, not a design choice: LITE_HIDDEN_PRIMARY has three members — `deals`, `portfolio`, `analytics`. The other two ARE in PRIMARY_NAV (Header.jsx:132 "Deals", :136 "P&L"). The set is literally named "tabs hidden FROM PRIMARY NAV in Lite mode" (TradingModeContext.jsx:14). `analytics` is the only member that is not in the primary nav to be hidden from. The gating config still believes the nav entry exists.

3. Corroborating drift: App.jsx:152 comments TAB_KEYS as "matches PRIMARY_NAV in Header". It does not — PRIMARY_NAV is listings/gallery/deals/traits/activity/collection/portfolio (7 items), TAB_KEYS is gallery/listings/traits/analytics/activity/collection.
