survived.title: Watchlist's target-price control and 'below target' alert can never fire
survived.claim: `belowTarget = data.targetPrice && nft.price && nft.price <= data.targetPrice` reads `nft.price` off tokens that always have price:null — App.jsx:763 passes `nfts.allTokens`, and api.js:147 hardcodes `price: null` in normalizeToken with no listing merge anywhere on this path (unlike Gallery, which receives `listings` separately). Nothing else in the codebase reads the watchlist's targetPrice either: grep for the watchlist store finds only this component and the userdata sync.
survived.failure_scenario: A user opens Watchlist, reads the subtitle 'Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts' (line 127) — reinforced by the empty state 'Add {collection} NFTs to track price changes and get alerts' (EmptyState.jsx:38) — types 0.09 into TARGET PRICE (line 192-200), and waits. The value persists to localStorage and Supabase but is never compared against anything: the price line at line 188 never renders, and the '⚠ Below target price!' badge at line 212-216 is unreachable code. The floor drops to 0.08 and the user is never told. They believe they have an alert set and they do not.
survived.suggested_fix: Either wire the watchlist rows to the listings feed (pass `listings` into Watchlist and merge as Gallery does) so the comparison is real, or remove the target input and route the copy to the Alerts tab, which does have a working floor engine.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end from the files. App.jsx:763 passes `nfts.allTokens` to Watchlist with no `listings` prop (contrast App.jsx:743/753/755, which do pass listings). useNfts.js:190 returns `allTokens: rankedTokens`; rankedTokens = computeRarity(tokens) (useNfts.js:148-151), and computeRarity (api.js:848-888) spreads `...token` while adding only `rank`/`rarityScore` — it never sets `price`. The tokens originate in normalizeToken, which hardcodes `price: null` at api.js:147; the offline path is identical, since every FALLBACK_NFTS entry at constants.js:212-223 is also `price: null`. The hook exposes no setter that could later decorate tokens with a price. Independent in-repo corroboration: Gallery.jsx:35 carries the comment that normalizeToken hard-sets price:null, which is why Gallery builds its own listingById map at Gallery.jsx:44-49 — Watchlist has no equivalent. Therefore at Watchlist.jsx:175 `data.targetPrice && nft.price && nft.price <= data.targetPrice` can never be true: the price line at :188 never renders and the "Below target price!" badge at :212-216 is unreachable, as is the `alert` class on the card at :177. A grep for targetPrice across frontend/src/nakamigos returns only Watchlist.jsx (59/93/100/102/107/175/198), lib/userdata.js (257/274/287/293 — pure persistence and Supabase sync, no comparison), and components/PriceAlerts.jsx (89-147/490/652), which is a wholly separate alert store on the `alerts` tab keyed to collection FLOOR price (see the notification body at PriceAlerts.jsx:147). Nothing evaluates the watchlist's targetPrice. Copy verified: Watchlist.jsx:127 "Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts" and EmptyState.jsx:38 "Add {collection} NFTs to track price changes and get alerts."
verdicts.correction: The finding is correct as to mechanism and unreachability; two details need tightening. (1) Persistence is not unconditionally dual: updateTarget (Watchlist.jsx:100-112) always writes localStorage, but only calls addWatchlistRemote when `wallet` is truthy (:104), so a disconnected user's target lives in localStorage alone. (2) The claimed "alert" was never a notification even in the intended design — it is an inline CSS class (:177) plus a static badge (:212-216) that is visible only while the Watchlist tab is mounted and rendered. There is no toast, no push, no background evaluation, unlike the real engine wired at App.jsx:686 (usePriceAlerts) and surfaced on the separate `alerts` tab. So the copy at Watchlist.jsx:127 and EmptyState.jsx:38 is overstated on two axes: the comparison can never fire because nft.price is always null, AND even a working comparison would never "alert" a user who is not already looking at that tab. Accurate title: "Watchlist target-price input is a dead control — the below-target comparison reads nft.price, which is hardcoded null on this data path, and the badge would not alert anyone even if it fired." Severity medium is right: no funds at risk and no false factual claim about a token's state, but it is a dead money-adjacent control whose surrounding copy promises monitoring the code cannot perform, and a user can plausibly rely on it and miss a floor move.

CONFIRMED, with two corrections.

1) CITATION FIX: the `price: null` hard-set is at `frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:146` (inside `normalizeToken`, which begins at line 116). There is no `frontend/src/nakamigos/lib/api.js`.

2) CATEGORY FIX (severity unchanged at medium): this is NOT finding-class 1 (failed-read laundering). The expression `data.targetPrice && nft.price && nft.price <= data.targetPrice` is a correctly-ordered guard that REFUSES to render a verdict when price is absent; no false factual sentence reaches the user, and a missing badge asserts nothing. The real class is 3 — a dead control plus UI copy describing behaviour the code does not have. Same severity, different remedy: either pass `listings` into this path and merge, or delete the TARGET PRICE input and correct both copy strings.

VERIFICATION PERFORMED (every branch that could supply a price):
- api.js:146 — normalizeToken hard-sets `price: null` (live path via fetchTokens, api.js:164).
- constants.js:211-224 — FALLBACK_NFTS, all 12 entries `price: null` (fallback path via api.js:170).
- api.js:848-897 — computeRarity spreads `...token` and adds only `rank`/`rarityScore` in both the precomputed and runtime branches; never touches price.
- useNfts.js:190 — `allTokens: rankedTokens`, no listing merge anywhere in the hook.
- App.jsx:763 — `<Watchlist tokens={nfts.allTokens} onPick={...} addToast={...} setTab={...} wallet={wallet} />`; no `listings` prop, and Watchlist.jsx:17's signature has no parameter to receive one.
Therefore `nft.price` is structurally and permanently null on this path, `belowTarget` (line 175) is always falsy, the price line at 188 never renders, and the badge at 212-216 is unreachable.

THE MAINTAINER DEFENCE AND WHY IT FAILS:
- "It's a personal memo field, and persistence is the feature." Dies on the component's own copy: Watchlist.jsx:127 renders "Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts", and EmptyState.jsx:38 renders "Add {collection} NFTs to track price changes and get alerts." The control is labelled "TARGET PRICE (ETH)" (line 192), typed `number step="0.001"` (194-195), and sits beside a "Below target price!" badge. The memo field is the separate one labelled NOTE.
- "Alerts live in the dedicated Alerts tab." This makes it worse. A full grep of frontend/src for `targetPrice` shows the watchlist value is read in exactly two places: Watchlist.jsx and userdata.js persistence (lines 257, 274, 287, 293). PriceAlerts.jsx keeps a wholly separate store (direction above/below at 129-130, notification body at 147) and never reads the watchlist.
- "The guard is defensive future-proofing." True about the guard's shape, irrelevant to impact: it is not defending against a transient read failure but against an architectural fact the team already documented. Gallery.jsx:35 carries the comment "normalizeToken hard-sets price:null, so the listings feed is the only source of a gallery card's price AND its buy route" — Gallery, Listings, Traits, Analytics, Sniper and Bids all receive `listings`; Watchlist is the one price-facing tab that never got the merge.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME FILE (not in the original finding, arguably worse and closer to the laundering class): Watchlist.jsx:114 computes `watchedNfts = tokens.filter((t) => watchedIds.has(t.id))`, but useNfts.js:33 pages at 40 tokens and `loadAll` (useNfts.js:119) is opt-in — App.jsx:763 does not pass it to Watchlist, though Gallery, Listings, Traits and Sniper all get it. A user who watchlists a high token id (e.g. #19000) via the search box, navigates away and returns sees a completely empty grid with no explanation: the card is filtered out because that page was never fetched, and the EmptyState at line 167 is suppressed because `watchlist.length !== 0`. The saved item is intact in localStorage and Supabase, yet absence-of-data renders as "you have nothing saved."
verdicts.reasoning: Read Watchlist.jsx in full and traced every possible source of `nft.price` on this path. normalizeToken (api.js:146) hard-sets price:null; FALLBACK_NFTS (constants.js:211-224) are all price:null; computeRarity (api.js:848-897) only adds rank/rarityScore in both branches; useNfts.js:190 returns rankedTokens with no listing merge; App.jsx:763 passes no `listings` prop and Watchlist.jsx:17's signature cannot receive one. So belowTarget at line 175 is permanently falsy — the price display (188) never renders and the alert badge (212-216) is unreachable. A grep of all of frontend/src for `targetPrice` confirms the watchlist's value is consumed only by Watchlist.jsx itself and userdata.js persistence; PriceAlerts.jsx is an independent store that never reads it. The copy at Watchlist.jsx:127 and EmptyState.jsx:38 both affirmatively promise alerts, and Gallery.jsx:35 contains an explicit maintainer comment establishing that a listings merge is mandatory to get a price — a rule every other price-facing tab follows and this one does not. The strongest maintainer defence (it is a memo field / alerts live elsewhere / the guard is defensive) fails against that copy and that grep. I corrected the file path (api.js:146, not lib/api.js:147) and reclassified from failed-read laundering to dead-control-plus-false-copy, since no false factual sentence is actually rendered — severity medium stands because the user acts on a false belief that monitoring exists and is never given an error surface. Also found an unreported adjacent defect: pagination means watched tokens outside the first 40 loaded silently vanish from the grid while EmptyState is suppressed.

survived.title: Watchlist silently drops persisted entries whose token is outside the loaded page window
survived.claim: `watchedNfts = tokens.filter(t => watchedIds.has(t.id))` shows only watched items present in the currently loaded token pages, and the empty state at line 167 is gated on `watchlist.length === 0` — not on `watchedNfts.length === 0`. When the watchlist is non-empty but nothing matches, the component renders a header, an Add button, and an empty grid with no message. useNfts loads 40 tokens per page and skips auto-loading entirely for collections with supply >= 1000 (useNfts.js:101), so Nakamigos starts each session with 40 of 20,000 tokens loaded.
survived.failure_scenario: A user scrolls the gallery deep in one session, adds #14320 to their watchlist, and closes the tab. Next visit they open Watchlist: the item is still in localStorage and still in Supabase, but only 40 tokens are loaded so it matches nothing. They see the WATCHLIST header over blank space — no items, no empty state, no 'not yet loaded' note. It reads as if their watchlist was wiped. Favorites handles the identical situation honestly (Favorites.jsx:74-78 prints 'N favorited NFTs not yet loaded'); Watchlist does not.
survived.suggested_fix: Mirror the Favorites disclosure: render a count of watched-but-unloaded entries, and change the empty-state condition to fire when the resolved grid is empty.

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced from source, all cited lines are accurate.

Watchlist.jsx:114 — `const watchedNfts = useMemo(() => tokens.filter((t) => watchedIds.has(t.id)), [tokens, watchedIds])` intersects the persisted watchlist with the currently loaded token window.

Watchlist.jsx:167 — `{watchlist.length === 0 && !showSearch && (<EmptyState type="watchlist" .../>)}` gates the empty state on the persisted array, NOT on watchedNfts. So when watchlist.length > 0 and watchedNfts.length === 0, the component renders the WATCHLIST header, the subtitle, the "+ Add to Watchlist" button, and then a bare `<div className="watchlist-grid">` (line 172) containing nothing. App.css:2303-2306 defines .watchlist-grid as a plain grid with no ::after / :empty fallback, so it is literally blank space. No "not yet loaded" note anywhere in the file.

Favorites.jsx:74-78 confirms the intended honest pattern exists in the sibling component: `{favoriteNfts.length < safeFavorites.length && (... "{N} favorited NFTs not yet loaded. Scroll the gallery to load more.")}`.

Reachability confirmed:
- useNfts.js:29-35 fetches limit: 40 per page.
- useNfts.js:101 `const shouldAutoLoad = collection.supply && collection.supply < 1000; if (!shouldAutoLoad) return;` — auto-pagination is skipped.
- constants.js:34/55/71 — supplies are 20000 (nakamigos), 9696 (gnssart), 5555 (junglebay). ALL THREE exceed 1000, so auto-load never fires for any configured collection, not just Nakamigos. Each session starts with 40 tokens.
- App.jsx:763 `<Watchlist tokens={nfts.allTokens} ... />` — allTokens is rankedTokens, i.e. all LOADED tokens (unaffected by trait filters, so filters are not a confound), and Watchlist is passed no `loadAll` prop, unlike Gallery/Analytics/TraitExplorer/RaritySniper (App.jsx:706, 736, 749, 753). The user has no in-tab way to load the missing tokens.

No type-coercion confound: api.js:131 sets `id: nft.tokenId` (string) and userdata.js keys via String(item.id), so the Set miss is genuine set membership, not a string/number mismatch.

CORRECTION / STRENGTHENING (the finding understates reachability): the scenario as written requires deep scrolling in a prior session. userdata.js:234-260 `syncWatchlist` merges remote-only Supabase token_ids into the returned list (`const mergedIds = new Set([...localMap.keys(), ...remoteMap.keys()])`), and Watchlist.jsx:31-40 calls it on wallet connect. So a user who watched tokens on one device and then connects the same wallet on a second device hits the blank state on a FRESH page load with zero scrolling and an empty localStorage. That is a far more common trigger than the one described.

Severity medium is right: no money path, no false factual claim about a token's market state, and the persisted data is not actually destroyed (localStorage and Supabase rows survive). But the user-visible result is a total apparent data loss with no explanation, and the correct pattern already ships in Favorites.jsx.
verdicts.correction: The finding is accurate as written; two refinements. (1) The gating condition is not Nakamigos-specific — constants.js:34/55/71 show all three configured collections (20000/9696/5555) are above the 1000 threshold at useNfts.js:101, so auto-load never fires for ANY collection and every session starts at 40 loaded tokens. (2) The most reachable trigger is cross-device Supabase sync, not deep scrolling: syncWatchlist (userdata.js:245-260) merges remote-only token_ids into the rendered list, so a user connecting the same wallet on a second device sees the blank WATCHLIST header immediately on first load with empty localStorage and zero interaction. Additionally, App.jsx:763 passes no `loadAll` prop to Watchlist (unlike App.jsx:706/736/749/753), so there is no way to recover from inside the tab.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at file:line, and the maintainer defense does not hold.

Defense considered: filtering to `watchedNfts` (Watchlist.jsx:114) avoids rendering a card with no name/image/price/rank, and gating EmptyState on `watchlist.length === 0` (line 167) avoids the literally-false "Watchlist is empty / Add NFTs to track price changes" (EmptyState.jsx:35-41) for a user who has 6 persisted entries. Both sub-choices are individually defensible. The defense fails because it presents a false dilemma: the third option — tell the user the entries exist but aren't loaded — is already implemented in the same codebase for the byte-identical situation at Favorites.jsx:74-78 ("{n} favorited NFTs not yet loaded. Scroll the gallery to load more."). Watchlist has no equivalent anywhere in the file.

Mechanics verified exactly as claimed:
- useNfts.js:101 `const shouldAutoLoad = collection.supply && collection.supply < 1000;` -> skipped for Nakamigos, whose `supply: 20000` (constants.js:34). Page limit 40 (useNfts.js:34). Session starts at 40/20,000.
- App.jsx:763 passes `nfts.allTokens` (trait-unfiltered), so trait filters are not a confound; pagination fully is.
- Watchlist is the only consumer receiving neither `loadAll` nor `hasMore` (those go to Deals.jsx:455, Gallery.jsx:17, Listings.jsx:238, TraitExplorer.jsx:367). It cannot widen the window and cannot detect that the window is narrow.
- Watchlist.jsx:167 gates EmptyState on `watchlist.length === 0 && !showSearch`; line 172 renders `.watchlist-grid` mapping `watchedNfts`. Non-empty watchlist + zero matches => header + Add button + empty grid, no message.

TWO UNDERSTATEMENTS in the original finding (the accurate version is worse):
1. The recovery path confirms the wrong conclusion. `searchResults` (Watchlist.jsx:45-54) searches the same 40 loaded `tokens`, so typing "14320" into "+ Add to Watchlist" yields "No results found" (line 147) for a token the user is currently watching — reads as if the NFT does not exist.
2. Sharper than the blank grid: `belowTarget` is computed at line 175 INSIDE the `watchedNfts.map`. A target price persisted on an out-of-window token is never evaluated, so the "Below target price!" badge (line 212-216) can never fire for it, in any session, while the subtitle at line 127 keeps promising "Track {collection} NFTs and set price alerts". PriceAlerts.jsx is a separate floor-price system and does not cover watchlist targets — grep for `targetPrice` shows Watchlist.jsx:175 is the only comparison site. The tab's advertised core function is silently inert for exactly the entries it fails to display.

ONE MINOR CORRECTION to the scenario: "still in Supabase" holds only if a wallet was connected at add time (Watchlist.jsx:62-66 gates the remote write on `wallet`); anonymously it is localStorage-only. This does not weaken the finding — localStorage alone produces the blank render.

Severity stays MEDIUM: no money path and no fabricated figure, but a persisted user artifact reads as wiped, the re-add path denies the token exists, and an advertised alert feature is permanently dead for the affected entries.
verdicts.correction: Accurate as stated, with two additions and one small correction. ADDITIONS: (a) the re-add path also fails misleadingly — searchResults (Watchlist.jsx:45-54) searches the same 40-token window, so searching the watched token ID returns "No results found" (line 147), implying the NFT does not exist; (b) more serious than the blank grid — `belowTarget` is computed at line 175 inside the `watchedNfts.map`, so a persisted target price on an out-of-window token is never evaluated and the "Below target price!" alert (lines 212-216) can never fire, while the subtitle at line 127 advertises "set price alerts". PriceAlerts.jsx is an unrelated floor-price system; Watchlist.jsx:175 is the only site that compares a watchlist targetPrice. CORRECTION: the entry survives in Supabase only if a wallet was connected at add time (Watchlist.jsx:62-66); anonymously it is localStorage-only, which still reproduces the bug. Severity remains medium. Fix shape already exists in-repo: mirror Favorites.jsx:74-78 by rendering a `watchlist.length - watchedNfts.length` "not yet loaded" note, and/or pass `loadAll`/`hasMore` to the Watchlist tab at App.jsx:763 as is already done for Deals/Gallery/Listings/TraitExplorer.

survived.title: About's stat cards present fallback stats as live, with none of the 'cached' disclosure Hero carries
survived.claim: statCards reads stats.floor / stats.volume / stats.owners and renders them at line 194-206 keyed only on `value != null`. The `fallback` flag that useCollection.js:16 deliberately attaches to FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED for exactly this purpose is never consulted. Hero.jsx:105-127 consumes the same object, computes `isFallback` and renders a CachedTag ('Cached estimate — live stats unavailable right now') — the F582 fix landed on Hero and not on About.
survived.failure_scenario: Both stats upstreams fail (or the first fetch throws, in which case useCollection.js:76-79 only console.warns and leaves the initial FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED in place). A visitor opens About and reads 'FLOOR PRICE 0.1048 ETH / TOTAL VOLUME 52.2K ETH / OWNERS 5,238' in confident gold/blue/green, styled identically to live data and directly beneath the collection's origin story. Those three numbers are hardcoded in constants.js:226-231 and are years stale. A user sizing a bid off that floor is acting on a constant.
survived.suggested_fix: Thread `stats.fallback` into statCards and reuse Hero's CachedTag (or render '—') so the two surfaces disclose the same thing about the same object.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on every load-bearing claim.

1. About never consults the flag. `frontend/src/nakamigos/components/About.jsx:71-76` builds statCards from `stats?.floor` / `stats?.volume` / `stats?.owners`, and `194-206` renders `value != null ? \`${value}${suffix}\` : "—"` in full-color `var(--gold)` / `var(--naka-blue)` / `var(--green)`. The string "fallback" appears ZERO times in the entire 359-line file — the flag is genuinely never read.

2. The flag exists and does reach About. `useCollection.js:16` `const FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED = { ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }` with the comment "so the UI can badge it 'cached' instead of presenting stale numbers as live (F582)". It is the initial state at `:22` and the collection-switch reset at `:46`. On the success path `:68-71` does `setStats({ ...statsData, supply: ... })` — a spread, so `fallback: true` survives into the object handed to About via `App.jsx:338` → `App.jsx:773`.

3. The failure path really does produce the constants. `frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:277`: when BOTH Alchemy and OpenSea stats fail, `if (contract.toLowerCase() === CONTRACT.toLowerCase()) return { ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }`. `constants.js:226-231` = floor 0.1048, volume 52200, owners 5238. Rendered: `formatPrice(0.1048)`="0.1048 ETH", `formatVol(52200)`="52.2K ETH", `formatNumber(5238)`="5,238" — exactly the strings the finding predicts.

4. Hero DID get the fix, About did not. `Hero.jsx:106-120` defines CachedTag with title "Cached estimate — live stats unavailable right now"; `:127` `const isFallback = !!stats.fallback`; rendered at `:181` (FLOOR) and `:194` (ALL-TIME VOL). Same `stats` object, same prop, opposite treatment.

5. Hero does not cover for About. `App.jsx:692-697` — `<Hero>` renders only under `case "gallery"`. The About tab is a separate switch case with no Hero, so on that tab there is no CachedTag anywhere on screen.

REFUTATION ATTEMPT THAT FAILED (and makes it worse): I checked whether the global header LIVE/DEMO badge mitigates this. It does not. `Header.jsx:580-585` renders LIVE/DEMO from `isLive`, but `App.jsx:820` passes `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` — an OR. `useNfts.js:40` sets its own `isLive` from the token-list fetch. So a healthy token fetch with a dead stats fetch shows the header badge reading "LIVE" while About displays the 2023-era constants. The one global disclosure is defeated in precisely the scenario described.

MINOR MIS-STATEMENT (does not change the verdict): the parenthetical "the first fetch throws, in which case useCollection.js:76-79 only console.warns" mis-attributes the mechanism. `fetchCollectionStats` swallows its own errors and returns the flagged fallback object rather than throwing (it only rethrows AbortError, api.js:263/274/276). The realistic throw into `useCollection.js:76` comes from `fetchActivity` rejecting the shared `Promise.all` at `:60-63`. The outcome is identical — `setStats` never runs and the initial FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED persists — so the scenario stands.

TWO THINGS THE FINDING UNDERSTATES:
- First paint. For the default collection the flagged constants are the INITIAL state (useCollection.js:22), so any visitor deep-linking straight to the About tab sees "0.1048 ETH / 52.2K ETH / 5,238" in confident color before any fetch resolves. Hero handles this with `isLoading` + StatSkeleton (Hero.jsx:95-102, 183-185); About has no loading state at all — `value != null` is true immediately.
- Scope bound (in the code's favor): non-default collections are honest. `api.js:278` returns all-null stats for them, so About renders "—". The defect is specific to the Nakamigos default collection.

Severity medium is right. It is display-only on an informational/lore tab rather than a trade-building surface, and it needs a two-upstream failure (or a first-paint window) to sustain — but it is a hardcoded, years-stale floor price presented with no disclosure whatsoever, styled identically to live data, on a tab where the app's one global "DEMO" signal can simultaneously read "LIVE".
verdicts.correction: Accurate as written, with three refinements. (a) Mechanism nit: fetchCollectionStats does not throw on upstream failure — it returns `{ ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }` at api.js:277; the throw reaching useCollection.js:76 comes from fetchActivity rejecting the shared Promise.all at useCollection.js:60-63. Same outcome. (b) The finding understates the trigger: because FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED is also the INITIAL state (useCollection.js:22), every Nakamigos visitor deep-linking to the About tab sees the constants on first paint before any fetch resolves — About has no loading/skeleton state, unlike Hero.jsx:95-102/183-185. (c) The finding omits that the app's one global mitigation is defeated: App.jsx:820 passes `isLive={isLive || nfts.isLive}` to Header.jsx:580-585, an OR, so a healthy token fetch (useNfts.js:40) keeps the header badge on "LIVE" while stats are the hardcoded fallback. Scope bound in the code's favor: only the default Nakamigos collection is affected — api.js:278 returns nulls for other collections, so About honestly renders "—".

verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced against the files. About.jsx:71-76 builds statCards from stats.floor/volume/owners and About.jsx:194-206 renders them keyed only on `value != null`; the `fallback` flag is never read anywhere in About.jsx. App.jsx:773 passes About the exact same `stats` object Hero receives at App.jsx:697, and that object carries `fallback: true` (useCollection.js:16,22,46 and api.js:277). Hero.jsx:127 computes `isFallback` and renders CachedTag at 181/194/204; About does not. Tabs are URL-routed (App.jsx:136,145), so /nakamigos/nakamigos/about is directly reachable without Hero ever mounting.

The maintainer defenses are real but insufficient. (a) "Lore page, not a trading surface" fails on presentation: line 186 is commented `{/* Live Stats */}` and the cards use the same label/value/color contract as Hero's live cards, giving the user no way to distinguish. (b) "Only one collection" is true — useCollection.js:22,46 seeds the fallback only for DEFAULT_COLLECTION, others get EMPTY_STATS and render em-dashes — but that is the default, most-trafficked collection. (c) "Not invented, just a snapshot" holds only for supply (20000, exact) and arguably volume (constants.js:228 labels it historical all-time, matching the card label "Total Volume"); floor 0.1048 and owners 5238 are stale and presented as current.

The finding UNDERSTATES the trigger. Three paths, not one: both upstreams fail (api.js:277); load() throws before setStats, where useCollection.js:76-79 only console.warns and leaves the seeded fallback in state indefinitely; and — not in the finding — every healthy first paint, because About has no loading skeleton (Hero has StatSkeleton at Hero.jsx:95-102 used at 170/184/207) so the seeded fallback satisfies `value != null` and paints 0.1048 confidently before the fetch resolves.

Correction to a premise: the finding treats Hero as fully fixed by F582. It is not. api.js:252-253 injects FALLBACK_STATS.volume into an OTHERWISE-SUCCESSFUL stats object when only the volume subcall is throttled, and that return (api.js:256-261) carries no `fallback` flag — so Hero.jsx:127 isFallback is false and "ALL-TIME VOL 52.2K ETH" renders with no CachedTag. Same defect class on the file cited as the good example; F582 covered the total-failure path, not the partial one.

Severity medium is correct: real, user-visible, reproducible on every deep-linked About load, but on a non-transacting surface, scoped to one collection, with only the floor number genuinely misleading.
verdicts.correction: Finding confirmed as written, with two amendments. (1) Broader trigger: besides double-upstream failure and the console.warn-only catch at useCollection.js:76-79, About shows the hardcoded stats on EVERY healthy first paint of a deep-linked /nakamigos/nakamigos/about, because About has no loading skeleton (contrast Hero.jsx:95-102 StatSkeleton used at 170/184/207) and the seeded FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED satisfies the `value != null` gate at About.jsx:202-203 until the fetch resolves. (2) Hero is not the clean reference the finding implies: api.js:252-253 substitutes FALLBACK_STATS.volume into a successful stats return that carries no `fallback` flag (api.js:256-261), so Hero.jsx:194 renders "ALL-TIME VOL 52.2K ETH" without a CachedTag whenever only the OpenSea volume subcall is throttled. Scope limiter worth recording: non-default collections are honest — useCollection.js:22,46 gives them EMPTY_STATS and About.jsx:203 renders an em-dash. The About Supply card (20000) is accurate and not part of this finding.

survived.title: Total Volume silently substitutes a hardcoded 52,200 on the success path with no fallback flag
survived.claim: Inside the SUCCESS branch of _fetchCollectionStatsUncached, when the OpenSea volume call throws or is rate-limited, `volume` is set to `FALLBACK_STATS.volume` (52,200) for the main collection — and the returned object carries no `fallback: true`. Every downstream consumer therefore treats a failed volume read as a live figure, including the surfaces that DO check the flag.
survived.failure_scenario: The landing page fans out stats for three collections at once and the per-collection OpenSea volume call gets throttled — the code comment at line 246-250 says this is the expected common case. About renders 'TOTAL VOLUME 52.2K ETH' and Hero renders it with no cached tag, because `fallback` is absent. The number is a constant from constants.js:228 whose own comment warns it is historical total volume, not current — and its magnitude (52,200) is suspiciously the same figure the About prose gives as the SALES COUNT ('52,000 sales totaling 7,562 ETH', About.jsx:148), so it may also be mislabelled in units.
survived.suggested_fix: Set a per-field marker (e.g. `volumeFallback: true`) when the substitution happens so consumers can badge or suppress just that card, and reconcile the 52,200 constant against a real lifetime-volume figure.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at source. frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:237-261: inside the SUCCESS branch, the OpenSea volume call is wrapped in its own try/catch (239-245) that swallows the error and leaves `volume = null`; lines 252-254 then do `if (volume == null && contract.toLowerCase() === CONTRACT.toLowerCase()) volume = FALLBACK_STATS.volume ?? null;` and the object returned at 256-261 is `{ floor, volume, owners, supply }` — no `fallback` key. Contrast with the two genuine-failure returns at 277-278, which DO set `fallback: true`. So the flag is set on total failure but omitted on the partial (volume-only) failure, which is the case the code comment at 246-250 says is the COMMON one ("the per-collection volume call is the first to get throttled"). Reachability is real: openseaGet (api.js:79-81) retries 3x then throws, and the 429 path is explicitly called out as common.

The constant is confirmed: frontend/src/nakamigos/constants.js:226-231, `volume: 52200, // Historical total volume, not 24h — do not use for volume comparisons or alerts`.

Downstream, confirmed: Hero.jsx:127 `const isFallback = !!stats.fallback` and Hero.jsx:188-193 renders ALL-TIME VOL with `{isFallback && <CachedTag />}` — with the flag absent, the CachedTag ("Cached estimate — live stats unavailable right now", Hero.jsx:105-119) is suppressed and 52.2K reads as a live fetch. About.jsx:73 renders `Total Volume` from `stats.volume` (fed by App.jsx:338/773 from useCollection).

TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding as written:

(1) "including the surfaces that DO check the flag" is true only of Hero. About.jsx:73 and CollectionLanding.jsx:632 never read `stats.fallback` at all — they render the constant undisclosed even in the total-failure case where the flag IS correctly set. So About is not evidence of flag-laundering; it is a second, independent disclosure gap.

(2) The "may be mislabelled in units / suspiciously the same as the 52,000 sales count in About.jsx:148" sub-claim is UNSUPPORTED. Nothing in the repo ties FALLBACK_STATS.volume to the prose figure, and 52,200 ETH lifetime is plausible for a collection that did 7,562 ETH in its first four days. Drop this speculation — it weakens an otherwise solid finding.

ONE CONSEQUENCE THE FINDING UNDERSTATES (strengthens it): the missing flag also propagates past display. useCollection.js:75 does `setIsLive(!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback)`, so the app affirmatively badges the render LIVE while showing a hardcoded number. Worse, useSmartAlerts.js:205-222 pushes `stats.volume` into a rolling-average history and fires a "Volume Spike" alert whose body text says "24h volume up X% vs rolling avg (N ETH)" — precisely the use constants.js:227 forbids in its own comment. Concrete failure: a user has volume alerts on; the OpenSea volume call gets throttled on one poll, so the history array receives 52200 instead of the live all-time figure; the next successful poll's ratio against the contaminated average crosses cfg.volume.spikeMultiplier and the user gets a push-style "Volume Spike — 24h volume up X%" alert describing market activity that never happened.

Severity medium is correct and I'd place it at the top of medium: no transaction is built from it, but it states a false factual number about a collection, actively suppresses the honesty badge the codebase built for exactly this, marks the render as live, and can manufacture a false alert. Minimal accurate restatement: "api.js:252-254 substitutes the hardcoded 52,200 for a failed/throttled volume read on the success path without setting `fallback: true`, so Hero drops its 'cached' tag, useCollection reports isLive=true, and useSmartAlerts ingests the constant into its volume-spike baseline."
verdicts.correction:
Title: Throttled volume read is replaced by the hardcoded 52,200 on the success path with no `fallback` flag, so the "cached" badge, the isLive indicator, and the volume-spike alert all treat it as live.

file: frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:252-261 (constant: constants.js:226-231; consumers: Hero.jsx:127,188-193; useCollection.js:75; useSmartAlerts.js:205-222; About.jsx:73; CollectionLanding.jsx:632)

Confirmed: the inner try/catch at api.js:239-245 swallows an OpenSea 429 leaving volume null; 252-254 substitutes FALLBACK_STATS.volume (52,200) for the main collection; the return at 256-261 omits `fallback: true`, unlike the genuine-failure returns at 277-278 which set it.

Drop from the finding: the claim that 52,200 may be a unit-mislabelled copy of the "52,000 sales" figure in About.jsx:148 — unsupported by anything in the repo.

Narrow from the finding: only Hero.jsx checks `stats.fallback`. About.jsx:73 and CollectionLanding.jsx:632 never check it, so they display the constant undisclosed even when the flag is correctly set — a separate disclosure gap, not flag-laundering.

Add to the finding: useCollection.js:75 sets isLive=true because the flag is absent, and useSmartAlerts.js:205-222 feeds the substituted constant into the rolling average behind a "24h volume up X%" alert — the exact use the constants.js:227 comment forbids — which can fire a spike alert for activity that never occurred.

verdicts.reasoning:
CONFIRMED at frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:252-254. Inside the success branch of _fetchCollectionStatsUncached, if the OpenSea stats call throws (swallowed at 243-245), `volume` is null and is overwritten with FALLBACK_STATS.volume (52200, constants.js:228) for the main collection only. The returned object (256-261) carries no `fallback` key, unlike the two total-failure returns at 277 and 278 which both set `fallback: true`.

Maintainer defense, steelmanned: the flag is object-level and means "the whole object is a constant." Setting it at 253 would badge floor/owners/supply as cached when those came from live Alchemy reads (217-235), and would flip useCollection.js:75 `isLive` false, tripping Header.jsx:581's global "Using demo/fallback data" indicator over one throttled nice-to-have call (api.js:237 marks volume non-critical; it is the only sub-call with its own swallow-catch). Scoping to the main collection is honest — others stay null.

That defense explains WHY no flag was set but does not justify shipping an unbadged constant; the right fix was a per-field marker (volumeFallback), not a choice between lying and saying nothing. Two facts kill it:
(1) git -S dating: the entire honesty apparatus (CachedTag, the fallback flag, FALLBACK_STATS_FLAGGED) landed in 7dfdc52b on 2026-06-13 ("landing/hero/orderbook honesty"). The laundering line landed in a7e1c311 on 2026-06-14 — the next day — with a comment stating a purely cosmetic motive: "so its landing card shows the same number as the detail Hero instead of a bare '—'."
(2) Because `fallback` is absent, isLive stays true, so Header.jsx:581 renders "Connected to live APIs" while Hero.jsx:188-196 prints ALL-TIME VOL 52.2K ETH with no CachedTag (the tag is gated on Hero.jsx:127 isFallback). A live badge over a hardcoded number is worse than either alone.

Repro: OpenSea collections/{slug}/stats returns 429 under the landing fan-out (the case api.js:246-250 calls expected). volume null at 242 -> 52200 at 253 -> spread untouched by useCollection.js:68-71 -> Hero unbadged 52.2K, About.jsx:73/202-204 "TOTAL VOLUME 52.2K ETH", header says live.

Corrections to the finding as written:
- "including the surfaces that DO check the flag" is overstated: only Hero.jsx:127 checks stats.fallback. About.jsx and CollectionLanding.jsx:632 never read it, so they render the constant unbadged on BOTH paths (a wider but separate gap).
- The units/mislabel sub-claim does NOT survive. About.jsx:148's "52,000 sales totaling 7,562 ETH" describes the FIRST FOUR DAYS, not all-time, so 52,200 ETH all-time is arithmetically compatible with it. There is no contradiction, only a numeric coincidence. Cannot verify the true figure offline — flag for operator check, do not report as a proven mislabel.
- Missed secondary consequence: useSmartAlerts.js:205-222 consumes stats.volume, directly against constants.js:228's own warning ("do not use for volume comparisons or alerts"). If true all-time volume is under 1/3 of 52,200, an intermittent throttle pushes the constant into volumeHistoryRef and can fire a false push notification reading "24h volume up N%" (also mislabelling an all-time figure as 24h). Mitigated by useSmartAlerts.js:17 defaulting volume.enabled to false.

Severity medium holds: real, user-visible, headline stat on the main collection, contradicted by a simultaneous live badge, but no money path and no loss.
verdicts.correction: Accurate statement: frontend/src/nakamigos/api.js:252-254 substitutes the hardcoded 52,200 (constants.js:228) for a failed/throttled OpenSea volume read on the SUCCESS path and omits any marker, so Hero (Hero.jsx:188-196), About (About.jsx:73, 202-204) and the landing card (CollectionLanding.jsx:632) present it as live while Header.jsx:581 simultaneously asserts "Connected to live APIs" (isLive at useCollection.js:75 is unaffected). Correct fix is a per-field flag (e.g. volumeFallback: true) consumed by Hero's CachedTag and added to About/Landing — NOT setting the object-level `fallback`, which would falsely badge the live floor/owners/supply and trip the global demo-mode indicator. Drop the units/mislabel sub-claim: About.jsx:148's "52,000 sales totaling 7,562 ETH" is a four-day figure, not all-time, so it does not contradict a 52,200 ETH all-time volume; the coincidence is unverified, flag it for operator confirmation against OpenSea rather than asserting it. Add: useSmartAlerts.js:205-222 consumes this value against constants.js:228's explicit "do not use for volume comparisons or alerts" warning and can emit a false "24h volume up N%" notification (default-off per useSmartAlerts.js:17). Severity remains medium.

survived.title: Green '0% suspect volume' headline when the window's sales carry no prices
survived.claim: The wash panel's headline chip colour and value both key on result.suspect.shareOfVolume (lines 199, 204), which analyzeWashTrading defines as `totalVolume > 0 ? suspectVolume / totalVolume : 0` (lib/marketIntegrity.js:325). When no sale in the window carries a parseable price, totalVolume is 0 and the ratio silently becomes 0 rather than null. `pricedSales` is computed (line 300) but never rendered anywhere in the UI, so the reader cannot see what fraction of sales the volume figures cover.
survived.failure_scenario: A window of 40 sales returns via the Alchemy path where sellerFee/protocolFee/royaltyFee all resolve to 0 (price null, api.js:417-421). The panel headline chip reads a green '0% suspect volume' while the tiles below show 'SAME-WALLET SALES 12' in red and 'SUSPECT SALES 12 (30.0% of sales)'. The green headline contradicts the body and was produced by an empty denominator, not by clean trading.
survived.suggested_fix: Return null for shareOfVolume when totalVolume is 0 and render the chip as '— suspect volume (no priced sales)' in a neutral colour; surface pricedSales / comparableSales so the coverage of the volume figures is visible.

survived.title: Sniper table silently truncates to 50 rows while the header counts all matches
survived.claim: `filtered.slice(0, 50)` caps the rendered table, but the header (line 366) reports '{filtered.length} / {opportunities.length} opportunities' and the summary (line 392) reports '{filtered.length} sniping opportunities found'. There is no 'showing first 50' note and no pagination or load-more control.
survived.failure_scenario: With a fully loaded token set and 180 matching listings, the user is told '180 sniping opportunities found' but can only ever see 50 rows, with no indication the list is cut off or how to see the rest.
survived.suggested_fix: Add a 'showing top 50 of N' footer, or a load-more control.

survived.title: Fallback whale rows link to nowhere
survived.claim: The address anchor uses `href={/^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/.test(h.address) ? etherscan : '#'}` with `target="_blank"`. FALLBACK_WHALES addresses are pre-truncated display strings such as '0xd8dA...6045' (constants.js:237-241), which fail the 40-hex test, so the href stays '#'.
survived.failure_scenario: During a holders outage the user clicks 'sample-whale-1.eth' expecting Etherscan and instead gets a new browser tab containing another copy of the marketplace.
survived.suggested_fix: Render the fallback rows as plain text rather than anchors when the address is not a full 0x-40-hex value.

survived.title: Watchlist renders rarity ranks that every other surface in the app suppresses as approximate
survived.claim: computeRarity marks ranks `rankApproximate: true` whenever fewer than 80% of the collection has been loaded (api.js:895-897). Card.jsx:45, Hero.jsx:46,78 and VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:353 all gate the rank badge on `nft.rank && !nft.rankApproximate`. Watchlist renders `Rank #{nft.rank}` at line 187 and `#{nft.rank}` in the add-search results at line 157 with no such guard. This only bites the non-Nakamigos collections (Nakamigos uses the precomputed rarity.json at api.js:852-861, which is exact); GNSS Art (9,696 supply) and Jungle Bay (5,555) fall to the runtime path with ~40 loaded tokens.
survived.failure_scenario: A user browsing Jungle Bay Ape Club watchlists an ape while ~40 of 5,555 tokens are loaded. The card reports 'Rank #3' — a rank computed against 0.7% of the collection — while the gallery card for the same ape, one tab over, deliberately shows no rank at all. The user treats it as a top-3 rarity and bids accordingly.
survived.suggested_fix: Add the `&& !nft.rankApproximate` guard at both call sites to match Card/Hero/VirtualGalleryGrid.

survived.title: MyCollection passes a listingPrice prop that Card does not accept, so listed NFTs show no price in the grid
survived.claim: Line 420 passes `listingPrice={listingMap.get(String(nft.id))?.price}` into AnimatedCard, which spreads its remaining props into Card (components/AnimatedCard.jsx:42). Card's signature is `{ nft, idx, onPick, view, isFavorite, onToggleFavorite, skipReveal }` (components/Card.jsx:8) — listingPrice is not destructured and is not referenced anywhere in the file. Grep confirms line 420 is the only occurrence of the identifier in the entire nakamigos tree. Card's price block keys on `nft.price` (Card.jsx:87), which is null for wallet tokens, so it falls through to rendering the bare token id.
survived.failure_scenario: A user with 5 of their 12 NFTs listed opens My NFTs. The grid shows all 12 cards identically, each with just '#1234' where a price would be, giving no way to tell which are on sale. The one piece of state that would distinguish them is computed, passed, and discarded.
survived.suggested_fix: Either accept and render `listingPrice` in Card (as a 'Listed Ξ x' pill) or drop the prop, so the grid does not silently lose information it already has.

survived.title: Hold-time uses post-merge block timing for pre-merge blocks, overstating holding periods by weeks
survived.claim: portfolio.js's blockToTimestamp applies a flat 12,000 ms/block on both sides of the merge (lines 37-44). api.js:285-296 carries the corrected two-branch version using 13,500 ms/block for pre-merge blocks. The derived timestamp feeds holdTime at lines 188-190 and renders as the 'Held Nd' badge (PortfolioTracker.jsx:496-503). Jungle Bay Ape Club is configured with mintBlock 14150000 and an explicit 'Feb 2022 — pre-merge (PoW era)' comment (constants.js:69), so its purchases sit in the mis-timed range.
survived.failure_scenario: A Jungle Bay holder who bought at block 14,150,000 (early Feb 2022) expands COLLECTION BREAKDOWN. The badge reads 'Held 1600d' when the true figure is roughly 1,626d — about 26 days off, and the error grows the further back the purchase sits. For anyone using hold time to reason about a long-term capital-gains threshold, a systematically short answer is the wrong direction to err.
survived.suggested_fix: Import or duplicate the two-branch blockToTimestamp from api.js:290-296 rather than keeping the stale single-slope copy.

survived.title: Acquisition cost divides every sale by 1e18 regardless of the payment token's decimals
survived.claim: saleToEth sums sellerFee/protocolFee/royaltyFee amounts and unconditionally divides by 1e18 (lines 47-53), ignoring the decimals/symbol fields Alchemy returns alongside each fee. Compare api.js:350-357, which correctly reads `event.payment.decimals ?? 18` before scaling. Any sale denominated in a non-18-decimal token collapses to a near-zero cost basis, which lands in totalCostBasis (line 192) and each row's costBasis (line 203).
survived.failure_scenario: A token was bought for 2,000 USDC (6 decimals, amount '2000000000'). saleToEth returns 0.000000002, so formatPrice renders COST BASIS as '<0.0001' and P&L as roughly the full floor value in profit — while the gainers panel shows a pnlPercent in the millions of percent because line 206 divides by that dust cost basis.
survived.suggested_fix: Scale by the fee entry's own `decimals` field the way parseOpenSeaEvents does, and skip (rather than mis-scale) any sale whose payment token is not ETH/WETH.

survived.title: The Favorites EST. VALUE tile is unreachable because favorited tokens never carry a price
survived.claim: totalValue sums `nft.price || 0` over favoriteNfts (lines 17-20), but those tokens come from nfts.allTokens, where normalizeToken hardcodes `price: null` (api.js:147) and no listing merge is ever applied to that array (enrichWithListing runs only on the modal selection and cart adds — App.jsx:395,505). totalValue is therefore always 0, and the tile is gated on `totalValue > 0` at line 49, so it never renders. This is dead UI rather than a false claim — the guard is what keeps it honest — but the intended feature does not exist.
survived.failure_scenario: A user favourites 12 NFTs, 4 of which are listed for a combined 0.6 ETH. The favorites header shows only 'SAVED 12'; the EST. VALUE figure the layout was built around never appears, on any collection, under any conditions.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass `listings` into Favorites and merge prices onto the favorited tokens (the same fix as the Watchlist price issue), or remove the tile.

survived.title: 'You can fill this' badge is suppressed permanently by a single failed holdings read
survived.claim: The board holdings map is fetched once per wallet and guarded by `holdingsWalletRef` (line 443) so it never retries. Each collection's count is `tokens?.length || 0` (line 450) with a `catch { return [...,0] }` (line 451); fetchWalletNfts returning `{tokens: [], error}` therefore yields a hard 0. `fillableHoldings` (lib/trades.js:455-456) reads that 0 as 'cannot fill'. Separately, fetchWalletNfts requests pageSize 100 with no pagination (api.js:654), so the count silently caps at 100.
survived.failure_scenario: A wallet holding the exact tokens an open board post asks for loads the board while Alchemy is throttled. The '✓ N open trades you can fill' header line and the per-card '✓ You can fill this — you hold N' badge never appear, and because the ref guard blocks any re-fetch they never appear for the rest of the session even after Alchemy recovers. The feature this code was explicitly added to provide (supply meeting demand) silently does not run.
survived.suggested_fix: Clear holdingsWalletRef when a read errors so the next board visit retries, and treat a failed read as unknown rather than zero.

survived.title: 'Total Savings' presented as a realized ETH figure
survived.claim: The stat card labelled 'Total Savings' shows `deals.reduce((s, d) => s + (d.maxTraitFloor - d.price), 0)` (line 716) formatted as a bare ETH amount (lines 821-826). That is the summed gap between each listing and the cheapest other listing sharing its most expensive trait — not money anyone saves, not a price anything has ever sold at, and only realizable by buying every deal at once and finding a buyer at the trait floor. Unlike the 'rarity-adjusted estimate' caveat TradeWindow puts under its balance meter (TradeWindow.jsx:481-483), this card carries no qualifier.
survived.failure_scenario: Deals surfaces 40 listings each a few hundredths below a trait floor. The card reads 'Total Savings 3.altogether ETH'. A user reads that as an available profit figure for the tab, when it is an unrealizable sum over comparables that would themselves move if bought.
survived.suggested_fix: Relabel to something like 'Combined gap to trait floor' and add the same 'estimate' qualifier the trade balance meter uses.

survived.title: The collection bid wall disappears the moment the user connects a wallet
survived.claim: CollectionOffersPanel is rendered only inside the `if (!wallet)` early-return. The connected render path has no collection-offers panel at all, so connecting a wallet removes information rather than adding it — the opposite of what the F698 comment above it describes.
survived.failure_scenario: A visitor lands on the Bids tab disconnected and sees the public "Collection Bids" ladder (line 526-527). They connect their wallet to place a bid against it. The component now takes the render path at lines 547-762, which contains only the three personal tabs — the bid ladder they were looking at is gone, and there is no way to get it back on this tab. (It still exists on the Listings tab at Listings.jsx:729, so the data is not lost, just unreachable from where the user was.) The comment at lines 518-522 states the intent was "Additive — the gate is unchanged, it now just sits under a public bid ladder", which is not what the code does.
survived.suggested_fix: Render CollectionOffersPanel above the tab bar in the connected path too, so the ladder persists across connect.

survived.title: "LIVE — Real active listings via merged" leaks an internal enum as a marketplace name
survived.claim: sourceLabel maps only "opensea" to a human name; the other two mergeListings values pass through raw, so the live banner reads "Real active listings via merged" or "via native".
survived.failure_scenario: The native orderbook has at least one listing. mergeListings (api.js:780-782) returns source "merged" (or "native" if OpenSea returned nothing). Listings.jsx:618-622 leaves those strings untouched, and line 847 renders "LIVE — Real active listings via merged". A user reading a provenance claim about where their prices come from is shown a word that names no marketplace and cannot be verified anywhere.
survived.suggested_fix: Map the remaining values: "native" → the app's own orderbook name, "merged" → "OpenSea + Tradermigos orderbook".

survived.title: Ninja subtype and rare-combo counts are hardcoded and asserted as collection-wide facts
survived.claim: NINJA_SUBTYPES (319/90/16) and RARE_COMBOS (4/43) are literal arrays in the component, rendered as '319 exist' (line 411) and 'Only 4 exist across the entire collection' (line 444-446). They are never cross-checked against the loaded token attributes, and the section header calls them 'Community-discovered'. CHARACTER_TYPES (constants.js:346-361) is at least internally consistent (the 12 counts sum to exactly 20,000), but is likewise never validated against metadata.
survived.failure_scenario: A user reads 'Only 4 exist across the entire collection' as a scarcity claim from the marketplace and prices a bid on it. The number originates from a community forum, not from the chain or the metadata the app has already loaded, and nothing in the UI attributes it. If it is wrong, or the source was about a different trait spelling, the app has no way to notice.
survived.suggested_fix: Compute these counts from the loaded token attributes once the full load completes (the data is already in `tokens`), or attribute them inline as community-reported rather than stating them flatly.

survived.title: "Showing cached example data" banner fires over genuinely live activity when only the STATS call fell back
survived.claim: `setIsLive(!statsData.fallback && !actData.fallback)` conflates two independent fetches. ActivityFeed renders the banner on `isLive === false && activities?.length > 0` (ActivityFeed.jsx:262-271). isLive also starts as false (line 27) and resets to false on every collection switch (line 50).
survived.failure_scenario: fetchCollectionStats falls back (its own fallback path is well flagged elsewhere) while fetchActivity returns fully live OpenSea sales. The user sees a yellow warning saying the real, current sales they are looking at are 'cached example data'. The same banner flashes on first paint and on every collection switch before the hook resolves. The net effect is that the banner stops meaning anything, which is exactly what makes it useless on the occasion when the data really IS fabricated (see the FALLBACK_ACTIVITY finding).
survived.suggested_fix: Track activityIsLive separately from statsIsLive and gate the activity banner on the former only.

survived.title: A failed date-range refetch leaves the previous range's rows and stats on screen under the new label
survived.claim: loadActivities' catch block toasts and returns without touching fetchedActivities, nextPageKey, apiEmpty or apiFallback — while daysBack has already been changed by the click handler, so the new range button is rendered as selected.
survived.failure_scenario: User is on '30d'. They click '24h'. fetchActivity throws (only AbortError normally escapes, but the native-orderbook and proxy layers can surface others). The toast 'Failed to load activity' appears for a few seconds and disappears; the 30-day rows and the 30-day SALES/VOLUME totals stay on screen with '24h' highlighted. The user reads 30 days of volume as 24-hour volume with nothing on screen contradicting it.
survived.suggested_fix: On error, clear fetchedActivities (or keep them but revert the highlighted range button) and set a sticky error state that renders in place of the list rather than a transient toast.

survived.title: Offer overcommitment warning silently disables itself when the active-offers read fails
survived.claim: fetchMyOffers(...).catch(err => console.warn(...)) leaves activeOfferTotal at its 0n initial value. The overcommitment guard at lines 316-338 compares activeOfferTotal + priceWei against the balance, so a failed read makes the condition unreachable and the red warning never renders.
survived.failure_scenario: User already has 1.2 WETH of live offers out. They open the trait-offer modal from the Traits tab; the fetchMyOffers call fails (same rate-limited OpenSea proxy). They enter 0.9 WETH against a 1.0 WETH balance. The warning that would have told them their combined commitments exceed their balance is silently absent, so they place an offer that can fail if another is accepted first. Absence of a warning reads as 'no problem detected'.
survived.suggested_fix: Track a fetchFailed flag and, when set, replace the warning slot with 'Could not read your existing offers — total exposure unknown' rather than rendering nothing.

survived.title: Declining the SIWE signature produces a second, contradictory toast blaming the network
survived.claim: `runAuthed` (lines 360-379) toasts "Sign-in is required to post in chat." and returns null when `signIn()` throws (user rejects, wrong chain, no provider). `handleSend` then sees a falsy `msg` and fires the else branch at line 558: "Failed to send message. Please check your connection and try again." The same double-toast happens when the retry after sign-in still returns needsAuth (line 376 returns null).
survived.failure_scenario: User clicks Send, gets a wallet signature prompt, hits Reject. Two toasts stack: one correctly saying sign-in is required, one telling them to check their internet connection. The user checks their connection, retries, and hits the same wall. A wrong-chain rejection (useSiweAuth.js:109-111 throws "Switch to Ethereum Mainnet") is likewise reported as a connection problem — the actual, actionable error message is thrown away by the empty catch at line 368.
survived.suggested_fix: Have runAuthed signal "aborted by auth" distinctly (e.g. a sentinel) so handleSend skips the generic failure toast, and surface the signIn error's message.

survived.title: Spam cooldown is recorded before the send is attempted, so a failed send blocks the retry for 5 seconds
survived.claim: `lastMessageTime[wallet] = Date.now()` is set at line 541, before the `sendMessage` / SIWE round-trip at lines 543-559. `isSpam` (lines 87-96) then rejects the next attempt within SPAM_COOLDOWN_MS=5000.
survived.failure_scenario: Send fails (network blip, or the user signs in on the second prompt). The user immediately clicks Send again and is told "Please wait a few seconds before sending another message" — a rate-limit message for a message that was never accepted. Compounded by the previous finding: they've just been told to check their connection, and now they're throttled for doing so.
survived.suggested_fix: Record lastMessageTime only after a successful send.

survived.title: "Live" badge and its "Connected to the shared community chat" tooltip reflect env-var presence, not connectivity
survived.claim: `CHAT_ENABLED = !!(VITE_SUPABASE_URL && VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)` (supabase.js:89) — a build-time env check. CommunityChat renders a green pill reading "Live" with title "Connected to the shared community chat" whenever that constant is true (lines 659-666). Nothing observes actual channel health: `subscribeToMessages` (supabase.js:358-376) calls `.subscribe()` with no status callback, so CHANNEL_ERROR / TIMED_OUT / CLOSED are invisible to the component.
survived.failure_scenario: Supabase Realtime is degraded or the websocket is blocked by a corporate proxy. The initial REST fetch succeeds so the message list renders normally and the badge shows green "Live", tooltip "Connected". Other users' messages never arrive during the session and the user has no signal that they are looking at a frozen room — they interpret silence as nobody talking.
survived.suggested_fix: Drive the pill from the realtime channel's subscribe() status (SUBSCRIBED → Live, otherwise Reconnecting), not from the env constant.

survived.title: Local mode still toasts "Message sent!" for a message that never leaves the browser
survived.claim: When CHAT_ENABLED is false the send path (lines 560-575) writes to `localStorage["<slug>_chat"]` and toasts "Message sent!". The empty state in the same mode reads "Welcome to Nakamigos Chat / Be the first to start a conversation in the Nakamigos community" (lines 711-718) — copy that describes a shared room. The only honest signal is the grey "Local mode" pill and its hover tooltip (lines 661-665), which most users never hover.
survived.failure_scenario: A production build ships without VITE_SUPABASE_URL/VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (the exact stale-prod-build class this repo hit on 07-26). Every visitor posts into their own localStorage, sees "Message sent!", sees their message in the feed, and believes they are talking to a community. Nobody ever replies because nothing was transmitted.
survived.suggested_fix: In local mode, toast "Saved locally — chat backend not configured" and make the empty/composer copy state it inline rather than only in a tooltip.

survived.title: Muting every author renders the "Be the first to start a conversation" welcome state over a room that has history
survived.claim: The mute filter is applied inside `visibleMessages` (lines 510-514), and the empty-state branch keys on `visibleMessages.length === 0` (line 694). It cannot distinguish "the room is empty" from "you have muted everyone currently in view", and the loadFailed branch doesn't cover it either.
survived.failure_scenario: A user mutes the 3 wallets posting in a quiet room. The feed then shows the cheerful "Welcome to Nakamigos Chat — Be the first to start a conversation in the Nakamigos community" as if the room were empty. The only counter-evidence is the small "3 wallets muted / unmute all" strip below the list (lines 865-881). Same effect with the Alpha/Discussion filters combined with mutes.
survived.suggested_fix: Compute the empty state against the pre-mute list and show "All visible messages are from muted wallets" when messages.length > 0.

survived.title: Silently-swallowed trades fetch removes the accept-from-thread control and mis-states trade history in the DM view of the chat tab
survived.claim: The Chat tab's DMs sub-view (CommunityChat.jsx:671-674 renders <DirectMessages embedded/>). `loadTradesMap` (lines 206-217) has a bare `catch { }` leaving `tradesById` as `{}`. Two consequences: (a) `hasTradeHistory` (lines 329-334) is computed over that empty map, so the ⚠ "No trade history with this wallet. Verify who you're talking to" banner (lines 560-568) fires for a counterparty you have traded with — a security assertion produced by a failed read; (b) every `DmTradeCard` falls to the `!trade` branch (lines 68-82), replacing the trade summary and the "Accept trade" button with a generic "Trade offer — view in Trades" link.
survived.failure_scenario: The /api/supabase-proxy trades read 500s once on mount. A counterparty has sent a live trade offer in the DM thread. The user opens it and sees only a bare link plus a scam warning contradicting their own trade history with that wallet. They cannot accept from the thread and are given no indication anything failed to load. (The warning errs safe; the missing accept control does not — a time-limited offer can expire while the UI shows no error.)
survived.suggested_fix: Track a tradesMapFailed flag; suppress the hasTradeHistory claim when it's set, and label the fallback card "Couldn't load this trade — retry" rather than a plain deep link.

survived.title: Pro status also launders a failed Alchemy read into "NOT YET A MEMBER" (latent behind PRO_PASS_LIVE)
survived.claim: `setIsPro((data?.totalCount || 0) > 0)` at line 32. Same root cause as the chat holder gate: `fetchWalletNfts` (api.js:648-664) never throws, so the `.catch` at lines 34-36 is dead and a failed read arrives as `totalCount: 0`. The returned `error` string is discarded. Currently unreachable — PRO_PASS_LIVE is false because TEGRIDY_PRO_PASS_ADDRESS is the zero address (constants.ts:70) and the effect returns early at line 23 — but it activates the instant the operator sets the address, with no other gate.
survived.failure_scenario: Post-launch: a wallet holding a Pro Pass opens the Pro tab while the Alchemy proxy is rate-limited. StatusPill renders "NOT YET A MEMBER" (line 21) and the CTA reads "Mint Pro Pass" with the footnote "One mint, lifetime access" (line 90) — actively inviting an existing holder to buy a second Pass. Unlike useHolderStatus this one at least does not persist the wrong answer.
survived.suggested_fix: Make fetchWalletNfts failure distinguishable and render a "couldn't check" state instead of a membership verdict.

survived.title: Composer shows "Own a Nakamigos to post" during the in-flight holder check because `loading` is never passed down
survived.claim: App.jsx:396 destructures only `{ tier: holderTier, count: holderCount }` from useHolderStatus and discards `loading`. CommunityChat's composer branch (lines 885/925) treats `!holderTier` as proven non-ownership, and useHolderStatus initialises tier to null (line 48) and resets it to null on every contract change (lines 56-61).
survived.failure_scenario: A genuine holder connects their wallet on the Chat tab. For the duration of the getNFTsForOwner round-trip (plus up to 2 retries with backoff on a slow connection — several seconds), they are shown a gold "HOLDER EXCLUSIVE" pill and the sentence "Own a Nakamigos to post" with no composer. It's a definitive claim about their wallet rendered before the app has any evidence either way; on the cold-cache mobile path it is the first thing they read.
survived.suggested_fix: Pass `loading` through and render a neutral "Checking your holdings…" state instead of the ownership denial.

survived.title: 'Transaction History' is an undisclosed per-browser localStorage log that reports 'no transactions' on any read failure
survived.claim: The tab is labelled 'History' in both navs and headed 'Transaction History', but its only source is `localStorage.getItem(`${slug}_tx_history`)` (line 9-15), written client-side by recordTransaction (lib/transactions.js:14) and capped at 50 entries. `loadHistory` returns [] on any parse failure, and the wallet filter at line 60-63 returns [] for anything not written by this browser. Nothing states the log is device-local.
survived.failure_scenario: A user buys two NFTs through the app on their desktop, then opens the same wallet on their phone (or in a private window, or after clearing site data) and taps History. They are told 'No Nakamigos transactions yet' with the follow-up 'Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here.' Both purchases exist on-chain and are attributable to the connected wallet. The same message appears if the stored JSON is corrupted. A user checking whether a purchase went through gets a confident 'no' from a read that simply had nothing local to read.
survived.suggested_fix: Add one line of provenance to the header and empty state ('Recorded on this device only — see Etherscan for your full on-chain history') with a link to etherscan.io/address/{wallet}, so an empty log never reads as an assertion about the wallet.

survived.title: About links to Discord invites for collections whose own lore record states there is no Discord
survived.claim: NAKAMIGOS_EXTRA_LINKS hardcodes ['Discord', 'https://discord.gg/nakamigos'] and JUNGLEBAY_EXTRA_LINKS hardcodes ['Discord', 'https://discord.gg/junglebay'] (line 46). The project's own curated record contradicts both: constants.js:273 sets `discord: null` for Nakamigos with the comment 'initially no Discord — radical minimalism', and constants.js:328 sets `discord: null` for Jungle Bay. The lore object is never consulted when building the links array. The same block also links 'nakamigos.io' while COLLECTION_LORE records the website as 'https://nakamigo.ai' (constants.js:275).
survived.failure_scenario: A visitor on the About page clicks Discord expecting the official community and lands on an expired or never-existent invite. Because the app's own data file records these as absent, at least one of the two representations is wrong on every render — either the link is dead or the lore is stale, and a user cannot tell which.
survived.suggested_fix: Build the extra-links arrays from COLLECTION_LORE[slug].community, dropping any null entry, so the links and the recorded facts cannot disagree.

survived.title: Landing page hardcodes the API badge to DEMO regardless of upstream health
survived.claim: LandingShell passes `isLive={false}` unconditionally to Header, so the badge at Header.jsx:580-586 always renders the grey DEMO pill with the tooltip 'Using demo/fallback data — some features may be limited'. Meanwhile CollectionLanding does perform live stats fetches for each collection card.
survived.failure_scenario: A first-time visitor lands on /nakamigos with every API healthy. The header tells them the app is on demo data and 'some features may be limited' while the collection cards below are showing live floors and volumes. It errs toward under-claiming rather than over-claiming, so nobody is misled into a trade — but the badge is decoupled from reality in both directions and trains users to ignore it, which blunts it on the collection views where it does matter.
survived.suggested_fix: Either omit the badge on the landing shell or wire it to the landing's own fetch state so it reflects something real.

survived.title: Footer and constants claim a flat 1% platform fee 'on all trades'; OpenSea-routed buys pay us nothing
survived.claim: The footer trust strip renders '✓ Flat 1% platform fee ↗' whenever PLATFORM_FEE_BPS > 0, and constants.js:193 comments it as '1% on all trades'. PLATFORM_FEE_BPS is only ever applied on the native paths — lib/orderbook.js:352 (native listing consideration) and api-offers.js:255-284 (offers). Buying an OpenSea-sourced listing routes to Seaport with OpenSea's consideration and adds no Tegridy fee; Modal.jsx:408 already distinguishes 'Tegridy order book · incl. 1% fee' from a bare 'OpenSea listing'.
survived.failure_scenario: A buyer reads the footer, assumes a 1% cut on every purchase, and prices that into a bid on an OpenSea listing where no such fee is taken. The direction of the error favours the user (we overstate our own fee rather than hide it), so no one is overcharged — but it is a blanket claim the code does not back, and Modal already scopes it correctly two clicks away.
survived.suggested_fix: Scope the footer copy to match Modal ('Flat 1% fee on Tegridy order-book trades') and fix the constants.js comment.
